# Document Control and Navigation

|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

## 00.1 Mandatory controlled artifacts

| **Artifact**             | **Minimum controlled content**                                                                                         | **System of record**              |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Experience contract**  | ID, version, gate, actors, scope, states, data authority, permissions, actions, AI, accessibility, tests and telemetry | Experience Contract Registry      |
| **Wireframe set**        | Annotated desktop reference, responsive rules, all applicable states, workflows, component usage and content examples  | Controlled Design Repository      |
| **State matrix**         | Universal states plus domain states, trigger, visual semantics, actions, recovery, audit and test evidence             | Experience Contract Registry      |
| **Design-system object** | Token/component version, semantics, keyboard behavior, accessibility, deprecation and consuming experiences            | Design System Registry            |
| **Content object**       | Term, status copy, error/recovery copy, AI disclosure, jurisdiction/locale, approver and effective version             | Content and Disclosure Registry   |
| **Traceability map**     | Requirements, APIs/events, data authority, permissions, evidence, tests, telemetry and release evidence                | Requirement Traceability Register |
| **Visual baseline**      | Approved render by viewport, theme, locale, state and feature flag                                                     | Visual Regression Repository      |
| **Release record**       | Implemented version, test results, exceptions, approvals, canary results and production observations                   | Release Evidence Register         |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                        | **Why it fails a Tier-1 review**                                                                 | **Refinement incorporated**                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Wireframes treated as pictures**                 | A picture omits data authority, permissions, failure behavior, audit events, AI and performance. | Every wireframe is a machine-linked experience contract and implementation package.                                          |
| **Happy path presented as the product**            | Security and assurance systems spend material time partial, stale, unauthorized or degraded.     | Seven mandatory state classes with acceptance evidence; non-complete never renders healthy.                                  |
| **Permission denial grouped with errors**          | It obscures whether the system failed or correctly protected access.                             | Unauthorized/restricted is an independent state with reason, request path and audit behavior.                                |
| **Design tool becomes source of truth**            | Comments and screens drift from requirements, APIs, schemas and tests.                           | Contract registry is authoritative; design files are versioned rendered views with traceability.                             |
| **Scores and gauges hide derivation**              | Opaque summaries create false assurance and cannot withstand audit.                              | Every number expands to factors, policy/evaluator version, scope, freshness, confidence and evidence.                        |
| **AI assistant added as a generic chat panel**     | Unbounded chat creates cross-tenant, injection, hallucination and action-authority risk.         | Risk-classed AI patterns with citations, tool reauthorization, review state, fallback and kill switches.                     |
| **Accessibility deferred to implementation**       | Late remediation changes hierarchy, components and workflows and creates legal/product risk.     | Accessibility is a design input, contract field and release gate from G0.                                                    |
| **Mobile responsiveness means hiding columns**     | Critical authority, state and evidence context can disappear on smaller screens.                 | Information-priority and safe-mobile behavior; high-impact actions may be read-only unless approved.                         |
| **Product analytics captures everything**          | Session replay or raw events can leak customer content, secrets and regulated data.              | Purpose-bound, minimized telemetry; immutable security audit remains separate; replay off by default.                        |
| **A/B experimentation applies to high-risk flows** | Experiments can weaken warnings, confirmation, disclosures or security behavior.                 | Security-, evidence-, compliance- and authority-critical interactions require controlled change, not casual experimentation. |
| **Exact inventory counts not gate-linked**         | Teams can claim G1 readiness while foundational screens or states are missing.                   | Exactly 38 contracts: 29 G1-blocking and 9 G2-blocking, with explicit evidence per contract.                                 |
| **Design-system changes treated as cosmetic**      | A token or component change can alter status meaning, focus, approval or data exposure.          | Risk-classed design-system lifecycle with impact analysis, deprecation and regression evidence.                              |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Explicit Exclusions

| **In scope**                                                                                               | **Out of scope / prohibited assumption**                                                                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Experience-contract architecture for customer, analyst, auditor, executive, AI and developer surfaces.** | Brand campaign pages, marketing-site visual design and speculative future marketplace experiences.                                              |
| **Information architecture, navigation, state semantics, page anatomy and shared patterns.**               | Pixel-perfect production visual design in this specification; visual styling remains governed by controlled design-system assets.               |
| **Data, permission, API/event, evidence, AI, accessibility, telemetry and test mappings.**                 | Replacing back-end authority with client-side calculations or hidden UI logic.                                                                  |
| **Exactly 38 minimum defensible wireframes and their G1/G2 gates.**                                        | Partner/MSP console, sovereign administration, mobile-native apps, marketplace and customer AI-governance workspace before phase authorization. |
| **Responsive, localized, accessible and degraded operation.**                                              | Assuming desktop, English, always-online or fully healthy operation.                                                                            |
| **Controlled prototype and remote-team custody.**                                                          | Production data, secrets, customer evidence or unrestricted threat details in design files.                                                     |

# 04 \| Binding Experience Architecture Invariants

| **ID**        | **Invariant**                                                                                                                        |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **UX-INV-01** | Tenant, environment and region are persistently visible on every authenticated page.                                                 |
| **UX-INV-02** | No material assertion, score or status exists without a drill-down to evidence, scope, version and freshness.                        |
| **UX-INV-03** | PARTIAL, STALE, COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY, PERMISSION_CHANGED and EVALUATOR_FAILED never render compliant or healthy.                      |
| **UX-INV-04** | Unauthorized/restricted is distinct from error/unavailable and produces a controlled audit event.                                    |
| **UX-INV-05** | Every destructive or privileged action restates tenant, target, authority, approvals, blast radius and rollback before confirmation. |
| **UX-INV-06** | AI output is labeled, source-cited, confidence-bearing, reviewable, overridable and never styled as a system fact.                   |
| **UX-INV-07** | No LLM is authoritative for authentication, authorization, entitlement, evidence integrity, compliance status or response approval.  |
| **UX-INV-08** | Composite numbers reveal their component factors and governing policy/evaluator version.                                             |
| **UX-INV-09** | No silent mutation: changed configuration, status, assignment or conclusion is versioned and attributable.                           |
| **UX-INV-10** | Accessibility and non-color semantics are release-blocking requirements.                                                             |
| **UX-INV-11** | Client applications do not become independent sources of truth or retain secrets/customer content without approved authority.        |
| **UX-INV-12** | Every page declares all applicable state classes, recovery paths and telemetry.                                                      |
| **UX-INV-13** | Wireframes are controlled contracts linked to requirements and tests, not screenshots attached to tickets.                           |
| **UX-INV-14** | Responsive adaptation preserves state, authority, evidence and privacy context.                                                      |
| **UX-INV-15** | Security-, evidence-, AI- and compliance-critical flows are not subjected to unapproved experimentation.                             |
| **UX-INV-16** | Every customer-visible claim follows the Claim and Disclosure Register.                                                              |
| **UX-INV-17** | Design-system changes cannot weaken an invariant or mandatory state.                                                                 |
| **UX-INV-18** | Experience release evidence is retained and reproducible by version, viewport, locale, state and feature configuration.              |

# 05 \| Actors, Personas and Experience Boundaries

| **Actor**                    | **Primary decisions**                                                   | **Default authority boundary**                                           | **Required experience qualities**                                            |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Customer administrator**   | Configure tenant, connectors, users, policies, entitlements and exports | Tenant-scoped administration; no hidden cross-tenant capability          | Guided, explicit permissions, reversible configuration, audit visibility.    |
| **Security analyst / SOC**   | Triage alerts, investigate, manage cases and propose response           | R0/R1 by default; higher authority per customer policy and role          | Dense data, keyboard efficiency, provenance, safe action controls.           |
| **Incident commander**       | Coordinate major incident, communications and recovery                  | Named incident authority; cannot alter evidence or bypass approvals      | Shared timeline, clocks, roles, decisions, reconciliation and handoff.       |
| **Compliance / GRC owner**   | Implement controls, assess evidence, manage risks and exceptions        | Can attest assigned controls; cannot self-approve conflicting exceptions | Completeness, lineage, expiry, approvals and audit-ready exports.            |
| **External auditor**         | Review frozen packages, evidence and comments                           | Read-only, purpose-bound, time-limited                                   | Independent verification, known limitations, activity logging.               |
| **Executive / Board reader** | Understand material risk, incidents and assurance posture               | Read/approve according to governance; no operational mutation            | Transparent factors, concise limitations, drill-down and immutable snapshot. |
| **Developer / integrator**   | Manage API clients, webhooks, schemas and sandbox                       | Technical scope only; production permissions explicit                    | Stable contracts, testability, rotation, delivery diagnostics.               |
| **Support engineer**         | Assist under customer-approved, JIT, purpose-bound access               | No standing customer-content access                                      | Visible support session, masking, audit trail and expiry.                    |
| **AI system / agent**        | Generate bounded advice or invoke allowlisted read/tools                | Separate principal; no implicit human authority                          | Visible provenance, review status, tool scope and kill-switch state.         |

# 08 \| Seven Mandatory State Classes and Domain-State Overlay

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image4.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image158.png" />

***Figure 4 - Seven mandatory experience state classes.***

| **State class**               | **Required semantics**                                                      | **Required controls and evidence**                                                                         |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Loading / resolving**       | The system is acquiring or evaluating data; no conclusion is yet available. | Progress semantics, timeout, cancel/retry where safe, skeletons that do not imply values, telemetry.       |
| **Empty / first use**         | No object exists or none match the current scope.                           | Distinguish first use, no results and no permission; provide safe next step and help.                      |
| **Nominal / populated**       | Authoritative data is available within freshness and completeness policy.   | Scope, source, effective time, actions, evidence link and status semantics.                                |
| **Partial / incomplete**      | Some expected inputs, sources, permissions or evaluations are missing.      | Enumerated gaps, affected conclusions, remediation owner, no green/compliant treatment.                    |
| **Stale / degraded**          | Data or service exceeded freshness/quality threshold or fallback is active. | Age, impact, fallback, last good state, recovery status and non-suppressible banner.                       |
| **Error / unavailable**       | A service or operation failed unexpectedly.                                 | Stable error code, correlation ID, retry/escalation, preserved input and no sensitive leakage.             |
| **Unauthorized / restricted** | Policy correctly denies or limits the operation or data.                    | Reason category, request/access path where allowed, support route, audit event; never presented as outage. |

## 08.1 Domain-state overlay

| **Domain state**                | **Examples**                                                    | **Relationship to universal states**                                                   |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Pending / awaiting approval** | Policy change, risk acceptance, R3 action, audit package freeze | May be nominal data with a pending workflow; does not replace partial or unauthorized. |
| **Simulation / preview**        | Playbook, response action, policy or report preview             | Must be visually unmistakable and cannot emit live side effects.                       |
| **Executing / reconciling**     | Connector backfill, action execution, export, package build     | Shows progress, cancel limits, idempotency and observed-state reconciliation.          |
| **Compensating / rolling back** | Failed response action or configuration deployment              | Shows original action, rollback status, residual risk and evidence.                    |
| **Legal hold / immutable**      | Evidence, case or export under hold                             | Disables deletion and explains authority without exposing restricted legal details.    |
| **Superseded / expired**        | Rule, package, exception, token or report                       | Read-only historical state with successor and effective dates.                         |

# 10 \| Evidence-Linked Assertions and Transparent Numbers

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image6.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image160.png" />

***Figure 6 - Assertion-to-evidence drill-down chain.***

| **Assertion type**     | **Minimum disclosure**                                                     | **Required drill-down**                                                             |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Control status**     | Scope, assessment period, completeness, freshness and evaluator version    | Tests, evidence, collectors, gaps, exceptions and assessment history.               |
| **Risk score**         | Factor values, weights/policy version, confidence and unknown inputs       | Assets, findings, controls, threat context, accepted risk and owner.                |
| **Detection priority** | Rule/version, severity, confidence, coverage state and enrichment snapshot | Input events, logic, factors, ATT&CK mapping and prior decisions.                   |
| **Executive metric**   | Population, period, definition, source and known limitations               | Constituent objects and frozen snapshot/package.                                    |
| **AI statement**       | Use case, sources, freshness, confidence/quality signal and review state   | Citations, retrieval bundle, model/prompt profile, human decision and tool history. |
| **Service health**     | Affected capability/region, measured indicator, start time and impact      | SLI/SLO source, incidents, dependencies, mitigation and status history.             |

# 11 \| High-Impact Actions, Authority and Confirmation Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image7.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image161.png" />

***Figure 7 - High-impact action proposal, approval and execution flow.***

| **Action risk**                | **Experience requirement**                                      | **Authorization / confirmation**                                                                   |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R0 Observe**                 | Read, collect, enrich, query and notify; no external change     | Standard permission; evidence of material access as applicable.                                    |
| **R1 Recommend**               | Proposal separated from execution; rationale and evidence shown | Named human accept/modify/reject; decision recorded.                                               |
| **R2 Pre-authorized low risk** | Reversible, bounded and customer-approved actions only          | Policy reference, blast radius, attestation, ceiling and receipt visible.                          |
| **R3 High impact**             | Privileged account, server, segment or workload action          | Dual approval/named customer authority, step-up, simulation history and customer-side attestation. |
| **R4 Emergency**               | Break-glass, time-boxed and exceptional                         | Explicit emergency banner, named authority, immediate escalation and post-action review.           |
| **Bulk / mass action**         | Any action exceeding resource or rate threshold                 | Independent policy and operational approval; preview sample; hard ceiling and freeze control.      |

# 12 \| AI Interaction, Agentic Controls and Human Oversight

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image8.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image162.png" />

***Figure 8 - AI interaction, grounding and human-oversight flow.***

| **AI experience element** | **Mandatory presentation**                                           | **Mandatory control**                                                                        |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AI region / label**     | Clearly distinct from system facts; use-case name and generated time | Gateway route, tenant/purpose context and approved use-case ID.                              |
| **Grounded answer**       | Citations per material claim; source freshness and coverage          | Citation validation, retrieval provenance and cross-tenant isolation.                        |
| **Confidence / quality**  | Plain-language uncertainty and limitations; no false precision       | Use-case-specific evaluation signal; never treated as probability of truth unless validated. |
| **Human review**          | Unreviewed, reviewed, modified, approved or rejected state           | Reviewer identity, rationale and decision evidence.                                          |
| **Agent/tool request**    | Planned tool, scope, side effect, authority and expected result      | Target-side reauthorization, budget, timeout, rate limits and kill switch.                   |
| **AI memory**             | Visible when an output uses retained preferences/case context        | Memory type, tenant, purpose, expiry, edit/delete path and no hidden cross-case memory.      |
| **Fallback**              | Deterministic non-AI workflow and degraded-state banner              | No routing to unapproved provider or region; critical path remains available.                |
| **Feedback / incident**   | Correction, unsafe output, bad citation and privacy report paths     | Creates evaluation/incident signal without exposing confidential prompt content broadly.     |

# 13 \| Design System, Components and Status Semantics

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image9.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image163.png" />

***Figure 9 - Controlled design-system architecture.***

| **Foundation / pattern**     | **Controlled requirements**                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Typography and hierarchy** | Readable scale, stable semantic headings, dense operational variant, minimum text sizes and no information encoded by font styling alone. |
| **Color and status**         | Approved semantic palette with text/icon/shape redundancy; dark mode parity; no green for non-COMPLETE; contrast tested.                  |
| **Spacing and density**      | Comfortable and dense modes under token control; keyboard/focus and touch target dimensions remain valid.                                 |
| **Focus and keyboard**       | Visible focus, logical order, skip links, no traps, shortcut discoverability and conflict management.                                     |
| **Motion**                   | Purposeful, bounded, reduced-motion alternative; no flashing, false urgency or motion-only state change.                                  |
| **Tables and queues**        | Column authority, sort/filter state, pagination/virtualization, row selection, bulk-action preview and persistent position.               |
| **Charts and graphs**        | Data table alternative, units, definition, time range, uncertainty, missing data and non-color series identification.                     |
| **Dialogs and drawers**      | Focus management, escape rules, unsaved state, explicit action hierarchy and no nested modal chains.                                      |
| **Files and exports**        | Classification, scope, format, size, integrity, virus-scan, progress, cancellation and audit behavior.                                    |
| **Status banners**           | State class, impact, start/age, affected scope, remediation and non-suppressible conditions.                                              |

# 14 \| Accessibility, Inclusive Design and Content Standard

| **Control area**         | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                | **Release evidence**                                 |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| **Semantic structure**   | Landmarks, headings, labels, descriptions, table headers and programmatic relationships                  | Automated checks plus manual screen-reader review.   |
| **Keyboard**             | Complete operation, visible focus, logical order, no trap, shortcuts documented                          | Keyboard walkthrough for every G1/G2 workflow.       |
| **Contrast / non-color** | Text, controls, focus and status meet approved contrast; status uses text/icon/shape                     | Token test and representative visual audit.          |
| **Zoom / reflow**        | Usable at 200% zoom and reflow target; no loss of evidence, authority or action context                  | Viewport matrix and manual review.                   |
| **Screen readers**       | Dynamic updates announced with appropriate priority; tables/timelines understandable                     | NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver coverage per supported platform. |
| **Cognitive clarity**    | Plain language, consistent terms, progressive disclosure, error prevention and recovery                  | Content review and moderated task testing.           |
| **Motor / touch**        | Adequate targets, no drag-only tasks, time limits adjustable where permitted                             | Touch and alternative-input test.                    |
| **Motion / sensory**     | Reduced motion, no seizure-inducing effects, audio not required, captions/transcripts where media exists | Preference and media test.                           |
| **Errors**               | Specific, field-linked, persistent until resolved; no sensitive data in error text                       | Negative tests and accessibility tree review.        |
| **Documents / exports**  | Generated reports and audit packages include structured headings, tables, alt text and language metadata | Export accessibility audit.                          |

# 15 \| Responsive, Device, Localization and Time-Zone Behavior

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image10.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image164.png" />

***Figure 10 - Responsive, localization and accessibility adaptation.***

| **Dimension**        | **Controlled rule**                                                                                                            |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Desktop**          | Reference operational experience; supports dense multi-panel workspaces and keyboard workflows.                                |
| **Tablet**           | Reflows panels, preserves context, provides safe drawers and avoids hover-only interaction.                                    |
| **Mobile web**       | Essential read/acknowledge/status tasks; high-impact actions disabled or separately approved; no hidden trust context.         |
| **Native mobile**    | Out of minimum scope; must not be inferred from responsive web designs.                                                        |
| **Locale**           | Externalized text, pluralization, number/currency/date formatting, text expansion and no concatenated sentences.               |
| **Time**             | Display customer/local time with explicit zone and source time; investigations permit UTC; ambiguous dates prohibited.         |
| **Right-to-left**    | Logical property usage, mirrored navigation where appropriate, non-mirrored security icons where meaning would change.         |
| **Network quality**  | Progressive rendering, retry, resumable workflows, offline-safe read cache only where approved and visible.                    |
| **Browser/platform** | Controlled support matrix; unsupported environments receive explicit guidance rather than silent failure.                      |
| **Print/export**     | Print styles preserve classification, scope, time, evidence and limitations; browser print is not an audit-package substitute. |

# 16 \| Security, Privacy and Sensitive-Data Experience Controls

| **Risk**                                | **Experience control**                                                                                                   |
|-----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cross-tenant context confusion**      | Persistent tenant/environment; explicit confirmation; no cached cross-tenant objects; tenant switch resets scoped state. |
| **Sensitive-data overexposure**         | Field masking, purpose/role-based reveal, copy/export controls, JIT support access and view audit events.                |
| **Credential/secret handling**          | Never render full secret after creation; one-time reveal only if approved; secure rotation and revocation paths.         |
| **Session and privilege**               | Session risk, elevation and expiry visible; privileged session banner; reauthentication for high-risk actions.           |
| **Clickjacking / deceptive overlays**   | Frame protections and trusted-origin behavior; no hidden action beneath overlays.                                        |
| **Prompt injection / attacker content** | Untrusted content labeled and safely rendered; scripts/markup neutralized; AI tool requests separately authorized.       |
| **File upload**                         | Type/size checks, malware scan, quarantine, content rendering isolation and customer-visible processing state.           |
| **Export / download**                   | Scope preview, classification, watermark/manifest where applicable, legal-hold check and audit event.                    |
| **Clipboard / screenshots**             | Minimize exposed data and log controlled exports; do not claim browser screenshot prevention as a security control.      |
| **Support access**                      | Customer-visible active support indicator where appropriate, purpose, expiry, masking and post-use record.               |
| **Client storage**                      | No secrets or unrestricted evidence in local storage; cache encrypted/scoped/expiring where approved.                    |
| **Error and diagnostics**               | Stable codes and correlation IDs; no stack traces, secrets, internal topology or cross-tenant identifiers.               |

# 17 \| Performance, Progressive Rendering and Offline/Degraded Behavior

| **Experience class**     | **Target architecture**                                                                   | **Failure / degradation treatment**                                                       |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Shell and navigation** | Render stable shell and trust context before secondary data; avoid layout shift           | Global state banner and cached non-sensitive navigation metadata.                         |
| **Operational queue**    | Server-side pagination/filtering, incremental rows, preserved cursor and selection        | Show coverage/window gap; never imply empty when query failed.                            |
| **Object detail**        | Prioritize identity, state, source, freshness and actions before secondary panels         | Panel-specific degraded states; primary status never derived from missing panel silently. |
| **Evidence / audit**     | Stream metadata first, content on demand, signed download for large artifacts             | Integrity/freshness visible; unavailable content does not erase metadata.                 |
| **Charts / reports**     | Progressive aggregates with definition and period; table alternative                      | Partial periods and missing sources visibly marked.                                       |
| **AI assistant**         | Streaming allowed only with clear generating state; citations validate before final state | Fallback to deterministic search/workflow; interrupted output remains unapproved.         |
| **Action workflows**     | Synchronous validation, durable command, resumable receipt polling                        | No duplicate execution; uncertain state enters reconciliation-required.                   |
| **Exports / packages**   | Asynchronous job, resumable progress, manifest and expiry                                 | Failed jobs retain scope and diagnostic; partial export not offered as complete.          |

# 18 \| Notifications, Interruptions, Communications and Acknowledgment

| **Class**                      | **Delivery and presentation rule**                                                           | **Acknowledgment / escalation**                                            |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Security critical**          | Persistent, severity-labeled, tenant-scoped and linked to case/incident                      | Explicit acknowledgment; escalation and clock visible.                     |
| **Evidence / assurance gap**   | Names affected controls, period and missing sources; cannot be dismissed as informational    | Owner assignment and remediation tracking.                                 |
| **Privileged change / access** | Shows actor, scope, reason, duration and result                                              | Review/confirm where policy requires; audit-linked.                        |
| **Service incident**           | Approved status wording, affected services/regions and update time                           | Customer acknowledgment where contractual; communication history retained. |
| **AI risk / fallback**         | Shows disabled/degraded AI capability, affected workflows and deterministic alternative      | AI Risk/Operations escalation; no silent provider fallback.                |
| **Commercial usage**           | Usage vs entitlement and forecast before overage; technical values only in engineering views | Customer/admin action path; no surprise billing claim.                     |
| **Routine workflow**           | Inbox/center first; email/webhook per preference and policy                                  | Quiet hours and digest permitted unless material clock applies.            |

# 19 \| Experience Telemetry, Auditability and Experimentation Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image11.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image165.png" />

***Figure 11 - Experience telemetry, privacy and audit flow.***

| **Signal class**          | **Permitted purpose**                                                                                           | **Controls**                                                                                               |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Product interaction**   | Task completion, friction, adoption and usability                                                               | Minimized fields, pseudonymous tenant/user context, retention and no sensitive content by default.         |
| **Operational telemetry** | Latency, errors, state transitions, queue and dependency health                                                 | Correlation IDs, tenant-safe labels, sampling rules and SLO ownership.                                     |
| **Security audit**        | Authentication, authorization, privileged action, configuration, evidence, export, AI tool and support activity | Append-only, attributable, reconciled and separate from analytics.                                         |
| **AI decision record**    | Use case, route, source bundle, output hash, tool calls, review and override                                    | Prompt/content access restricted; no broad raw prompt analytics.                                           |
| **User research**         | Approved design-partner tasks and findings                                                                      | Consent, de-identification, no production secrets/data and controlled retention.                           |
| **Experiment**            | Low-risk presentation or workflow optimization only                                                             | Pre-approved hypothesis, population, guardrails, opt-out, stop criteria and no critical-control weakening. |

# 29 \| Testing, Quality, Accessibility and Visual Regression

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image14.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image168.png" />

***Figure 15 - Experience acceptance and release evidence.***

| **Test family**           | **Minimum coverage**                                                                    | **Blocking failures**                                                                          |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Contract/state**        | Every applicable universal and domain state; transitions and recovery                   | Missing/incorrect partial, stale, unauthorized, simulation or reconciliation state.            |
| **Authorization/tenancy** | Role/purpose, cross-tenant negative, elevation expiry and support access                | Any cross-tenant path, silent denial, or privileged action without step-up/approval.           |
| **Evidence/assertion**    | Drill-down, source/version/freshness, package and immutable snapshot                    | Dead-end assertion, stale shown healthy, unverifiable export or editable audit record.         |
| **High-impact action**    | R0-R4, blast radius, dual approval, attestation, duplicate prevention and rollback      | Live action from simulation, missing authority, replay/duplicate or unknown execution state.   |
| **AI**                    | Grounding, citations, injection, tool scope, review, fallback, memory and kill switches | Cross-tenant leakage, unsafe tool call, unsupported claim, no fallback or unrecorded override. |
| **Accessibility**         | Automated, keyboard, screen reader, zoom/reflow, contrast, motion and export            | Critical workflow unavailable to supported assistive technology.                               |
| **Responsive/locale**     | Viewport, orientation, text expansion, RTL, time zone and poor network                  | Hidden trust/authority/evidence context or ambiguous time/number.                              |
| **Performance**           | Budget, query/payload, progressive rendering, long tasks and resource use               | Critical journey exceeds approved budget without degraded treatment/exception.                 |
| **Visual regression**     | Viewport/theme/locale/state/flag baselines; semantic diff review                        | Unapproved status, hierarchy, focus or destructive-action change.                              |
| **Telemetry/audit**       | Product events, operational signals, security audit and privacy minimization            | Missing material audit event or sensitive content in analytics.                                |

# 30 \| Versioning, Design-System Change and Deprecation Governance

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image15.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image169.png" />

***Figure 14 - Experience contract lifecycle and change control.***

| **Change class**               | **Examples**                                                                                       | **Minimum control**                                                                           |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **UX-C0 Editorial**            | Non-material typo with no legal/status effect                                                      | Content owner review; no contract version if semantics unchanged.                             |
| **UX-C1 Visual non-semantic**  | Spacing or decorative change within tokens                                                         | Design-system test and visual regression.                                                     |
| **UX-C2 Interaction**          | Navigation, workflow, keyboard, responsive or component behavior                                   | Contract minor version, requirements/test impact and product/engineering approval.            |
| **UX-C3 Control-semantic**     | Status color/label, evidence, permission, AI disclosure, confirmation or error behavior            | Security/compliance/AI/accessibility review; release evidence; migration plan.                |
| **UX-C4 Breaking / high risk** | Removed capability, changed authority, data exposure, irreversible action or jurisdiction behavior | ADR, major version, customer impact, staged rollout and executive approval as applicable.     |
| **Deprecation**                | Pattern/page/API no longer supported                                                               | Successor, usage inventory, notice, migration, telemetry, removal date and archived baseline. |

# 31 \| Controlled Design Repository and Remote-Team Safeguards

| **Control**                 | **Mandatory implementation**                                                                                              |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity and access**     | Individual SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, workstream groups, EC-3 named access, automatic contractor expiry.                |
| **Repository separation**   | Controlled design library, prototype workspace, restricted annexes and public/marketing assets remain logically separate. |
| **Sharing**                 | No anonymous/public links, personal accounts, external email attachments or uncontrolled exports.                         |
| **Production data**         | Synthetic/anonymized data only; no customer evidence, secrets, credentials or restricted incident content.                |
| **Version and approval**    | Immutable approved milestone, named reviewers, change history, source-document versions and supersession banner.          |
| **Component governance**    | Published library packages; local detachment or shadow components prohibited without exception.                           |
| **Comments and recordings** | No secrets/customer data in comments; meeting recordings/transcription require approved tool and purpose.                 |
| **Plugins and AI tools**    | Approved plugins/providers only; no uncontrolled design upload or training use; tool activity logged where possible.      |
| **Exports**                 | Logged, classified, watermarked where appropriate, time-bound and stored in controlled engineering library.               |
| **Offboarding**             | Session revoke, group removal, local copy cleanup, ownership transfer and access evidence.                                |
| **Segregation of duties**   | Designer/implementer cannot unilaterally approve a material control-semantic change and production release.               |
| **Incident reporting**      | Suspected leak, unauthorized share, customer data, plugin misuse or anomalous export reported immediately.                |

# 33 \| Metrics, Performance Budgets and Experience Objectives

| **Objective**                      | **Definition**                                                                             | **Initial internal target / rule**                                   |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Task success**                   | Qualified users complete critical workflow without assistance or policy bypass             | Measured per actor and state; target set in register before G1.      |
| **State coverage**                 | Implemented/tested applicable universal and domain states                                  | 100% for G1/G2 blocking contracts.                                   |
| **Evidence reachability**          | Material assertions with valid one-click evidence path                                     | 100%; any dead end blocks release.                                   |
| **Unauthorized clarity**           | Denied actions correctly identified as restricted rather than error                        | 100% sampled critical permissions.                                   |
| **Accessibility critical defects** | Open blockers in critical workflows                                                        | Zero at release.                                                     |
| **AI citation validity**           | Material AI claims supported by accessible approved sources                                | Threshold set per use case; critical unsupported claims block route. |
| **AI override evidence**           | Accepted/modified/rejected material proposals with decision record                         | 100% for governed workflows.                                         |
| **High-impact action safety**      | Actions showing authority, blast radius, approval, attestation and recovery before confirm | 100% R2-R4 and bulk actions.                                         |
| **Performance budget**             | Critical page/workflow within approved LCP/interaction/query/payload limits                | Per experience profile in SLO/scale register.                        |
| **Visual regression review**       | Material semantic diffs reviewed and approved                                              | 100% changed G1/G2 contracts.                                        |
| **Telemetry minimization**         | Analytics events containing prohibited sensitive fields                                    | Zero.                                                                |
| **Design-contract drift**          | Released pages not matching current approved experience contract                           | Zero unresolved material drift.                                      |

# 34 \| Threat Model and Abuse-Case Verification

| **Threat / abuse case**                 | **Required verification**                                                                                                                   |
|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cross-tenant object or cached state** | Switch tenant during deep workflow; back/forward; stale tab; shared URL; verify no prior tenant data/action persists.                       |
| **Authorization confusion**             | Expired elevation, changed role, deleted user, delegated partner and indeterminate policy; verify fail closed and correct restricted state. |
| **False assurance**                     | Missing connector/evidence/evaluator, stale source and incomplete framework; verify no healthy/compliant visual.                            |
| **Dangerous-action misdirection**       | Rapid click, keyboard shortcut, modal overlay, changed target, duplicate submit and delayed receipt; verify no unintended execution.        |
| **Prompt injection / hostile content**  | Logs, emails, filenames, evidence and comments contain instructions/markup; verify safe rendering and AI/tool isolation.                    |
| **AI overtrust**                        | Confident unsupported output, invalid citation, stale source and conflicting evidence; verify limitation, review and no privileged effect.  |
| **Sensitive-data leakage**              | Error, tooltip, URL, analytics, browser storage, export, support session and screen share; verify masking/minimization.                     |
| **Audit suppression**                   | Client network failure or blocked analytics; verify server-side material audit remains authoritative and reconciled.                        |
| **Accessibility bypass**                | Keyboard/screen reader cannot reach warning/approval or distinguish state; release blocked.                                                 |
| **Design-system supply chain**          | Compromised package/plugin or detached local component; verify signed package/admission and inventory.                                      |
| **Dark pattern**                        | Preselected consent/action, misleading hierarchy, ambiguous cancel, urgency or concealed limitation; control-owner review fails release.    |
| **Feature-flag divergence**             | Flag removes mandatory warning/state/audit; automated invariant tests block rollout.                                                        |

# 35 \| Definitions of Ready and Done

| **Definition of Ready - experience implementation**                                | **Definition of Done - released experience**                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Approved experience ID, owner, gate and version.                                   | Implemented behavior reconciles to the approved contract and design-system version. |
| Requirements, actor, journey and scope traceable.                                  | All applicable universal/domain states verified.                                    |
| Data authority, classification, freshness and region defined.                      | Authorization, tenancy, privacy and support-access negative tests pass.             |
| API/event/webhook and error contracts approved.                                    | Evidence, audit and assertion drill-downs verified.                                 |
| Permission, purpose, step-up and SoD defined.                                      | High-impact action and AI control tests pass.                                       |
| State matrix and recovery paths complete.                                          | Accessibility, responsive, locale and content reviews pass.                         |
| Evidence, audit, AI and action controls mapped.                                    | Performance, telemetry and visual regression meet budget.                           |
| Accessibility and responsive behavior specified.                                   | Documentation, support and runbook impacts complete.                                |
| Performance and telemetry contracts defined.                                       | Release evidence, approvals, exceptions and canary result recorded.                 |
| Prototype/contract reviewed by Product, Engineering and applicable control owners. | Production monitoring confirms expected states and no material drift.               |

# 00 \| Document Authority, Ownership and Required Artifacts

***Figure 1 - Operational authority, evidence and decision hierarchy.***

| **Authority layer**          | **Authoritative artifact**                                                         | **Owner**                       | **Engineering consequence**                                              |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Service intent**           | Approved service outcome, tier, boundary and customer obligation                   | Product / Service Owner         | Operations does not invent service commitments.                          |
| **Architecture / ownership** | Service catalog, dependency map, data authority and regional topology              | Chief Architect / Engineering   | Every signal and runbook maps to a controlled component and owner.       |
| **Measurement**              | Signal contracts, SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and capacity thresholds                | SRE / Service Owner             | Dashboards use reproducible measurements and bounded exclusions.         |
| **Response**                 | Alerts, on-call, incidents, runbooks, communications and recovery                  | Service Operations / CISO       | Material events follow named authority and evidence-preserving workflow. |
| **Readiness / release**      | ORR record, risk, exceptions, game days, canary and production validation          | Release / Operational Authority | Delivery teams cannot self-authorize material production operation.      |
| **Assurance / claims**       | Service history, restore tests, audit evidence, status records and approved claims | Compliance / Legal / Product    | Customer and public statements follow measured evidence.                 |

## 00.1 Mandatory controlled artifacts

| **Artifact**               | **Minimum controlled content**                                                                      | **System of record**         |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Service record**         | Owner, tier, criticality, dependencies, region, data class, SLOs, runbooks, on-call and lifecycle   | Service Catalog              |
| **Signal contract**        | Name, type, producer, semantics, tenant context, class, units, retention, cardinality and consumers | Telemetry Registry           |
| **SLI/SLO object**         | Eligibility, formula, window, objective, exclusions, source, owner, burn policy and claim status    | SLO Register                 |
| **Alert policy**           | Condition, severity, customer impact, routing, suppression, escalation, runbook and test evidence   | Alert Registry               |
| **Runbook**                | Trigger, scope, prerequisites, safe actions, rollback, escalation, evidence and last exercise       | Operations Repository        |
| **Incident record**        | Timeline, severity, scope, roles, actions, communications, recovery, reconciliation and CAPA        | Incident System              |
| **ORR record**             | Release, services, SLO/capacity/recovery evidence, risks, exceptions, decision and approvers        | Release Evidence Register    |
| **Customer status record** | Affected service/region/tenant class, approved text, timestamps, updates and resolution             | Status/Communications System |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                                | **Why it fails a Tier-1 review**                                                                                  | **Refinement incorporated**                                                                                |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Observability reduced to logs and dashboards**           | Collection does not prove ownership, actionability, correctness or customer outcome.                              | Controlled signal contracts, service ownership, SLIs, runbooks and decision evidence.                      |
| **One availability number for every workload**             | Point detections, windowed rules, connectors, evidence, APIs and asynchronous workflows have different semantics. | Class-specific SLIs/SLOs with explicit eligible populations and windows.                                   |
| **“100% audit completeness” stated as a metric**           | Unlogged events cannot be directly observed, creating false assurance.                                            | Active audit-event reconciliation with detection-latency objective and integrity incident on gaps.         |
| **Multi-tenant telemetry centralized without controls**    | Observability can leak customer content, secrets and cross-tenant identifiers.                                    | Regional routing, minimization, tokenization, tenant-safe indexes, JIT investigations and access evidence. |
| **Error budgets treated as SRE reporting only**            | They do not influence release pace, feature work or risk decisions.                                               | Binding change policy, release restrictions, recovery work and executive exceptions.                       |
| **Alert volume used as coverage proof**                    | High volume may indicate duplication, poor thresholds or unowned noise.                                           | Actionability, page precision, acknowledgment, customer impact, runbook and quality review measures.       |
| **AI logs capture raw prompts by default**                 | Prompts can contain customer data, secrets, attacker content and privileged context.                              | Metadata-first AI observability, bounded secure sampling, redaction and case-scoped access.                |
| **Recovery ends when infrastructure is online**            | Data, actions, evidence and customer-visible outcomes may remain inconsistent.                                    | Mandatory state and evidence reconciliation before HEALTHY is restored.                                    |
| **Operational readiness is a checklist owned by the team** | Self-attestation can conceal untested recovery, capacity or on-call gaps.                                         | Named independent ORR decision, evidence requirements, conditional states and expiry.                      |
| **Remote on-call has broad permanent production access**   | Increases insider, credential and accidental-change risk.                                                         | JIT, incident/change-scoped access, session recording, SoD and post-use review.                            |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Explicit Exclusions

This document defines the required content architecture for engineering and operations teams to design, implement, validate and govern ZoikoShield observability, SLOs, error budgets, production operations and readiness. It governs all production and production-like services, managed-security workflows, AI systems, regional data planes, evidence systems, customer-facing health surfaces and critical third-party dependencies.

| **In scope**                                                                                                            | **Explicitly excluded**                                                                                 |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Metrics, logs, traces, audit events, profiles, synthetic checks, health models and business/service signals.            | Selection or procurement of a specific monitoring, paging, ITSM or status-page vendor.                  |
| Service catalog, ownership, dependencies, SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, alerts, runbooks, on-call and incident management. | Public uptime or compliance claims not approved through the Claim Register.                             |
| Evidence, AI, detection, response, connector, data-pipeline, infrastructure and customer service observability.         | Unrestricted collection of raw customer content, secrets, prompts or forensic data.                     |
| Operational Readiness Reviews, production validation, recovery reconciliation, game days and recurring assurance.       | Creation of a separate operations authority outside the controlled architecture and release governance. |
| Internal, customer, executive, audit and incident-command views.                                                        | Use of dashboards as the sole source of truth where authoritative records exist elsewhere.              |

# 04 \| Binding Observability and Operations Invariants

| **ID**         | **Invariant**                                                                                                                                   |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **OPS-INV-01** | Every production service, module and critical dependency has one accountable owner and current operational contact.                             |
| **OPS-INV-02** | Every material signal carries service, environment, region, release and trace context; tenant context is mandatory where customer scope exists. |
| **OPS-INV-03** | No raw secret, credential, private key or unnecessary customer content is emitted to telemetry.                                                 |
| **OPS-INV-04** | SLOs declare exact eligible population, formula, source, window, objective, exclusions, owner and claim status.                                 |
| **OPS-INV-05** | UNKNOWN, PARTIAL, STALE, UNAUTHORIZED and RECONCILIATION REQUIRED never render as HEALTHY.                                                      |
| **OPS-INV-06** | An alert has a named owner, severity rationale, customer-impact model, action path, runbook and test record.                                    |
| **OPS-INV-07** | No single engineer may implement a material change, suppress its failures and authorize production operation.                                   |
| **OPS-INV-08** | AI and agent operations use metadata-first observability; direct model-provider access remains prohibited.                                      |
| **OPS-INV-09** | Recovery is incomplete until authoritative data, actions, evidence and customer-visible state reconcile.                                        |
| **OPS-INV-10** | Error-budget exhaustion changes release and work priorities under controlled policy.                                                            |
| **OPS-INV-11** | Customer status information is approved, scoped and traceable to incident facts; internal speculation is not published.                         |
| **OPS-INV-12** | Operational access is least-privilege, JIT, purpose-bound, logged and reviewed.                                                                 |
| **OPS-INV-13** | Telemetry pipelines have their own SLOs, backpressure, loss detection and cost controls.                                                        |
| **OPS-INV-14** | No service is production-ready without tested runbooks, on-call, capacity, backup/restore, security and customer communication.                 |
| **OPS-INV-15** | No operational or public claim exceeds measured capability and current evidence.                                                                |

# 06 \| Telemetry Taxonomy and Signal Authority

| **Signal class**         | **Purpose**                                                          | **Authoritative constraints**                                                      |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Metric**               | Quantitative time-series health, performance, capacity and cost.     | Stable units, bounded labels, explicit aggregation and source.                     |
| **Log**                  | Discrete diagnostic and audit-relevant records.                      | Structured, classified, redacted, immutable where required and correlation-linked. |
| **Trace**                | Distributed request, event and workflow causality.                   | Sampling declared; tenant/customer content excluded unless authorized.             |
| **Audit event**          | Material security, administrative, evidence, AI and response action. | Required-event registry, append-only controls and reconciliation.                  |
| **Domain event**         | Business/security state change.                                      | Canonical schema, ordering/replay semantics and source authority.                  |
| **Synthetic check**      | Controlled customer-journey or component probe.                      | Named synthetic tenant, safe data, release context and no customer side effects.   |
| **Profile / diagnostic** | Restricted performance or failure analysis.                          | Time-bounded, EC-3 where sensitive, privacy reviewed and deleted on schedule.      |
| **Customer signal**      | Tenant-scoped service status and coverage.                           | Permission checked, non-color state cues and no cross-tenant comparison.           |
| **Evidence artifact**    | Operational proof supporting control or assurance claim.             | Integrity, lineage, freshness, completeness and retention state.                   |

# 07 \| Instrumentation and Semantic Convention Standard

| **Required context**     | **Rule**                                                                                                |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**             | Service/module, workload identity, actor class and customer-visible operation where applicable.         |
| **Scope**                | Tenant, legal entity, environment, region, data plane and isolation class where applicable.             |
| **Release**              | Artifact digest, configuration/policy version, feature flag and deployment identifier.                  |
| **Causality**            | Trace, span, request, event, case, incident, change and evidence identifiers as applicable.             |
| **Purpose / data class** | Processing purpose and data classification sufficient to enforce routing, access and retention.         |
| **Time**                 | Observed, source, accepted and processed times distinguished; clock quality and skew visible.           |
| **Outcome**              | Success, failure, partial, denied, timed out, canceled, rolled back or unknown with stable reason code. |
| **Cost / resource**      | Compute, storage, query, model, network and human-service dimensions where applicable.                  |

# 08 \| Tenant, Privacy, Residency and Sensitive-Telemetry Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image19.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image143.png" />

***Figure 4 - Multi-tenant observability and privacy boundary.***

| **Control area**            | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                           |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Collection minimization** | Allowlist fields; block secrets; hash/tokenize identifiers where diagnostic value remains.                          |
| **Residency**               | Route telemetry before durable storage according to tenant region, data class, purpose and provider eligibility.    |
| **Isolation**               | Tenant-safe indexes, object prefixes, row/field policies, cache keys, queries and exports; negative tests required. |
| **Access**                  | Role/purpose/tenant/case-bound authorization; customer-content access JIT with session evidence.                    |
| **Sampling**                | Never sample required audit events. Trace/log sampling must preserve material errors and declare bias.              |
| **Retention**               | Separate operational, audit, forensic, AI and customer-visible retention schedules.                                 |
| **Export/deletion**         | Customer export and deletion must include operational records promised by contract while respecting legal hold.     |
| **Support tooling**         | Support views mask customer content by default and prevent unrestricted fleet searches.                             |

# 10 \| SLI Architecture and Measurement Contracts

| **SLI family**           | **Illustrative eligible measurement**                                                                          |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Availability**         | Successful eligible customer operations / eligible operations; excludes only predeclared non-service requests. |
| **Latency**              | Eligible operation completion time measured at the customer or service boundary; percentiles by class.         |
| **Durable acceptance**   | Authenticated valid records durably accepted / eligible records presented to the boundary.                     |
| **Detection latency**    | Durable acceptance to alert; labeled point, windowed or batch and interpreted with declared window.            |
| **Coverage**             | Expected protected scope with current healthy telemetry / expected protected scope.                            |
| **Evidence freshness**   | Required evidence within control-specific freshness threshold / required evidence.                             |
| **Audit reconciliation** | Material operation to reconciled required audit event; gaps are integrity incidents.                           |
| **Action success**       | Approved commands with verified receipt and observed-state match / eligible commands.                          |
| **AI quality**           | Use-case-specific grounded/acceptable outputs under controlled evaluation; never a universal “accuracy” score. |
| **Restore integrity**    | Recovery exercises meeting time target and authoritative-state reconciliation / scheduled exercises.           |

# 11 \| SLO Portfolio, Error Budgets and Change Policy

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image21.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image145.png" />

***Figure 6 - SLI, SLO and error-budget lifecycle.***

| **SLO control**      | **Required rule**                                                                                   |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Objective source** | Internal engineering objective until measured history and approved contract support an SLA.         |
| **Window**           | Rolling and calendar windows explicitly separated; short and long burn monitored.                   |
| **Exclusions**       | Minimal, predeclared, measurable and reviewed; provider failure is not automatically excluded.      |
| **Error budget**     | Computed from eligible events/time; owner and remaining budget visible.                             |
| **Policy linkage**   | Burn states alter deployment pace, feature flags, risky changes and reliability work.               |
| **Exhaustion**       | Material new feature release paused unless named authority accepts bounded risk.                    |
| **Recalibration**    | Based on customer need, measured capability, cost and architecture; never to hide poor performance. |
| **Contract/claim**   | Legal and Claim Register approval required before customer or public wording.                       |
| **Budget state**     | **Required change policy**                                                                          |
| **Healthy**          | Normal controlled release cadence.                                                                  |
| **Elevated burn**    | Increase review, reduce concurrent risk and prioritize diagnostics.                                 |
| **At risk**          | Reliability work scheduled; high-risk releases require explicit approval.                           |
| **Exhausted**        | Feature release freeze for affected service except mitigation, security or approved emergency.      |
| **Unmeasurable**     | Treat as NOT READY or DEGRADED; restore measurement before claiming service health.                 |

# 18 \| Alerting, Paging, Suppression and Noise Governance

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image25.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image149.png" />

***Figure 10 - Alert evaluation, routing and noise-control pipeline.***

| **Alert requirement** | **Control**                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Actionability**     | Page only when a responder can take time-sensitive action; otherwise ticket, dashboard or report.            |
| **Customer impact**   | Severity reflects potential/observed customer harm, tenant scope, evidence integrity and response authority. |
| **Freshness**         | Stale or missing source telemetry cannot silently resolve or suppress a material alert.                      |
| **Ownership**         | On-call route, fallback route and executive/security escalation are tested.                                  |
| **Runbook**           | Current runbook and safe first actions linked; missing runbook is a readiness defect.                        |
| **Suppression**       | Maintenance, deduplication and dependency suppression are bounded, visible and evidence-logged.              |
| **Testing**           | Alert fires in simulation; routing, acknowledgment, escalation and customer communication clocks verified.   |
| **Quality**           | Precision, repeat pages, non-actionable rate, false resolution and manual toil reviewed.                     |
| **Retirement**        | Unused or obsolete alerts removed through change control; silent orphan alerts prohibited.                   |
