| **Secondary / specialist**     | Provide domain expertise, privileged operation or security/AI/privacy support.                             |
| **Incident commander**         | Own severity, coordination, timeline, decisions, roles and restoration strategy.                           |
| **Operations liaison**         | Coordinate status page, customer support, executive updates and service commitments.                       |
| **Security / privacy / legal** | Own breach, forensic, notification and evidence-preservation decisions.                                    |
| **Scribe**                     | Maintain authoritative timeline, hypotheses, actions, approvals, communications and pending work.          |
| **Service owner**              | Validate customer outcome, approve risk and own corrective action after restoration.                       |
| **Executive authority**        | Resolve material trade-offs, risk acceptance and cross-business escalation.                                |
| **On-call control**            | **Requirement**                                                                                            |
| **Coverage**                   | Defined by service criticality and contractual operation; no unsupported 24/7 claim.                       |
| **Handover**                   | Structured acknowledgment of open incidents, risks, changes, customer commitments and impaired services.   |
| **Fatigue**                    | Rotation, page volume, rest, follow-the-sun and overflow monitored; chronic overload is an operating risk. |
| **Access**                     | JIT, incident/change linked, least privilege, recorded and reviewed.                                       |
| **Drills**                     | Routing and escalation tested on schedule, including unavailable primary responders.                       |
| **Contractor/partner**         | Named scope, supervision, data access, tooling, handoff and exit controls.                                 |

# 20 \| Runbooks, Automation and Operational Knowledge

| **Runbook field**           | **Mandatory content**                                                                          |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Trigger and scope**       | Alert/event, affected service, tenant/region boundaries and applicability.                     |
| **Safety prerequisites**    | Required access, approvals, backups, customer authority, response level and stop conditions.   |
| **Diagnosis**               | Known signals, health checks, dependencies, decision tree and evidence to preserve.            |
| **Actions**                 | Ordered commands or procedures, expected result, timeout, blast radius and prohibited actions. |
| **Rollback / compensation** | Reversal steps, irreversibility warning, validation and escalation.                            |
| **Communications**          | Internal, customer, security, legal and executive templates/clocks.                            |
| **Verification**            | How restoration and authoritative-state reconciliation are proven.                             |
| **Ownership**               | Owner, reviewers, version, last exercise, expiry and linked incidents/CAPA.                    |
| **Automation**              | Idempotency, permission, simulation, approvals, rate ceiling, evidence and kill switch.        |

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>RUNBOOK AUTHORITY</strong></p>
<p>A runbook is not permission. The operator and automation must still pass current authorization, tenant, policy, change and response-authority checks.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 21 \| Incident, Problem, CAPA and Service-Restoration Management

| **Lifecycle**                | **Required control**                                                                                      |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Detection / declaration**  | Stable severity criteria, customer impact, evidence integrity and authority for declaration.              |
| **Containment / mitigation** | Risk-bounded actions, approvals, customer policy and change evidence.                                     |
| **Restoration**              | Service, data, action, evidence and customer-journey validation.                                          |
| **Closure**                  | No material unknowns, pending customer commitments or unreconciled authoritative state hidden by closure. |
| **Post-incident review**     | Blameless fact analysis with accountable corrective action; not a substitute for performance management.  |
| **Root cause**               | Technical, process, organizational and control contributors separated.                                    |
| **CAPA**                     | Owner, priority, due date, test/evidence, effectiveness review and risk/exception link.                   |
| **Problem record**           | Recurring or systemic issue tracked beyond the individual incident.                                       |
| **Learning**                 | Runbooks, tests, alerts, capacity, SLO, architecture, training and claims updated.                        |

# 22 \| Customer Status, Transparency and Communications

| **Surface**                       | **Required content and control**                                                                        |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Public status**                 | Approved services/regions, current state, incident/update times and no sensitive security detail.       |
| **Authenticated customer status** | Tenant-specific impact, connector/evidence coverage, case/action status and contractual communications. |
| **Incident notification**         | Scope, observed impact, mitigation, required customer action, next update and known limitations.        |
| **Maintenance**                   | Affected service/region, expected impact, window, rollback and completion/reconciliation.               |
| **Service review**                | SLO history, incidents, coverage, obligations, capacity, risks and agreed actions with evidence links.  |
| **Security communication**        | Legal/Security-approved channel, restricted facts, secure delivery and acknowledgment.                  |
| **AI disclosure**                 | Affected AI capability, fallback, human oversight and customer rights where relevant.                   |
| **Resolution**                    | Restored outcome, remaining limitations, data/evidence reconciliation and post-incident follow-up.      |

# 23 \| Operational Readiness Review and Production Authorization

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image27.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image151.png" />

***Figure 12 - Operational Readiness Review and authorization flow.***

| **ORR domain**              | **Minimum evidence**                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Service ownership**       | Catalog current, owners/on-call assigned, dependency and escalation map validated.                    |
| **Customer journeys**       | Critical journeys instrumented, synthetic checks passing and degraded states visible.                 |
| **SLOs / alerts**           | Measurement validated, objectives approved, burn alerts and response routes tested.                   |
| **Capacity / cost**         | Reference envelope, headroom, quotas, scaling, cost allocation and limits proven.                     |
| **Security / privacy / AI** | Threat controls, audit events, data handling, AI gates and access reviewed.                           |
| **Recovery**                | Backup, restore, failover, rollback, evidence/data/action reconciliation exercised.                   |
| **Operations**              | Runbooks, on-call, incident command, status/customer communications and support handoff ready.        |
| **Risk / exceptions**       | Known gaps, compensating controls, owners, expiry and customer/claim impact visible.                  |
| **Release evidence**        | Exact artifacts/config, test results, canary plan, approvers and rollback recorded.                   |
| **Decision**                | **Meaning**                                                                                           |
| **READY**                   | All mandatory evidence current; no blocking risk; authorized for stated scope.                        |
| **READY WITH CONDITIONS**   | Bounded exception, compensating control, owner, expiry and monitoring; no silent expansion.           |
| **NOT READY**               | Blocking evidence, ownership, recovery, capacity, security or customer-impact gap.                    |
| **WITHDRAWN**               | Approval invalidated by material change, incident, expired exception or failed production validation. |

# 24 \| Release, Change, Maintenance and Production Validation

| **Control**               | **Requirement**                                                                                   |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Release context**       | Artifact/config/policy/schema/feature flag and environment digests visible in telemetry.          |
| **Progressive delivery**  | Synthetic tenant, canary cohort, dwell period, health criteria, rollback and promotion authority. |
| **Maintenance**           | Declared scope/window/impact, suppression policy, backup/rollback and customer communication.     |
| **Change risk**           | SLO/error budget, dependency, migration, AI, evidence and response-authority impact assessed.     |
| **Production validation** | Critical journeys, signals, audit events, SLOs and customer views validated after deployment.     |
| **Rollback/forward fix**  | Decision threshold, safe state, data compatibility and evidence of execution.                     |
| **Closure**               | No unresolved drift; release evidence updated; status/claims remain accurate.                     |
| **Emergency change**      | Incident/change reference, minimal scope, enhanced monitoring, retrospective approval and CAPA.   |

# 25 \| Capacity, Performance, Cost and Unit-Economics Operations

| **Dimension**     | **Operational requirement**                                                                                    |
|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Demand**        | Tenant, endpoint/identity, connector, event/GB, alert/case, evidence, search, model and concurrency forecasts. |
| **Capacity**      | Current allocation, safe operating limit, reserved headroom, autoscaling lag and hard quota.                   |
| **Performance**   | Latency/throughput by operation class and reference envelope, not fleet average only.                          |
| **Saturation**    | CPU, memory, IO, partitions, connections, queue, storage, search and provider quota.                           |
| **Cost**          | Tenant/service/region/connector/retention/model attribution with anomaly and forecast.                         |
| **Guardrails**    | Ingestion, retention, model and human-service cost constraints from the controlled register.                   |
| **Load shedding** | Priority classes, safe degradation, customer impact and prohibited dropping of required audit/evidence events. |
| **Planning**      | Capacity review before major customer, connector, region, framework or retention commitment.                   |

# 26 \| Backup, Restore, Disaster Recovery and Integrity Reconciliation

| **Recovery area**           | **Required observability and evidence**                                                            |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Backup**                  | Coverage, success, age, encryption, immutability, regional location and restore eligibility.       |
| **Restore**                 | Selected point, duration, data scope, dependency order, errors and recovered service state.        |
| **Event replay**            | Offsets/manifests, duplicate protection, late data, consumer progress and side-effect suppression. |
| **Evidence reconciliation** | Last witnessed root, chain continuity, object hashes, package verifier and divergence handling.    |
| **Action reconciliation**   | Issued commands, receipts, customer observed state and duplicate-action prevention.                |
| **Customer outcome**        | Critical journeys, connector coverage, cases, evidence and exports validated.                      |
| **Failover**                | Decision, DNS/routing, data consistency, residency, identity, provider and rollback state.         |
| **Exercise**                | Scenario, owner, result, target, deficiencies, CAPA and next test date.                            |

# 27 \| Synthetic Monitoring, Canary Tenants and Game Days

| **Control**          | **Requirement**                                                                                                        |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Synthetic tenant** | Zoiko-owned, isolated, clearly labeled, region/tier representative and free of real customer data.                     |
| **Journey**          | Covers identity, ingest, detection, case, response simulation, evidence, AI fallback and export as applicable.         |
| **Canary**           | Receives release first; thresholds, dwell, rollback and promotion evidence controlled.                                 |
| **Provider probe**   | Exercises approved external providers without unsafe side effects or unbounded cost.                                   |
| **Game day**         | Tests dependency loss, queue backlog, regional failure, identity outage, AI outage, connector drift and action freeze. |
| **Safety**           | No live destructive customer action; simulation and dedicated test targets required.                                   |
| **Evidence**         | Scenario, release/config, result, incident behavior, recovery/reconciliation and improvements.                         |
| **Expiry**           | Synthetic credentials/data rotated; stale probes removed; false confidence prevented.                                  |

# 28 \| Security Monitoring, Privileged Activity and Forensic Readiness

| **Security domain**                | **Required operational evidence**                                                                               |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication / authorization** | Success/failure, policy/reason, step-up, token/session, anomalous route and tenant scope.                       |
| **Privileged access**              | Request, approver, purpose, duration, session, actions, evidence accessed and post-use review.                  |
| **Tenant isolation**               | Denied cross-tenant attempts, policy-test canaries, query/export boundary violations and cache/index anomalies. |
| **Configuration / release**        | Policy, detection, playbook, prompt, model, connector, price/entitlement and infrastructure changes.            |
| **Supply chain**                   | Artifact provenance, admission, signature failure, revoked dependency and runtime drift.                        |
| **Data exfiltration**              | Unusual export/query/egress, customer-content access, mass action and download patterns.                        |
| **Forensics**                      | Time synchronization, immutable audit, protected snapshots, chain of custody and EC-3 access.                   |
| **Incident readiness**             | Detection route, containment controls, customer/legal clocks and evidence-preservation runbooks.                |

# 29 \| Telemetry Pipeline Reliability and Observability-of-Observability

| **Pipeline risk**         | **Required control**                                                                        |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Signal loss**           | Sequence/heartbeat, expected volume, gap detection, buffering and declared affected window. |
| **Collector failure**     | Health, config/version, resource pressure, export retries and safe local buffer.            |
| **Backpressure**          | Queue depth, lag, shed policy, priority and customer/coverage impact.                       |
| **Schema drift**          | Registry validation, quarantine, owner notification and source-version change.              |
| **Sampling bias**         | Sampling policy/version visible; errors, security and required audit events preserved.      |
| **Cardinality explosion** | Budgets, top contributors, rejection, exemplars and owner escalation.                       |
| **Query failure**         | Dashboard freshness, partial result, timeout and source status visible.                     |
| **Time skew**             | Clock health, source/observed time divergence and ordering impact.                          |
| **Cost runaway**          | Ingest/storage/query budget, forecast, anomaly and controlled degradation.                  |
| **False healthy**         | Independent synthetic/reconciliation checks challenge the telemetry source itself.          |

# 30 \| Retention, Access, Export and Deletion of Operational Telemetry

| **Record class**             | **Control requirements**                                                                                   |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Service metrics**          | Aggregated, low-content, retention by operational and capacity need.                                       |
| **Application logs**         | Minimized/redacted; retention by diagnostic, security and contractual purpose.                             |
| **Distributed traces**       | Sampled and time-limited; customer content prohibited by default.                                          |
| **Security/audit events**    | Protected, access-controlled and retained to policy; required events not sampled.                          |
| **Incident/forensic data**   | Case-scoped, EC-3, legal-hold aware and chain-of-custody protected.                                        |
| **AI operational records**   | Metadata-first; sensitive prompt/output capture exceptional and restricted.                                |
| **Customer-visible history** | Available per service/contract; tenant-scoped export and deletion behavior defined.                        |
| **Deletion**                 | Store inventory, backups, indexes and derived data covered; evidence/hold conflict routed to legal review. |

# 31 \| Explicit Service-Health and Readiness States

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image28.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image152.png" />

***Figure 13 - Operational health and readiness state model.***

| **State**                   | **Required meaning**                                                                    |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **HEALTHY**                 | Current evidence supports normal operation within objective and no hidden material gap. |
| **AT RISK**                 | Leading indicators or budget burn threaten objective; service remains available.        |
| **DEGRADED**                | Material capability impaired with declared scope and customer impact.                   |
| **PARTIAL / INCOMPLETE**    | Some data, coverage, evidence or dependency is missing; no healthy/compliant rendering. |
| **STALE**                   | Last known state exceeds freshness threshold.                                           |
| **UNKNOWN**                 | Measurement or authority is insufficient; investigate rather than assume healthy.       |
| **UNAVAILABLE**             | Eligible operation cannot be delivered.                                                 |
| **UNAUTHORIZED**            | Required permission absent or denied; distinct from system failure.                     |
| **QUARANTINED**             | Input, component or release isolated pending validation.                                |
| **MAINTENANCE**             | Approved bounded change window with visible impact.                                     |
| **RECOVERING**              | Service returning, but validation/reconciliation incomplete.                            |
| **RECONCILIATION REQUIRED** | Authoritative state, actions or evidence not yet aligned.                               |
| **ERROR BUDGET EXHAUSTED**  | Reliability policy restricts change.                                                    |
| **READINESS CONDITIONAL**   | Approved only with bounded conditions and expiry.                                       |
| **NOT READY**               | Mandatory evidence or control missing.                                                  |
| **WITHDRAWN**               | Prior health/readiness authorization invalidated.                                       |

# 34 \| Metrics, Thresholds and Operational Objectives

| **Metric**                         | **Definition**                                                               | **Control objective**                   |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| **service_owner_coverage**         | Production services with current accountable and on-call owners              | 100%                                    |
| **slo_contract_validity**          | Active SLOs with reproducible source, formula, window and owner              | 100%                                    |
| **critical_journey_observed**      | Required journeys with synthetic/customer-boundary measurement               | 100% before G1/G2 as applicable         |
| **alert_runbook_coverage**         | Paging alerts with current tested runbook                                    | 100%                                    |
| **non_actionable_page_rate**       | Pages requiring no time-sensitive responder action                           | Downward; threshold approved by service |
| **audit_reconciliation_latency**   | Material operation to required audit-event reconciliation                    | Objective in SLO register; gaps page    |
| **connector_visibility_latency**   | Detected connector failure to customer/operations visibility                 | p95 objective in register               |
| **evidence_freshness_rate**        | Required evidence within threshold                                           | By control; stale never healthy         |
| **ledger_verification_pass**       | Synthetic package verified by independent verifier                           | 100% per release                        |
| **action_reconciliation_pass**     | Approved actions with receipt and observed-state match                       | 100% for material actions               |
| **ai_critical_failure**            | Cross-tenant leak, unauthorized tool/action or fabricated material assertion | 0                                       |
| **error_budget_policy_compliance** | Affected changes following current burn policy                               | 100%                                    |
| **restore_reconciliation_pass**    | Exercises meeting target and authoritative reconciliation                    | 100%                                    |
| **orr_evidence_complete**          | Production authorizations with all mandatory evidence                        | 100%                                    |
| **operational_exception_overdue**  | Exceptions past expiry                                                       | 0                                       |
| **telemetry_cost_guardrail**       | Telemetry ingest/store/query cost within approved envelope                   | Within register limit                   |

# 35 \| Verification, Recurring Assurance and Audit Readiness

| **Control test**                     | **Cadence / trigger**                  | **Pass condition**                                                        |
|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Service ownership reconciliation** | Weekly and release                     | No active production service without current owner/on-call/runbook links. |
| **Signal contract lint**             | Each merge/release                     | Required context, class, units, cardinality, privacy and retention valid. |
| **SLO replay**                       | Each material SLO change and quarterly | Independent recomputation matches reported objective/budget.              |
| **Alert route drill**                | Monthly and on-call change             | Page reaches current responder, escalates and records acknowledgment.     |
| **Runbook exercise**                 | By criticality and change              | Procedure is current, safe, executable and evidence-producing.            |
| **Synthetic journey canary**         | Continuous / release                   | Critical path works in target region/release without unsafe side effects. |
| **Audit reconciliation canary**      | Continuous / release                   | Required audit events reconcile within objective.                         |
| **Ledger verifier job**              | Each release and scheduled             | Package verifies against witnessed root.                                  |
| **Action-broker safety check**       | Each relevant release                  | Ceiling, signing, attestation, receipt, reconciliation and freeze pass.   |
| **AI operations assurance**          | Each AI change and scheduled           | Route, grounding, tool, cost, fallback and kill switches valid.           |
| **Restore/failover exercise**        | Quarterly / material change            | Targets met and authoritative state reconciled.                           |
| **ORR recertification**              | Material change / expiry               | Readiness evidence remains current and approval valid.                    |
| **Access/SoD review**                | Quarterly and role change              | No expired/incompatible production, incident or telemetry privileges.     |
| **Customer-status drill**            | Semiannual / template change           | Approval, publication, update and resolution paths function.              |

# 36 \| Remote-Team Controls and Segregation of Duties

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image30.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image154.png" />

***Figure 15 - Remote operations and production-control separation.***

| **Control**            | **Mandatory rule**                                                                                                |
|------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity/device**    | Individual identity, phishing-resistant MFA and approved managed device for production operations.                |
| **Access**             | JIT, least-privilege, incident/change scoped, geographically controlled where required and automatically expired. |
| **Separation**         | Author, reviewer, release authority, production controller and evidence approver separated for material changes.  |
| **Sessions**           | Privileged sessions logged/recorded as permitted; commands and accessed resources attributable.                   |
| **Secrets**            | Vault only; no secrets in documents, tickets, chat, logs or local files.                                          |
| **Handover**           | Structured shift/service handover with acknowledgment and unresolved risk.                                        |
| **Partner/contractor** | Sponsor, scope, expiry, supervision, customer-data restrictions and immediate offboarding.                        |
| **Emergency**          | Break-glass dual-controlled where practicable, alerted, time-boxed and reviewed.                                  |
| **Communication**      | Approved secure channels; incident facts, customer data and restricted evidence not posted in general chat.       |
| **Wellbeing**          | Page volume, consecutive hours, rest and escalation monitored; fatigue is a safety risk.                          |

# 37 \| Definitions of Ready and Done for Operations

| **Level**                | **Ready requires**                                                                               | **Done requires**                                                                                           |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Service design**       | Owner, tier, architecture, dependencies, data class, SLI candidates and operating model.         | Service record, instrumentation plan, SLOs, alerts, runbooks, capacity/recovery and risks controlled.       |
| **Implementation**       | Requirements/contracts, telemetry semantics, test plan and environment available.                | Signals emitted, privacy/isolation tested, dashboards/alerts/runbooks linked and evidence current.          |
| **Release candidate**    | Exact artifact/config, quality gates, capacity, backup/restore, customer impact and canary plan. | ORR approved, deployment complete, production validation and dwell pass, evidence retained.                 |
| **Service operation**    | On-call staffed, access current, status/support paths ready and dependencies monitored.          | SLO/error budget reviewed, incidents closed/reconciled, obligations delivered and operational debt managed. |
| **Incident restoration** | Scope, command, evidence, communications and recovery plan established.                          | Customer outcome restored, authoritative state reconciled, communications resolved and CAPA owned.          |
| **Retirement**           | Replacement/export/retention/contract/dependency plan approved.                                  | Traffic/data/alerts/runbooks/access removed, customers handled and historical evidence retained.            |

# 38 \| Workstream Handoff and G0-G4 Approval Gates

| **Gate**                                    | **Minimum operational evidence**                                                                                                                               |
|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **G0 Build Authorization**                  | Service ownership model, signal standards, SLI/SLO architecture, incident/readiness processes, privacy/security controls and test strategy approved.           |
| **G1 Design-Partner Readiness**             | Critical journeys, connector/evidence health, tenant-safe views, on-call, runbooks, restore and customer communications demonstrated for design-partner scope. |
| **G2 Commercial GA**                        | Measured SLOs, error-budget policy, 24/7 operating coverage as sold, incident/DR exercises, status/support, capacity/cost and ORR evidence complete.           |
| **G3 Enterprise/Sector Scale**              | Dedicated/sector/second-region/provider operating evidence, enterprise support, contractual objectives and isolation/recovery tests.                           |
| **G4 Sovereign/OT/Critical Infrastructure** | Topology-specific observability, offline/sovereign operations, safety, customer command, independent assurance and no inherited readiness by assumption.       |
| **Workstream handoff**                      | **Required content**                                                                                                                                           |
| **Service/domain**                          | Catalog record, owner, dependencies, tier, SLOs, risks and customer impact.                                                                                    |
| **Instrumentation**                         | Signal contracts, semantic fields, privacy/residency, sampling and cost.                                                                                       |
| **Operations**                              | Dashboards, alerts, runbooks, on-call, escalation, status and maintenance.                                                                                     |
| **Recovery**                                | Backup, restore, failover, reconciliation, game-day and rollback evidence.                                                                                     |
| **AI/security/evidence**                    | Specialized signals, kill/freeze controls, audit reconciliation and restricted handling.                                                                       |

|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Outcome / scope**            | Approved release outcome, user journeys, service obligations and exclusions          | Product / Engineering            | Testing does not invent or expand scope.                     |
| **Requirement / architecture** | Requirements, acceptance criteria, ADRs, invariants, threats and quality attributes  | Product / Chief Architect / CISO | Every material quality claim traces to controlled authority. |

## 00.1 Mandatory controlled artifacts

| **Artifact**                 | **Minimum controlled content**                                                                               | **Source of truth**             |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Release quality profile**  | Release class, affected risks, test obligations, independence, thresholds, exceptions and decision authority | Requirement / Release Register  |
| **Test strategy and plan**   | Scope, levels, scenarios, oracles, data, environments, entry/exit criteria and ownership                     | Quality Repository              |
| **Test case / evaluation**   | Requirement/risk link, preconditions, steps/model, expected result, evidence and automation status           | Test Management / Code          |
| **Environment manifest**     | Topology, versions, configuration, data class, policy, fidelity and health                                   | Environment Registry            |
| **Data/fixture manifest**    | Synthetic source, classification, generation, reset, retention, integrity and prohibited use                 | Data Register / Test Data Store |
| **Execution result**         | Artifact digest, config, test version, environment, executor, start/end, result, evidence and integrity      | CI/Test Evidence Store          |
| **Defect and CAPA record**   | Impact, severity, root cause, containment, correction, regression and effectiveness review                   | Defect / Risk Register          |
| **Release-quality evidence** | Gate results, residual risk, exceptions, named approval, canary/runtime and claim impact                     | Release Evidence Register       |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                           | **Why it fails a Tier-1 review**                                                                             | **Refinement incorporated**                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Test count or code coverage used as quality proof** | Volume metrics do not show whether material risks, failure states or customer outcomes were verified.        | Risk-based release profiles, requirement/risk traceability, mutation/escape analysis and explicit residual risk.                 |
| **Generic “test pyramid” applied to every subsystem** | Distributed, event-driven, AI and evidence systems require different oracles, timing and integration depth.  | Layered test architecture selected by system behavior and consequence, not a fixed ratio.                                        |
| **A pass/fail result without result provenance**      | The tested artifact, configuration, data or environment may not match the release being approved.            | Signed execution metadata binding result to artifact digest, config, environment, test version and evidence.                     |
| **LLM-as-judge treated as objective validation**      | Model judges can be correlated, biased, prompt-sensitive and non-deterministic.                              | Deterministic, statistical, human and adversarial evaluation are separate; LLM judge never sole authority for material controls. |
| **Flaky tests retried until green**                   | Retries can convert uncertainty into false assurance and hide concurrency, isolation or environment defects. | Explicit flaky/quarantine state, owner, expiry, release impact and root-cause obligation.                                        |
| **Production-like used as an unmeasured claim**       | Configuration drift and synthetic workload mismatch invalidate performance and resilience claims.            | Versioned fidelity statement, reference scale envelope, environment health and release-digest binding.                           |
| **Happy-path focus on response automation**           | High-impact actions can fail through replay, scope expansion, stale approval or partial execution.           | Negative, abuse, blast-radius, rollback and customer-side attestation tests are release-blocking.                                |
| **Definition of Done ends at merge**                  | Service readiness, runbooks, recovery, SLOs, customer impact and runtime validation remain unproven.         | Layered DoD for component, feature, service, release and production outcome.                                                     |
| **QA as a late independent department**               | Late testing creates handoffs without preventing design defects and cannot own quality alone.                | Quality engineering begins at requirement/oracle design; developers own tests, QA owns strategy and independent evidence.        |
| **Remote team trusted through broad tool access**     | A single person may author tests, suppress failures and promote a release.                                   | Role separation, protected evidence, independent review and named release authority.                                             |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Explicit Exclusions

| **In scope**                                                                                                                                     | **Out of scope / separate authority**                                                                               |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Test strategy, risk coverage, automation, environments, data, result evidence, defects, release gates and Definitions of Ready/Done.             | Product prioritization, pricing, employment performance management and legal certification decisions.               |
| Functional, security, tenancy, privacy, evidence, AI, accessibility, performance, resilience, migration, connector and operational verification. | Penetration-test exploitation details or red-team reports beyond approved engineering disclosure.                   |
| G0-G2 quality controls and design patterns required for later G3/G4 deployment classes.                                                          | Automatic authorization of sovereign, OT, safety-critical or customer-managed topologies without separate evidence. |
| Employees, contractors, partners, automation, test agents and approved AI-assisted quality tooling.                                              | Use of real customer data or production actions unless explicitly authorized by a controlled test plan.             |

# 04 \| Binding Quality-Engineering Invariants

| **ID**    | **Invariant**                                 | **Binding consequence**                                                                                               |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **QA-01** | Outcome traceability                          | Every material test traces to an approved requirement, invariant, risk, obligation or incident.                       |
| **QA-02** | Risk-proportionate evidence                   | Verification depth reflects impact, irreversibility, uncertainty and blast radius.                                    |
| **QA-03** | Independent oracle                            | Expected behavior is defined independently of the code under test.                                                    |
| **QA-04** | Exact release binding                         | Results bind to artifact digest, configuration, schema, policy, data and environment.                                 |
| **QA-05** | No silent waiver                              | Failures, skips, retries, quarantines and exceptions remain visible and attributable.                                 |
| **QA-06** | Fail closed on indeterminate material control | Unavailable or ambiguous security, isolation, evidence or signing checks block release.                               |
| **QA-07** | Negative paths are mandatory                  | Unauthorized, invalid, partial, stale, replayed and degraded behavior is tested.                                      |
| **QA-08** | Tenant isolation is a release blocker         | Cross-tenant negative tests cover every relevant storage, interface, cache, queue, search, observability and AI path. |
| **QA-09** | Evidence properties are separate              | Integrity, completeness, freshness, coverage, effectiveness and certification are never conflated.                    |
| **QA-10** | Deterministic replay where promised           | Recorded inputs, versions, enrichment and timing semantics reproduce the original decision or expose divergence.      |
| **QA-11** | No LLM critical oracle                        | AI evaluation may assist but cannot be sole authority for material security, compliance or response outcomes.         |
| **QA-12** | Customer data is not test data                | Synthetic or approved anonymized data is default; production data use requires explicit authority and controls.       |
| **QA-13** | Same artifact through release                 | The tested and approved digest is the digest promoted to production.                                                  |
| **QA-14** | Migrations reconcile                          | Schema, data and backfill changes prove compatibility, rollback/forward-fix and reconciliation.                       |
| **QA-15** | Safe failure and recovery                     | Graceful degradation, backup, failover, restore and alternate-history detection are verified.                         |
| **QA-16** | Performance and cost are quality              | Latency, throughput, headroom and unit-cost guardrails are release evidence.                                          |
| **QA-17** | Accessibility is release quality              | Keyboard, screen-reader, focus, contrast and non-color status behavior are tested.                                    |
| **QA-18** | Flaky is a defect state                       | A flaky result cannot satisfy a material gate and must have owner, expiry and remediation.                            |
| **QA-19** | Defect closure requires regression protection | Correction, root cause, affected-scope review and updated tests are mandatory.                                        |
| **QA-20** | Independence for high-risk change             | Authors cannot be sole approvers of tests/results for material controls.                                              |
| **QA-21** | Production validation completes the release   | Canary/runtime reconciliation and claim review are part of Done.                                                      |
| **QA-22** | Named human release authority                 | Tools, bots and AI systems may recommend but cannot independently authorize material production release.              |

# 06 \| Risk-Based Test Planning and Release Quality Profiles

***Figure 3 - Risk-based verification depth and release authority.***

| **Release quality profile field** | **Required content**                                                                                     |

| **Release identity**              | Release ID, digest set, target environments, configuration/policy/content versions and effective window. |

# 07 \| Requirement, Risk, Test and Release Traceability

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image34.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image128.png" />

***Figure 4 - Bidirectional requirement-to-release traceability.***

| **Trace condition**      | **Release requirement**                                                                                           |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Requirement coverage** | Every material requirement has approved acceptance criteria and at least one current verification method.         |
| **Risk coverage**        | Every material risk/threat has prevention or detection evidence and an owner for residual risk.                   |
| **Test authority**       | Every test identifies the requirement/risk/oracle it proves; orphan tests are maintained or retired deliberately. |
| **Defect impact**        | Defects link to affected requirements, releases, tenants, controls, claims and regression tests.                  |
| **Exception trace**      | Every waived result links to a time-bound exception, compensating evidence, owner and expiry.                     |
| **Release closure**      | All included changes, tests, defects, exceptions and runtime evidence reconcile to one release manifest.          |

# 08 \| Test Architecture, Levels and Test Selection

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image35.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image129.png" />

***Figure 5 - Test architecture and assurance layers.***

| **Test level**                   | **Best suited to**                                                                             | **Must not be used as sole evidence for**                                          |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Static / policy**              | Syntax, type, schema, architecture, security pattern, secret, license and configuration rules. | Runtime authorization, concurrency, integration, resilience or user outcomes.      |
| **Unit / component**             | Pure logic, state machines, transformations, evaluators and deterministic policy decisions.    | Distributed timing, provider behavior or storage isolation.                        |
| **Contract / compatibility**     | API/event/schema/webhook/SDK/provider interface behavior and evolution.                        | Complete business workflow or runtime failure interaction.                         |
| **Integration**                  | Real service/storage/broker/policy/model/evidence interactions within bounded scope.           | Full customer journey, regional failure or scale behavior.                         |
| **System / E2E**                 | Vertical slices, stateful workflows, customer/auditor outcomes and release configuration.      | Every edge case or component fault; use targeted lower-level tests too.            |
| **Non-functional / adversarial** | Security, isolation, AI, accessibility, scale, resilience, restore and cost.                   | Routine functional correctness without corresponding functional evidence.          |
| **Production validation**        | Canary, synthetic tenant, SLO, drift and reconciliation.                                       | Pre-production verification or authorization to experiment in customer production. |

# 09 \| Test Oracles and Evidence Semantics

| **Oracle type**              | **Application**                                                        | **Control requirements**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Specification oracle**     | Expected output/state from controlled requirement or state machine.    | Versioned and independent from implementation.                                           |
| **Reference implementation** | Known-good deterministic implementation or independent verifier.       | Separate ownership and divergence analysis.                                              |
| **Invariant/property**       | Condition that always holds across generated inputs or sequences.      | Counterexample preservation and reproducibility.                                         |
| **Metamorphic relation**     | Expected relationship when input or context changes.                   | Relation defined before execution; useful where exact answer is difficult.               |
| **Statistical threshold**    | Distributional quality, latency, drift or model metric.                | Sample design, confidence interval, seed/cohort and threshold version retained.          |
| **Human expert rubric**      | Complex investigation, narrative, usability or policy interpretation.  | Named reviewers, calibrated rubric, disagreement handling and bias controls.             |
| **Model-assisted judge**     | Supplemental evaluation of language or behavior.                       | Prompt/model/version retained; never sole material authority; calibrated against humans. |
| **Runtime reconciliation**   | Observed production state compared with release/evidence expectations. | Source authority, sampling and alert threshold controlled.                               |

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>ORACLE RULE</strong></p>
<p>A test without a controlled expected outcome is an experiment, not release evidence. Where the expected result is probabilistic, the evaluation design, confidence and acceptable error must be explicit.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 10 \| Environment, Configuration and Test-Data Governance

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image36.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image130.png" />

***Figure 6 - Quality environment and synthetic-tenant architecture.***

| **Control area**         | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                                            |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Environment manifest** | Versioned topology, services, policies, feature flags, schemas, provider routes, regions and fidelity statement.                     |
| **Health gate**          | Environment instability, stale fixtures or policy drift invalidates material results; no “best effort” pass.                         |
| **Data classification**  | Synthetic by default; anonymized/derived data approved by Privacy; customer production data prohibited unless explicitly authorized. |
| **Isolation**            | Unique tenant/test namespace, least-privilege credentials, reset and destructive-test boundaries.                                    |
| **Time control**         | Clock, timezone, timestamp, expiration, watermark and scheduled-job behavior controllable and recorded.                              |
| **Randomness**           | Seeds and generators retained for reproducibility; fuzz/property counterexamples preserved.                                          |
| **External providers**   | Simulators plus controlled live-provider validation; rate, cost, region and failure modes explicit.                                  |
| **Reset / cleanup**      | Idempotent setup, verified teardown, legal-hold awareness and no contamination across tests.                                         |

# 11 \| Unit, Component and State-Machine Verification

| **Target**                  | **Minimum verification**                                                                            |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Domain logic**            | Boundaries, invariants, valid/invalid transitions, duplicate commands and correction semantics.     |
| **Authorization policy**    | Permit/deny/indeterminate decisions, context omissions, stale attributes and explicit reason codes. |
| **Parsers / normalization** | Valid, malformed, ambiguous, oversized and adversarial payloads; provenance and quarantine.         |
| **Evaluators / controls**   | Exact input/version, completeness/freshness states, deterministic output and no implicit green.     |
| **Risk calculations**       | Component contributions, unknown/incomplete handling, policy version and monotonic properties.      |
| **Schedulers / clocks**     | Expiry, retry, daylight saving, time zones, late data and backoff semantics.                        |
| **Error handling**          | Stable codes, no sensitive leakage, retryability and safe default.                                  |
| **Idempotency**             | Repeated command/event/webhook produces one controlled effect and complete evidence.                |

# 12 \| API, Event, Schema, Webhook and Compatibility Testing

| **Contract family**          | **Required tests**                                                                                                                |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **API**                      | Authentication, authorization, tenant scope, idempotency, concurrency, pagination, quota, bulk partial failure and stable errors. |
| **Event**                    | Schema, producer authority, ordering, partitioning, duplicate, late, missing, replay, poison message and retention.               |
| **Webhook inbound**          | Signature, timestamp, nonce, replay, rotation, malformed payload, rate limit and source compromise.                               |
| **Webhook outbound**         | Signing, retry, dedupe, receipt, dead letter, secret rotation, endpoint failure and customer visibility.                          |
| **Schema evolution**         | Backward/forward compatibility, unknown fields, defaulting, migration, rollback and historical replay.                            |
| **SDK**                      | Generated contract parity, auth, retries, type safety, pagination and supported-version matrix.                                   |
| **Consumer-driven contract** | Every critical consumer publishes expectations; provider change blocks on incompatible impact.                                    |
| **Offboarding/export**       | Open formats, completeness manifest, evidence proofs, large-volume resume and deletion-attestation linkage.                       |

# 13 \| Integration, Workflow and Vertical-Slice Testing

| **Vertical slice**      | **Minimum end-to-end evidence**                                                                     |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant onboarding**   | Legal entity, region, residency, retention, identity, roles and first evidence record.              |
| **Connector to alert**  | Credential scope, ingest, normalization, coverage health, detection, alert and replay.              |
| **Alert to case**       | Triage, AI assist, citations, case state, notes, communications and audit timeline.                 |
| **Case to response**    | Authority, approval, signing, customer attestation, execution receipt, reconciliation and rollback. |
| **Control assurance**   | Collector, evidence, evaluator, completeness/freshness, control status and remediation.             |
| **Audit package**       | Scope, gap precheck, freeze, Merkle proof, independent verifier and auditor access.                 |
| **Usage / entitlement** | Meter event, entitlement check, overage forecast, service obligation and reconciliation.            |
| **Exit / offboarding**  | Export, integrity manifest, legal hold, deletion workflow and attestation.                          |

# 14 \| Identity, Authorization, Tenancy and Residency Verification

| **Verification domain**      | **Release-blocking negative tests**                                                                                         |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication / session** | Expired, revoked, replayed, wrong audience/issuer, weak step-up and device/session risk.                                    |
| **Authorization**            | Missing tenant/purpose, cross-workspace, stale role, delegated scope escape, relationship manipulation and deny-by-default. |
| **Segregation of duties**    | Self-approval, incompatible roles, inherited group privilege and break-glass abuse.                                         |
| **Storage isolation**        | Database, object, search, cache, queue, lakehouse, metrics, logs, backups and export.                                       |
| **AI isolation**             | Retrieval, embedding, memory, prompt, tool, model output and evaluation datasets.                                           |
| **Support / partner access** | JIT expiry, customer approval, masking, session evidence and non-transitive delegation.                                     |
| **Residency**                | Pre-persistence routing, provider eligibility, support location, transfer mechanism, failover and backup region.            |
| **Deletion / key scope**     | Tenant-scoped erasure, residual indexes/caches/backups and evidence/legal-hold conflict.                                    |

# 15 \| Evidence Ledger, Control Evaluation and Independent Verifier Testing

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image37.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image131.png" />

***Figure 7 - Evidence-ledger and verifier test chain.***

| **Property**                 | **Required verification**                                                                                              |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Integrity**                | Content hash, collector signature, chain continuity, timestamp and Merkle inclusion detect mutation/reorder/insertion. |
| **Completeness**             | Expected-evidence model identifies missing, partial, stale, permission-changed and evaluator-failed states.            |
| **Lineage**                  | Source -\> fact -\> test -\> assessment -\> assertion is traversable and versioned.                                    |
| **Reproducibility**          | Frozen inputs, evaluator, mappings and enrichment replay the original conclusion.                                      |
| **Independent verification** | Offline CLI/library validates package without Zoiko credentials or runtime trust.                                      |
| **Witnessing**               | Root publication, witness receipt, split-view/delay handling and customer-held proof validation.                       |
| **Restore integrity**        | Recovered state reconciles to external anchor and event replay; divergence becomes integrity incident.                 |
| **Retention / deletion**     | WORM, legal hold, tombstone, key destruction and deletion attestation behave as policy requires.                       |

# 16 \| Detection, Correlation and Deterministic Replay Testing

| **Area**                    | **Required tests**                                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Point rules**             | Exact version, input eligibility, threshold, suppression and latency.                                                   |
| **Windowed correlation**    | Window, ordering, watermark, late/missing data, duplicate and boundary timestamps.                                      |
| **Sequence rules**          | Out-of-order events, partial sequences, reset, timeout and entity resolution.                                           |
| **Enrichment**              | Recorded asset/identity/intel/policy versions; mutable current context never silently substituted.                      |
| **Replay**                  | Bit-for-bit decision reproduction or explicit NON_DETERMINISTIC divergence record.                                      |
| **Noise / precision**       | Representative benign/adversarial datasets, analyst feedback and customer-specific tuning without cross-tenant leakage. |
| **Content lifecycle**       | Propose, test, peer review, sign, staged publish, monitor, tune and retire.                                             |
| **AI-generated candidates** | Sandboxed, adversarially reviewed and deterministically re-expressed before blocking production use.                    |

# 17 \| Case, SOAR, Action-Broker and Response-Safety Testing

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image38.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image132.png" />

***Figure 8 - Governed response safety verification.***

| **Control**                 | **Required verification**                                                                                   |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Case state machine**      | Valid/invalid transitions, duplicate/false-positive/accepted-risk/legal-hold paths and audit timeline.      |
| **Playbook typing**         | Inputs, outputs, version, preconditions, approval gates, timeouts, retries, compensation and simulation.    |
| **Authority R0-R4**         | Policy resolves correct authority; missing/ambiguous context fails closed.                                  |
| **Approvals**               | Named authority, step-up, dual control, freshness, revocation and customer approval.                        |
| **Command signing**         | Per-tenant key, nonce, expiry, policy version, action scope and signature failure.                          |
| **Customer attestation**    | Unsigned, expired, replayed, wrong-tenant and modified command rejected at execution point.                 |
| **Blast radius / ceilings** | Mass-action rate, target expansion, global freeze and per-tenant kill switch.                               |
| **Receipt / rollback**      | Partial execution, lost receipt, observed-state mismatch, compensation and irreversible failure escalation. |

# 18 \| AI, Retrieval, Agentic and Model-Risk Assurance

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image39.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image133.png" />

***Figure 9 - AI evaluation dimensions and decision rights.***

| **Test family**                | **Minimum controlled evidence**                                                                                                            |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Gateway / provider routing** | Approved model/provider/region/data class, timeout, fallback, retention and no direct SDK bypass.                                          |
| **Prompt / configuration**     | Version, precedence, prohibited override, prompt leakage and rollback.                                                                     |
| **Retrieval / grounding**      | Source authority, tenant scope, freshness, citation precision/recall and poisoning resistance.                                             |
| **Memory**                     | Type, purpose, tenant/user scope, retention, deletion and cross-session contamination.                                                     |
| **Agent planning**             | Goal bounds, max steps/time/cost, checkpoints, stop conditions and no hidden side effects.                                                 |
| **Tools**                      | Allowlist, typed schema, target-side authorization, least privilege, replay, output validation and side-effect class.                      |
| **Quality / safety**           | Gold sets, factuality, omission, false reassurance, harmful recommendation, calibration and human override.                                |
| **Adversarial**                | Direct/indirect prompt injection, telemetry poisoning, jailbreak, extraction, cross-tenant leakage, excessive agency and denial-of-wallet. |
| **Drift / provider change**    | Model/version/prompt/retrieval change triggers regression and disclosure review.                                                           |
| **Kill / fallback**            | Feature/model/provider/retrieval/agent/tool kill switches and deterministic workflow continuation.                                         |
