# 19 \| Application, Platform and Software-Supply-Chain Security Testing

| **Control family**             | **Verification**                                                                                                 |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Threat model / abuse cases** | Every material boundary and privileged path has mapped negative tests.                                           |
| **SAST / code review**         | High-confidence findings, sensitive paths, generated code and suppression governance.                            |
| **Dependency / SBOM**          | Known components, reachability, malicious/typosquat checks, license and exception age.                           |
| **DAST / API abuse**           | Auth, injection, deserialization, SSRF, file handling, rate limits, business logic and data leakage.             |
| **IaC / cloud policy**         | Network, IAM, encryption, logging, public exposure, drift and destructive change.                                |
| **Container / runtime**        | Image provenance, non-root, capabilities, seccomp, filesystem, egress and admission.                             |
| **Supply-chain integrity**     | Protected source, isolated builder, provenance, signing, substitution and admission negative tests.              |
| **Independent testing**        | Penetration test and red team before applicable G1/G2 gates; critical/high findings closed or formally accepted. |

# 20 \| Privacy, Retention, Legal Hold, Deletion and Export Testing

| **Area**                   | **Required scenarios**                                                                                   |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Purpose / minimization** | Disallowed field/purpose blocked; source-side filtering and redaction verified.                          |
| **Residency / transfer**   | Every supported region-data-purpose route has explicit expected result; unmatched route quarantines.     |
| **Retention**              | Hot/warm/archive/evidence/audit schedules, extension, expiry and legal-hold precedence.                  |
| **DSR / access**           | Search, export, correction and deletion across authoritative stores with identity and deadline controls. |
| **Deletion**               | Primary, replica, cache, search, object, queue and backup expiry; key-scoped erasure where applicable.   |
| **Legal hold**             | Deletion conflict fails into legal-review queue; no silent retention or deletion.                        |
| **Offboarding export**     | Completeness, open formats, resume, manifest, proofs and customer verification.                          |
| **Deletion attestation**   | Signed store inventory, key destruction, backup window and exceptions accurately represented.            |

# 21 \| Experience-State, Accessibility and Human-Factors Testing

| **Experience control**      | **Required verification**                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Seven state classes**     | Loading, empty, nominal, partial, stale, error and unauthorized are distinct where applicable.             |
| **Evidence drill-down**     | Every material assertion reaches source evidence, evaluator version and freshness without dead end.        |
| **No false green**          | Partial/stale/collector-unhealthy/evaluator-failed never render compliant or healthy.                      |
| **Authority before action** | R0-R4, approvers, blast radius, attestation and rollback visible before confirmation.                      |
| **AI transparency**         | AI region, citations, confidence, human-review state, override and deterministic fallback.                 |
| **Accessibility**           | WCAG 2.2 AA target: keyboard, focus, semantics, screen reader, contrast, zoom/reflow and non-color status. |
| **Human error prevention**  | Destructive confirmation, tenant restatement, undo/rollback where possible and clear recovery.             |
| **Usability / workload**    | Analyst, auditor, admin and executive tasks tested for time, error, comprehension and alert fatigue.       |

# 22 \| Performance, Scale, Endurance, Capacity and Cost Verification

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image40.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image134.png" />

***Figure 10 - Performance, resilience and cost verification cycle.***

| **Test class**            | **Minimum design**                                                                              |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Baseline / regression** | Pinned release, dataset and hardware; compare statistically meaningful changes.                 |
| **Load / concurrency**    | Expected fleet, tenant skew, search/investigation concurrency and provider limits.              |
| **Burst / spike**         | Ingestion surge, incident storm, webhook retry, case fan-out and notification burst.            |
| **Endurance / soak**      | Memory/resource leaks, compaction, index growth, queue lag, model spend and long-running jobs.  |
| **Scalability**           | Stepwise scale with headroom, bottleneck attribution and auto-scaling behavior.                 |
| **SLO latency**           | Point vs windowed detection, API, evidence collection, action and export by declared class.     |
| **Cost / unit economics** | Compute, storage, search, model, egress and analyst-driving signals against release guardrails. |
| **Noisy neighbor**        | Per-tenant quotas, fairness, isolation and bounded degradation under skew.                      |

# 23 \| Resilience, Chaos, Failover, Backup, Restore and Reconciliation

| **Failure scenario**           | **Pass condition**                                                                        |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Service/pod/node/zone loss** | Recovery within target; no cross-tenant effect, duplicate action or silent evidence loss. |
| **Queue/backbone outage**      | Backpressure/quarantine, durable replay and controlled catch-up.                          |
| **Search unavailable**         | Ingestion/evidence persist; user sees degraded state; no data loss.                       |
| **AI provider unavailable**    | Deterministic workflow continues; no unapproved provider or data route.                   |
| **ZoikoID outage**             | Existing read paths bounded; privileged/action paths fail closed.                         |
| **KMS/signing unavailable**    | No unsigned fallback; actions/releases/anchors wait or fail safely.                       |
| **Region loss**                | Declared topology behavior, controlled failover, residency and customer communication.    |
| **Backup restore**             | RTO/RPO met; transactional, event and external-anchor reconciliation complete.            |
| **Alternate history**          | Divergence from anchored root detected and declared as integrity incident.                |
| **SOC/service disruption**     | Queue ownership, overflow, handover and customer commitments remain controlled.           |

# 24 \| Data Migration, Backfill, Upgrade and Rollback Testing

| **Stage**                  | **Required evidence**                                                                                  |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Design**                 | Forward/backward compatibility, expand-contract sequence, authority and rollback/forward-fix decision. |
| **Preflight**              | Data shape, null/constraint, volume, tenant/region and expected duration.                              |
| **Rehearsal**              | Production-representative synthetic copy, checkpoints, failure injection and cost.                     |
| **Dual-read/write**        | Consistency, ordering, idempotency and divergence monitoring where used.                               |
| **Backfill**               | Bounded batch, resume, throttling, per-tenant isolation, reconciliation and evidence.                  |
| **Cutover**                | Version gates, maintenance/customer impact, feature flag and stop criteria.                            |
| **Rollback / forward fix** | What is reversible, what is compensating and how partial state is reconciled.                          |
| **Historical assurance**   | Old audit packages, replay and evidence remain verifiable after schema evolution.                      |

# 25 \| Connector, Provider and Partner Certification Testing

| **Certification level**             | **Required evidence**                                                                        |
|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **C0 - Schema intake**              | Authentication, schema, rate, provenance, errors and health states.                          |
| **C1 - Read-only production**       | Least privilege, data minimization, retry/backfill, coverage gaps and support matrix.        |
| **C2 - Detection eligible**         | Normalization quality, event-time semantics, mapping provenance and detection datasets.      |
| **C3 - Response eligible**          | Action scope, signing/attestation, simulation, rollback, receipts and vendor edge cases.     |
| **C4 - Regulated / high assurance** | Residency, retention, audit, incident notice, version/deprecation and independent assurance. |
| **Provider change**                 | API/schema/terms/model/version/rate change triggers impact and recertification.              |
| **Partner delivery**                | Delegated access, tenant isolation, operational quality, handover and exit tested.           |
| **Retirement**                      | Customer impact, export, historical replay, replacement and deprecation evidence.            |

# 26 \| Observability, Testability and Production Validation

| **Testability capability** | **Requirement**                                                                                                     |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Correlation**            | Every request/event/action/evidence/test carries traceable tenant, actor, purpose, release and correlation context. |
| **Deterministic controls** | Clock, randomness, retries, provider responses and fault injection controllable in approved environments.           |
| **Health and coverage**    | Connectors, evidence collectors, evaluators, AI routes and dependencies expose machine-readable state.              |
| **Audit events**           | Material test actions and production validations are reconciled to expected audit events.                           |
| **Synthetic probes**       | Critical user/security/assurance journeys run continuously in non-customer synthetic tenants.                       |
| **Canary validation**      | Release-specific assertions, SLOs, errors, drift, security and cost evaluated during dwell.                         |
| **Escape detection**       | Production incidents, customer reports and SLO breaches link back to missed test coverage.                          |
| **Evidence retention**     | Logs, traces and test artifacts are redacted, integrity-protected and retained by risk/classification.              |

# 27 \| Test Automation, Framework and Result-Provenance Architecture

| **Control**                     | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                              |
|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tests as code**               | Versioned, reviewed, owned and released with compatibility to the system under test.                   |
| **Framework governance**        | Approved libraries/runners, dependency policy, security maintenance and migration path.                |
| **Isolation**                   | Parallel tests cannot share uncontrolled tenant, data, secrets or mutable global state.                |
| **Result provenance**           | Test ID/version, source revision, artifact digest, config, environment, data/seed, executor and time.  |
| **Result integrity**            | Protected storage, immutable history for release evidence and no manual editing of original result.    |
| **Retry policy**                | Retries visible; first failure retained; material flaky result does not become pass by retry.          |
| **Parallelism**                 | Ordering, resource contention, rate limits and deterministic sharding controlled.                      |
| **AI-assisted test generation** | Human-owned, reviewed, no sensitive input to unapproved providers and subject to normal quality gates. |

# 28 \| Synthetic Tenants, Test Data and Customer-Data Restrictions

| **Data class**                  | **Permitted use**                                       | **Controls**                                                                                              |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Synthetic generated**         | Default for all development and automated testing.      | Versioned generator, realism assertions, no accidental real identifiers.                                  |
| **Curated adversarial corpus**  | Security/AI/parser/detection testing.                   | Restricted repository, provenance, license, minimization and review.                                      |
| **Anonymized/derived**          | Only when synthetic data cannot represent the behavior. | Privacy approval, re-identification assessment, restricted access and expiry.                             |
| **Production telemetry sample** | Exceptional debugging or incident reproduction.         | Explicit incident/data-owner approval, purpose, minimization, isolated environment and deletion evidence. |
| **Customer evidence/content**   | Prohibited in general engineering environments.         | Only approved customer-support/incident path with JIT access and complete audit.                          |
| **Secrets / credentials**       | Never embedded in fixtures or documents.                | Vaulted test identities, rotation, least privilege and automated expiry.                                  |

# 29 \| Defect Severity, Triage, Root Cause and CAPA

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image41.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image135.png" />

***Figure 11 - Defect, escape and corrective-action workflow.***

| **Severity**    | **Definition**                                                                                                                      | **Required action**                                                                                                   |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **S0 Critical** | Cross-tenant, evidence forgery, unauthorized high-impact action, key compromise, unrecoverable loss or active severe customer harm. | Immediate stop/freeze, incident command, executive/security authority, customer/regulatory process and release block. |
| **S1 High**     | Material security/privacy/availability/assurance failure with plausible customer impact or no safe workaround.                      | Contain, owner, expedited correction, independent retest and release block unless Board-level acceptance.             |
| **S2 Medium**   | Material functional/operational defect with bounded impact and safe workaround.                                                     | Planned correction, risk assessment, regression and release decision by authorized owner.                             |
| **S3 Low**      | Minor functional, usability or documentation defect without material control impact.                                                | Backlog with owner and priority; no hidden accumulation.                                                              |
| **Observation** | Potential improvement, ambiguity or non-blocking trend.                                                                             | Track and review; cannot be used to relabel a failure.                                                                |

# 30 \| Flaky Tests, Quarantine and Quality-Debt Governance

| **Rule**           | **Controlled behavior**                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Detection**      | Any non-deterministic pass/fail across identical declared conditions is flagged automatically.       |
| **Classification** | Product defect, test defect, environment defect, data defect or unknown.                             |
| **Quarantine**     | Visible, scoped, owner, issue, expiry and release impact; no silent skip.                            |
| **Material gate**  | Flaky/quarantined test cannot satisfy security, isolation, evidence, response, AI or migration gate. |
| **Budget**         | Maximum allowed quarantined count/age by suite; breach blocks or requires approved exception.        |
| **Remediation**    | Root cause, deterministic reproduction, fix and evidence of stability across defined runs.           |
| **Metrics**        | First-failure rate, retry rate, quarantine age, owner and affected release trend.                    |
| **Retirement**     | Obsolete tests removed only after authority/coverage analysis and approval.                          |

# 31 \| Coverage, Mutation, Escape and Effectiveness Measures

| **Measure**                   | **Correct use**                                                                      | **Prohibited interpretation**                                            |
|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Requirement/risk coverage** | Find orphan requirements and material risks without verification.                    | A row marked covered does not prove test quality.                        |
| **Code coverage**             | Identify unexecuted code and support local test design.                              | No universal threshold proves correctness or security.                   |
| **Branch/state coverage**     | Validate decisions and state transitions in critical logic.                          | Does not replace integration or adversarial testing.                     |
| **Mutation score**            | Assess whether tests detect plausible code faults in bounded components.             | Not applied blindly to generated/trivial code or used alone for release. |
| **Defect escape rate**        | Measure missed defects by severity and source.                                       | Never optimize by suppressing incident/customer reports.                 |
| **Test effectiveness**        | Defects detected before release, false confidence, time-to-detection and recurrence. | No volume-only metric.                                                   |
| **Risk burn-down**            | Material risks closed, mitigated, accepted or still exposed.                         | Cannot hide overdue acceptance or stale evidence.                        |
| **Suite economics**           | Runtime, infrastructure/model cost and maintenance effort.                           | Cost reduction cannot remove required risk evidence.                     |

# 32 \| Quality Gates, Release Decisions and Exception Control

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image42.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image136.png" />

***Figure 12 - Quality gate and decision authority by release class.***

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image43.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image137.png" />

***Figure 13 - Quality evidence and release state model.***

| **Gate**                   | **Release-blocking condition**                                                                      |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Requirements**           | Missing/ambiguous acceptance criterion, unresolved scope conflict or orphan material requirement.   |
| **Functional**             | Failed core journey/state transition or uncontrolled partial failure.                               |
| **Security/tenancy**       | Known cross-tenant path, authorization bypass, secret exposure or critical/high unaccepted finding. |
| **Evidence/assurance**     | Failed verifier, broken chain/anchor, non-reproducible conclusion or false compliant state.         |
| **AI**                     | Critical grounding, cross-tenant, tool-abuse, prompt-injection or kill/fallback failure.            |
| **Response safety**        | Unauthorized action, attestation/signing/replay/ceiling/rollback failure.                           |
| **Data/migration**         | Unreconciled loss/corruption, unsafe migration or unbounded backfill.                               |
| **Reliability/operations** | Unmet recovery, missing runbook/alert/ownership, or reference-envelope failure.                     |
| **Accessibility**          | Blocking keyboard/screen-reader/focus/status issue in required G1/G2 journey.                       |
| **Evidence state**         | Indeterminate, stale, invalid environment/data or expired exception used as pass.                   |

# 33 \| Definition of Ready

| **Ready dimension**  | **Mandatory condition before implementation/test execution**                              |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authority**        | Approved requirement/work item with owner, release and source master/register.            |
| **Outcome**          | User/system outcome and explicit non-goals are understood.                                |
| **Acceptance**       | Behavioral, negative, degraded, security, evidence and operational criteria are testable. |
| **Risk**             | Threat, privacy, tenancy, AI, response, migration and service impact classified.          |
| **Architecture**     | Affected boundaries, interfaces, data authority and ADR decisions are current.            |
| **Dependencies**     | Upstream/downstream contracts, providers, data, environments and owners identified.       |
| **Test design**      | Oracle, levels, fixtures, environment, automation and independence defined.               |
| **Observability**    | Required logs, metrics, traces, audit events and correlation fields specified.            |
| **Rollout/recovery** | Migration, feature flag, rollback/forward-fix and canary intent known.                    |
| **Security/access**  | Approvals, restricted data, test accounts and JIT access planned.                         |

# 34 \| Definitions of Done by Delivery Level

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image44.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image138.png" />

***Figure 14 - Definition-of-Ready and Definition-of-Done hierarchy.***

| **Delivery level**           | **Done means**                                                                                                                         |
|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Code / component**         | Requirement linked; implementation reviewed; unit/component and static controls pass; no secrets; documentation and ownership current. |
| **Contract / interface**     | Schemas/API/events versioned; compatibility and negative tests pass; consumer impact resolved; observability present.                  |
| **Feature / vertical slice** | End-to-end acceptance, degraded states, accessibility, security/privacy/AI/evidence controls and audit events verified.                |
| **Service / deployable**     | SLOs, capacity, resilience, backup/restore, alerts, runbooks, on-call, cost, dependencies and operational ownership proven.            |
| **Connector / provider**     | Certification level met; permissions, health, scale, failure, versioning, support and exit complete.                                   |
| **AI capability**            | Use case approved; evaluations/adversarial tests pass; human oversight, disclosure, kill/fallback, monitoring and cost controls live.  |
| **Release**                  | All changes and results reconcile; defects/exceptions owned; migration/rollout/rollback ready; named approval recorded.                |
| **Production outcome**       | Canary/dwell passes; runtime matches manifest; no material drift; customer communication and claims remain accurate; evidence closed.  |

# 35 \| Exploratory, Usability and Independent Human Validation

| **Activity**                    | **Controlled use**                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Exploratory testing**         | Charter tied to risk; time-boxed; notes, evidence and defects retained; not a substitute for regression.               |
| **Scenario-based review**       | Realistic analyst/auditor/admin/executive workflows, interruptions and incomplete data.                                |
| **Usability test**              | Task success, time, error, comprehension, trust calibration and recovery.                                              |
| **Accessibility expert review** | Assistive-technology and cognitive/visual/motor review beyond automation.                                              |
| **Security review**             | Abuse, attacker mindset, business logic and privilege interactions.                                                    |
| **AI human evaluation**         | Calibrated rubric, multiple reviewers for material uses, disagreement and escalation.                                  |
| **Design-partner validation**   | Approved scope, customer consent, no uncontrolled production risk, observations separated from contractual acceptance. |
| **Independent assurance**       | External tester/auditor findings enter the same defect/risk/CAPA system.                                               |

# 36 \| Remote-Team Quality Controls and Segregation of Duties

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image45.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image139.png" />

***Figure 15 - Remote-team quality-control separation.***

| **Control**                    | **Requirement**                                                                                                     |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Individual identity**        | No shared repository, test-management, CI, cloud, customer or evidence accounts.                                    |
| **Managed environment**        | Approved device, MFA, endpoint posture and restricted local customer data.                                          |
| **Least privilege**            | Workstream/environment/time-bound access; EC-3 corpora and production fault controls restricted.                    |
| **Author/reviewer separation** | Material code and tests require independent review; author cannot suppress own failure.                             |
| **Result custody**             | Original results stored in protected system; manual summaries link to originals.                                    |
| **Release custody**            | No individual can author, approve, alter evidence and promote material release alone.                               |
| **Contractor controls**        | Named sponsor, scope, automatic expiry, IP/confidentiality and immediate offboarding.                               |
| **AI tool controls**           | Approved provider/use; no confidential data to public tools; generated tests remain human-owned.                    |
| **Stop-work**                  | Conflicting authority, invalid environment/data, suspected tampering or material untestability triggers escalation. |

# 39 \| Verification, Recurring Assurance and Audit Readiness

| **Control test**                    | **Cadence / trigger**                           | **Pass condition**                                                             |
|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Requirement orphan scan**         | Each merge/release                              | No material requirement without current acceptance/test link.                  |
| **Result provenance verification**  | Each material execution/release                 | Result binds to exact artifact/config/environment/data and protected evidence. |
| **Tenant isolation suite**          | Each relevant change and full scheduled run     | All applicable negative tests pass; no cross-tenant observation.               |
| **Ledger verifier job**             | Each release                                    | Synthetic audit package verifies offline against external witness proof.       |
| **AI adversarial suite**            | Each AI-surface change and scheduled red team   | No critical injection, leakage, unauthorized tool use or unsafe fallback.      |
| **Action-broker safety suite**      | Each broker/policy/integration change           | Signing, attestation, replay, ceiling, receipt and rollback pass.              |
| **Accessibility regression**        | Each UI release                                 | Required journeys meet automated/manual gate; no blocking defect.              |
| **Scale/cost benchmark**            | Each performance-affecting change and milestone | Reference envelope and unit-cost guardrails met with headroom.                 |
| **Restore/reconciliation exercise** | Quarterly and material storage change           | Restore meets target and reconciles to event/anchor authority.                 |
| **Flaky-debt review**               | Weekly                                          | No expired quarantine or material gate satisfied by flaky evidence.            |
| **Defect escape review**            | Monthly/incident                                | Escapes mapped to coverage gap, CAPA and suite update.                         |
| **Access/SoD recertification**      | Quarterly and role change                       | No incompatible or expired quality/evidence/release privileges.                |

# 40 \| Metrics, Thresholds and Quality Objectives

| **Metric**                            | **Definition**                                                                           | **Control objective**                      |
|---------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| **material_requirement_traceability** | Material requirements with current acceptance, test and release links                    | 100%                                       |
| **release_result_provenance**         | Material release tests with complete signed context                                      | 100%                                       |
| **critical_gate_indeterminate**       | Material gates treated as pass while indeterminate                                       | 0                                          |
| **tenant_isolation_pass**             | Applicable negative tests passed                                                         | 100%; any failure blocks                   |
| **ledger_verification_pass**          | Release synthetic audit package verified offline                                         | 100%                                       |
| **high_impact_action_safety_pass**    | Applicable signing/attestation/replay/rollback tests passed                              | 100%                                       |
| **critical_ai_failure**               | Cross-tenant, unauthorized tool/action, fabricated material assertion or unsafe fallback | 0                                          |
| **flaky_material_gate_use**           | Material release gate satisfied by flaky/quarantined test                                | 0                                          |
| **escaped_S0_S1**                     | Critical/high defects first detected after release                                       | 0 target; every occurrence incident + CAPA |
| **restore_reconciliation_pass**       | Scheduled restore meets target and reconciles authoritative state                        | 100%                                       |
| **accessibility_blockers**            | Blocking defects in required journey at release                                          | 0                                          |
| **reference_envelope_headroom**       | Measured capacity above committed phase envelope                                         | Threshold by service; no unsupported claim |
| **unit_economics_headroom**           | Measured cost vs release guardrail                                                       | Within approved guardrail                  |
| **exception_overdue**                 | Quality exceptions past expiry                                                           | 0                                          |

# Document Control and Navigation

| **Control**              | **Value**                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Normative language**   | MUST = mandatory; SHOULD = expected unless an approved exception exists; MAY = optional.                                                                                                                                                |
| **Delivery authority**   | Controlled requirements, approved ADRs, protected source, machine-readable policies, signed artifacts, immutable manifests and verified release evidence. Issue trackers and CI tools are execution systems, not independent authority. |
| **Build-once rule**      | A release candidate is built once, tested, signed and promoted by digest. Rebuilding for production invalidates prior evidence.                                                                                                         |
| **Human accountability** | No AI tool, bot or pipeline agent may independently approve, merge, sign or deploy a material production change.                                                                                                                        |
| **No secret disclosure** | This document never contains credentials, signing keys, production tokens, private endpoints or recovery codes.                                                                                                                         |
| **Approval dependency**  | Engineering Document 14 must not proceed until this document is approved or explicitly returned for amendment.                                                                                                                          |

# 00 \| Document Authority, Ownership and Required Artifacts

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image46.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image111.png" />

***Figure 1 - Software-delivery authority and evidence hierarchy.***

| **Authority layer**         | **Authoritative artifact**                                                                | **Owner**                        | **Engineering consequence**                              |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Product / requirements**  | Release scope, requirement IDs, acceptance criteria, customer impact and exclusions       | Product / Engineering            | Unapproved work does not enter the release path.         |
| **Architecture / security** | ADRs, trust boundaries, data/AI/evidence rules and release blockers                       | Chief Architect / CISO           | Code cannot override architecture or control invariants. |
| **Source / build**          | Protected source, ownership, build definitions, policies, dependency locks and test plans | Engineering / Developer Platform | Every artifact has attributable, reviewed inputs.        |
| **Artifact / release**      | SBOM, provenance, signatures, release manifest, approvals and deployment targets          | Release Engineering              | Only immutable, verified digests may be promoted.        |
| **Runtime / operations**    | Deployment records, inventory, health, rollback, incidents and reconciliation             | SRE / Security Operations        | Running state must match the approved release identity.  |
| **Assurance / claims**      | Release evidence, exceptions, customer communication and claim approval                   | Risk / Compliance / Product      | Claims follow measured capability and retained evidence. |

## 00.1 Mandatory controlled artifacts

| **Artifact**                      | **Minimum controlled content**                                                                                | **Source of truth**               |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Repository catalog**            | Repository class, owner, code owners, sensitivity, build path, deployment scope, retention and archive state  | Service/Module Catalog            |
| **Change record**                 | Requirement, risk class, affected domains, reviewers, tests, migration, rollout, rollback and customer impact | Change / Requirement Register     |
| **Build policy**                  | Approved runner, image/toolchain, network, identity, inputs, outputs, tests, evidence and retention           | Policy Repository                 |
| **Dependency lock and inventory** | Exact versions/digests, source, license, owner, use, vulnerability status and exception                       | Dependency / Vendor Register      |
| **SBOM and provenance**           | Component graph, build identity, source revision, inputs, process, outputs and attestations                   | Artifact Store / Release Evidence |
| **Release manifest**              | Artifact digests, configuration, schemas, policies, detection/AI content, target, approvals and rollback      | Release Evidence Register         |
| **Deployment record**             | Controller, target, time, result, cohort, versions, health, rollback and reconciliation                       | Deployment Platform               |
| **Emergency change record**       | Incident authority, minimal scope, approvals, tests, expiry, customer decision and branch reconciliation      | Incident / Change Register        |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                            | **Why it fails a Tier-1 review**                                                                                | **Refinement incorporated**                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **CI pipeline treated as a sequence of tools**         | Tool success can be mistaken for release authority; traceability and policy become vendor-specific.             | Define an authority model and machine-readable contracts independent of CI/CD vendor.                                          |
| **Branch protection without source-integrity design**  | Compromised identities, stale approvals, bot tokens or hidden generated changes can still enter trusted source. | Repository classes, CODEOWNERS, approval freshness, merge queue, signed events and protected automation identities.            |
| **Build scans without trustworthy builders**           | A compromised runner can fabricate results, replace dependencies or steal signing credentials.                  | Ephemeral isolated runners, pinned toolchains, bounded egress, short-lived identity and independent signing.                   |
| **SBOM produced as a compliance attachment**           | An unverified SBOM that is not bound to the artifact provides little trust.                                     | SBOM, provenance and policy results are generated during build and cryptographically bound to the exact digest.                |
| **Artifact rebuilt for each environment**              | Production may differ from what passed tests, invalidating assurance.                                           | Build once and promote by immutable digest with one bound release manifest.                                                    |
| **AI coding assistant outside SDLC controls**          | Sensitive input leakage, license contamination and insecure generated code can bypass normal ownership.         | Approved gateway/use cases, input minimization, human accountability, AI-use evidence and normal gates.                        |
| **Emergency path as pipeline bypass**                  | Urgency can create unaudited privilege and unreconciled production drift.                                       | Compressed but controlled emergency workflow with independent review, signed manifest, rollback and post-event reconciliation. |
| **Dependency automation optimized only for freshness** | Automated upgrades may introduce malicious, incompatible or license-prohibited code.                            | Risk-based dependency intake, internal mirrors, policy, sandboxing, owner/expiry and staged update evidence.                   |
| **Deployment approval separated from customer impact** | Technically healthy release may breach contract, residency, evidence, AI disclosure or service obligation.      | Release manifest includes customer/tenant scope, obligations, communication and claim impact.                                  |
| **Remote-team control based on trust statements**      | Shared access or broad production privileges defeat accountability.                                             | Individual identities, managed devices, least privilege, authorship/review/release separation and JIT production custody.      |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Explicit Exclusions

| **In scope**                                                                                                                                                    | **Out of scope / separate authority**                                                                                               |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Repositories, review, build, test, dependency intake, SBOM, provenance, signing, artifact stores, promotion, deployment, change, rollback and release evidence. | Product prioritization, pricing, customer contracting, provider procurement and production credential issuance.                     |
| Application, infrastructure, schema, event, policy, detection, playbook, prompt, agent and documentation delivery controls.                                     | Detailed domain behavior, data semantics, model-risk decisions and infrastructure topology already governed by companion documents. |
| G0-G2 software-delivery controls and design patterns for later enterprise/sovereign delivery.                                                                   | Automatic authorization for private, air-gapped, OT or customer-managed build/deployment systems.                                   |
| Technical and organizational controls for employees, contractors, automation, bots and approved AI assistants.                                                  | HR disciplinary procedure, legal investigations and Board risk acceptance beyond engineering implementation.                        |

# 04 \| Binding CI/CD, Change and Supply-Chain Invariants

| **ID**      | **Invariant**                      | **Binding consequence**                                                                                    |
|-------------|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **CICD-01** | Controlled source only             | Production changes originate from approved repositories and protected merge paths.                         |
| **CICD-02** | Requirement-linked change          | Every material change links to an approved requirement, defect, risk, incident or ADR.                     |
| **CICD-03** | Independent review                 | Author, required approver and production releaser are separated for material changes.                      |
| **CICD-04** | Build once                         | The same immutable artifact digest is tested, signed and promoted to production.                           |
| **CICD-05** | Ephemeral builders                 | Build runners are disposable, isolated, identity-bound and free of standing production credentials.        |
| **CICD-06** | Pinned inputs                      | Dependencies, base images, toolchains and generated inputs are versioned and integrity verified.           |
| **CICD-07** | No builder-held signing key        | Artifact signing occurs through independent policy-gated key use.                                          |
| **CICD-08** | Provenance before promotion        | No artifact advances without acceptable source/build provenance and SBOM.                                  |
| **CICD-09** | Policy is executable               | Repository, dependency, build, security, privacy, AI, artifact and deployment rules are machine-evaluated. |
| **CICD-10** | No fail-open material gate         | Unavailable or indeterminate security/tenancy/evidence/signing policy blocks promotion.                    |
| **CICD-11** | Configuration is release identity  | Schemas, policies, prompts, agent/tool definitions and detection content are version-bound to the release. |
| **CICD-12** | No autonomous AI release authority | AI tools may assist but cannot independently approve, merge, sign or deploy material production changes.   |
| **CICD-13** | No secrets in source or logs       | Secrets are referenced from approved vaults and prevented from entering code, artifacts, logs or evidence. |
| **CICD-14** | Every deployment is attributable   | Target, controller, identity, digest, configuration, approval and outcome are recorded.                    |
| **CICD-15** | Every rollout is bounded           | Canary/cohort/ceiling, pause criteria, rollback and customer impact are decided before production.         |
| **CICD-16** | Emergency is controlled            | Urgency compresses time; it never removes identity, review, signing, evidence or reconciliation.           |
| **CICD-17** | Unknown supply chain is prohibited | Unverifiable source, dependency, builder, artifact or signature cannot be trusted.                         |
| **CICD-18** | Runtime reconciles to release      | Running artifacts/configuration must match the approved release manifest.                                  |
| **CICD-19** | Claims follow release evidence     | Security, availability, AI and assurance claims require measured, approved evidence.                       |
| **CICD-20** | Access follows role and time       | Repository, pipeline, signing and production privileges are least-privilege, time-bound and reviewable.    |

# 05 \| Trusted Software-Delivery Lifecycle and Trust Boundaries

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image47.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image112.png" />

***Figure 2 - Trusted software-delivery lifecycle.***

| **Stage**   | **Authoritative input**                      | **Required output / evidence**                                  | **Stop condition**                                            |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Plan**    | Approved requirement/risk/incident and scope | Change class, owner, affected domains, tests and rollout intent | No controlled source authority.                               |
| **Source**  | Protected repository and branch policy       | Reviewed immutable source revision                              | Missing owner/review, stale approval or prohibited secret.    |
| **Build**   | Pinned source/inputs and trusted runner      | Digest, logs, test results, SBOM and provenance                 | Unknown input, compromised runner or non-reproducible output. |
| **Verify**  | Security/privacy/AI/quality policies         | Pass/fail decisions, findings and exceptions                    | Blocking finding or indeterminate material policy.            |
| **Sign**    | Verified digest and approved attestation set | Artifact signature and signed release metadata                  | Builder-controlled key or incomplete evidence.                |
| **Promote** | Immutable signed candidate                   | Target-specific release manifest and approval                   | Rebuild, mutable tag or unapproved configuration.             |
| **Deploy**  | Authorized target and rollout policy         | Deployment record, cohort and runtime identity                  | Target mismatch, admission failure or missing rollback.       |
| **Operate** | Runtime telemetry and release manifest       | Health, drift, incident, rollback and closure evidence          | Unreconciled runtime or breached stop threshold.              |

# 06 \| Source-Control Organization, Repository Classes and Ownership

| **Repository class**                  | **Examples**                                                                                      |                                                                                                       | **Required controls**                                                                                |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Class A - Crown jewel**             | Authorization, tenant isolation, evidence ledger, action broker, signing, identity and key policy |                                                                                                       | Two qualified approvals; Security owner; signed merge; restricted bot access; heightened monitoring. |
| **Class B - Production service**      | Core modules, ingestion, connectors, APIs, AI gateway, data services and deployment code          |                                                                                                       | CODEOWNERS; independent approval; protected merge queue; complete CI gates.                          |
| **Class C - Controlled content**      | Detections, playbooks, prompts, agents, policies, schemas, templates and framework mappings       |                                                                                                       | Typed validation, domain owner approval, simulation/replay/evaluation and versioned publication.     |
| **Class D - Tooling / documentation** | Internal tools, SDKs, docs, examples and non-production utilities                                 |                                                                                                       | Peer review, scanning, license/dependency policy and controlled publication.                         |
| **Archive / retired**                 | Superseded or unsupported source                                                                  |                                                                                                       | Read-only, owner, retention, vulnerability exposure decision and no active release path.             |
| **Ownership field**                   |                                                                                                   | **Requirement**                                                                                       |                                                                                                      |
| **Accountable owner**                 |                                                                                                   | One named engineering owner for availability, security, maintenance and retirement.                   |                                                                                                      |
| **CODEOWNERS**                        |                                                                                                   | Paths map to qualified reviewers; broad catch-all ownership is insufficient for sensitive areas.      |                                                                                                      |
| **Backup owner**                      |                                                                                                   | Named successor; no single-person repository dependency.                                              |                                                                                                      |
| **Automation identities**             |                                                                                                   | Explicit purpose, scopes, permitted branches/actions, owner and expiry.                               |                                                                                                      |
| **Repository settings**               |                                                                                                   | Managed through approved policy where platform supports it; drift is monitored.                       |                                                                                                      |
| **Visibility**                        |                                                                                                   | Private by default; public/open-source publication requires legal/security/product approval.          |                                                                                                      |
| **Forks**                             |                                                                                                   | Organization-controlled only for production code; personal/private forks of EC-3 material prohibited. |                                                                                                      |
| **Retention / deletion**              |                                                                                                   | Aligned to legal hold, release reconstruction and intellectual-property requirements.                 |                                                                                                      |

# 07 \| Branch, Merge, Review and Commit-Integrity Model

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image49.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image114.png" />

***Figure 4 - Source-control and review workflow.***

| **Control**                  | **Minimum standard**                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Branch strategy**          | Short-lived branches or equivalent controlled workspace; long-lived divergence requires an ADR.                    |
| **Protected default branch** | No direct human push; status checks, review count, owner review and merge queue enforced.                          |
| **Approval freshness**       | Any material source, dependency, generated file, policy or build-definition change invalidates prior approval.     |
| **Review quality**           | Reviewer confirms requirement, behavior, threat/data/AI impact, tests, observability and rollback—not only syntax. |
| **Sensitive path**           | Crown-jewel paths require qualified owner and Security review; self-approval prohibited.                           |
| **Merge identity**           | Merge event attributable and tamper-evident; commit/merge signing used for release-critical repositories.          |
| **Generated code/files**     | Generator and inputs versioned; diffs reviewable; generated output not exempt from scanning/tests.                 |
| **Bot changes**              | Bot identity and permitted action constrained; auto-merge only for explicitly approved low-risk classes.           |
| **History rewrite**          | Prohibited on protected/released history except controlled incident response with evidence.                        |
| **Release tag**              | Created by trusted release automation after manifest approval; human mutable tags are not authority.               |

# 08 \| Change Taxonomy, Risk Classification and Approval Authority

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image50.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image115.png" />

***Figure 5 - Change classification and minimum approval authority.***

| **Change class**                | **Examples**                                                                                | **Required risk dimensions**                                                                            |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **CH-0 editorial**              | Non-normative documentation, comments and formatting                                        | No runtime, security, customer, legal or control effect.                                                |
| **CH-1 routine**                | Low-risk application change within established pattern                                      | Blast radius, rollback, tests and backward compatibility.                                               |
| **CH-2 material**               | New behavior, dependency, interface, state, data path or operational responsibility         | Architecture, customer, SLO, cost, privacy, evidence and migration impact.                              |
| **CH-3 security / crown jewel** | IAM, tenant isolation, cryptography, evidence, action broker, signing, secret or admin path | Threat model, independent Security review, abuse/negative tests and explicit rollback.                  |
| **CH-4 data / schema**          | Migration, retention, deletion, residency, lineage or authority change                      | Compatibility, backfill, rollback/forward fix, integrity reconciliation and DPA impact.                 |
| **CH-5 AI / agent**             | Model route, prompt, retrieval, memory, tool, autonomy or evaluation change                 | Use-case risk, data policy, adversarial tests, grounding, cost and kill switch.                         |
| **CH-6 emergency**              | Active incident, critical vulnerability or severe customer impact                           | Minimal scope, named authority, focused evidence, immediate verification and post-event reconciliation. |
