# 09 \| Requirement, Work-Item, Code and Release Traceability

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image51.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image116.png" />

***Figure 6 - Requirement-to-runtime software-release trace.***

| **Trace object**        | **Mandatory links**                                                                                 |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Work item**           | Requirement/defect/risk/incident, owner, acceptance criteria, change class and target release.      |
| **Pull request**        | Work item, affected components, tests, security/privacy/AI/evidence impact, migration and rollback. |
| **Build**               | Repository/ref/commit, runner identity, recipe, inputs, dependencies, toolchain and output digest.  |
| **Finding / exception** | Rule, severity, affected artifact, owner, expiry, compensating control and release decision.        |
| **Release manifest**    | Artifacts, configuration, policies, schema, detection/AI content, target, approvals and rollout.    |
| **Deployment**          | Release manifest, controller identity, target/cell/cohort, timestamps, outcome and rollback.        |
| **Runtime**             | Observed artifact/configuration, health, SLO, drift, incident and customer impact.                  |
| **Claim / assurance**   | Approved claim, scope, evidence, verification date, limitation and expiry.                          |

# 10 \| Developer Workstation and Engineering-Environment Controls

| **Area**              | **Required control**                                                                                                        |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity / device** | Individual SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, managed/approved device, disk encryption, supported OS and endpoint security.       |
| **Local privilege**   | Restricted administrator rights; elevated actions attributable; no shared accounts or family devices.                       |
| **Workspace**         | Approved source client, encrypted storage, automatic lock, organization-controlled repository and dependency configuration. |
| **Secrets**           | No production/customer secrets locally; secret scanning pre-commit and server-side; vault references only.                  |
| **Customer data**     | Synthetic data by default; no production export to local devices; exceptional diagnostics controlled separately.            |
| **Network**           | Approved access path; prohibited exposure of local services; restricted access to EC-3 source and artifacts.                |
| **Coding assistants** | Only approved AI tools/routes; confidential input policy; no unapproved public paste/upload.                                |
| **Build parity**      | Local results are advisory; trusted release artifacts originate only from approved build infrastructure.                    |
| **Offboarding**       | Access/session/token revocation, source entitlement removal and managed-device handling immediately upon role/contract end. |
| **Monitoring**        | Source, repository and access events logged; abnormal bulk clone/download or token use investigated.                        |

# 11 \| Secure Coding, Review and Sensitive-Code Ownership

| **Control domain**                 | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                           |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Input and output**               | Validate, constrain, encode and safely serialize across trust boundaries; reject ambiguous tenant/purpose context.    |
| **Authentication / authorization** | Use approved libraries and policy interfaces; no bespoke bypass, implicit admin or client-side authority.             |
| **Tenant isolation**               | Tenant/environment/region mandatory in queries, events, cache, objects, search, observability and AI context.         |
| **Cryptography**                   | Use approved primitives/services; no custom cryptography, embedded keys or disabled verification.                     |
| **Errors / logs**                  | Stable safe errors; no secrets or sensitive payloads; correlation and audit events present.                           |
| **Concurrency / idempotency**      | Safe retries, deduplication, ordering and compensation for externally visible side effects.                           |
| **Data lifecycle**                 | Classification, purpose, minimization, retention, legal hold, deletion and export implemented as controlled behavior. |
| **Evidence / audit**               | Material decisions and changes produce attributable, immutable or compensating evidence.                              |
| **AI / agents**                    | Gateway-only, typed tools, target-side authorization, citations, bounded memory, fallback and human control.          |
| **Review evidence**                | Reviewer records material concerns and confirms tests; “LGTM” alone is insufficient for CH-2+ changes.                |

# 12 \| AI-Assisted Engineering and Generated-Code Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image52.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image117.png" />

***Figure 7 - AI-assisted engineering control lifecycle.***

| **Area**                 | **Binding rule**                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Approved route**       | Use only AI tools/providers/configurations approved in the AI Register and accessible through controlled identity.                     |
| **Input handling**       | Minimize and classify code/context; no secrets, customer data, EC-3 threat details or restricted contracts without explicit authority. |
| **Generated output**     | Treat as untrusted; developer verifies correctness, security, license/provenance, tests and fit to requirement.                        |
| **Attribution**          | Human committer remains accountable; material AI assistance recorded where required by policy.                                         |
| **Agent authority**      | No autonomous merge, branch protection change, release approval, signing, production deploy or secret retrieval.                       |
| **Repository bots**      | Scoped identities and typed actions; generated PRs enter normal review and policy gates.                                               |
| **Evaluation**           | Track security defects, rework, license findings, hallucinated APIs and test escape rate by approved use case.                         |
| **Kill control**         | Disable model/provider/prompt/agent/tool route without stopping deterministic source, build or release operations.                     |
| **Retention / training** | Provider retention and training terms follow D1-D4; customer/source content not used outside approved purpose.                         |
| **Disclosure**           | Engineering-facing indicators distinguish AI suggestions from verified system facts and human approvals.                               |

# 13 \| Third-Party Dependency, Package and License Governance

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image53.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image118.png" />

***Figure 8 - Third-party dependency intake and update lifecycle.***

| **Control**             | **Minimum requirement**                                                                                         |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source**              | Approved registry, vendor or source repository; direct arbitrary download in release build prohibited.          |
| **Integrity**           | Cryptographic digest/signature where available; lockfile/digest pinning; mirror preserves source metadata.      |
| **Malware / confusion** | Typosquat, dependency-confusion, maintainer-takeover and malicious-package checks proportionate to risk.        |
| **License / IP**        | Approved license policy, attribution/notice and distribution obligations; prohibited or unknown licenses block. |
| **Vulnerability**       | Current vulnerability status plus reachability/exploitability and compensating runtime controls.                |
| **Maintenance health**  | Owner, release activity, support status, bus factor, deprecation and replacement plan.                          |
| **Update policy**       | Automated proposal allowed; high-risk or breaking updates require sandbox, tests and staged adoption.           |
| **Transitives**         | Complete graph visible in SBOM; transitive changes receive the same policy evaluation.                          |
| **Exceptions**          | Specific version/use, owner, rationale, compensating controls, expiry and removal plan.                         |
| **Retirement**          | Remove unused dependencies, stale mirrors, credentials and associated attack surface.                           |

# 14 \| Build System, Runner and Toolchain Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image54.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image119.png" />

***Figure 9 - Build trust and provenance chain.***

| **Component**           | **Required architecture**                                                                                        |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Runner lifecycle**    | Ephemeral per job or verified clean reset; no cross-job workspace, secret or cache contamination.                |
| **Identity**            | Short-lived workload identity constrained by repository, ref, workflow, environment and intended action.         |
| **Network**             | Default-deny/bounded egress; internal mirrors and approved endpoints; no unrestricted production network path.   |
| **Build image**         | Approved, scanned, signed and pinned; compiler/runtime/tool versions declared and updateable.                    |
| **Inputs**              | Source, submodules, dependencies, base images, generators and configuration pinned and integrity checked.        |
| **Caches**              | Content-addressed, policy-scoped and non-authoritative; cache poisoning detected; sensitive outputs excluded.    |
| **Logs**                | Complete enough for reconstruction; secret/redaction controls; immutable retention and correlation.              |
| **Output**              | Write only to candidate artifact namespace; immutable digest; cannot overwrite released artifact.                |
| **Administration**      | Separate from application teams; JIT, recorded and dual-controlled for sensitive changes.                        |
| **Compromise response** | Freeze builders, revoke identities, invalidate affected attestations, rebuild from trusted baseline and re-sign. |

# 15 \| Hermetic, Deterministic and Reproducible Build Controls

| **Property**                   | **Required interpretation**                                                                                                            |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Hermetic**                   | All material inputs declared and retrieved from approved sources; undeclared network/time/host dependencies prohibited where feasible. |
| **Deterministic**              | Same declared inputs and environment produce functionally equivalent output; differences are explained and bounded.                    |
| **Reproducible**               | Independent trusted rebuild can verify the released digest or a documented equivalence class for supported artifact types.             |
| **Timestamp / locale**         | Normalized or declared; timezone, locale, ordering and generated metadata do not create unexplained variation.                         |
| **Generator control**          | Code/schema/client generators pinned; generated output and generator identity included in provenance.                                  |
| **Native / platform builds**   | Platform-specific variance declared; each build target separately signed, tested and represented in SBOM.                              |
| **Non-reproducible exception** | Technical reason, risk, owner, compensating attestation, expiry and roadmap to reduce uncertainty.                                     |
| **Verification cadence**       | Critical release types independently rebuilt on schedule and after builder/toolchain compromise or major change.                       |

# 16 \| Test Orchestration and Release-Gate Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image55.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image120.png" />

***Figure 10 - Policy-as-code and release-gate evaluation.***

| **Gate family**          | **Minimum release checks**                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Quality**              | Compile/type, unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, compatibility, migration, accessibility and defect thresholds.       |
| **Security**             | SAST, secret, dependency, container, IaC, API/authorization, tenant isolation, abuse-case and artifact verification.        |
| **Privacy / data**       | Purpose, classification, retention, residency, deletion, export, data migration and audit event checks.                     |
| **Evidence / assurance** | Evidence object, ledger/verifier, completeness-state, evaluator determinism and audit-package regression.                   |
| **AI**                   | Grounding, citation, prompt injection, tool authorization, memory isolation, deterministic fallback, cost and kill control. |
| **Detection / response** | Rule replay, false-positive/noise, playbook simulation, authority R0-R4, signing and receipt reconciliation.                |
| **Reliability**          | Performance, endurance, queue/backpressure, zone/dependency failure, restore, rollback and SLO burn.                        |
| **Supply chain**         | Approved source/runner, SBOM, provenance, signatures, license, vulnerability and policy.                                    |
| **Commercial / cost**    | Capacity and unit-economics headroom where change affects ingestion, storage, search, AI or labor.                          |
| **Claims**               | No release enables a public/contract claim without approved evidence and Claim Register status.                             |

# 17 \| SBOM, VEX, Provenance, Attestation and Artifact Signing

| **Artifact**                   | **Required content / control**                                                                                           |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **SBOM**                       | Complete package/component relationships, versions, licenses, hashes, supplier/source and build target; bound to digest. |
| **Vulnerability status / VEX** | Known issue applicability, reachability, exploitability, mitigation, decision owner and review/expiry.                   |
| **Build provenance**           | Source revision, builder identity, workflow, inputs, dependencies, build image/toolchain, parameters and output digest.  |
| **Test attestations**          | Gate, version, environment, result, evidence reference and exception; generated by attributable systems.                 |
| **Policy decision**            | Policy/rule version, evaluated facts, result, reason code and decision identity.                                         |
| **Artifact signature**         | HSM/KMS-backed or equivalent protected signing; key purpose/rotation/revocation and transparency/evidence as approved.   |
| **Release attestation**        | Binds signed artifact, configuration, schema, policy, target and approvals.                                              |
| **Verification**               | Consumer/deployment side verifies digest, signature, provenance and policy before admission.                             |
| **Revocation**                 | Compromised key/artifact/build invalidated; affected deployments identified and containment initiated.                   |
| **Retention**                  | Long enough to reconstruct supported releases, incidents, customer obligations and legal hold.                           |

# 18 \| Artifact Repository, Immutability, Retention and Promotion

| **Area**               | **Required control**                                                                                                         |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Namespaces**         | Candidate, quarantined, approved/released and archived/retired states separated by policy and identity.                      |
| **Immutability**       | Digest-addressed; released artifact cannot be overwritten or silently deleted; mutable tags are convenience only.            |
| **Admission metadata** | Signature, provenance, SBOM, policy status, vulnerability/exception and release eligibility visible.                         |
| **Replication**        | Region/recovery replication follows residency, integrity and retention policy; verification after transfer.                  |
| **Access**             | Builders publish candidates; signing service attests; release automation promotes; humans do not manually replace artifacts. |
| **Quarantine**         | Suspected malicious, unknown provenance, policy-failing or compromised artifacts isolated and blocked.                       |
| **Retention**          | Supported release lifecycle, rollback window, investigations, customer obligations and legal hold.                           |
| **Deletion**           | Controlled retirement with dependency/deployment check; evidence remains where required; no dangling production reference.   |
| **External artifacts** | Vendor binaries/images mirrored or referenced by digest with evidence; availability and exit risk tracked.                   |
| **Recovery**           | Artifact catalog, metadata, signatures and manifests included in recovery testing.                                           |

# 19 \| Pipeline Identity, Secrets, Tokens and Signing-Key Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image56.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image121.png" />

***Figure 11 - Pipeline credential and signing-key separation.***

| **Identity / secret**       | **Required controls**                                                                                       |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Repository application**  | Repository/ref/action scoped, short-lived where possible, owner, rotation and audit.                        |
| **Build identity**          | Federated per job, no static cloud key, constrained audience/claims and minimal read/write.                 |
| **Dependency credentials**  | Read-only mirror access; no broad package publish unless dedicated publisher job.                           |
| **Artifact publisher**      | Candidate namespace only; cannot sign or deploy.                                                            |
| **Signing service**         | Independent policy and protected key; receives digest/attestations, not mutable build workspace.            |
| **Deployment controller**   | Environment/target scoped; verifies release manifest; no source or signing-key access.                      |
| **Human production access** | Separate JIT identity, case/change reference, managed device and recorded session.                          |
| **Secret injection**        | Runtime/job-specific delivery from vault; masked; not written to workspace, logs or artifacts.              |
| **Rotation / revocation**   | Automated where feasible; immediate on compromise/role change; affected artifacts and deployments assessed. |
| **Break glass**             | Dual-controlled, time-limited, independently logged and followed by credential rotation/reconciliation.     |

# 20 \| Infrastructure, Schema, Detection, Policy and AI Content as Code

| **Controlled content**         | **Required delivery controls**                                                                                          |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Infrastructure as code**     | Plan/impact, policy, module ownership, non-prod apply, drift, rollback and runtime reconciliation.                      |
| **Database/schema migrations** | Expand-contract, compatibility window, backup/restore, backfill, validation, rollback/forward fix and tenant isolation. |
| **Event/API schemas**          | Versioning, consumer compatibility, deprecation, generated clients, contract tests and adoption telemetry.              |
| **Authorization/policy**       | Typed policy, negative tests, decision explainability, staged rollout, policy version binding and fail-closed behavior. |
| **Detection content**          | Detection-as-code, data prerequisites, replay, noise/performance, ATT&CK mapping, staged publication and retirement.    |
| **Playbooks/actions**          | Simulation, R0-R4 authority, approvals, per-tenant signing, compensation, rollback and receipt checks.                  |
| **Prompts/retrieval/agents**   | Risk classification, prompt/tool versions, evaluation, injection tests, budgets, human oversight and kill switches.     |
| **Compliance mappings**        | Licensed content mode, SME/legal review, evaluator version and no implied certification.                                |
| **Configuration**              | Schema, owner, environment/tenant scope, defaults, secrets references, validation and audit history.                    |
| **Documentation**              | Versioned with release, role-appropriate, limitations explicit and obsolete instructions retired.                       |

# 21 \| Environment Promotion, Deployment Strategies and Release Binding

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image57.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image122.png" />

***Figure 12 - Artifact promotion and production rollout.***

| **Strategy**                | **Permitted use**                                        | **Required controls**                                                                            |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Preview / ephemeral**     | Per-change verification                                  | Time-bound environment, synthetic data, approved blueprint and automatic destruction.            |
| **Rolling**                 | Backward-compatible stateless/service changes            | Capacity, readiness, max unavailable/surge, health and rollback.                                 |
| **Canary**                  | Material or uncertain production change                  | Small cohort/cell, explicit metrics, dwell time, pause/rollback and no hidden bypass.            |
| **Blue/green**              | High rollback-value application/config change            | Data/schema compatibility, traffic control, state synchronization and expiry of old environment. |
| **Shadow**                  | Detection/AI/query behavior without customer-side effect | Privacy, cost, output isolation and no unauthorized action.                                      |
| **Feature flag**            | Behavior decoupled from deploy                           | Owner, tenant/region scope, safe default, expiry, audit, kill switch and test matrix.            |
| **Maintenance / migration** | Stateful or compatibility-sensitive change               | Window, backup, customer communication, rehearsal, reconciliation and forward-fix.               |
| **Emergency**               | Incident containment                                     | Section 24 controls; no silent permanent divergence.                                             |

# 22 \| Feature Flags, Compatibility, Migrations and Progressive Delivery

| **Area**                     | **Required rule**                                                                                                  |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Flag registry**            | Owner, purpose, type, default, scope, creation, expiry, dependencies and kill behavior.                            |
| **Security-sensitive flags** | Cannot weaken authentication, authorization, tenancy, evidence integrity or signing without CH-3 approval.         |
| **Tenant targeting**         | Explicit tenant/environment/region; no accidental broad enablement; customer agreement where required.             |
| **Compatibility**            | N-1 or declared producer/consumer window; schema and API compatibility tests before rollout.                       |
| **Database migration**       | Expand-contract, idempotent operations, bounded locks, progress, validation and safe interruption.                 |
| **Backfill**                 | Rate/cost/tenant controls, checkpointing, replay safety, audit and reconciliation.                                 |
| **Data transformation**      | Original authority preserved; migration version and evidence; no silent loss or semantic change.                   |
| **Progressive criteria**     | Technical, security, business and customer indicators; dwell time and sample size defined.                         |
| **Expiry / cleanup**         | Temporary flag/migration compatibility code removed by owner and date; stale flags are defects.                    |
| **Rollback limits**          | Where state prevents rollback, approved forward-fix/compensation and customer impact plan required before release. |

# 23 \| Change Approval, Release Authority and Segregation of Duties

| **Role**                             | **May**                                                                | **Must not**                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Author**                           | Prepare source, tests, documentation and change evidence.              | Self-approve a material change or issue release signature.                                |
| **Code owner / reviewer**            | Review assigned domain, request changes and approve based on evidence. | Approve outside competence or while materially contributing without independent reviewer. |
| **Security / privacy / AI reviewer** | Approve applicable control impact and findings.                        | Convert missing evidence into implicit acceptance.                                        |
| **Build platform**                   | Execute controlled build and emit evidence.                            | Hold production deployment or artifact-signing authority by default.                      |
| **Signing service**                  | Sign eligible digest after policy success.                             | Build, alter or choose artifact content.                                                  |
| **Release authority**                | Confirm manifest, approvals, risk, customer impact and rollout.        | Edit source, bypass failed gates or use unsigned artifacts.                               |
| **Deployment controller**            | Deploy approved manifest to authorized target.                         | Select alternate artifact/configuration or broaden scope.                                 |
| **SRE / incident commander**         | Pause, rollback, freeze or invoke emergency path.                      | Permanently normalize emergency drift without review/reconciliation.                      |

# 24 \| Emergency Change and Security-Hotfix Workflow

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image58.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image123.png" />

***Figure 13 - Emergency and security-hotfix workflow.***

| **Control**         | **Emergency requirement**                                                                                         |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Trigger**         | Active incident, exploited critical vulnerability, severe outage or imminent material customer harm.              |
| **Authority**       | Named incident commander and independent release/security approver; scope and duration recorded.                  |
| **Branch / source** | Dedicated protected emergency branch or equivalent; minimal change; no direct production editing.                 |
| **Verification**    | Focused unit/integration/security checks proportionate to risk; skipped checks explicitly recorded and scheduled. |
| **Artifact**        | Normal trusted builder, provenance, SBOM and signing; no unsigned manual binary.                                  |
| **Rollout**         | Canary or smallest safe scope, immediate observability and pre-authorized rollback/freeze.                        |
| **Communication**   | Customer, regulator, insurer, partner and executive decisions follow incident/legal authority.                    |
| **Expiry**          | Temporary feature, rule, credential or exception has owner and automatic review/expiry.                           |
| **Reconciliation**  | Merge to normal history, rebuild if needed, compare artifact, rotate credentials and remove drift.                |
| **Post review**     | Root cause, control bypass analysis, CAPA, documentation/test update and evidence closure.                        |

# 25 \| Rollback, Roll-Forward, Kill Switches and Trust Re-Establishment

| **Capability**                    | **Required design**                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Application rollback**          | Prior signed manifest retained and compatible; automation tested; target state verified.                             |
| **Configuration rollback**        | Versioned configuration with safe default; secrets and schema dependencies considered.                               |
| **Schema rollback / forward fix** | Defined per migration; irreversible changes require backup, compatibility and compensating plan.                     |
| **Feature kill switch**           | Independent of failed component where feasible; scoped by tenant/region/feature and evidence logged.                 |
| **AI kill controls**              | Disable model/provider/prompt/retrieval/agent/tool/tenant/global route independently; deterministic fallback.        |
| **Detection/action freeze**       | Disable content or action class; action-broker global/per-tenant freeze independent of application plane.            |
| **Artifact revocation**           | Mark digest/key/provenance invalid, block admission and identify all deployed instances.                             |
| **Trust re-establishment**        | Rebuild from trusted source and builder, rotate identities/keys, re-attest, redeploy and reconcile runtime/evidence. |
| **Customer effect**               | Rollback/forward-fix decision includes data integrity, missed detection, action, evidence and contractual impact.    |
| **Evidence**                      | Trigger, authority, versions, timestamps, outcome, reconciliation and residual risk retained.                        |

# 26 \| Software-Supply-Chain Threat Model and Abuse Cases

| **Threat / abuse case**               | **Primary controls**                                                                 | **Required verification**                                             |
|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Developer identity compromise**     | Phishing-resistant MFA, managed device, branch protection, review, anomaly detection | Simulated stolen token / impossible-travel / bulk-clone response.     |
| **Malicious insider source change**   | Independent owner review, SoD, signed merge, release authority separation            | Unauthorized protected-path and self-approval tests.                  |
| **Build runner compromise**           | Ephemeral runners, pinned image, bounded egress, no signing key, provenance          | Runner escape, cache poisoning and fabricated test/attestation tests. |
| **Dependency confusion / typosquat**  | Internal mirror, namespace control, lockfile/digest and provenance                   | Negative package resolution and malicious package exercises.          |
| **Compromised dependency maintainer** | Update policy, sandbox, owner, diff/SBOM/vulnerability/behavior tests                | High-risk update quarantine and rollback exercise.                    |
| **Artifact registry substitution**    | Immutable digest, signature/provenance verification and access separation            | Tampered artifact/tag substitution blocked at admission.              |
| **Signing key compromise**            | HSM/KMS, policy, dual control, rotation/revocation and transparency evidence         | Key revocation and fleet impact identification drill.                 |
| **Deployment controller compromise**  | Target-scoped identity, signed manifest, admission and out-of-band freeze            | Unauthorized target/scope/configuration deployment tests.             |
| **CI secret exfiltration**            | Short-lived identity, secret masking, scoped injection, egress and logs              | Canary secret / log redaction / fork-PR isolation tests.              |
| **AI assistant poisoning or leakage** | Approved gateway, input policy, human review, tool limits and monitoring             | Prompt injection, secret request and insecure-code corpus tests.      |
| **Emergency-path abuse**              | Named authority, minimal scope, signing, evidence, expiry and reconciliation         | Attempted bypass and expired exception tests.                         |
| **Release evidence falsification**    | Independent systems, immutable logs, artifact/runtime reconciliation                 | Mismatched provenance/test/deployment evidence detected.              |

# 27 \| Vendor Binaries, Base Images, Build Images and External Services

| **Category**                    | **Required controls**                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Base images**                 | Minimal, approved publisher/source, digest pinned, signed/verified, SBOM, rebuild cadence and retirement.             |
| **Build images/toolchains**     | Versioned, scanned, reproducible acquisition, owner, compatibility tests and no hidden auto-update.                   |
| **Vendor binaries/agents**      | Contracted source, signature/hash, license, update/rollback, telemetry/data behavior and support lifecycle.           |
| **Hosted CI/CD service**        | Identity federation, runner isolation, audit export, retention, region/data handling, incident notification and exit. |
| **Package registry/mirror**     | Namespace governance, provenance, malware controls, immutability, availability, backup and access logs.               |
| **Signing/attestation service** | Key custody, policy, availability, auditability, revocation, export and independent verification.                     |
| **Code scanning service**       | Data sent, retention/training, region, false-negative/positive governance, API and provider failure mode.             |
| **AI coding service**           | D1-D4 controls, source/confidentiality handling, model/provider registry, no autonomous release authority.            |
| **Third-party action**          | No vendor system may deploy to customer estate or production without Zoiko policy and release authority.              |
| **Exit**                        | Artifact/source/evidence portability, key/identity revocation, data deletion and replacement plan tested.             |

# 28 \| Release Evidence, Customer Impact, Communications and Claims

| **Evidence domain**      | **Required release record**                                                                           |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope**                | Requirements, components, tenants/regions/features, exclusions and change class.                      |
| **Source / review**      | Commit(s), PR(s), author, owners, approvals, stale-approval status and exceptions.                    |
| **Build / supply chain** | Runner identity, recipe, toolchain, dependencies, SBOM, provenance, signatures and findings.          |
| **Quality / control**    | Tests and policy results for security, privacy, AI, evidence, reliability, accessibility and cost.    |
| **Configuration**        | Schemas, policies, prompts/agents/tools, detections/playbooks, feature flags and migrations.          |
| **Deployment**           | Target, strategy, cohort, timestamps, controller, versions, pause/rollback and observed runtime.      |
| **Customer impact**      | Downtime, behavior, data, residency, security, AI disclosure, support and contractual obligations.    |
| **Communication**        | Release notes, maintenance, incident/security notice, support briefing and Trust Center/claim update. |
| **Residual risk**        | Accepted findings, owner, controls, expiry and customer disclosure if required.                       |
| **Closure**              | SLO/security/evidence reconciliation, defects, rollback status and final approval.                    |

# 29 \| Pipeline Observability, SLOs, Capacity, Cost and Continuity

| **Metric / capability**              | **Required measure**                                                                                            |
|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source-control availability**      | Protected merge path and audit availability; offline/bypass behavior prohibited.                                |
| **Build queue / duration**           | By repository/class; p50/p95, failure, retry, cache and capacity saturation.                                    |
| **Gate health**                      | Pass/fail/indeterminate by policy; false-positive/negative and exception trend.                                 |
| **Provenance/signing success**       | Eligible artifacts receiving complete attestations and signature without manual intervention.                   |
| **Lead time / deployment frequency** | Measured without rewarding bypass, oversized batches or unsafe automation.                                      |
| **Change failure / rollback**        | Customer-impacting defects, rollback/forward fix, time to detect and recovery.                                  |
| **Approval latency**                 | By change class and owner; staffing bottleneck visible without weakening SoD.                                   |
| **Dependency exposure**              | Unowned, unsupported, vulnerable, unlicensed, exception-expired and update-lag counts.                          |
| **Runner / artifact cost**           | Per build, repository, release, environment, cache, storage, retention and egress.                              |
| **Continuity**                       | Source/build/artifact/signing/deploy provider outage runbooks, recovery tests and alternate controlled path.    |
| **Security telemetry**               | Failed policy bypass, unusual clone/download, token misuse, signing anomalies and unauthorized target attempts. |
| **Evidence completeness**            | Releases with complete manifest and runtime reconciliation; incomplete release cannot be closed.                |

# 30 \| Remote-Team Delivery Controls and Production Custody

| **Control area**               | **Binding implementation**                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Individual accountability**  | No shared repository, CI/CD, artifact, cloud or production identities.                                                      |
| **Least privilege**            | Access based on role, workstream, environment, information class and time; broad seniority does not imply broad access.     |
| **Managed endpoints**          | Required for EC-2/EC-3 access; security posture and patching enforced.                                                      |
| **Repository access**          | Class-based; contractor access time-bounded; bulk export monitored; personal forks prohibited for sensitive code.           |
| **Pipeline administration**    | Restricted group, JIT for material changes, independent review and complete audit.                                          |
| **Production custody**         | Developers do not hold routine production write access; deployment by controller and approved release authority.            |
| **Segregation**                | Author, reviewer, signing policy owner, release approver and production operator separated for CH-2+.                       |
| **Secrets**                    | Vault-delivered short-lived credentials only; no chat/email/document exchange.                                              |
| **Contractors/subcontractors** | Named sponsor, defined scope, IP/confidentiality, approved location/device and automatic expiry.                            |
| **Offboarding**                | Immediate session/token/access revocation and ownership reassignment; active release duties transferred.                    |
| **Incident response**          | Suspected misuse, code exfiltration, policy bypass or credential exposure reported immediately and evidenced.               |
| **Need-to-know**               | Engineers receive complete requirements for assigned components, not unrelated commercial, customer or crown-jewel details. |

# 31 \| Failure States, Quarantine and Safe Degradation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image59.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image124.png" />

***Figure 14 - Pipeline failure and safe-degradation state model.***

| **State**              | **Required behavior**                                                                                  |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **BLOCKED**            | Mandatory check failed; merge/sign/promote/deploy prevented; owner and reason visible.                 |
| **INDETERMINATE**      | Policy or evidence unavailable; material gate fails closed; retry/alternate approved check only.       |
| **QUARANTINED**        | Artifact/dependency/runner output isolated; not consumable by normal build or deployment.              |
| **STALE APPROVAL**     | Source, policy, dependency, manifest or time window changed; review must be renewed.                   |
| **UNKNOWN PROVENANCE** | Artifact cannot be linked to approved source/build; use prohibited.                                    |
| **SIGNING DEGRADED**   | Signing unavailable; unsigned fallback prohibited; candidate may wait but cannot promote.              |
| **SOURCE DEGRADED**    | Source provider unavailable; existing runtime continues; bypass merge path prohibited.                 |
| **BUILD DEGRADED**     | Builder unavailable; no unapproved local/manual production build.                                      |
| **DEPLOY DEGRADED**    | Deployment controller unavailable; no routine manual production mutation.                              |
| **COMPROMISED**        | Freeze affected path, revoke identities/keys, preserve evidence, rebuild trust and assess all outputs. |
| **EMERGENCY**          | Named incident authority and constrained workflow; all temporary changes expire/reconcile.             |
| **WITHDRAWN RELEASE**  | Artifact/manifest revoked; future admission blocked; deployed instances identified and remediated.     |

| **V09 Release manifest builder**    | Artifacts, config, schema, policy, AI/detection content, targets, approvals and rollback.          |

| **V22 Retired release / component** | End-of-support, deployed remnants, vulnerabilities, archival and deletion state.                   |

# 34 \| Verification, Recurring Assurance and Release Evidence

| **Control test**                      | **Cadence / trigger**                     | **Pass condition**                                                                   |
|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Protected-branch negative test**    | Continuous and quarterly control exercise | Direct push, self-approval and missing-owner merge blocked.                          |
| **Runner isolation test**             | Each runner-image change and quarterly    | No cross-job state/secret; bounded egress and identity claims enforced.              |
| **Dependency-confusion test**         | Each resolver/mirror change and quarterly | Private namespace cannot resolve to unapproved external package.                     |
| **Artifact substitution test**        | Each registry/admission change            | Digest/signature/provenance mismatch blocked.                                        |
| **Signing key drill**                 | Quarterly and after key-service change    | Unauthorized use blocked; rotation/revocation and impact query succeed.              |
| **Reproducible build check**          | Critical release types on schedule        | Independent build matches digest or approved equivalence.                            |
| **Emergency release exercise**        | Semiannual                                | Rapid controlled release, rollback and reconciliation complete.                      |
| **Deployment target escape test**     | Each controller/policy change             | Unauthorized tenant/region/environment target rejected.                              |
| **AI coding assistant test**          | Each route/model/policy change            | Secrets, restricted input and autonomous merge/deploy requests blocked.              |
| **Release-to-runtime reconciliation** | Each release and continuous               | Running digest/configuration matches approved manifest.                              |
| **Provider continuity exercise**      | Annual and material provider change       | Source/build/artifact/signing/deploy recovery or controlled alternate path verified. |
| **Access / SoD recertification**      | Quarterly and role change                 | No incompatible privilege combination or expired contractor access.                  |

# 35 \| Metrics, Thresholds and Control Objectives

| **Metric**                            | **Definition**                                              | **Control objective**                     |
|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **protected_merge_bypass**            | Protected changes entering without required policy/review   | 0                                         |
| **artifact_provenance_coverage**      | Released digests with accepted provenance                   | 100%                                      |
| **artifact_signature_coverage**       | Released digests with valid approved signature              | 100%                                      |
| **release_manifest_completeness**     | Production releases with all required bindings/approvals    | 100%                                      |
| **runtime_release_reconciliation**    | Running production workloads matching approved manifest     | 100%; discrepancies page/incident         |
| **secret_detection_escape**           | Confirmed secrets reaching protected source/artifact/log    | 0                                         |
| **critical_dependency_exception_age** | Age of unresolved critical/unsupported dependency exception | Within approved expiry; overdue = blocker |
| **change_failure_rate**               | Production changes causing rollback/incident/customer harm  | Trend and threshold by change class       |
| **rollback_readiness**                | Releases with tested rollback or approved forward-fix plan  | 100% CH-2+                                |
| **approval_staleness_rejection**      | Stale approvals invalidated after material change           | 100%                                      |
| **emergency_reconciliation_time**     | Emergency changes reconciled to normal controls             | Within approved incident target           |
| **ai_generated_code_defect_rate**     | Security/quality defects associated with approved AI use    | Monitored; threshold per use case         |
| **pipeline_availability**             | Eligible delivery operations completed within SLO           | Per R19; no bypass when unavailable       |
| **release_evidence_latency**          | Deployment completion to complete evidence package          | Within defined target                     |

# 36 \| Workstream Handoff, Definition of Ready and Definition of Done

## 36.1 Definition of Ready

| **Ready criterion**    | **Required evidence**                                                                          |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authority**          | Approved requirement/defect/risk/incident and current architecture/ADR context.                |
| **Ownership**          | Repository, code owners, delivery owner, reviewers and release authority identified.           |
| **Change class**       | Risk classification and required gate set determined.                                          |
| **Design**             | Interfaces, data, tenancy, evidence, AI, security, migration and observability impact defined. |
| **Test plan**          | Positive, negative, failure, compatibility, rollback and acceptance tests identified.          |
| **Dependencies**       | Approved/pinned components and provider implications assessed.                                 |
| **Rollout / rollback** | Target, cohort, pause, rollback/forward fix and customer communication defined.                |
| **Access**             | Required repository/environment access granted; no unnecessary production privilege.           |

## 36.2 Definition of Done

| **Done criterion** | **Required evidence**                                                                   |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source**         | Protected merge, independent review, owners and traceability complete.                  |
| **Build**          | Trusted runner, pinned inputs, SBOM/provenance, immutable digest and signature.         |
| **Verification**   | All applicable quality/security/privacy/AI/evidence/reliability/cost gates pass.        |
| **Exceptions**     | Specific, approved, time-bound and visible to release authority.                        |
| **Release**        | Complete manifest, approvals, customer impact and rollback.                             |
| **Deployment**     | Controlled rollout, observed health, no unreconciled drift.                             |
| **Documentation**  | Runbooks, APIs/schemas, release notes, limitations and support material current.        |
| **Closure**        | Runtime reconciliation and release evidence recorded; temporary flag/change has expiry. |

# 37 \| Approval Gates, Decisions and Controlled Annexes

| **Gate**                                    | **Minimum CI/CD and supply-chain evidence**                                                                                                                              |
|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **G0 Build Authorization**                  | Repository classes/owners; protected source; trusted build design; dependency policy; secret controls; test strategy; provenance/signing design; SoD and risk owners.    |
| **G1 Design-Partner Readiness**             | End-to-end signed release to staging/production canary; SBOM/provenance verification; rollback; release evidence; access review; emergency workflow rehearsal.           |
| **G2 Commercial GA**                        | Measured pipeline SLOs; production reconciliation; security exercises; provider continuity; release communications; artifact retention; recurring assurance cadence.     |
| **G3 Enterprise/Sector Scale**              | Dedicated/regulated delivery requirements, stronger customer evidence, extended retention, key/residency controls and enterprise change procedures.                      |
| **G4 Sovereign/OT/Critical Infrastructure** | Customer/private build and update model, offline verification, restricted supply chain, sovereign key/custody, manual continuity and separate threat/acceptance package. |

## 37.1 Open decisions required before approval

| **Decision**                               | **Owner**                | **Default if unresolved**                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source-control and repository platform** | CTO / Developer Platform | Use approved enterprise platform with SSO, protected branches, audit export and organization policy.                  |
| **CI runner model**                        | Platform / Security      | Ephemeral managed/self-hosted isolated runners; no shared persistent production runner.                               |
| **Artifact and package registry**          | Platform / Security      | Private immutable registry/mirror with digest, retention, audit and recovery.                                         |
| **Provenance/signing stack**               | Security / Platform      | Standards-based attestations and HSM/KMS-backed signing with independent verification.                                |
| **AI coding tools**                        | AI Risk / Security       | No production-source use until provider, data and route approved in AI Register.                                      |
| **Commit/merge signing scope**             | Security / Engineering   | Mandatory for release-critical/crown-jewel repos; expand based on operational evidence.                               |
| **Emergency authority**                    | CTO / CISO / SRE         | Named incident commander + independent Security/Release approver.                                                     |
| **Pipeline SLOs and retention**            | SRE / Legal / Compliance | Internal objectives only until measured and approved; retain release reconstruction evidence for supported lifecycle. |

# 00 \| Document Authority, Ownership and Required Artifacts

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image60.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image97.png" />

***Figure 1 - Infrastructure authority and release-evidence hierarchy.***

| **Authority layer**     | **Authoritative artifact**                                                                    | **Owner**                    | **Engineering consequence**                                                                              |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Product / service**   | Approved release scope, deployment class, service tier, customer obligation and exclusions    | Product / Service Operations | Infrastructure does not implement unapproved commitments or speculative topology.                        |
| **Architecture**        | Regional-cell model, bounded global plane, modules, trust boundaries, ADRs and data authority | Chief Architect              | Topology and dependency direction are decided before provisioning.                                       |
| **Security / privacy**  | Identity, network, key, tenancy, residency, logging, retention and recovery controls          | CISO / Privacy               | A resource cannot be accepted because it is convenient if it violates isolation or processing authority. |

| **Runtime truth**       | Inventory, health, drift, capacity, cost, backup, restore and security telemetry              | SRE / FinOps / Security      | Observed state must reconcile to approved desired state.                                                 |
| **Release / assurance** | Readiness decision, tests, exceptions, risk, rollback, customer-impact and evidence           | Release Authority            | A release is authorized by evidence, not by completion claims.                                           |

## 00.1 Mandatory controlled artifacts

| **Artifact**                       | **Minimum controlled content**                                                                           | **Source of truth**                |
|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Environment catalog**            | Purpose, owner, class, data eligibility, identity boundary, regions, lifecycle, access and SLO tier      | Environment Registry               |
| **Cloud hierarchy**                | Organization/account/project structure, ownership, billing, policy inheritance and separation boundaries | Infrastructure Architecture / ADR  |
| **Regional-cell blueprint**        | Edge, core, satellites, data services, operations, dependencies, failure domains and capacity            | C1/H1 blueprint repository         |
| **Network and route catalog**      | Ingress, egress, DNS, service, data and management paths with owners and policy                          | Network Policy Repository          |
| **Infrastructure modules**         | Versioned IaC modules, tests, provider constraints, inputs, outputs, migration and ownership             | Source repository / module catalog |
| **Release configuration manifest** | Artifact digests, schemas, policies, config, infrastructure revision, regions and rollout                | R20 Release Evidence Register      |
| **Runtime inventory**              | Actual resources, versions, ownership, tenancy, region, drift and health                                 | Cloud inventory / CMDB view        |
| **Recovery package**               | Backups, manifests, runbooks, credentials references, restore tests, RTO/RPO and reconciliation          | BCDR repository / R20              |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                              | **Why it fails a Tier-1 review**                                                                        | **Refinement incorporated**                                                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **“Cloud architecture” without environment contracts**   | Resources drift by team and purpose; production and non-production assumptions become implicit.         | Every environment is a machine-readable contract with owner, data eligibility, identities, topology, SLO and lifecycle.  |
| **Provider product names treated as architecture**       | Creates lock-in, hides capability requirements and allows vendor defaults to become security decisions. | Define provider-neutral capabilities; map chosen services through ADRs and an approved capability matrix.                |
| **Regional cell named but not operationally decomposed** | No clear failure, deployment, data or cost boundary.                                                    | Cell blueprint specifies edge, core, four satellites, data services, operations, capacity and recovery responsibilities. |
| **IaC described but manual changes tolerated**           | Runtime truth diverges from code and audit evidence becomes unreliable.                                 | Console-only drift is an incident; emergency changes must be reconciled to code and release evidence.                    |
| **Deployment separated from configuration and schema**   | Artifact, policy, schema and infrastructure versions can mismatch.                                      | One immutable release manifest binds all deployable and configuration authorities.                                       |
| **High availability confused with disaster recovery**    | Multi-zone uptime does not prove regional loss recovery or integrity.                                   | Availability, backup, restore, replay, failover and trust reconciliation are separate tested capabilities.               |
| **Autoscaling without tenant quotas or economics**       | One source can starve the fleet or destroy margin.                                                      | Capacity, admission, fair use, backpressure and unit-cost controls are release-blocking.                                 |
| **AI infrastructure treated as ordinary outbound HTTP**  | Ignores data routing, prompt injection, provider terms, tool authority and spend attacks.               | Regional AI gateway, provider egress zone, tenant-isolated retrieval/memory, budgets and granular kill controls.         |
| **Management plane insufficiently isolated**             | A compromised engineer or CI path can become a fleet-wide event.                                        | Separate management identities, projects, routes, JIT access, recorded sessions, policy and independent audit.           |
| **Recovery declared complete at traffic restoration**    | Corrupted, cross-tenant or divergent evidence state can be reintroduced.                                | Re-enable requires data, tenant, identity, key, evidence and release-manifest reconciliation.                            |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Explicit Exclusions

| **In scope**                                                                                                                                                            | **Out of scope / separate authority**                                                                                    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cloud organization, environment classes, regional cells, network, compute, data services, messaging, secrets, observability, deployment, resilience, capacity and cost. | Provider procurement, commercial negotiation, customer-specific private architecture and sovereign commitment approval.  |
| Infrastructure contracts, IaC modules, policy, GitOps, release manifests, runtime inventory, drift, backup, restore and operational views.                              | Application-domain behavior, detection content, evidence semantics, AI decision rights and API/event contract ownership. |
| G0-G2 pooled and enhanced deployment foundations and design patterns for later dedicated/sovereign tiers.                                                               | Automatic authorization to build T3/T4, OT, on-premises or air-gapped deployments.                                       |
| Technical controls required by security, privacy, evidence, AI, managed response and service objectives.                                                                | Production credentials, private keys, exact network addresses and emergency access procedures in the general document.   |

# 04 \| Binding Infrastructure and Deployment Invariants

| **ID**     | **Invariant**                             | **Binding consequence**                                                                                                                    |
|------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **INF-01** | Infrastructure is code                    | Production resources and material configuration originate from reviewed, versioned, testable code and policy.                              |
| **INF-02** | Regional cell is the operational boundary | Customer telemetry and evidence remain within the approved cell unless an explicit transfer policy permits otherwise.                      |
| **INF-03** | Global plane is bounded                   | No raw telemetry, evidence content, customer secret or unrestricted personal data in global services.                                      |
| **INF-04** | Immutable promotion                       | Artifacts, schemas, policies, configuration and infrastructure revisions are promoted by digest/version, never rebuilt or edited in place. |
| **INF-05** | Environment independence                  | Identity, keys, data, routes and access do not cross environments by default.                                                              |
| **INF-06** | No standing privilege                     | Human production access is JIT, purpose-bound, approved, logged and time-limited.                                                          |
| **INF-07** | Default deny                              | Network, egress, identity, admission, data and deployment policies deny unapproved behavior.                                               |
| **INF-08** | No hidden single point                    | Every critical dependency has an explicit failure mode, owner, detection and recovery strategy.                                            |
| **INF-09** | Failure is visible                        | Degradation never renders as healthy; coverage, SLO, evidence and customer impact are explicit.                                            |
| **INF-10** | Restore before promise                    | RTO/RPO and regional recovery claims require repeated measured restore/failover evidence.                                                  |
| **INF-11** | Economics are architecture                | Capacity, retention, provider egress, AI and data costs are designed and release-gated.                                                    |
| **INF-12** | No LLM critical path                      | Core access, evidence, entitlement, detection transport and response authorization continue without AI providers.                          |
| **INF-13** | Tenant isolation at every store           | Database, object, search, cache, queue, telemetry, AI, backup and support paths enforce tenant context.                                    |
| **INF-14** | Customer action trust is independent      | Action commands are signed, verified customer-side and not executable solely because the Zoiko cloud requests them.                        |
| **INF-15** | Runtime truth reconciles to desired state | Unexplained drift, unknown ownership or unmanaged resources are defects.                                                                   |
| **INF-16** | Every deployment is reversible or bounded | A rollback, compensating action or controlled forward-fix exists before promotion.                                                         |
| **INF-17** | Evidence survives platform failure        | Audit packages and cryptographic proofs remain verifiable independently of platform availability.                                          |
| **INF-18** | Scope follows gates                       | Dedicated, sovereign, OT and private deployments require separate team, cost, threat, operations and acceptance gates.                     |

# 05 \| Environment Taxonomy and Promotion Boundaries

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image61.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image98.png" />

***Figure 2 - Environment and promotion boundary model.***

| **Environment**      | **Purpose**                                                    | **Data / access rule**                                                          | **Lifecycle / gate**                                      |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **LOCAL**            | Developer build, unit tests and isolated component work.       | Synthetic data; no production route, credentials or trust roots.                | Developer-controlled within approved tooling; disposable. |
| **PREVIEW**          | Per-change integration and UX/API verification.                | Synthetic seeded tenant; no standing secret; internet exposure bounded.         | Automatic create/destroy; hard TTL.                       |
| **DEV**              | Shared feature integration and engineering validation.         | Synthetic or approved masked fixtures; non-production identity and keys.        | Continuously reconciled; not release evidence by itself.  |
| **INT**              | Cross-service, contract, connector and migration tests.        | Representative synthetic datasets and test provider accounts.                   | Release candidate begins contract evidence.               |
| **SEC/PERF**         | Adversarial, scale, chaos, restore and tenant-isolation tests. | Synthetic/high-volume generated data; isolated egress and cost ceiling.         | Time-bounded test campaign; destructive tests permitted.  |
| **STAGE**            | Production-equivalent topology and promotion process.          | No routine customer data; production-like policies with separate keys/accounts. | Required G1/G2 rehearsal and soak.                        |
| **PROD**             | Customer contractual operation in approved regional cells.     | Customer data and production identities; strict change/access controls.         | Continuous operation; only approved releases.             |
| **RECOVERY**         | Regional continuity, restore and failover capability.          | Encrypted replicated/backup data under residency and key policy.                | Exercised on schedule; not assumed ready.                 |
| **SYNTHETIC CANARY** | Zoiko-owned tenant exercising full production paths.           | Non-customer synthetic data; no privileged bypass.                              | Receives release first; continuous control checks.        |
