<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>ENVIRONMENT RULE</strong></p>
<p>Production data must not be copied to lower environments merely to make testing easier. Where a production defect cannot be reproduced synthetically, use controlled production diagnostics or an exceptional, minimized, time-bounded dataset workflow with Privacy and Security approval.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 06 \| Cloud Organization, Accounts, Projects and Ownership

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image62.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image99.png" />

***Figure 3 - Cloud organization and account / subscription / project hierarchy.***

| **Boundary**                        | **Minimum requirement**                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Enterprise root**                 | Named legal owner, protected root credentials, billing authority, organization policy and break-glass custody.                                    |
| **Security/audit**                  | Independent log archive, security telemetry, evidence access and investigation capability not administered solely by application teams.           |
| **Build/artifacts**                 | Separate builders, mirrors and registries; no production runtime role; signed provenance and artifact promotion.                                  |
| **Regional production**             | Separate accounts/projects by region and material trust boundary; no broad cross-region administrative role.                                      |
| **Action/evidence sensitive zones** | Independent policy, identity and key custody for action broker and evidence anchoring where required by threat model.                             |
| **Non-production**                  | No inherited production credentials, data routes or trust roots; separate budgets and policy.                                                     |
| **Recovery**                        | Separate enough to survive primary account/project compromise; tested administration and key access.                                              |
| **Ownership**                       | Every account/project/resource has owner, cost center, environment, region, data class, criticality, repository and lifecycle tags.               |
| **Guardrails**                      | Organization-level restrictions for regions, public exposure, root use, identity, logging, encryption, service eligibility and resource creation. |
| **Unknown resources**               | Unowned or untagged production resource is quarantined or escalated; it cannot remain an accepted permanent state.                                |

# 07 \| Regional Cells and Bounded Global Control Plane

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image63.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image100.png" />

***Figure 4 - Reference regional-cell deployment architecture.***

| **Plane**                  | **May contain**                                                                                                                            | **Must not contain**                                                                                                       |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Global control plane**   | Tenant directory, catalog metadata, approved entitlement/config policy, deployment inventory, feature policy and bounded aggregate health. | Raw telemetry, evidence content, customer secrets, unrestricted personal data, broad search index or response credentials. |
| **Regional cell**          | Tenant/customer APIs, ingestion, detections, cases, controls, evidence, AI context, action workflows and regional data services.           | Another region’s tenant data unless explicit transfer/failover authority exists.                                           |
| **Cross-region channel**   | Signed configuration, deployment metadata, bounded health, encrypted recovery transfer and approved customer routing.                      | Implicit replication, unrestricted support queries or hidden global analytics copy.                                        |
| **Dedicated tenant plane** | Contracted tenant-isolated compute/data/key boundary.                                                                                      | Unreviewed forks of product code or parallel operational stack.                                                            |
| **External witness**       | Signed roots/proofs required for independent verification.                                                                                 | Customer evidence content or credentials.                                                                                  |

# 08 \| Edge, Network, DNS, Ingress and Egress Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image64.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image101.png" />

***Figure 5 - Network, ingress, east-west and egress architecture.***

| **Layer**              | **Required controls**                                                                                                        | **Failure behavior**                                            |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **DNS / certificates** | Controlled zones, automated issuance/rotation, DNSSEC where applicable, no ad hoc records and expiry monitoring.             | Fail closed for identity-sensitive routes; alert before expiry. |
| **Internet edge**      | DDoS/WAF, TLS, bot/rate controls, request limits, origin protection and approved geographies.                                | Rate/deny/degrade without exposing origin.                      |
| **Regional gateways**  | Separate customer API, ingestion/webhook and administration routes; auth, tenant, schema, replay and quota controls.         | Reject/quarantine invalid traffic; preserve core availability.  |
| **East-west**          | Workload identity, mTLS, method authorization, default deny, explicit dependencies and timeouts.                             | No permit-on-policy-failure.                                    |
| **Data access**        | Private endpoints, service identity, tenant/purpose binding and no public data-service access.                               | Deny and alert; never fall back to broad credential.            |
| **Egress**             | Destination allowlist, DNS control, gateway/proxy, provider/region/data policy, malware/exfiltration monitoring and budgets. | Block unapproved destination; no automatic alternate provider.  |
| **Management**         | Separate access path, JIT, managed device, recorded session, case/change reference and dual control for critical work.       | No direct internet or standing engineer access.                 |
| **Network evidence**   | Policy version, route inventory, flow logs, denied attempts and change history retained.                                     | Missing required logs is a control degradation.                 |

# 09 \| Management Plane, Administrative Access and Remote Operations

| **Control area**    | **Mandatory design**                                                                                                         |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**        | Separate privileged identity; phishing-resistant MFA; managed device; no shared account.                                     |
| **Access**          | JIT, purpose/ticket/case-bound, approved, time-limited and environment/resource scoped.                                      |
| **Path**            | Zero-trust/bastion-class controlled path; no direct public administrative endpoint where avoidable.                          |
| **Session**         | Recorded or command-audited for privileged work; clipboard/file transfer restricted by class.                                |
| **Production data** | Masked and minimized by default; no routine shell/database browsing; approved query workflow.                                |
| **Emergency**       | Separate break-glass identity and credential, dual control for high-impact scope, immediate alert and mandatory review.      |
| **Automation**      | Operational automation uses workload identity and policy, not an engineer’s personal credentials.                            |
| **Contractors**     | Assignment and contract-expiry-bound access; no inherited standing production role.                                          |
| **Offboarding**     | Immediate session/token/role revocation; ownership and active approvals reassigned; evidence reconciled.                     |
| **Monitoring**      | Privilege grants, use, denials, data access, configuration changes and break-glass activity feed independent security audit. |

| **Workload class**          | **Isolation / scaling requirement**                                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **shield-core**             | Stable latency, multi-zone replicas, transactional dependency protection, bounded concurrency and no direct customer-estate credentials. |
| **shield-ingest**           | Burst/throughput scaling, per-source/tenant quotas, queue isolation, parser sandboxing and backpressure.                                 |
| **shield-ai-gateway**       | Restricted provider egress, per-tenant budgets, model/request telemetry, retrieval isolation and independent kill.                       |

| **Batch / replay**          | Separate quotas and scheduling; cannot starve real-time detection, ingestion or customer APIs.                                           |
| **Operational controllers** | Restricted system pools, signed images, least privilege and independent availability monitoring.                                         |
| **Sensitive jobs**          | Dedicated node/pool/account where key, evidence, customer export or isolation risk requires it.                                          |
| **Ephemeral debug**         | Time-limited, approved and removed; production images remain shell-minimized and immutable.                                              |
| **Placement controls**      | Affinity/anti-affinity, topology spread, disruption budgets, tolerations and region/zone constraints are code-reviewed.                  |

# 11 \| Runtime Identity, Secrets, Certificates and Configuration

| **Object**                | **Required contract**                                                                                                            |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Workload identity**     | Short-lived, audience/purpose bound, environment/region specific and automatically rotated.                                      |
| **Service authorization** | Identity alone is insufficient; method/resource/tenant/purpose policy is enforced at target.                                     |
| **Secrets**               | Created and stored in approved vault; runtime-brokered; no source, image, log, document, ticket or prompt exposure.              |
| **Certificates**          | Automated issuance, renewal, revocation and expiry monitoring; trust stores versioned and minimized.                             |
| **Configuration**         | Typed, schema-validated, versioned, reviewed and environment-specific; sensitive values referenced, not embedded.                |
| **Feature policy**        | Signed, scoped by environment/tenant/region, safely defaulted and included in release/runtime evidence.                          |
| **Key access**            | Purpose/tenant/context bound; HSM/KMS policy; high-value operations dual-controlled where required.                              |
| **Rotation**              | Tested without broad outage; consuming services expose version and health; failure never causes plaintext fallback.              |
| **Revocation**            | Rapid propagation target; affected sessions/artifacts/commands assessed and recorded.                                            |
| **Inventory**             | Every secret, certificate, identity and configuration object has owner, purpose, consumers, expiry and last-use/health metadata. |

# 12 \| Data Services, Storage Authority and Durability

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image66.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image103.png" />

***Figure 7 - Regional data-service authority and durability architecture.***

| **Store**              | **Authority / durability rule**                                                               | **Failure / recovery rule**                                                      |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Relational**         | System of record for declared domains; multi-zone; tenant keys and transactional constraints. | Restore + event/outbox reconciliation; no silent stale promotion.                |
| **Event backbone**     | Durable accepted event transport and replay manifest; not business source of truth.           | Replay idempotently; response actions and evidence conclusions cannot duplicate. |
| **Lakehouse/object**   | Raw/normalized telemetry, long-term analytics and replay in open formats.                     | Lifecycle and manifest validation; corruption/quarantine explicit.               |
| **Search/analytics**   | Derived hot query/detection projection with bounded query/resource policies.                  | Rebuild from authority; search loss cannot destroy ingestion.                    |
| **Evidence vault**     | Content hash, tenant context, encryption, WORM/object lock by policy and ledger linkage.      | Restore/verify against chain and anchors before trust.                           |
| **Cache/coordination** | Non-authoritative; tenant-namespaced; loss tolerated.                                         | Rebuild; never infer durable success from cache.                                 |
| **Observability**      | Operational/security evidence with data-minimization and access controls.                     | Buffer/degrade; missing audit stream may block sensitive changes.                |
| **Backup/archive**     | Encrypted, access-separated, immutable where required, region/key/purpose aware.              | Regular restore tests and deletion/hold reconciliation.                          |

# 13 \| Messaging, Ingestion, Queues, Backpressure and Replay

| **Control**                  | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                          |
|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Durable acceptance**       | Acknowledge only after required durable boundary; acceptance SLI defined per channel.                                |
| **Partitioning**             | Tenant/source/order key selected to preserve required ordering without creating fleet-wide hot partitions.           |
| **Quotas**                   | Per tenant, source, connector, event type and plan; global emergency ceilings separate from commercial entitlements. |
| **Backpressure**             | Bounded queues, producer signals, source throttling, priority classes and customer-visible degradation.              |
| **Dead letter / quarantine** | Reason, payload reference, schema/permission state, owner, retry policy and expiry; never silent drop.               |
| **Replay**                   | Manifested range, source, versions, purpose, approver and idempotency; no duplicate response/action/evidence effect. |
| **Late data**                | Rule-declared watermark/window behavior; monitoring for completeness impact and replay need.                         |
| **Poison messages**          | Parser isolation, bounded retry, quarantine and no queue starvation.                                                 |
| **Cross-region**             | No implicit replication of customer event content; recovery/transfer path explicitly approved.                       |
| **Cost**                     | Events, bytes, retention, egress and replay attributed; unbounded retry/replay blocked by policy.                    |

# 14 \| Evidence Ledger, Vault, Anchoring and Verifier Infrastructure

| **Component**           | **Infrastructure requirement**                                                                                         |
|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Evidence metadata**   | Transactional durability, immutable versioning and tenant/region binding.                                              |
| **Content vault**       | Content-addressed encrypted object storage, WORM/object lock by policy, retention/hold and independent access logging. |
| **Tenant chain writer** | Strict sequence ownership, idempotent append, signed collector/evaluator context and explicit failure state.           |
| **Merkle aggregation**  | Deterministic root construction over tenant heads with retained inclusion proofs.                                      |
| **Anchoring signer**    | Separate identity/key/purpose, HSM/KMS-backed, narrow queue access and no general application role.                    |
| **External witnesses**  | At least two independent publication paths where approved; retry and split-view detection.                             |
| **Verifier artifacts**  | Open, signed, reproducibly built CLI/library/package instructions and public root retrieval.                           |
| **Restore**             | Reconcile database, vault, chain heads, roots and witnesses; divergence is an integrity incident.                      |
| **Availability**        | Evidence collection may queue, but integrity must never be weakened to maintain apparent availability.                 |
| **Customer export**     | Package/proof generation isolated, rate-limited, manifest-signed and independently verifiable after offboarding.       |

# 16 \| Action-Broker Infrastructure and Customer Command Trust

| **Control**               | **Infrastructure requirement**                                                                                     |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| **Command queue**         | Tenant/action partition, expiry, nonce, priority, rate and freeze semantics; no unbounded global queue.            |
| **Policy decision**       | Current tenant policy, authority R0-R4, approvals, target state, action class, ceilings and rollback verified.     |
| **Signing**               | Per-tenant/purpose signing under KMS/HSM policy; no bulk export of private keys.                                   |
| **Customer verification** | Customer-side integration verifies signature, nonce, expiry, tenant, allowlist and local policy before execution.  |
| **Credentials**           | Customer credentials remain tenant-scoped and action-specific; broker cannot browse customer estate generally.     |
| **Receipts**              | Transport receipt, execution receipt and observed-state reconciliation separately recorded.                        |
| **Freeze**                | Tenant, connector, action type, region and global freeze; out-of-band dual control for critical global freeze.     |
| **Recovery**              | Queue purge/reconciliation, key revocation, replay prohibition for expired actions and controlled reauthorization. |
| **Scale**                 | Mass-action ceilings and concurrency independent of customer entitlement; breach opens security incident.          |

# 18 \| Infrastructure-as-Code, Policy-as-Code, GitOps and Drift

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image69.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image106.png" />

***Figure 10 - Infrastructure-as-code and GitOps control lifecycle.***

| **Control**       | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                                       |
|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Modules**       | Versioned, owned, documented inputs/outputs, least-privilege defaults, tests, examples and migration notes.                     |
| **State**         | Encrypted, access-controlled, locked, backed up and separated by environment/region; no personal state files.                   |
| **Plans**         | Machine and human review of resource, route, identity, data, cost and replacement impact.                                       |
| **Policies**      | Organization, network, admission, encryption, region, tagging, identity and service-eligibility controls execute automatically. |
| **GitOps**        | Desired state reconciled by workload identity; no broad personal production credential in pipeline.                             |
| **Drift**         | Continuous inventory comparison; classify authorized transient, emergency, provider-managed or unauthorized drift.              |
| **Manual change** | Prohibited except emergency procedure; creates incident/change record and mandatory code reconciliation.                        |
| **Destruction**   | Protected resources require explicit approval, retention/hold check, backup/export verification and blast-radius preview.       |
| **Secrets**       | Only references and policy; secret values never in state/plan/output where avoidable.                                           |
| **Evidence**      | Plan, approvals, apply identity, outputs, tests, inventory and drift result retained in release evidence.                       |

# 19 \| CI/CD Handoff, Environment Promotion and Deployment Strategies

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image70.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image107.png" />

***Figure 11 - Artifact and configuration promotion flow.***

| **Strategy**                   | **Permitted use**                                                               | **Required safeguards**                                                                                |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Rolling**                    | Low-risk stateless changes with strong compatibility.                           | Health gates, surge/unavailable limits, rollback and mixed-version contract.                           |
| **Canary**                     | Default for material application/config/policy changes.                         | Synthetic tenant first, small tenant/cell cohort, SLO/control checks and automatic halt.               |
| **Blue/green**                 | High rollback-value application or platform changes.                            | Data/schema compatibility, traffic cutover controls, dual-run cost and stale-environment expiry.       |
| **Shadow**                     | Detection, AI route, query or pipeline evaluation without authoritative effect. | No customer action/claim, data policy, cost ceiling and result isolation.                              |
| **Feature flag**               | Tenant/region/capability activation after code deploy.                          | Owner, safe default, expiry, dependency and audit; not a substitute for authorization.                 |
| **Schema expand/contract**     | Data/API/event evolution.                                                       | Backward compatibility, dual-read/write where approved, migration evidence and rollback path.          |
| **Emergency patch**            | Active security or severe incident only.                                        | Independent approval, bounded change, enhanced monitoring and immediate baseline reconciliation.       |
| **Infrastructure replacement** | Cluster/store/network/provider migration.                                       | Parallel validation, data/integrity reconciliation, rollback/forward plan and customer-impact control. |

| **Release element**      | **Binding requirement**                                                                                |

| **Application artifact** | Content digest, source revision, builder identity, provenance, SBOM and signature.                     |
| **Container/base**       | Digest-pinned image and approved base/version; no mutable tag as authority.                            |
| **Infrastructure**       | IaC repository revision, module versions, provider constraints and applied plan ID.                    |
| **Configuration**        | Typed config bundle version, feature policy, route policy, limits and environment overlay.             |
| **Schemas/contracts**    | Database, event, API, webhook, connector, evidence and AI tool versions.                               |
| **Security policies**    | Authorization, network, admission, egress, key, signing, action and retention policy versions.         |
| **Data migrations**      | Migration IDs, checks, duration, rollback/forward plan and reconciliation result.                      |
| **Deployment**           | Environment, cell, cohort, approvers, timestamps, controller identity and observed health.             |
| **Rollback**             | Prior compatible manifest or approved forward-fix; state/data impact and maximum safe decision window. |
| **Evidence**             | One release record binds all elements and their verification output.                                   |

# 21 \| Availability, Dependency Isolation and Graceful Degradation

| **Dependency / failure**              | **Required behavior**                                                                                          |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Single zone loss**                  | Cell remains operational within approved capacity; no manual rebuild required.                                 |
| **Search unavailable**                | Ingestion and durable state continue; investigation/search degraded and visible.                               |
| **AI provider unavailable**           | Deterministic/human workflows continue; no unapproved provider routing.                                        |
| **ZoikoID control plane unavailable** | Bounded read for valid sessions if approved; privilege/action/config change denied.                            |
| **Event consumer failure**            | Durable backlog, isolated consumer, alerting and replay; producer/source not silently dropped.                 |
| **Connector failure**                 | Other tenants/sources continue; coverage marked incomplete; customer remediation visible.                      |
| **KMS/HSM unavailable**               | No plaintext or unsigned fallback; queue/block operations that require key use.                                |
| **Evidence witness unavailable**      | Queue signed roots, expose delay and retry; never fabricate publication.                                       |
| **Relational primary failure**        | Managed failover or controlled recovery with transaction/outbox reconciliation.                                |
| **Observability impairment**          | Critical service may continue only within defined blind-operation limits; high-risk changes/actions may block. |
| **Provider regional incident**        | Contain cell, protect integrity, invoke tested recovery/failover decision and communicate bounded impact.      |
| **Cost-control service failure**      | Hard quotas remain; no fail-open unlimited AI/query/ingestion use.                                             |

# 22 \| Backup, Restore, Disaster Recovery and Regional Failover

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image71.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image108.png" />

***Figure 12 - Resilience, restore and regional recovery lifecycle.***

| **Capability**        | **Minimum specification**                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Backup coverage**   | All authoritative data, critical configuration, IaC state, keys/cert references, registries and release manifests.                         |
| **Protection**        | Encryption, access separation, immutability where required, deletion/hold policy and malware/ransomware resistance.                        |
| **Restore order**     | Identity/policy/key dependencies, transactional state, event manifests, objects/evidence, indexes/projections, configuration and services. |
| **Reconciliation**    | Tenant counts/keys, outbox/inbox, event offsets, evidence chain/anchor, search rebuild, action queues and release manifest.                |
| **RPO/RTO**           | Defined by capability/tier in R19; not inferred from provider marketing or backup frequency alone.                                         |
| **Regional failover** | Residency/legal authority, capacity, DNS/routing, keys, customer contracts and data transfer path decided before activation.               |
| **Testing**           | Quarterly restore at minimum for critical systems; scheduled cell failover/region-loss exercise; destructive tests in isolated estate.     |
| **Evidence**          | Test inputs, timestamps, operators, automation, duration, loss, reconciliation, defects, CAPA and approval.                                |
| **Re-enable**         | Independent operational/security approval after invariants pass; traffic restoration alone is insufficient.                                |
| **Customer claims**   | Only measured and approved recovery capability appears in SLA/Trust Center/contract.                                                       |

# 24 \| FinOps, Cost Attribution and Unit-Economics Guardrails

| **Cost domain**          | **Required control**                                                                                                |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Attribution**          | Tenant, service, module, cell, region, connector, store, retention, query, egress, AI and environment tags/metrics. |
| **Budgets**              | Environment, team, product, tenant and provider budgets with forecasts, anomalies and accountable owner.            |
| **Ingestion**            | Fully loaded compute/storage/search/enrichment cost per contracted GB/day measured against approved ceiling.        |
| **Retention**            | Hot/warm/archive/evidence cost and margin by tier; lifecycle changes cannot silently reduce contracted coverage.    |
| **AI**                   | Per use case/tenant/provider/model/token/tool cost, hard cap and deterministic fallback.                            |
| **Search/query**         | Concurrency, scan, result, timeout and expensive-query controls; customer forecast before overage where applicable. |
| **Replay/backfill**      | Approval and cost estimate for material replay; separate from normal operating budget.                              |
| **Non-production**       | Automatic shutdown/TTL for ephemeral estates; production parity only where required by gate.                        |
| **Release gate**         | Infrastructure or application change breaching R19 economics blocks release without named exception.                |
| **Procurement feedback** | Measured utilization and exit cost inform provider commitments; discounts do not justify unportable architecture.   |

# 25 \| Residency, Data Routing, Dedicated and Sovereign Topologies

| **Topology**              | **Required architecture position**                                                                                  | **Authorization**                                                                    |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **T1 pooled regional**    | Shared regional cell with tenant isolation across all stores and paths.                                             | G1/G2 baseline.                                                                      |
| **T2 enhanced**           | Dedicated namespace/node pools/schema/index and tenant-dedicated key where contracted.                              | G2/G3 with capacity and operations evidence.                                         |
| **T3 dedicated**          | Dedicated cluster/data services/account under Zoiko management; optional BYOK.                                      | G3; contracted demand covers topology and team.                                      |
| **T4 sovereign/private**  | Customer cloud/on-premises, customer key custody, restricted operations and offline/update model.                   | G4 only; separate threat, support, recovery, supply-chain and certification package. |
| **Cross-region transfer** | Explicit policy based on tenant, data class, source/destination, purpose, legal mechanism, provider and key policy. | Fail closed if unmatched.                                                            |
| **Failover**              | Pre-approved residency/legal route and customer contract; no emergency invention of a transfer.                     | BCDR decision authority.                                                             |
| **Sector packs**          | Configuration, control, evidence and workflow overlays on one platform.                                             | No product fork or ungoverned infrastructure fork.                                   |

# 26 \| Non-Production Data, Ephemeral Environments and Test Estates

| **Area**                  | **Required rule**                                                                                        |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Test data**             | Synthetic by default; generated to exercise tenancy, privacy, edge cases, scale and regulated workflows. |
| **Masked data**           | Exceptional, approved, minimized, irreversible where feasible, purpose-bound and time-limited.           |
| **Secrets/accounts**      | Non-production credentials and provider test accounts; no production credential reuse.                   |
| **Ephemeral environment** | Created from approved blueprint, isolated, tagged, budgeted and automatically destroyed.                 |
| **Public exposure**       | Preview links authenticated/restricted where sensitive; no uncontrolled indexing or customer data.       |
| **Security test estate**  | Supports destructive, fuzz, abuse, chaos and compromised-component tests without production impact.      |
| **Performance estate**    | Representative topology and data volume; cost cap; no false extrapolation from undersized tests.         |
| **Synthetic tenant**      | Exercises full production path, alerts, cases, evidence, AI fallback and rollback without customer data. |
| **Cleanup**               | Data, objects, indexes, secrets, DNS, routes and provider artifacts verified deleted at expiry.          |
| **Evidence**              | Environment manifest, tests, results, exceptions and destruction receipt retained where gate-relevant.   |

# 27 \| Infrastructure Vulnerability, Patching and Configuration Management

| **Layer**                       | **Required control**                                                                                                             |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Managed services**            | Provider advisory monitoring, version policy, maintenance windows, unsupported-version prevention and exit plan.                 |
| **Orchestration/control plane** | Supported versions, upgrade rehearsal, skew policy, add-on compatibility and rollback.                                           |
| **Nodes/images**                | Immutable replacement, approved base, vulnerability scan, minimal packages and rapid rebuild.                                    |
| **Network/edge**                | Rule review, WAF/signature updates, certificate policy, exposed-service inventory and change evidence.                           |
| **IaC/modules**                 | Dependency/provider pinning, policy tests, module ownership, deprecation and migration.                                          |
| **Configuration**               | Benchmark/policy posture, drift detection, exception expiry and automated remediation where safe.                                |
| **Secrets/certificates**        | Rotation, weak/expired item detection, revocation and affected-service reconciliation.                                           |
| **Containers**                  | Image rebuild cadence, exploitability/reachability, emergency block and runtime control.                                         |
| **Prioritization**              | Internet exposure, tenant reach, privilege, evidence/action authority, exploit maturity and customer impact override base score. |
| **Verification**                | Patch/rebuild deployed, runtime inventory updated, exploit path retested and release/incident evidence closed.                   |

# 28 \| Infrastructure Incident, Emergency Change and Trust Re-Establishment

| **Phase**     | **Infrastructure actions**                                                                                                       |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Declare**   | Classify cell, tenant, provider, management, identity, key, data, action, evidence and customer impact.                          |
| **Contain**   | Freeze deployment/action, revoke identities/keys, isolate routes/accounts/workloads and preserve audit evidence.                 |
| **Stabilize** | Maintain safe core functions, explicit degradation and customer/operations communication.                                        |
| **Eradicate** | Rebuild from trusted source/artifact; rotate trust roots; remove unauthorized resources/configuration.                           |
| **Restore**   | Restore/replay according to dependency order; verify backups and manifests.                                                      |
| **Reconcile** | Desired/runtime state, tenant boundaries, data, event offsets, evidence anchors, action queues, identities and release manifest. |
| **Validate**  | Synthetic transactions, security tests, SLO/control health, customer-specific checks and independent review.                     |
| **Re-enable** | Named incident/release authority; staged traffic/action/deployment restoration.                                                  |
| **CAPA**      | Root cause, threat model, requirement, IaC/policy/test/runbook and training updates.                                             |
| **Claims**    | Assess SLA, Trust Center, audit and customer assurance implications before closure.                                              |

# 29 \| Infrastructure Failure States and Safe Degradation

| **State**                       | **Meaning**                                                             | **Required behavior**                                                       |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **INFRA_NOMINAL**               | Desired and runtime state reconcile; controls and dependencies healthy. | Normal operation within approved envelope.                                  |
| **DRIFT_DETECTED**              | Runtime differs from desired state.                                     | Classify, contain if material, reconcile or approve time-bound exception.   |
| **REGION_DEGRADED**             | Cell or critical regional dependency impaired.                          | Protect integrity, shed noncritical load, assess failover and notify.       |
| **ZONE_LOSS**                   | One availability zone unavailable.                                      | Remain operational within tested capacity; replace/rebalance automatically. |
| **CAPACITY_PRESSURE**           | Headroom or dependency limit below threshold.                           | Throttle/queue/shed by priority; no unbounded autoscale or hidden loss.     |
| **INGEST_BACKPRESSURE**         | Source volume exceeds safe processing.                                  | Durably queue/throttle; expose lag and coverage; protect other tenants.     |
| **IDENTITY_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE** | Current access decision cannot be established.                          | Sensitive path denied; bounded approved read only where designed.           |
| **KEY_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE**     | Required cryptographic operation unavailable.                           | Queue/block; no plaintext/unsigned fallback.                                |
| **AI_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE**     | Approved AI route unavailable.                                          | Deterministic/human fallback; no unapproved provider.                       |
| **SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE**          | Hot investigation/search unavailable.                                   | Ingestion and durable state continue; rebuild projection.                   |
| **EVIDENCE_ANCHOR_DELAYED**     | External witness publication delayed.                                   | Queue signed roots, display delay and retry; do not claim publication.      |
| **OBSERVABILITY_BLIND**         | Required telemetry missing/stale.                                       | Alert; block high-risk change/action if visibility prerequisite.            |
| **ACTION_FROZEN**               | Response commands disabled.                                             | Detection/case continue; proposals remain pending/denied with reason.       |
| **BACKUP_UNVERIFIED**           | Backup exists but restore/integrity not proven.                         | Do not count toward recovery claim; escalate and retest.                    |
| **RECOVERY_DIVERGENCE**         | Restored state conflicts with event/evidence/release authority.         | Declare integrity incident; do not silently promote.                        |
| **COST_GUARDRAIL_BREACH**       | Measured unit cost exceeds approved limit.                              | Block affected GA/release or apply approved exception and containment.      |
| **PRODUCTION_ACCESS_REVOKED**   | Operator identity/role no longer valid.                                 | Sessions and derived access terminated; actions reconciled.                 |
| **EMERGENCY_CHANGE_ACTIVE**     | Unplanned production change under incident authority.                   | Enhanced monitoring, time limit and mandatory code/baseline reconciliation. |

| **IV-23** | Infrastructure risk/exception view    | Risk, affected cells/releases, compensating control, owner, expiry and evidence.               |

## 31.1 Mandatory contract types

| **Contract**         | **Required dimensions**                                                                                 |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Environment**      | Purpose, class, owner, data, identity, region, services, SLO, recovery, access, cost and lifecycle.     |
| **Regional cell**    | Region, zones, edge, services, stores, capacity, dependencies, keys, operations and recovery.           |
| **Resource**         | Type, owner, environment, cell, tenant scope, authority, data, encryption, backup, IaC, drift and cost. |
| **Network route**    | Source/destination identity, protocol, data class, purpose, policy, owner, expiry and evidence.         |
| **Workload**         | Artifact, identity, permissions, resources, placement, network, secrets, SLO, health and owner.         |
| **Release manifest** | Artifacts, schemas, policies, config, IaC, environments, rollout, rollback, approvals and evidence.     |
| **Backup/recovery**  | Coverage, location, keys, retention, restore order, RPO/RTO, tests, reconciliation and defects.         |
| **Capacity**         | Demand dimensions, limits, headroom, burst, failover, quota, autoscaling, cost and benchmark result.    |
| **Exception**        | Scope, requirement, risk, compensating control, owner, expiry, affected releases and evidence.          |

# 32 \| Verification, Chaos, Restore and Release Evidence

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image73.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image110.png" />

***Figure 14 - Infrastructure requirement-to-runtime evidence trace.***

| **Verification layer**   | **Minimum scope**                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Static IaC/policy**    | Syntax, modules, prohibited services/regions, public exposure, encryption, identity, tagging, cost and destructive change. |
| **Plan/impact**          | Resource replacements, network/route changes, data/key impact, capacity, cost and rollback.                                |
| **Environment contract** | Data eligibility, identity boundary, services, SLO, access and lifecycle reconcile.                                        |
| **Deployment**           | Artifact/config/schema/policy/IaC binding, canary, health, audit events and rollback.                                      |
| **Tenant isolation**     | Cross-tenant negatives across compute, database, object, search, cache, queue, logs, AI, backup and support.               |
| **Security/adversarial** | Management-plane abuse, secret/key access, egress, supply chain, broker, connector and provider compromise.                |
| **Performance**          | Reference scale, burst, queue, zone loss, search, replay, package build and cost.                                          |
| **Chaos**                | Pod/node/zone/service/provider/identity/key/observability failure with explicit expected degradation.                      |
| **Backup/restore**       | Authoritative stores, event replay, evidence reconciliation, keys, release manifest and customer-facing readiness.         |
| **Regional failover**    | Routing, capacity, residency, keys, data, dependencies, customer impact and re-enable authority.                           |
| **Drift**                | Unauthorized/manual/provider drift detection and reconciliation drill.                                                     |
| **FinOps**               | Measured unit cost and headroom against R19 thresholds.                                                                    |
| **Evidence**             | All results attributable, reproducible, signed/approved and retained in R20.                                               |

# 33 \| Infrastructure Metrics, SLOs, Error Budgets and Thresholds

| **Metric**                       | **Definition / use**                                                                                                             |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **cell_service_availability**    | Successful eligible requests by regional cell and capability; source for internal SLO and contractual claim only after evidence. |
| **deployment_success_rate**      | Deployments completing required gates without rollback or control violation.                                                     |
| **rollback_start_seconds**       | Decision/trigger to rollback initiation for rollback-capable releases.                                                           |
| **drift_detection_latency**      | Runtime divergence to classified alert.                                                                                          |
| **unmanaged_resource_count**     | Production resources without approved desired-state authority; target zero.                                                      |
| **zone_loss_headroom**           | Capacity remaining after loss of one zone under reference load.                                                                  |
| **ingestion_acceptance_rate**    | Eligible authenticated events durably accepted.                                                                                  |
| **queue_lag / backlog_age**      | Per tenant/source/class backlog and oldest age.                                                                                  |
| **backup_coverage_rate**         | Authoritative assets with current protected backup and policy.                                                                   |
| **restore_test_success**         | Scheduled restore tests passing integrity and reconciliation.                                                                    |
| **measured_rpo / rto**           | Observed data loss and recovery time by capability/tier.                                                                         |
| **evidence_anchor_delay**        | Ledger root creation to independent witness publication.                                                                         |
| **secret_cert_expiry_risk**      | Items inside warning/critical windows.                                                                                           |
| **privileged_access_duration**   | JIT access duration, use and stale grants.                                                                                       |
| **ai_route_availability / cost** | Approved route availability, latency and spend by tenant/use case.                                                               |
| **unit_economics_headroom**      | Measured platform cost relative to approved ingestion/retention/AI guardrail.                                                    |
| **cost_forecast_variance**       | Forecast vs. actual by environment, region and service.                                                                          |
| **control_health_coverage**      | Critical infrastructure controls with current observable status.                                                                 |
| **error_budget_burn**            | Burn rate by capability and release impact.                                                                                      |
| **ephemeral_ttl_compliance**     | Preview/test environments destroyed by approved expiry.                                                                          |

Numeric targets are authoritative only in the SLO, Error-Budget, Scale-Envelope and Unit-Economics Register. This document defines measurement and gate behavior, not a competing value source.

# 34 \| Workstream Handoff, Definition of Ready and Definition of Done

## 34.1 Required workstream handoff package

| **Handoff item**      | **Minimum content**                                                                         |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Mandate**           | Release, environment, regional cell, capability, owner and explicit exclusions.             |
| **Requirements**      | Applicable IDs, SLO/cost constraints, data/residency, security and acceptance criteria.     |
| **Architecture**      | Cell/zone/network/data/dependency diagrams and approved ADRs.                               |
| **Contracts**         | Environment, resource, network, workload, release, capacity and recovery contracts.         |
| **Code and policy**   | Repositories, modules, owners, review rules, state, tests and deployment controller.        |
| **Access**            | Roles, JIT workflow, non-production access, EC-3 annex need and offboarding.                |
| **Verification**      | IaC/policy, security, performance, chaos, restore, failover and cost tests.                 |
| **Operations**        | SLIs, dashboards, alerts, runbooks, on-call, incident, maintenance and dependency contacts. |
| **Rollback/recovery** | Rollback manifest, data/schema impact, backup/restore and re-enable criteria.               |
| **Evidence**          | R20 location, required approvers, exceptions and gate checklist.                            |

## 34.2 Definition of Ready

- Environment and regional-cell scope are approved; no provider or region decision remains implicit.

- Applicable requirements, ADRs, data classes, residency, SLO, capacity and cost thresholds are current.

- Infrastructure modules, contracts, identities, policies and state locations are defined.

- Threat model and management/data/action/evidence boundaries are reviewed.

- Test, rollout, rollback, restore and operational-readiness plans exist.

- Required access is approved without granting unnecessary production privilege.

- Dependencies, provider limits, unresolved risks and exceptions are visible.

## 34.3 Definition of Done

- Infrastructure and policies are merged, signed/approved, versioned and reproducible.

- Desired state and runtime inventory reconcile with no unexplained production drift.

- Artifacts, configuration, schemas, policies and IaC are bound in the release manifest.

- Security, tenant-isolation, performance, capacity, chaos, restore and cost tests pass.

- SLIs, dashboards, alerts, runbooks, ownership and on-call handoff are operational.

- Rollback or bounded forward-fix has been rehearsed where material.

- All findings and exceptions have owner, severity, compensating control and expiry.

- Release Evidence Register contains approvals and machine-verifiable evidence.

- Customer-facing claims remain within measured capability.

# 35 \| Approval Gates, Decisions and Controlled Annexes

| **Gate**                                    | **Minimum infrastructure evidence**                                                                                                                                          |
|---------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **G0 Build Authorization**                  | Environment model, cloud hierarchy, regional-cell blueprint, network/identity/data boundaries, IaC/GitOps control, threat model, test strategy and Gate-0 ADR closure.       |
| **G1 Design-Partner Readiness**             | Production cell, staging parity, synthetic tenant, P0 integrations, evidence infrastructure, backup/restore, monitoring, access controls, scale and signed readiness review. |
| **G2 Commercial GA**                        | Measured SLOs/error budgets, 24/7 operations, canary/rollback, DR exercise, cost guardrails, independent security findings resolved and customer claims approved.            |
| **G3 Enterprise/Sector Scale**              | T2/T3 isolation, additional regions/providers, enterprise capacity, dedicated keys/data services, enhanced support and contracted economics.                                 |
| **G4 Sovereign/OT/Critical Infrastructure** | Customer/private topology, offline/update chain, customer key custody, restricted operations, sector threat model, recovery and certification package.                       |

## 35.1 Decisions required before approval

| **Decision**                    | **Required result**                                                               |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Primary cloud/provider**      | ADR with capability, security, portability, operations, cost and exit analysis.   |
| **Initial regions**             | Legal entity, customer pipeline, residency, support and recovery decision.        |
| **Orchestration/runtime**       | Managed orchestration and workload identity approach.                             |
| **Event backbone**              | Managed Kafka-compatible or approved equivalent with replay/portability evidence. |
| **Hot analytics/search**        | Benchmark against reference scale and cost envelope.                              |
| **IaC/GitOps toolchain**        | Approved source, state, plan, policy, reconcile and evidence path.                |
| **Observability stack**         | Metrics/logs/traces/security audit, retention, tenancy and cost.                  |
| **Backup/DR design**            | RPO/RTO profiles, recovery region/account, keys, testing and customer claims.     |
| **AI provider connectivity**    | Approved providers, regions, data terms, egress and fallback.                     |
| **Production access**           | JIT platform, managed-device, session evidence, break-glass and offboarding.      |
| **Cost guardrails**             | R19 thresholds and exception authority.                                           |
| **Dedicated/sovereign roadmap** | Explicitly deferred or separately funded/gated.                                   |

# 36 \| Standards Alignment and Authoritative Reference Inputs

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                              | **Why it fails a Tier-1 review**                                                                        | **Refinement incorporated**                                                                                                            |
|----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Generic “best practice” language**                     | Cannot be tested, owned or defended; teams claim compliance while implementation differs.               | Every mandatory control maps to an enforcement point, failure state, test, owner and evidence.                                         |
| **Security mixed with infrastructure and CI/CD detail**  | Creates duplication with Documents 12-14 and leaves ownership unclear.                                  | This document defines platform-security invariants and handoffs; later documents specify deployment, pipeline and test implementation. |
| **Perimeter-centric design**                             | A multi-tenant remote-managed security platform is not protected by network location.                   | Continuous identity, device, workload, tenant, purpose and state decisions at every boundary.                                          |
| **Threat model treated as a one-time workshop**          | Drifts immediately as connectors, AI, response actions and cloud services change.                       | Threat models are versioned engineering inputs with automated fitness tests and change triggers.                                       |
| **Cryptography reduced to “encrypt at rest/in transit”** | Omits key separation, signing, independent verification, rotation, compromise and migration.            | Purpose-specific trust hierarchy, per-tenant context, short-lived identity and crypto-agility contracts.                               |
| **Vulnerability priority based only on CVSS**            | Under-prioritizes exposed, exploited or authority-bearing paths and over-prioritizes unreachable noise. | Risk model includes reachability, exploit maturity, privilege, tenant blast radius, action authority and active exploitation.          |
| **Supply-chain assurance ends at SBOM**                  | An SBOM does not prove source, build process, artifact integrity or approved deployment.                | Protected source, isolated build, provenance, signing, admission verification, staged release and revocation chain.                    |
| **AI security isolated in the AI document**              | Prompt injection and tool abuse cross into core, evidence and response systems.                         | AI security becomes a platform-security boundary with target-side authorization and kill controls.                                     |
| **Remote-team controls framed as distrust**              | Creates adversarial culture without improving security.                                                 | Compartmentalization, least privilege, managed endpoints, segregation of duties and auditable JIT access.                              |
| **Pen test used as final gate**                          | Late testing cannot compensate for missing design invariants or automation.                             | Design review, automated negative testing, continuous verification and independent adversarial assessment form one assurance stack.    |
| **Security logs treated as operational logs**            | May be mutable, incomplete, unscoped or unusable for incident reconstruction.                           | Material security events are separately governed, reconciled and evidence-preserved.                                                   |
| **Recovery defined as service availability**             | A compromised platform can return online with broken trust.                                             | Recovery requires identity, keys, tenant isolation, evidence, action authority and supply-chain integrity to be re-established.        |

# 02 \| Executive Platform-Security Mandate

ZoikoShield must be engineered as though a capable adversary will target the platform to reach multiple customer estates, alter assurance evidence, suppress detections or misuse response authority. The security model must therefore prevent standing trust, separate high-consequence capabilities, make cross-tenant access testably impossible, preserve independent proof and recover integrity after partial compromise.

| **Mandate**                           | **Binding outcome**                                                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Secure by design and default**      | Strong controls ship enabled; customers are not charged extra to obtain basic security; insecure compatibility modes require explicit exception.        |
| **Assume breach**                     | Compromise of one service, engineer, connector, provider or build step must not grant customer-estate command, cross-tenant access or evidence rewrite. |
| **Minimum privilege and time**        | Human/workload access is narrowly scoped, short-lived, purpose-bound, observable and revocable.                                                         |
| **Independent high-impact authority** | Core, AI and orchestration cannot self-authorize customer response actions, key release, risk acceptance or evidence truth.                             |
| **Cryptographic verifiability**       | Releases, evidence, commands, webhooks and attestations carry purpose-specific signatures and verifiable provenance.                                    |
| **Deterministic critical controls**   | Identity, authorization, tenant isolation, entitlement, evidence integrity and action approval do not depend on probabilistic AI.                       |
| **Explicit degraded behavior**        | Loss of identity, policy, key, evidence, connector, provider or monitoring capability does not silently become healthy operation.                       |
| **Security evidence before release**  | No material feature reaches production without mapped security requirements, tests, residual risk, rollback and monitoring evidence.                    |

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
