| Security observability requirements, metrics and release evidence.                                                                                                                                        | Complete SLO/error-budget and operational-runbook implementation - Document 15.                                  |
| Security-related experience states and admin/security views.                                                                                                                                              | Pixel-level experience contracts and screen wireframes - Document 16.                                            |
| Restricted implementation requirements for named engineers.                                                                                                                                               | Production credentials, private keys, customer secrets, active exploit chains and unrestricted red-team reports. |

# 04 \| Binding Security and Secure-Engineering Invariants

| **ID**          | **Invariant**                                       | **Engineering consequence**                                                                                            |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **SEC-INV-001** | Tenant context is mandatory                         | Every request, event, object, cache entry, index, trace, AI context and audit record carries validated tenant context. |
| **SEC-INV-002** | No standing customer-estate authority               | Core, analysts and AI hold no broad persistent credentials to execute response actions.                                |
| **SEC-INV-003** | Fail closed for privilege and action                | Identity, policy, key or approval uncertainty blocks privileged or external-change paths.                              |
| **SEC-INV-004** | No secret in code, prompt or document               | Secrets exist only in approved vaults and are referenced by identity/purpose.                                          |
| **SEC-INV-005** | Short-lived workload identity                       | Services authenticate using automatically rotated workload credentials, not static shared tokens.                      |
| **SEC-INV-006** | Object-level authorization everywhere               | Endpoint authentication never substitutes for object, property, function, purpose and state authorization.             |
| **SEC-INV-007** | No silent mutation                                  | Security-relevant state changes are versioned or represented by compensating records.                                  |
| **SEC-INV-008** | Independent action authorization                    | Response actions are reauthorized and signed outside core/AI/orchestrator control.                                     |
| **SEC-INV-009** | Evidence is not operational logging                 | Material evidence has integrity, provenance, retention and independent verification requirements.                      |
| **SEC-INV-010** | Artifact provenance before execution                | Only approved, signed artifacts with verified provenance and policy may deploy.                                        |
| **SEC-INV-011** | Default-deny network and egress                     | Connections exist only for explicit, current and observable purposes.                                                  |
| **SEC-INV-012** | Unsafe input is expected                            | External, customer, telemetry, file, retrieval and tool content is untrusted and bounded.                              |
| **SEC-INV-013** | Security failure is visible                         | Unknown, stale, degraded, denied and quarantined states are explicit and customer-visible where relevant.              |
| **SEC-INV-014** | Critical controls remain deterministic              | AI may assist but cannot become the authority for security-critical decisions.                                         |
| **SEC-INV-015** | One change cannot self-approve                      | Material code/config changes require independent review and release approval.                                          |
| **SEC-INV-016** | Security exception expires                          | Exceptions have owner, compensating control, expiry, test impact and release visibility.                               |
| **SEC-INV-017** | Recovery restores trust, not only uptime            | Keys, identities, isolation, evidence, artifacts and action authority are reconciled before full re-enable.            |
| **SEC-INV-018** | Customer-impacting security claims require evidence | Claims, certifications and test summaries are bounded to current verified scope.                                       |

# 05 \| Crown-Jewel Model, Threat Actors and Security Objectives

| **Crown jewel**                  | **Primary abuse**                                                                     | **Non-negotiable objective**                                                                             |
|----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant data and evidence**     | Cross-tenant disclosure, alteration, deletion or false completeness                   | Isolation, integrity, provenance, minimization, legal retention/deletion and independent verification.   |
| **Response authority**           | Mass isolation, account disablement, token revocation or destructive customer change  | Separate broker, per-action authorization/signing, customer verification, ceilings, receipts and freeze. |
| **Identity and privilege**       | Session theft, support impersonation, workload credential abuse or break-glass misuse | Phishing-resistant identity, JIT privilege, SoD, short-lived credentials and complete access evidence.   |
| **Build and release chain**      | Malicious commit, dependency, builder, artifact, registry or deployment policy        | Protected source, provenance, signing, verified admission, canary and revocation.                        |
| **Cryptographic roots and keys** | Forge evidence/commands/releases, decrypt data or block recovery                      | HSM/KMS custody, purpose separation, dual control, rotation, revocation and tested recovery.             |
| **Detection and case state**     | Suppress/alter alerts, close cases falsely or conceal data gaps                       | Versioning, approvals, immutable history, deterministic replay and audit reconciliation.                 |
| **AI gateway and tools**         | Prompt injection, cross-tenant retrieval, excessive agency or unsafe tool call        | Gateway-only access, isolation, target-side authorization, budgets, evaluations and kill switches.       |
| **Management plane**             | Take control of regions, observability, backups, identities or policy                 | Strong segmentation, JIT access, independent monitoring, immutable evidence and recovery isolation.      |

## 05.1 Threat actors and assumed capabilities

| **Actor**                                 | **Assumed capability**                                                                                          | **Design response**                                                                                               |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **External adversary**                    | Credential theft, API abuse, supply-chain exploitation, malware, DDoS, prompt injection and social engineering. | Identity/device/risk controls, bounded interfaces, default deny, rate limits, detection and incident containment. |
| **Compromised tenant**                    | Valid tenant credentials, malicious telemetry/files, API automation and attempts to reach other tenants.        | Strict tenant enforcement at every store and service; no trust based on customer legitimacy.                      |
| **Malicious or coerced insider**          | Legitimate knowledge, access requests, code changes or support pathways.                                        | JIT/SoD, session evidence, limited data visibility, two-person controls and independent audit.                    |
| **Compromised engineer endpoint/account** | Source access, dependency manipulation, pipeline attempts and secret theft.                                     | Managed endpoint, branch protections, isolated build, ephemeral credentials and release separation.               |
| **Compromised vendor/provider**           | Model, cloud, dependency, SaaS, identity or security-tool compromise.                                           | Provider isolation, least privilege, alternate paths, evidence, contractual notification and exit.                |
| **AI-mediated attacker**                  | Untrusted content influences models, retrieval, memory or tools.                                                | Prompt-injection defense, deterministic enforcement, capability limits, target authorization and kill.            |

# 06 \| Security Zones, Trust Boundaries and Blast-Radius Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image75.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image84.png" />

***Figure 2 - ZoikoShield security zones and blast-radius boundaries.***

| **Boundary**                                       | **Required controls**                                                                                                               | **Failure behavior**                                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **External/customer to edge**                      | TLS, source authentication, WAF/API schema, rate limits, replay protection, file limits, malware/content scanning and quarantine.   | Reject or quarantine; do not partially persist or silently normalize.                             |
| **Edge to connector/ingest**                       | Authenticated workload identity, tenant binding, canonical envelope, size/burst controls and explicit routes.                       | Backpressure or isolate source; core remains available.                                           |
| **Connector to customer estate**                   | Per-tenant scoped credentials, outbound allowlist, separate read/action permissions and credential rotation.                        | Connector fails independently; coverage marked degraded; credentials revoked without core outage. |
| **Regional service to data stores**                | Service identity, tenant policy, encryption context, schema/data authority and purpose.                                             | Deny/alert; never fall back to unscoped query.                                                    |
| **Core to action broker**                          | Typed intent, authority, approval and tenant references; no credentials or direct action path.                                      | Action remains pending/denied; security monitoring alerted.                                       |
| **AI gateway to providers/tools**                  | Data/region/provider policy, redaction, budgets, typed tool contracts and target authorization.                                     | Deterministic/human fallback or feature disabled.                                                 |
| **Management to production**                       | Phishing-resistant identity, managed device, JIT, recorded session, change/case reference and dual control for critical operations. | No standing bypass; break-glass separately controlled and reviewed.                               |
| **Platform to external witness/customer verifier** | Signed, replay-safe, independently verifiable proof and command formats.                                                            | Verification failure blocks trust assertion/action acceptance.                                    |

# 07 \| Secure Design, Abuse Cases and Security-Requirement Workflow

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image76.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image85.png" />

***Figure 3 - Secure design and abuse-case lifecycle.***

| **Change trigger**                                | **Mandatory security work**                                                                                              |
|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **New service/module or trust boundary**          | Context diagram, data flow, identities, assets, abuse cases, requirements, tests and monitoring.                         |
| **New data class, purpose or jurisdiction**       | Privacy/security classification, minimization, residency, key, retention and deletion controls.                          |
| **New connector or customer permission**          | Permission inventory, compromise blast radius, credential lifecycle, rate limits, negative tests and certification.      |
| **New response action or authority level**        | Action threat model, approvals, signing, customer verification, ceilings, rollback, simulation and independent red team. |
| **New AI use, retrieval source, agent or tool**   | AI risk class, injection/poisoning tests, tenant isolation, tool authorization, budgets, kill and disclosure.            |
| **New dependency, builder, registry or provider** | Supply-chain due diligence, pinning, provenance, incident/exit plan and concentration risk.                              |
| **New deployment or isolation tier**              | Tenant and management-plane model, data/key separation, recovery, operational capacity and verification.                 |
| **Material incident or red-team finding**         | Threat-model update, control redesign, regression tests, CAPA and claims impact review.                                  |

# 08 \| Identity, Workload and Policy-Enforcement Security

| **Control domain**         | **Mandatory architecture**                                                                                                                              |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Human identity**         | Federated identity, phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles, session risk, device posture, short session lifetimes and explicit reauthentication.   |
| **Workload identity**      | SPIFFE-class or equivalent short-lived identity, mutual authentication, audience/purpose binding and automatic rotation.                                |
| **Machine clients**        | OAuth client/workload grants with narrow scopes, no human impersonation and independent lifecycle.                                                      |
| **Policy decision**        | Central policy semantics with local enforcement; actor, tenant, resource, action, purpose, environment, entitlement, risk, approvals and current state. |
| **Policy enforcement**     | Every interface and data access path enforces; downstream services never trust upstream claims blindly.                                                 |
| **Delegation**             | Non-transitive, purpose-bound and time-bounded; agent, partner, support and service delegation distinguish subject and actor.                           |
| **Step-up**                | Required for privilege elevation, sensitive export, key operations, response actions and security-control changes.                                      |
| **Revocation**             | Session/token/credential revocation propagates within defined target; failed propagation is a security degradation.                                     |
| **ZoikoID outage**         | Authenticated read may continue under bounded cached validation; privileged, policy-changing and response paths fail closed.                            |
| **Authorization evidence** | Stable decision ID, policy version, reason, inputs, outcome and enforcement point; sensitive attributes minimized.                                      |

# 09 \| Network, Edge, Service-to-Service and Egress Security

| **Layer**                   | **Required controls**                                                                                                                             |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Internet edge**           | DDoS protection, WAF, bot/automation controls, TLS policy, rate limits, request-size/time limits, secure headers and origin protection.           |
| **API/ingestion gateway**   | Authentication, tenant binding, schema/protocol validation, replay prevention, quotas, idempotency, canonical errors and abuse telemetry.         |
| **East-west services**      | Workload identity, mTLS, service and method authorization, default-deny network policy, timeout/circuit controls and no implicit namespace trust. |
| **Data services**           | Private endpoints, service-specific identities, explicit ports/protocols, no public exposure and auditable administrative access.                 |
| **Egress**                  | Default deny, destination allowlists, DNS controls, proxy/gateway mediation, data-class/provider policy and anomaly alerts.                       |
| **Management plane**        | Separate networks/accounts/projects, stronger access, no route from customer/data plane except controlled administration and telemetry.           |
| **Partner/provider**        | Mutual authentication, fixed contracts, bounded data, region/processing rules, breach notification, monitoring and kill/exit controls.            |
| **Telemetry/observability** | Sensitive-field policy, tenant pseudonymization, no secrets, independent security stream and restricted access.                                   |
| **Failure**                 | Network-policy/controller outage does not open access; policy uncertainty fails closed for sensitive paths.                                       |

# 10 \| Cryptography, Key Management, PKI and Signing Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image77.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image86.png" />

***Figure 4 - Cryptographic trust and key hierarchy.***

| **Control**               | **Required specification**                                                                                                                                      |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Approved algorithms**   | Versioned cryptographic profile; modern approved algorithms/protocols; deprecated algorithms blocked with migration plan.                                       |
| **Encryption in transit** | TLS 1.3 preferred; mutual authentication on service paths; certificate and hostname/audience validation mandatory.                                              |
| **Encryption at rest**    | Envelope encryption for databases, objects, backups, search and sensitive queues; encryption context includes tenant/purpose where supported.                   |
| **Key separation**        | Distinct purposes and identities for data encryption, evidence anchoring, release signing, provenance, webhooks, response commands and tokens.                  |
| **Custody**               | HSM/KMS-backed operations for high-value keys; no private key export where feasible; dual control for roots and recovery.                                       |
| **Rotation**              | Automated for workload/session keys; scheduled and event-driven for other keys; old data/references remain decryptable/verifiable during controlled transition. |
| **Revocation/compromise** | Immediate disable, propagation, artifact/command/evidence impact analysis, re-sign/re-encrypt plan and customer/assurance review.                               |
| **Tenant keys**           | Tenant-scoped context baseline; dedicated keys by tier; BYOK/HYOK requires operationally tested lifecycle and outage behavior.                                  |
| **Trusted time**          | Security and evidence events use authoritative time; timestamp failure is explicit and may block signing/anchoring.                                             |
| **Crypto agility**        | Algorithms, key versions and signatures are metadata; verification supports transition; migration tested before emergency need.                                 |
| **Secret material**       | Never logged, embedded, exported into prompts, copied into tickets or stored in document repositories.                                                          |
| **Verification**          | Known-answer tests, certificate/path tests, rotation drills, revocation tests, signature verification and restore/compromise exercises.                         |

# 11 \| Secrets, Privileged Access, Support Access and Break-Glass

| **Area**                    | **Mandatory controls**                                                                                                                           | **Evidence**                                             |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Secret creation**         | Approved vault, owner, purpose, scope, rotation, expiry and consuming workload identity.                                                         | Vault metadata and access policy.                        |
| **Secret use**              | Runtime injection or brokered access; never exposed to developers, build logs, images, source or user interfaces.                                | Access and use telemetry.                                |
| **Privileged human access** | Named account, managed device, phishing-resistant MFA, JIT request, purpose, ticket/case, approval, bounded duration.                            | Session, command and data-access record.                 |
| **Support access**          | Customer-approved or contractually defined, tenant-scoped, masked by default, visible to customer where appropriate.                             | Access request, grant, session and post-use record.      |
| **Break-glass**             | Separate identity/credential path, dual control for critical scope, immediate alert, time limit and mandatory review.                            | Break-glass activation and post-use assessment.          |
| **Production data**         | No routine developer access; secure query/workflow with minimization, purpose and case linkage.                                                  | Query/access evidence and result handling.               |
| **Revocation**              | Immediate on role/contract change, incident or compromise; active sessions and derived tokens invalidated.                                       | Lifecycle reconciliation.                                |
| **Standing access**         | Prohibited for broad production, KMS/HSM, action broker, evidence vault and customer credentials except explicitly justified service identities. | Quarterly access recertification and exception evidence. |

# 12 \| Multi-Tenant Isolation and Cross-Tenant Verification

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image78.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image87.png" />

***Figure 5 - Tenant-isolation verification matrix.***

| **Isolation layer**     | **Required pattern**                                                                                              | **Prohibited pattern**                                                          |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Request/API**         | Tenant derived from authenticated authority and verified against resource; not accepted blindly from body/header. | Caller-selected tenant used without authorization.                              |
| **Relational**          | Tenant key in primary/unique relationships, row-level or equivalent policy, scoped queries and migration checks.  | Unscoped repository method or shared global identifier without tenant relation. |
| **Objects/evidence**    | Tenant-prefixed/isolated namespace, signed access, key context, manifest checks and export tests.                 | Predictable paths or global listing.                                            |
| **Search/analytics**    | Tenant-filtered index/partition or dedicated index by tier; policy injected server-side and query audited.        | Client-supplied filter as sole isolation.                                       |
| **Cache**               | Tenant in key, namespace and invalidation; no shared sensitive cache without cryptographic/logic isolation.       | Global cache key for tenant data.                                               |
| **Queues/events**       | Tenant-bound topic/partition/envelope, consumer authorization and dead-letter isolation.                          | Untrusted event tenant controls routing.                                        |
| **Observability**       | Pseudonymous tenant context, access-controlled queries and leakage tests.                                         | Raw cross-tenant payloads in general logs.                                      |
| **AI retrieval/memory** | Tenant ACL at index, retrieval, context and output; cache/memory separated and deletion verified.                 | Prompt instruction used as isolation.                                           |
| **Partner/support**     | Explicit delegated scope and customer visibility; no inherited cross-tenant role.                                 | Broad MSP/support role without per-tenant grant.                                |
| **Testing**             | Generated tenants and cross-product negative tests across every store/interface in each release.                  | Manual spot checks only.                                                        |

# 13 \| Data Protection, Storage, Backup and Secure Deletion

| **Control**                    | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Classification and purpose** | Every data object and flow has class, owner, purpose, tenant, region, source authority, retention and permitted consumers.                                          |
| **Minimization**               | Collect/store only fields required; source-side suppression and tokenization preferred; raw payload retention is explicit and plan/policy-bound.                    |
| **Storage authority**          | Transactional, lakehouse, search, cache, evidence and observability stores have distinct authority; derived stores cannot silently become source of truth.          |
| **Encryption**                 | Storage and backup encryption with key/purpose separation; sensitive fields may receive additional application-level protection.                                    |
| **Integrity**                  | Checksums/signatures/manifests for evidence, exports, imports, backups and critical configuration; corruption is explicit.                                          |
| **Retention and legal hold**   | Policy evaluation at write and deletion; legal-hold conflict enters reviewed queue; no silent retention or deletion.                                                |
| **Deletion**                   | Deletes across primary, replicas, search, cache, lakehouse and derived stores; backup expiry and cryptographic erasure documented; attestation for contracted exit. |
| **Backups**                    | Encrypted, access-separated, immutable where required, tested restores, region/purpose rules and ransomware-resistant controls.                                     |
| **Restore**                    | Reconcile against event manifests, evidence anchors, tenant boundaries and current keys before service trust is restored.                                           |
| **Non-production**             | Synthetic/anonymized data by default; production copies require exceptional approval, minimization, isolation and expiry.                                           |
| **Export**                     | Purpose-scoped, approved, rate-limited, encrypted, manifest-signed and logged; very large or high-risk export requires step-up/dual approval.                       |
| **Observability**              | No secrets; sensitive attributes redacted/tokenized; security traces sufficient for reconstruction without duplicating full customer content.                       |

# 14 \| Application, API, Webhook and File-Handling Security Baseline

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image79.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image88.png" />

***Figure 6 - Application and API security control stack.***

| **Domain**                 | **Minimum verification requirements**                                                                                                                     |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication/session** | Secure federation, token validation, audience/issuer/time checks, rotation, logout/revocation, CSRF where relevant and secure cookie/session controls.    |
| **Authorization**          | Object/property/function-level checks, tenant and purpose enforcement, deny by default, stable reason codes and negative tests.                           |
| **Input**                  | Typed schemas, canonicalization, length/range limits, allowlists where feasible, Unicode/path/URL normalization, safe parsers and query parameterization. |
| **Output**                 | Contextual encoding, safe rendering, data minimization, security headers/CSP, cache control and no stack/secret/internal-detail leakage.                  |
| **Business logic**         | State machine, concurrency, idempotency, replay protection, rate/velocity/volume controls and approval invariants.                                        |
| **Webhooks**               | Mutual/strong source identity, HMAC/signatures, timestamp/nonce, replay window, rotation, idempotency, delivery receipt and failure visibility.           |
| **Files/archives**         | Type/content validation, decompression and archive limits, path traversal prevention, malware scanning, sandboxed parsing and quarantine.                 |
| **Queries/search**         | Server-side tenant filter, resource limits, query complexity/timeout, safe templating and audit of sensitive searches.                                    |
| **Errors**                 | Stable machine code, correlation ID and safe message; authorization and existence errors do not leak protected resource state.                            |
| **Client/front-end**       | No authoritative security logic in client; secrets absent; dependency integrity; XSS/DOM/URL/open-redirect protections; secure download handling.         |
| **Admin interfaces**       | Separate role/route, stronger authentication, no public exposure where avoidable, action preview and immutable audit.                                     |
| **Verification level**     | ASVS 5.0 requirements tailored by component risk; API Top 10, OWASP Top 10 2025 and component threat models supplement, not replace, ASVS.                |

# 15 \| AI, Agentic and Retrieval Security Integration

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image80.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image89.png" />

***Figure 7 - AI and agentic security boundary within platform security.***

| **Threat/control**           | **Platform-security requirement**                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Prompt injection**         | Treat user, telemetry, email, file, web, retrieval and tool content as untrusted data; policy and tool authority enforced outside model.          |
| **Cross-tenant retrieval**   | Tenant policy at source ingestion, index, retrieval, cache, context and citation validation; negative tests mandatory.                            |
| **Excessive agency**         | Separate agent identity; hard step/time/token/tool/cost limits; checkpoints; no standing credentials; target-side reauthorization.                |
| **Tool abuse**               | Typed operation, argument schema, action class, resource scope, idempotency, rate, compensation and receipt.                                      |
| **Poisoning/memory**         | Source authority, review/quarantine, versioning, expiry, deletion and no uncontrolled persistent memory.                                          |
| **Sensitive disclosure**     | Input minimization/redaction, provider policy, output scanning, trace controls and no secrets in context.                                         |
| **Denial of wallet**         | Per-tenant/user/agent budgets, concurrency, recursion and provider failover ceilings; anomaly detection.                                          |
| **Unsafe generated content** | Generated code/query/HTML/command is never executed without parsing, validation, authorization and sandbox/approval appropriate to risk.          |
| **Model/provider change**    | Pinned route or governed alias; impact review and regression before material production change.                                                   |
| **Kill/fallback**            | Feature, prompt, source, agent, tool, route, provider, tenant or global AI plane independently disableable; deterministic core remains available. |

# 16 \| Connector Runtime and Customer-Estate Boundary Security

| **Control area**          | **Required design**                                                                                                                    |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Credential scope**      | Per tenant and connector instance; least privileges; read and response permissions separated; no shared vendor credential.             |
| **Credential custody**    | Vaulted; connector workload retrieves short-lived/brokered value; secrets never pass through core, logs or UI after enrollment.        |
| **Runtime isolation**     | Connector workloads segmented from core, action broker and other tenants; resource quotas and restricted egress.                       |
| **Source authentication** | Validate endpoint/account/tenant, signature or identity; bind payload to registered connector and expected source.                     |
| **Parser safety**         | Schema/version identification, bounded parsing, quarantine, fuzzing and preservation of source-native payload/hash where permitted.    |
| **Permission drift**      | Periodic capability/permission check; drift changes health state and may block collection/action; customer receives exact remediation. |
| **Vendor change**         | Schema/API/permission/version changes detected; connector certification and action safety revalidated before enablement.               |
| **Backpressure**          | Per-tenant/source quotas and queues; one source cannot starve fleet or force uncontrolled cost.                                        |
| **Action certification**  | Read-only certification separate from write/action certification; each action has contract, test, rollback and receipt verification.   |
| **Compromise response**   | Disable instance/vendor action route, revoke credential, preserve evidence, assess tenant window, reauthorize and recertify.           |
| **Customer transparency** | Connector permissions, health, coverage, changes and action eligibility visible to customer.                                           |

# 17 \| Action Broker, Command Attestation and Mass-Action Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image81.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image90.png" />

***Figure 8 - Action-broker compromise containment.***

| **Control**               | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                                             |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Separation**            | Action broker is an isolated deployable and identity; core, AI and case services cannot directly execute customer actions.            |
| **Reauthorization**       | Broker evaluates current policy, tenant, environment, entitlement, authority R0-R4, approvals, target state, rate and freeze.         |
| **Signing**               | Per-tenant/purpose signing key use released per action; command binds all material fields, nonce and expiry.                          |
| **Customer verification** | Customer-side integration verifies signature, allowed action, target, nonce/expiry and local policy; unsigned/replayed commands fail. |
| **Mass-action ceiling**   | Per tenant, action, target class and time window; crossing threshold requires additional approval or automatic freeze.                |
| **Simulation**            | All R2+ playbooks have simulation/dry-run and tenant rehearsal before first live execution.                                           |
| **Idempotency**           | Unique transaction/action ID and state preconditions prevent duplicate or stale execution.                                            |
| **Receipts**              | Execution receipt is signed/verified where feasible and reconciled to observed state; absence/ambiguity remains UNKNOWN.              |
| **Rollback/compensation** | Reversible actions carry rollback; irreversible/high-impact actions require stronger approval and explicit consequence.               |
| **Freeze**                | Out-of-band tenant and global freeze under dual control; queue, key and route behavior tested.                                        |
| **Red team**              | Independent assessment before R2 GA and after material broker/key/attestation changes.                                                |

# 18 \| Workload, Container, Kubernetes and Runtime Hardening

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image82.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image91.png" />

***Figure 9 - Cloud-native workload security architecture.***

| **Layer**           | **Baseline controls**                                                                                                                                             |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Image**           | Minimal pinned base; supported versions; no package manager/shell where not required; non-root; read-only filesystem; no embedded secret; signed SBOM/provenance. |
| **Registry**        | Private/approved, immutable tags or digest pinning, access control, malware/vulnerability policy, retention and revocation.                                       |
| **Admission**       | Verify signature/provenance, approved builder/source, policy, image age, vulnerability status, security context, resources, network and secret references.        |
| **Pod/workload**    | Non-root, drop capabilities, no privilege escalation, seccomp/AppArmor-class profile, restricted host mounts/namespaces and resource limits.                      |
| **Node**            | Hardened image, dedicated sensitive pools, patching, restricted metadata, no developer login, runtime protection and control-plane separation.                    |
| **Kubernetes RBAC** | Least privilege, namespace/service account separation, no wildcards without exception, aggregated role review and JIT admin.                                      |
| **Network**         | Default-deny ingress/egress, explicit services/destinations, mTLS where required, DNS policy and egress gateway.                                                  |
| **Secrets**         | CSI/brokered retrieval, short-lived values, no environment/log leakage where avoidable and automatic rotation/restart strategy.                                   |
| **Runtime**         | Behavior monitoring, unexpected process/file/network alerting, integrity and policy violations, immutable redeploy response.                                      |
| **Debug**           | Ephemeral, approved, time-bound, recorded and removed; no permanent debug containers or production shells.                                                        |
| **Multi-tenancy**   | Production tenants share only approved T1 controls; higher tiers map to dedicated namespaces/pools/keys or deployments per contract.                              |

# 19 \| Cloud, Infrastructure-as-Code and Configuration Security

| **Control domain**            | **Required engineering baseline**                                                                                                         |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Account/project structure** | Separate production, non-production, security/logging and management scopes; no shared root/admin identity.                               |
| **IaC authority**             | Infrastructure and security configuration are versioned, reviewed, scanned, planned, approved and deployed through controlled automation. |
| **Policy as code**            | Mandatory controls for public exposure, encryption, identity, logging, key use, regions, tags, backups, network and workload admission.   |
| **Drift**                     | Continuous detection; unauthorized drift alerts and is reconciled; high-risk drift triggers containment.                                  |
| **Cloud identity**            | Workload federation and short-lived roles; no long-lived access keys; external identities constrained by condition and purpose.           |
| **Public exposure**           | Default prohibited; explicit approved service, WAF/gateway, DNS/TLS, monitoring, ownership and expiry.                                    |
| **Storage/database**          | Private endpoints, encryption, backup, access policy, deletion, monitoring and no default public/admin access.                            |
| **Management plane**          | Separate access route, strong identity/device/JIT, command/session evidence and independent monitoring.                                   |
| **Regions/residency**         | Allowed regions and provider services enforced; unsupported route fails closed to quarantine/deny.                                        |
| **Resource ownership**        | Every resource has owner, environment, tenant/isolation class where applicable, data class, cost center and lifecycle.                    |
| **Emergency change**          | Time-bound and recorded; post-change reconciliation and permanent IaC update mandatory; no silent console drift.                          |

# 20 \| Software Supply Chain, Artifact Integrity and Admission

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image83.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image92.png" />

***Figure 10 - Software supply-chain trust chain.***

| **Stage**             | **Required controls**                                                                                                                           |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source**            | Protected branch, required reviewers/code owners, signed/attributable commits, no shared accounts, secret scanning and immutable history.       |
| **Build definition**  | Versioned pipeline and builder image; approved actions/plugins; pinned versions/digests; no unreviewed network fetch.                           |
| **Build environment** | Ephemeral/isolated where feasible; least privilege; no production credentials; deterministic or reproducible techniques for critical artifacts. |
| **Dependencies**      | Lock files, approved repositories, integrity verification, dependency confusion defenses and license/security policy.                           |
| **Testing/scanning**  | Unit/integration/security, SAST, SCA, IaC, secrets, container, malware and policy checks with controlled exceptions.                            |
| **SBOM**              | CycloneDX or SPDX-class machine-readable inventory for released artifacts; component/version/license/source and relationships.                  |
| **Provenance**        | SLSA-compatible attestation identifies source, builder, build definition, inputs, outputs and environment.                                      |
| **Signing**           | Artifact and relevant metadata signed by controlled release identity after gates; developer signatures do not equal release approval.           |
| **Registry**          | Immutable trusted storage, retention, access, replication, revocation and no unsigned bypass.                                                   |
| **Admission**         | Verifies digest, signature, provenance, builder/source, environment, vulnerability/exception state and deployment policy.                       |
| **Promotion**         | Same artifact promoted; no rebuild between environments; staged canary and rollback reference.                                                  |
| **Revocation**        | Compromised artifact/builder/key can be denied, located fleet-wide and rolled back; customer impact assessed.                                   |
| **Evidence**          | Every release stores source, tests, SBOM, provenance, signature, approvals, exceptions, deployment and runtime version evidence.                |

# 21 \| Source Control, Coding and Secure Review Requirements

| **Area**                 | **Mandatory control**                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Repository access**    | Individual SSO/MFA, least privilege, managed device for controlled code, contractor expiry and review.                                  |
| **Branches**             | Protected default/release branches; no force push/delete; required checks and independent reviewers.                                    |
| **Code ownership**       | Sensitive paths (authorization, tenancy, crypto, evidence, action, AI tools, deployment) require named specialist reviewers.            |
| **Change traceability**  | Every change links requirement/defect/risk, design/ADR where relevant and test evidence.                                                |
| **Secure coding**        | Language/framework secure patterns, safe libraries, parameterized access, memory/type safety preference, validation and error handling. |
| **Generated/AI code**    | Treated as untrusted contribution; approved tool/data use; human review; tests; license and dependency checks; no secret/customer data. |
| **Secrets**              | Pre-commit/server scanning; block and rotate on discovery; do not merely delete from latest commit.                                     |
| **High-risk changes**    | Pair/review by security-qualified owner, targeted threat review and negative test update.                                               |
| **Tests**                | Changed control path includes positive, negative, boundary, misuse, failure and regression tests.                                       |
| **Documentation**        | Interface, security assumptions, failure behavior, operational signals and runbook impact updated before merge.                         |
| **Release independence** | Author cannot be sole approver and production promoter for material change.                                                             |
| **Security debt**        | Tracked as risk/finding with owner/expiry; “later” is not a control state.                                                              |

# 22 \| Open-Source, Dependency, Vendor and Subprocessor Security

| **Control**                | **Requirement**                                                                                                              |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Intake**                 | Business/technical owner, purpose, alternatives, data/access scope, license, maintenance, security posture and exit plan.    |
| **Source trust**           | Official repository/package source, publisher verification, signed release/integrity hash and dependency-confusion controls. |
| **Versioning**             | Pin direct dependencies; lock transitive graph; controlled update automation; no floating production versions.               |
| **Maintenance health**     | Release cadence, unresolved vulnerabilities, bus factor, project governance, archival status and ecosystem signals.          |
| **Security due diligence** | Known issues, secure-development evidence, SBOM/provenance where available, disclosure process and incident history.         |
| **License/IP**             | Approved license and obligations; no incompatible code/data/model terms; attribution and source obligations tracked.         |
| **Provider data**          | Data classes, purposes, regions, retention, training/use, subprocessors, access and deletion confirmed before integration.   |
| **Access**                 | Least privilege, dedicated tenant/account, scoped tokens, rotation, logs and no broad shared admin.                          |
| **Monitoring**             | Vulnerabilities, provider changes, breach notices, terms, availability, cost and concentration monitored.                    |
| **Exit**                   | Export, replacement, key/credential revocation, deletion, contract termination and continuity test.                          |
| **Critical vendor**        | Independent assurance, contractual notification, audit rights where appropriate, resilience and alternate/manual path.       |
| **Exception**              | Unmaintained or high-risk component requires explicit risk acceptance, containment and replacement deadline.                 |

# 23 \| Vulnerability, Patch and Exposure Management

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image84.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image93.png" />

***Figure 11 - Risk-based vulnerability and exposure lifecycle.***

| **Priority factor**                       | **Effect on urgency**                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Known exploitation / KEV-class signal** | Immediate priority regardless of base score when relevant/reachable.                                                       |
| **Internet/customer-estate exposure**     | Raises priority due to direct attack path or customer impact.                                                              |
| **Tenant isolation/evidence/action path** | Criticality increases where weakness can cross tenants, alter evidence or issue response actions.                          |
| **Privilege and identity**                | Raises priority for auth, session, workload identity, KMS, PAM and management-plane paths.                                 |
| **Exploitability and prerequisites**      | Working exploit, low complexity, no auth and common path raise; strong unreachable prerequisites may reduce with evidence. |
| **Reachability/deployment**               | Actual deployed vulnerable path, feature flag and dependency reachability determine exposure.                              |
| **Data sensitivity**                      | Regulated, credential, evidence, secret or customer-security data raise impact.                                            |
| **Compensating controls**                 | Can reduce residual risk only if tested, monitored and time-bound.                                                         |
| **Fleet prevalence**                      | Widespread dependency/image/provider weakness increases urgency and blast radius.                                          |
| **Detection/containment**                 | Weak visibility or inability to isolate raises priority.                                                                   |
| **Customer/regulatory obligations**       | Notification, contractual remediation or assurance commitments influence timeline.                                         |
| **Fix risk**                              | Operational risk informs deployment sequence but does not justify indefinite exposure.                                     |

## 23.1 Baseline remediation targets

| **Class**                                                   | **Target**                                                                          | **Minimum handling**                                                                                   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **P0 actively exploited / tenant/action/evidence critical** | Immediate containment; fix or durable mitigation target 24 hours                    | Incident command, executive/security owner, fleet search, customer impact and continuous verification. |
| **P1 critical reachable**                                   | Fix/mitigate target 7 days                                                          | Named owner, release plan, detection and exception only with CISO approval.                            |
| **P2 high relevant**                                        | Fix target 30 days                                                                  | Prioritized backlog, deployment evidence and monitoring.                                               |
| **P3 medium/low or defense in depth**                       | Fix in planned cycle, normally 90/180 days                                          | Risk/context documented; aggregate debt tracked.                                                       |
| **Provider-controlled**                                     | Contain or disable where necessary; vendor SLA does not replace Zoiko risk decision | Vendor escalation, alternate route, customer impact and exit assessment.                               |

Targets are internal baseline objectives, not contractual promises. The risk owner may shorten them; extensions require time-bound exception with tested compensating controls and release visibility.

# 24 \| Runtime Protection, Security Monitoring and Deception Boundaries

| **Signal/control**      | **Required coverage**                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**            | Authentication anomalies, token misuse, privilege grants, JIT/break-glass, dormant credentials and revocation failures.         |
| **Workload**            | Unexpected process, file, network, syscall, identity or resource behavior; image/config drift and policy violations.            |
| **Network/egress**      | Unexpected destination, protocol, DNS, volume, lateral movement and blocked policy attempts.                                    |
| **Data/evidence**       | Unusual export/query, integrity/anchor failure, deletion/hold conflict, cross-tenant denial and mass access.                    |
| **Action broker**       | Denied/abnormal actions, ceiling approach, signature/key errors, replay attempts, receipt mismatch and freeze activation.       |
| **Supply chain**        | Protected-branch changes, builder/pipeline changes, signing/provenance failure, unexpected artifact and admission denial.       |
| **Cloud/control plane** | IAM/policy/network/KMS/logging changes, console use, public exposure, drift and disabled monitoring.                            |
| **Connectors**          | Credential/permission drift, source change, anomalous volume, parser failures, action mismatch and suspicious egress.           |
| **AI**                  | Prompt injection signals, cross-tenant denials, tool authorization failures, budget loops, poisoning and kill events.           |
| **Deception/canary**    | Synthetic tenant, honey credential/token/resource or canary action only where legally/operationally reviewed; no customer harm. |
| **Response**            | Signals route to cases with severity, tenant/context, source evidence, owner and runbook; logging alone is not detection.       |

# 25 \| Security Logging, Auditability and Evidence Preservation

| **Event class**            | **Mandatory fields / treatment**                                                                                                      |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication/session** | Actor/subject, method, device/risk, issuer, result/reason, session ID, tenant and time; no secret/token content.                      |
| **Authorization**          | Decision ID, actor/subject, tenant, resource, action, purpose, policy/version, outcome/reason and enforcement point.                  |
| **Privileged/support**     | Request, approver, scope, purpose, duration, session/commands, data access, break-glass and post-review.                              |
| **Security configuration** | Before/after reference, author, reviewer, deployment, environment, affected tenants/services and rollback.                            |
| **Cryptographic**          | Key/cert ID and version, operation/purpose, requester, policy result, rotation/revocation and errors; no key material.                |
| **Supply chain/release**   | Source, commit, builder, inputs, SBOM, provenance, scans, signature, admission, deployment and rollback.                              |
| **Tenant isolation**       | Denied cross-tenant attempts, policy mismatch, query filter failure, test result and incident linkage.                                |
| **Data/evidence**          | Sensitive access/export, evidence create/read/freeze/verify, deletion/hold and integrity failures.                                    |
| **Response actions**       | Intent, authority, approvals, policy, signed envelope hash, target, receipt, observed outcome and rollback.                           |
| **AI**                     | Use case, tenant, policy, data classes, model/prompt/tool/source versions, validation, human decision, cost and incident reference.   |
| **Integrity**              | Security logs are append-only or tamper-evident, access-restricted, time-synchronized, retained and independently monitored.          |
| **Reconciliation**         | Sampled material operations must reconcile to required security events within defined latency; gaps page and open integrity incident. |

# 26 \| Platform Incident Containment, Recovery and Assurance Re-Establishment

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image85.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image94.png" />

***Figure 12 - Platform security incident containment and assurance recovery.***

| **Scenario**                     | **First containment controls**                                                                            | **Trust re-establishment evidence**                                                                             |
|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity compromise**          | Revoke sessions/tokens, disable principal, isolate device, freeze privilege and inspect delegation.       | Identity source clean, MFA/device reset, access reconciliation and activity review.                             |
| **Action broker/key compromise** | Freeze actions, revoke key/route, purge queues, notify affected tenants and preserve commands.            | New keys/policy, customer verifier update, replay/receipt reconciliation and independent assessment.            |
| **Build/release compromise**     | Stop promotion, revoke artifacts/keys/builders, locate fleet, rollback and isolate source/pipeline.       | Clean source/build root, provenance, rebuilt artifacts, admission and fleet verification.                       |
| **Cross-tenant exposure**        | Block affected path, freeze exports/support/AI as needed, preserve evidence and identify tenant window.   | Fix and exhaustive negative tests, data-access reconstruction, customer/legal review and red-team confirmation. |
| **Evidence integrity incident**  | Stop affected attestations/packages, preserve anchors, isolate writers and compare witnesses/backups.     | Chain/root reconciliation, verifier success, corrected packages and claim impact review.                        |
| **Connector compromise**         | Disable instance/vendor action route, revoke credentials, isolate worker and identify data/action window. | Reissue least-privilege credentials, recertify connector and customer confirmation.                             |
| **Cloud/management compromise**  | Lock management access, isolate accounts/projects, preserve provider logs and rotate trust roots.         | Known-clean control plane, IAM/policy diff, key/release/data reconciliation and independent validation.         |
| **AI incident**                  | Disable feature/model/source/tool, preserve context and bound tenant/tool impact.                         | Re-evaluation, poisoning/memory cleanup, regression/red team and controlled re-enable.                          |

# 27 \| Remote Engineering, Contractor and Environment Security

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image86.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image95.png" />

***Figure 13 - Compartmentalized remote engineering security model.***

| **Control**                    | **Required baseline**                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**                   | Individual corporate identity; phishing-resistant MFA; role/workstream/time-bound groups; no shared accounts.                          |
| **Device**                     | Managed/approved endpoint for EC-2/EC-3; encryption, EDR, supported OS, patching, posture, screen lock and restricted local admin.     |
| **Source/workspace**           | Approved repositories and collaboration; no personal email/storage/messaging; external sharing blocked/logged.                         |
| **Development data**           | Synthetic/anonymized; no raw customer production data on local device; controlled secure test datasets.                                |
| **Secrets**                    | Vault/short-lived credentials; no copied production values, .env files in source, tickets or AI tools.                                 |
| **Environments**               | Developer default to local/non-production; staging/production access separately approved and JIT.                                      |
| **AI coding tools**            | Only approved providers/configurations; no customer data, secrets, restricted threat details or proprietary code outside approved use. |
| **Review and release**         | Protected branches, code owners, independent review, automated gates and separation from production promotion.                         |
| **Contractors/subcontractors** | Named sponsor, contract/IP/confidentiality, explicit scope, automatic expiry, no onward sharing and rapid offboarding.                 |
| **Monitoring/privacy**         | Access and security events logged proportionately and lawfully; controls focus on systems and risk, not covert employee surveillance.  |
| **Incident/loss**              | Immediate report, token/session revocation, device containment, source/access review and evidence preservation.                        |
| **Offboarding**                | Identity, source, CI/CD, cloud, vault, customer and document access revoked; device/data return or wipe; ownership transferred.        |

# 28 \| Security Failure States and Safe Degradation

| **State**                     | **Meaning**                                                   | **Required behavior**                                                                              |
|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **SECURE_NOMINAL**            | All required controls current and verified.                   | Normal operation within approved scope.                                                            |
| **IDENTITY_DEGRADED**         | Primary identity/control dependency unavailable or stale.     | Bounded read for valid sessions where approved; privilege/action/config change denied.             |
| **POLICY_UNAVAILABLE**        | Current authorization/network/key policy cannot be evaluated. | Sensitive operation denied; no permit-by-cache beyond approved lifetime.                           |
| **KEY_UNAVAILABLE**           | Required key/certificate/HSM operation unavailable.           | Do not weaken encryption/signing; queue, degrade or block; alert.                                  |
| **ISOLATION_UNCERTAIN**       | Tenant scope/enforcement cannot be proven.                    | Quarantine/deny affected path and open P0 integrity incident.                                      |
| **EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_FAILED** | Hash/chain/anchor/verifier mismatch.                          | Stop affected assertions/packages; preserve state and investigate.                                 |
| **SUPPLY_CHAIN_UNVERIFIED**   | Artifact signature/provenance/policy cannot be verified.      | Admission/deployment blocked; existing fleet assessed.                                             |
| **MONITORING_BLIND**          | Required security telemetry missing or stale.                 | Expose degradation; increase containment; block high-risk operation if monitoring is prerequisite. |
| **CONNECTOR_COMPROMISED**     | Credential/runtime/source integrity suspect.                  | Disable instance/action, revoke credential and mark coverage incomplete.                           |
| **ACTION_FROZEN**             | Tenant/global response actions disabled.                      | Detection/case continue; action attempts denied with reason; customer/ops notified.                |
| **AI_DISABLED**               | AI route/source/tool disabled or unsafe.                      | Deterministic/human workflows continue; no silent alternate provider.                              |
| **SECURITY_INCIDENT**         | Declared active compromise/integrity event.                   | Incident command controls override normal change; re-enable only by evidence gate.                 |
| **EXCEPTION_EXPIRED**         | Security exception past approved date.                        | Release/change blocked; owner escalated; compensating control not assumed valid.                   |
| **ACCESS_REVOKED**            | Identity/role/contract no longer authorized.                  | Sessions/tokens/access removed and reconciliation recorded.                                        |

## 30.1 Mandatory policy contracts

| **Contract**                | **Required dimensions**                                                                                             |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authorization**           | Actor/subject, tenant, resource, action, purpose, environment, entitlement, risk, approval and current state.       |
| **Network/egress**          | Workload identity, source/destination, protocol, port, data class, region, purpose, owner and expiry.               |
| **Cryptographic use**       | Key purpose, tenant/context, algorithm/version, operation, caller, approval, rate and audit.                        |
| **Admission**               | Source, builder, provenance, SBOM, signature, scans, exception, environment and region.                             |
| **Security requirement**    | Threat, objective, applicability, enforcement, failure state, tests, evidence, owner and review trigger.            |
| **Vulnerability exception** | Asset/component, versions, reachability, residual risk, compensating controls, owner, expiry and test/claim impact. |
| **Privileged access**       | Requester, role, scope, purpose, ticket/case, device, approvers, start/end, session and post-review.                |
| **Incident containment**    | Scope, tenants, affected trust roots, freeze/revoke actions, evidence, owner and re-enable gate.                    |

# 31 \| Verification, Adversarial Testing and Release Evidence

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image87.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image96.png" />

***Figure 14 - Security requirement-to-release evidence trace.***

| **Verification layer**          | **Minimum scope**                                                                                                            |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Static design checks**        | Architecture fitness functions, prohibited dependencies, tenant context, direct data/service access and secret patterns.     |
| **Code and configuration**      | SAST, secure linters, secret scanning, IaC/policy checks, dependency/license and container scanning.                         |
| **Unit/property tests**         | Authorization decisions, state machines, cryptographic handling, parsers, limits, idempotency and failure invariants.        |
| **Contract/integration**        | Identity, API/event/webhook, tenant, key, connector, action, data and provider boundary tests.                               |
| **Tenant isolation**            | Automated cross-tenant negatives across API, storage, search, cache, queue, logs, AI, support, export and action.            |
| **Dynamic/fuzz**                | DAST, API abuse, parser/file/archive/webhook fuzzing, concurrency/rate and malformed protocol tests.                         |
| **Supply chain**                | Source/build/provenance/signature/admission/revocation test and compromised-artifact drill.                                  |
| **Privilege and secrets**       | JIT, approval, session, vault, rotation, revocation, break-glass and no-secret-leak tests.                                   |
| **AI/agentic**                  | Injection, retrieval isolation, tool denial, budget/loop, poisoning, safe output and kill/fallback tests.                    |
| **Resilience/security failure** | Identity/policy/key/logging/provider outage, freeze, restore, queue/replay and fail-safe behavior.                           |
| **Penetration test**            | Independent application/API/cloud/tenant assessment before G1/G2 as scoped; findings remediated/retested.                    |
| **Red team**                    | Crown-jewel scenarios including action broker, supply chain, identity, tenant, evidence and AI before high-impact authority. |
| **Operational exercise**        | Incident, key/artifact revocation, customer action freeze, restore and offboarding/security-exit tests.                      |
| **Release evidence**            | Test versions/results, findings, exceptions, risk owner, rollback, monitoring, approvers and deployed artifact/provenance.   |

## 31.1 Extended P0 release blockers

- Known cross-tenant access or isolation uncertainty in a production path.

- Privileged or response action executable without current independent authorization, required approval, signing or receipt.

- Production artifact without verified source, provenance, signature, SBOM and admission decision.

- Credential, private key, customer secret or regulated data embedded in source, image, log, prompt, document or uncontrolled test data.

- Evidence integrity, anchor, audit reconciliation or security-log gap affecting material assertions.

- Critical/high exploitable finding without remediation or explicitly authorized non-GA containment.

- Unbounded AI/agent tool authority, missing target-side authorization or failed kill/fallback control.

- Missing rollback/containment for a material security-affecting change.

- Expired exception governing the release or unsupported security/assurance claim.

- Inability to identify deployed artifact/component versions or revoke a compromised version fleet-wide.

# 32 \| Security Metrics, SLOs, Risk Thresholds and Unit-Cost Controls

| **Metric**                          | **Definition / purpose**                                                                                                    |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **security_requirement_coverage**   | Applicable security requirements with enforcement, tests and release evidence.                                              |
| **tenant_isolation_test_pass**      | Automated negative tests passed across all required layers; target 100% for release.                                        |
| **privileged_access_jit_rate**      | Privileged sessions using approved JIT path versus total; standing/bypass sessions separately zero-targeted.                |
| **secret_exposure_count**           | Confirmed secret/key/customer-credential exposure in source, artifact, log, prompt or document; zero-tolerance critical.    |
| **artifact_admission_pass**         | Production workloads admitted with valid provenance/signature/SBOM/policy.                                                  |
| **critical_vulnerability_sla**      | P0/P1 findings remediated or durably mitigated within target, with exception age.                                           |
| **security_event_reconciliation**   | Sampled material operations with required security events within target latency.                                            |
| **security_monitoring_coverage**    | Required identity, workload, data, action, supply-chain, cloud and AI signals current and tested.                           |
| **key_certificate_expiry_headroom** | High-value keys/certificates with sufficient rotation lead time; failed/late rotations.                                     |
| **authorization_denial_anomaly**    | Denied requests/actions by tenant, identity, policy and source; used for abuse and drift detection.                         |
| **action_attestation_success**      | Commands verified and receipts reconciled; unknown/mismatched outcomes.                                                     |
| **supply_chain_revocation_time**    | Time from artifact/builder/key compromise decision to fleet deny/rollback state.                                            |
| **access_revocation_time**          | Time from termination/incident/role change to session and access removal by class.                                          |
| **security_exception_age**          | Open exceptions by severity, releases affected and time to expiry.                                                          |
| **security_cost_guardrail**         | Security logging, scanning, signing, key, runtime and control costs attributed without silently reducing required coverage. |
