# 33 \| Workstream Handoff, Definition of Ready and Definition of Done

## 33.1 Security Definition of Ready

| **Ready criterion**       | **Required evidence**                                                                                    |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope and owner**       | Feature/component, accountable engineering and security owners, release/gate and supported environments. |
| **Data and identity**     | Data classes/purposes/regions, actors/workloads, tenant model, privileges and source authority.          |
| **Trust boundaries**      | Context/data-flow diagram and affected crown jewels.                                                     |
| **Threats/abuse**         | Threat-model delta, misuse cases, assumptions and risk classification.                                   |
| **Security requirements** | Stable IDs, enforcement points, failure states, tests and evidence path.                                 |
| **Dependencies**          | Connectors, providers, libraries, builders, secrets/keys and exit/failure behavior.                      |
| **AI/action impact**      | AI use/tool authority and response authority level declared; required independent gates identified.      |
| **Test plan**             | Automated, negative, adversarial, resilience and independent assessment scope.                           |
| **Operational plan**      | Security telemetry, alert/runbook, containment, rollback and owner.                                      |
| **Access**                | Required engineer/environment/secret access approved and time-bound.                                     |

## 33.2 Security Definition of Done

| **Done criterion**     | **Required evidence**                                                                                |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Design implemented** | Approved architecture and policy are reflected in code/config; deviations have ADR/exception.        |
| **Controls verified**  | Required automated and adversarial tests pass; tenant and privilege negatives pass.                  |
| **Supply chain**       | SBOM, provenance, signatures, scans and admission evidence generated.                                |
| **Findings**           | No prohibited release blocker; accepted findings have owner, compensating control and expiry.        |
| **Secrets/access**     | No exposed secret/customer data; access and rotation/revocation paths tested.                        |
| **Telemetry**          | Security events, metrics, alerts and runbook validated without prohibited data leakage.              |
| **Failure/recovery**   | Safe degradation, containment, rollback and integrity reconciliation tested.                         |
| **Documentation**      | Interfaces, threat assumptions, security states, operations and customer-facing limitations current. |
| **Release decision**   | Security, engineering, SRE and applicable privacy/AI/evidence owners approve R20 evidence.           |
| **Post-release**       | Canary/monitoring period and escalation/kill criteria defined.                                       |

# 34 \| Approval Gates, Decisions and Controlled Annexes

| **Gate**                                    | **Minimum security evidence**                                                                                                                                               |
|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **G0 Build Authorization**                  | Approved security doctrine; crown-jewel model; trust zones; identity/tenant/crypto/supply-chain baseline; requirement/test model; owner and risk register.                  |
| **G1 Design-Partner Readiness**             | Real-data threat models; tenant-isolation suite; product/API/connector security; evidence and AI controls; pen test; incident/access/offboarding readiness; no P0 blockers. |
| **G2 Commercial GA**                        | Measured security SLOs; 24/7 security operations; action controls/red team as applicable; vulnerability and release evidence; customer assurance and contractual scope.     |
| **G3 Enterprise/Sector Scale**              | Dedicated isolation, BYOK/enterprise federation, sector controls, enhanced support/access, scale/resilience and independent assurance.                                      |
| **G4 Sovereign/OT/Critical Infrastructure** | Separate deployment/operations model, customer key custody, offline/controlled updates, OT safety, sovereign staffing/support and specialist independent assessment.        |

## 34.1 Decisions required before approval

| **Decision**                                                               | **Owner**                             | **Default if not closed**                                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Security verification profile by component risk (ASVS level/tailoring)** | CISO / Product Security               | Highest applicable profile for customer-facing/control-plane components; no self-declared lower level. |
| **Workload identity and certificate model**                                | CTO / Platform Security               | Short-lived workload identity with mTLS for service paths; static service secrets prohibited.          |
| **Cryptographic profile and HSM/KMS custody**                              | CISO / Data / Platform                | Managed HSM/KMS, purpose-separated keys and no export for high-value signing roots.                    |
| **Supply-chain target and provenance format**                              | CTO / DevSecOps                       | SLSA v1.2-compatible provenance and signed artifacts; verify at admission.                             |
| **Security logging and independent retention**                             | CISO / SRE                            | Separate controlled security stream with integrity protection and access separation.                   |
| **Vulnerability SLA and exception authority**                              | CISO / CTO                            | Baseline targets in Section 23; P0/P1 extension requires CISO approval.                                |
| **Independent penetration/red-team provider and scope**                    | CISO / Procurement                    | No G1/G2/high-impact action gate without approved independent assessment.                              |
| **Managed-device and contractor security policy**                          | Head of Engineering / CISO / HR-Legal | EC-2/EC-3 requires managed/approved device and automatic contract expiry.                              |
| **Action-broker freeze and customer verification design**                  | Security / Response / Platform        | R2+ GA blocked until design and independent test approved.                                             |
| **Security incident re-enable authority**                                  | CISO / CTO                            | CISO and service owner jointly approve high-severity re-enable based on evidence.                      |

# 35 \| Standards Alignment and Authoritative Reference Inputs

The following are design and verification inputs, not blanket conformance claims. The controlled requirements register must identify the exact version, tailored requirement and evidence used. Draft standards are monitored but do not silently replace approved final baselines.

| **Reference**                                              | **Current controlled use**                                                                                                                                                |
|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **NIST SP 800-218, SSDF Version 1.1 (final)**              | Core secure-software-development practices. NIST SP 800-218 Rev.1 / SSDF 1.2 remains a public draft at the document date and is monitored through the Standards Register. |
| **NIST SP 800-207 and SP 800-207A**                        | Zero-trust and cloud-native access-control principles: continuous verification, policy decision/enforcement and no network-location trust.                                |
| **NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 and SP 800-53A Rev.5**              | Control objectives and assessment methods used selectively; not a claim of federal authorization.                                                                         |
| **NIST SP 800-161 Rev.1 Update 1**                         | Cybersecurity supply-chain risk management for systems, providers and acquisition.                                                                                        |
| **NIST SP 800-190 and SP 800-204C**                        | Container and cloud-native DevSecOps security design inputs.                                                                                                              |
| **OWASP ASVS 5.0.0**                                       | Primary application-security verification catalog, tailored by component risk.                                                                                            |
| **OWASP Top 10:2025 and API Security Top 10:2023**         | Awareness and abuse-case inputs; not substitutes for ASVS or product threat models.                                                                                       |
| **OWASP AISVS 1.0 and OWASP GenAI Security guidance**      | AI-system verification and GenAI/agentic threat inputs, coordinated with ZS-ENG-AI-001.                                                                                   |
| **SLSA Specification v1.2**                                | Build provenance and software-supply-chain assurance target.                                                                                                              |
| **CycloneDX / SPDX**                                       | Machine-readable SBOM formats; exact organizational profile controlled separately.                                                                                        |
| **CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1 and CIS Benchmarks** | Prioritized operational controls and hardened configuration inputs subject to licensing and tailoring.                                                                    |
| **CISA Secure by Design / Secure by Default guidance**     | Manufacturer accountability, secure defaults, elimination of avoidable classes and customer security outcomes.                                                            |
| **OpenSSF secure development guidance**                    | Developer, open-source and dependency-security inputs.                                                                                                                    |
| **ZoikoShield controlled baselines**                       | The binding implementation authority where they are stricter or more specific than external guidance.                                                                     |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                                                        | **Risk if uncorrected**                                                           | **Required refinement**                                                                                            |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AI treated as a feature rather than a controlled system**                        | Model, prompt, data, retrieval, tool and provider changes escape governance.      | Define the AI system as the complete socio-technical configuration and version every material component.           |
| **LLM-centric architecture excludes classifiers, embeddings and deterministic ML** | Unregistered models create decisions without model-risk controls.                 | Inventory all AI/ML components; apply controls proportionate to impact and autonomy.                               |
| **Prompt text used as a security boundary**                                        | Injection bypasses instructions and reaches data or tools.                        | Enforce tenant, data, tool, budget and authorization boundaries outside the model.                                 |
| **RAG described as search quality only**                                           | Poisoned or mis-scoped sources create false or cross-tenant output.               | Govern source authority, license, parsing, embeddings, index scope, freshness, injection resistance and citations. |
| **Agent loop described without transaction semantics**                             | Repeated or ambiguous tool calls cause duplicate side effects or runaway cost.    | Use typed tools, capability grants, idempotency, preconditions, budgets, checkpoints and stop conditions.          |
| **Human-in-the-loop used as a slogan**                                             | Reviewers rubber-stamp opaque output without evidence or alternatives.            | Design effective oversight: rationale, sources, uncertainty, impact, authority, alternatives and override.         |
| **Model evaluation based on average quality**                                      | Catastrophic tenant leakage or unsafe action is hidden by acceptable mean scores. | Define zero-tolerance critical failures and slice results by risk, data, language, tenant and scenario.            |
| **Memory added as convenience**                                                    | Persistent poisoning, secret retention and cross-purpose reuse emerge.            | Default to no memory; type, scope, expire, inspect and authorize every memory write.                               |
| **Provider fallback assumed safe**                                                 | Restricted data silently routes to an ineligible provider or region.              | Fallback is policy-controlled; deterministic/human-only degradation is preferable to noncompliant rerouting.       |
| **AI observability captures raw prompts indiscriminately**                         | Logs become a shadow sensitive-data store.                                        | Separate operational metadata from protected prompt/output content; hash/manifests remain auditable.               |
| **AI incident response folded into generic application response**                  | Unsafe routes, sources, prompts or tools cannot be disabled quickly.              | Provide granular kill switches and tested rollback by feature, model, provider, source, agent, tool and tenant.    |
| **AI-generated security/compliance content treated as truth**                      | Plausible fabrications become incidents, control conclusions or public claims.    | AI outputs remain proposals; deterministic evidence and accountable human approval govern material conclusions.    |

# 02 \| Executive AI Engineering Mandate

Build an AI control plane that safely improves investigation speed, evidence interpretation, control mapping, content creation and decision support while preserving deterministic authority, independent verification, tenant isolation, human accountability and safe degradation.

| **Mandate**                          | **Engineering obligation**                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Gateway-only access**              | Every production model call, embedding operation and agent execution uses approved gateway/runtime controls.           |
| **No-LLM critical path**             | Critical security and assurance functions continue without any model provider.                                         |
| **Purpose-bound context**            | Every input is tied to tenant, actor, purpose, feature, data class, region and source authority.                       |
| **Agentic least privilege**          | Agents receive a separate identity, typed tools, bounded memory, budgets, checkpoints and no standing credentials.     |
| **Evidence-backed output**           | Material claims cite authoritative sources and expose limitations, confidence and review state.                        |
| **Effective human control**          | Humans see evidence, uncertainty, alternatives and impact before approving material outcomes.                          |
| **Independent target authorization** | Tool and response services reauthorize every operation; model output is never a permit.                                |
| **Adversarial-by-default data**      | Telemetry and retrieved content are treated as untrusted, including hidden or machine-readable instructions.           |
| **Measured release**                 | No AI configuration reaches customers without evaluation, red team, canary, monitoring, rollback and release evidence. |
| **Commercially sustainable AI**      | Per-tenant and per-feature cost, latency and quality budgets are release constraints.                                  |

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image89.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image69.png" />

***Figure 2 - AI system context and control-plane boundaries.***

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Explicit Exclusions

| **In scope**                                                          | **Out of scope / prohibited in current plan**                                          |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Analyst investigation assistance, summarization and query suggestions | AI as the sole detector, incident declarer or case closer for material events          |
| Evidence summarization, gap explanation and mapping suggestions       | AI altering evidence, ledger history, hashes, control truth or audit package integrity |
| Executive narrative from approved structured facts                    | Uncited free-form claims presented as platform facts or certifications                 |
| Detection and playbook candidate generation in sandbox                | Direct production publication by a model or agent                                      |
| Bounded tool-assisted read operations with target authorization       | Standing customer-estate credentials or unrestricted shell/database/cloud access       |
| Typed agent workflows with budgets and checkpoints                    | Open-ended autonomous agents or self-modifying policies/prompts/tools                  |
| Model/provider abstraction and governed fallback                      | Silent routing to unapproved provider, model, region or data terms                     |
| Customer-facing AI disclosure and feedback mechanisms                 | Covert AI use or dark-pattern consent                                                  |
| Evaluation, monitoring, drift and incident management                 | Training foundation models on customer data in the baseline plan                       |
| AI governance for ZoikoShield internal systems                        | Certification claims or legal conclusions without qualified approval                   |

## 03.1 AI component classes

| **Class**                          | **Examples**                                              | **Control consequence**                                                               |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Generative language model**      | Summarization, explanation, narrative, planning           | Prompt, context, grounding, safety, disclosure, evaluation and provider controls.     |
| **Embedding model**                | Semantic indexing and retrieval                           | Region, tenant scope, reindex/version, inversion risk, deletion and quality controls. |
| **Classifier/ranker**              | Severity aid, relevance, routing or confidence estimation | Dataset, threshold, drift, explainability and fallback controls.                      |
| **Deterministic rules/statistics** | Policy, validation, aggregation and guardrails            | Not AI authority; remains auditable and testable baseline.                            |
| **Agentic orchestrator**           | Planning, tool selection and multi-step workflows         | Separate principal, budgets, tool contracts, checkpoints, kill switch and trace.      |
| **Third-party AI feature**         | Vendor-native AI in integrated products                   | Vendor due diligence, data flow, disclosure, opt-out, evidence and contract controls. |

# 04 \| Binding AI Architecture and Risk Principles

| **ID**    | **Principle**                             | **Binding consequence**                                                                                                    |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AI-01** | No model response is authoritative        | Material decisions are made by controlled policy or accountable humans using evidence.                                     |
| **AI-02** | No LLM on a critical path                 | Identity, authorization, entitlement, evidence integrity, compliance truth and response approval remain deterministic.     |
| **AI-03** | Gateway-only execution                    | No product service calls a provider model or embedding endpoint directly.                                                  |
| **AI-04** | Tenant and purpose context everywhere     | Every request, retrieval, memory and tool call is tenant-, actor-, purpose- and region-bound.                              |
| **AI-05** | Untrusted content stays untrusted         | Retrieved or user content cannot change policy, tool authority or instruction precedence.                                  |
| **AI-06** | Agents are principals, not personas       | Every agent has identity, owner, scope, capabilities, budgets, logs, expiry and kill state.                                |
| **AI-07** | No credentials in prompts                 | Models never receive standing secrets, private keys, access tokens or customer credentials.                                |
| **AI-08** | Target service reauthorizes               | Every tool call is independently authorized by the system that owns the resource.                                          |
| **AI-09** | No silent memory                          | Memory is explicit, typed, scoped, inspectable, expiring and never a source of authority.                                  |
| **AI-10** | Evidence before AI assertion              | Outputs cite current authoritative sources; missing or conflicting evidence is visible.                                    |
| **AI-11** | Human oversight must be effective         | Reviewers receive sources, uncertainty, alternatives, impact and override controls.                                        |
| **AI-12** | Critical failures are zero tolerance      | Tenant leakage, fabricated evidence, unsafe action and control-state misrepresentation block release.                      |
| **AI-13** | Fallback is governed                      | Failure degrades to deterministic or human workflows, not unapproved providers.                                            |
| **AI-14** | Cost is a safety boundary                 | Token, loop, concurrency and spend ceilings prevent denial-of-wallet and runaway agents.                                   |
| **AI-15** | Every material configuration is versioned | Model, provider, prompt, retrieval, tool, memory, policy and evaluator changes are traceable.                              |
| **AI-16** | AI claims follow proof                    | Public capability, accuracy, safety or compliance statements require current release evidence and Claim Register approval. |

# 05 \| AI System Inventory, Ownership and Risk Classification

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image90.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image70.png" />

***Figure 3 - AI use-case risk classification matrix.***

| **Risk class**                    | **Typical use**                                                                                                             | **Minimum control set**                                                                                                       |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AR-0 Prohibited/Deterministic** | Authentication, authorization, evidence integrity, compliance status, entitlement, signing, release approval                | AI excluded from authority path; deterministic controls only.                                                                 |
| **AR-1 Assistive Low**            | Formatting, translation, low-risk summarization of non-sensitive content                                                    | Approved model route, basic grounding, disclosure, logging, feedback and cost limits.                                         |
| **AR-2 Controlled Advisory**      | Triage support, evidence explanation, control mapping suggestions, internal narrative                                       | Use-case assessment, source citations, human decision, quality/security evaluation, monitoring and kill switch.               |
| **AR-3 High-Control Agentic**     | Multi-step investigation, bounded tools, customer-visible recommendations                                                   | Agent identity, typed tools, target authorization, checkpoints, strong evaluation, red team, canary, incident readiness.      |
| **AR-4 High-Impact/Restricted**   | Material decision support affecting customers, controls, privileged access or regulatory outcomes                           | Named human authority, enhanced assessment, legal/privacy review, dual control where relevant; autonomy generally prohibited. |
| **AR-X Prohibited**               | Cross-tenant reasoning, covert manipulation, unrestricted action, unapproved training, unsupported compliance certification | Must not be built or enabled; attempts are logged and escalated.                                                              |

# 06 \| Controlled AI Lifecycle and State Model

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image91.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image71.png" />

***Figure 4 - Controlled AI system lifecycle.***

| **State**      | **Permitted activity**                                                                | **Exit evidence**                                                |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **PROPOSED**   | Business and technical discovery only; no customer or production data.                | Use-case record, owner, scope and initial prohibited-use screen. |
| **CLASSIFIED** | Risk, data, autonomy and oversight identified.                                        | Approved risk class and review path.                             |
| **DESIGNING**  | Architecture, threat model, data flow, prompts, retrieval, tools and evaluation plan. | Design review and unresolved-risk log.                           |
| **EVALUATING** | Offline and adversarial testing with controlled datasets.                             | Threshold results, failure analysis and remediation.             |
| **SHADOW**     | Runs without affecting users or state; compared with deterministic/human baseline.    | Shadow quality, latency, cost and safety evidence.               |
| **CANARY**     | Limited tenants/users, explicit monitoring, granular kill switch.                     | Canary acceptance and no unresolved critical findings.           |
| **ACTIVE**     | Approved production configuration within scope.                                       | Current release evidence, monitoring and review date.            |
| **DEGRADED**   | Fallback or reduced capability due to provider, quality, cost, data or safety issue.  | Visible state, bounded operations and recovery owner.            |
| **SUSPENDED**  | Route/feature/tool/source disabled pending investigation.                             | Incident or change decision.                                     |
| **SUPERSEDED** | Replaced by newer controlled version; historical trace retained.                      | Migration and rollback evidence.                                 |
| **RETIRED**    | No new processing; data, index, memory and provider cleanup complete.                 | Retirement, export/deletion and claim updates.                   |

# 07 \| AI Control Plane and Model Gateway

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image92.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image72.png" />

***Figure 5 - Model gateway enforcement pipeline.***

## 07.1 Gateway responsibilities

| **Control domain**       | **Mandatory gateway behavior**                                                                                         |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity and tenancy** | Require authenticated actor/service/agent, tenant, environment, region, purpose and feature.                           |
| **Eligibility**          | Check use-case, role, entitlement, customer policy, consent, model/provider status and release state.                  |
| **Data protection**      | Classify, minimize, redact/tokenize, detect secrets, enforce provider and region eligibility.                          |
| **Routing**              | Use controlled route policy; pin or govern model alias; record model and provider version.                             |
| **Prompt/context**       | Load signed prompt profile; construct bounded context; freeze source manifest; separate untrusted content.             |
| **Budgets**              | Apply request, user, tenant, agent and feature limits for tokens, rate, concurrency, time, loops and spend.            |
| **Execution**            | Use approved endpoint, timeout, retries, retention and training flags; prohibit provider tools unless approved.        |
| **Validation**           | Parse typed output; check grounding, citations, policy, sensitive data, unsupported claims and schema.                 |
| **Evidence**             | Emit request/route/policy/model/prompt/source/output-validation/cost/audit metadata.                                   |
| **Degradation**          | Select approved alternate, deterministic workflow, human-only path or disablement; never silent downgrade of controls. |

## 07.2 Direct-access prohibition

<th><p><strong>RELEASE BLOCKER</strong></p>
<p>Any product service, connector, agent or script that can invoke a production AI provider outside the gateway is a release-blocking architecture defect.</p></th>

# 08 \| Model, Provider, Route and Version Governance

| **Area**              | **Required controls**                                                                                                                               |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Provider approval** | Security/privacy due diligence, contract/data terms, subprocessors, regions, incident notice, export/deletion, availability and concentration risk. |
| **Model approval**    | Capabilities, context limits, modalities, safety behavior, latency, cost, evaluation results, known limitations and approved use cases.             |
| **Version control**   | Prefer pinned versions for high-risk uses; model aliases require monitored provider-change detection and re-evaluation triggers.                    |
| **Routing**           | Policy by use case, data class, region, tenant, latency, quality, cost and availability; no lowest-cost-only routing.                               |
| **Fallback**          | Only approved fallback routes; data/region eligibility re-evaluated; deterministic/human fallback allowed and often preferred.                      |
| **Provider change**   | Terms, retention, training, model, safety, endpoints or regions trigger impact assessment and possible suspension.                                  |
| **Open/local models** | Artifact provenance, license, model card, weights integrity, serving isolation, patching, sandboxing and internal evaluation.                       |
| **Sunset**            | Migration, re-evaluation, prompt adaptation, customer notice, historical reproducibility and delete/export controls.                                |
| **Route status**      | **Runtime behavior**                                                                                                                                |
| **APPROVED**          | May serve only listed use cases/data/regions under current release.                                                                                 |
| **SHADOW_ONLY**       | May evaluate without user-visible output or side effects.                                                                                           |
| **DEGRADED**          | Restricted use or reduced traffic while issue is investigated.                                                                                      |
| **SUSPENDED**         | No calls; use controlled fallback.                                                                                                                  |
| **REVOKED**           | Configuration removed; active sessions/runs terminated where safe.                                                                                  |
| **EXPIRED**           | Blocked until owner review and renewal.                                                                                                             |

# 09 \| AI Data Governance, Minimization, Redaction and Residency

| **Control**                     | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Purpose limitation**          | Input fields must be necessary for the registered use case; broad record dumps are prohibited.                              |
| **Source authority**            | Context references authoritative records; mutable displays and analyst notes are labeled accordingly.                       |
| **Classification**              | Each field/source carries data class, tenant, region, retention and provider-eligibility metadata.                          |
| **Minimization**                | Prefer structured facts, IDs and summaries over raw payloads; source-side filtering before gateway.                         |
| **Secrets**                     | Detect and block credentials, private keys, tokens and high-risk secrets; never store in prompt logs.                       |
| **Personal and regulated data** | Redact/tokenize where feasible; provider, region and retention rules enforced before dispatch.                              |
| **Customer-data training**      | Prohibited unless explicit contractual authorization, approved purpose and separate governance exist.                       |
| **Provider retention**          | Use zero/limited retention controls where contracted; record actual terms and exceptions.                                   |
| **Residency**                   | Route before provider execution; embeddings, vector indexes, caches, traces and backups follow the same policy.             |
| **Deletion**                    | Delete prompts, outputs, embeddings, index entries, memory and provider-held data according to policy and proof capability. |
| **Synthetic test data**         | Default for development; production-derived data requires approved de-identification and restricted environment.            |
| **Cross-border transfer**       | Legal mechanism and provider eligibility are evaluated by policy; unmatched routes fail closed.                             |

# 10 \| Prompt, Instruction and Context Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image93.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image73.png" />

***Figure 6 - Instruction, context and prompt precedence architecture.***

| **Prompt-profile element** | **Required content**                                                                                              |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**               | Prompt ID, version, owner, use case, risk class, model routes, effective/expiry dates.                            |
| **Objective**              | Narrow task and permitted output; explicitly prohibited decisions and actions.                                    |
| **Instruction precedence** | Platform safety, feature profile, tenant overlay, task context, retrieved content and user instruction.           |
| **Output contract**        | Typed schema, citation format, confidence/uncertainty, limitation and refusal fields.                             |
| **Context rules**          | Required facts, optional sources, maximum scope, truncation priority and conflict handling.                       |
| **Injection handling**     | Treat all content as data; ignore instructions from retrieved/user-controlled sources; report suspicious content. |
| **Tool rules**             | Allowed tools, argument schema, read/write class, human checkpoints and target-side reauthorization.              |
| **Privacy rules**          | Forbidden fields, redaction, regional restrictions, retention and logging level.                                  |
| **Evaluation**             | Gold cases, adversarial cases, thresholds, critical failures and approved model versions.                         |
| **Change control**         | Diff, review, test, canary, rollback and supersession; emergency disablement.                                     |

# 11 \| Retrieval, Knowledge and Citation Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image94.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image74.png" />

***Figure 7 - Retrieval and knowledge assurance pipeline.***

| **Stage**             | **Required controls**                                                                                                |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source onboarding** | Owner, authority, license/display rights, purpose, data class, tenant/region, freshness and deletion.                |
| **Ingestion**         | Malware scan, file validation, parser version, immutable source hash, lineage and quarantine.                        |
| **Transformation**    | Structure extraction, page/section coordinates, tables, metadata, redaction and quality confidence.                  |
| **Chunking**          | Versioned policy preserving semantic and citation boundaries; no cross-tenant or cross-purpose mixing.               |
| **Embedding**         | Approved model, region, version, batch manifest, sensitivity and deletion/reindex behavior.                          |
| **Indexing**          | Tenant-scoped namespace, ACL propagation, encryption, cache isolation and poisoned-source quarantine.                |
| **Retrieval**         | Authorization before search; hybrid retrieval/rerank; freshness, diversity, authority and relevance thresholds.      |
| **Context assembly**  | Bounded source count/tokens; provenance and injection markers; conflict and missing-source behavior.                 |
| **Citation**          | Output claims map to exact source spans and versions; citation validator detects nonexistent/unsupported references. |
| **Feedback**          | Incorrect or malicious sources can be reported, quarantined, corrected and reindexed with evidence.                  |
| **Expiry/deletion**   | Expired, revoked or held content is handled consistently across originals, chunks, embeddings, caches and packages.  |

# 12 \| Embeddings, Vector Stores and Tenant Isolation

| **Control surface**           | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                                 |
|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Namespace**                 | Tenant and purpose are physical/logical partition keys; workspace labels alone are insufficient.                          |
| **Authorization**             | ACL and relationship filters apply before candidate retrieval and again before context use.                               |
| **Metadata**                  | Every vector binds source ID/version, tenant, region, data class, owner, timestamps, license and deletion state.          |
| **Model version**             | Embedding model/version recorded; incompatible version change requires controlled reindex and quality comparison.         |
| **Inversion/membership risk** | High-sensitivity data assessed for leakage; do not assume embeddings are anonymous.                                       |
| **Cache**                     | Query/result caches are tenant-, user- and policy-scoped with short TTL and no sensitive raw context in cache keys.       |
| **Backups**                   | Regional, encrypted, access-controlled and covered by deletion/retention commitments.                                     |
| **Deletion**                  | Source deletion propagates to chunks, embeddings, indexes, caches and derived memory; reconciliation verifies completion. |
| **Poisoning**                 | Source reputation, ingestion review, anomaly detection, feedback, quarantine and rollback to prior index snapshot.        |
| **Observability**             | Index coverage, stale vectors, ACL drift, failed deletion, retrieval crossovers and quality monitored.                    |
| **Testing**                   | Automated cross-tenant negative queries, adversarial similarity cases, stale index and deletion verification.             |

# 13 \| AI Memory Architecture and Persistence Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image95.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image75.png" />

***Figure 8 - AI memory hierarchy and write controls.***

| **Memory type**              | **Default**             | **Allowed content**                                                  | **Prohibited content / controls**                                                             |
|------------------------------|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Working**                  | Ephemeral               | Current plan, observations and tool receipts within one run.         | No cross-run reuse; destroyed at run end except decision evidence.                            |
| **Session**                  | Off for sensitive flows | Conversation context and user-selected temporary facts.              | Explicit TTL, user visibility, tenant/user binding, delete/reset.                             |
| **Case/task**                | Controlled              | References and summaries tied to one case, control or assessment.    | Facts link to authoritative records; no silent state change.                                  |
| **User preference**          | Opt-in                  | Language, display and low-risk workflow preferences.                 | No security facts, risk status, evidence conclusions, credentials or protected attributes.    |
| **Agent scratchpad**         | Private ephemeral       | Internal plan/state needed for bounded execution.                    | Not treated as explanation or evidence; never contains secrets; bounded and deleted.          |
| **Organizational knowledge** | Governed retrieval      | Curated policies, runbooks, standards mappings and approved content. | Managed through source pipeline, not conversational writes.                                   |
| **Long-term learned memory** | Prohibited baseline     | None in current plan.                                                | Requires separate ADR, privacy/legal review, poisoning model, user rights and deletion proof. |

# 14 \| Agentic Runtime, Planning and Orchestration

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image96.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.97222in" alt="Image: image76.png" />

***Figure 9 - Bounded agent execution loop.***

| **Agent control**     | **Requirement**                                                                                                          |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**          | Separate workload principal and agent ID; never impersonates a human invisibly.                                          |
| **Owner and purpose** | Named business/technical owner; one registered objective; prohibited goals explicit.                                     |
| **Autonomy level**    | A1 assistive, A2 recommend, A3 bounded agentic or A4 high-impact restricted.                                             |
| **Planning**          | Plans are proposals validated against policy, tools, budget, data and human-checkpoint rules.                            |
| **Budgets**           | Maximum steps, recursion, tokens, time, retrieval calls, tool calls, concurrency and cost.                               |
| **State**             | Typed run state; authoritative records remain external; plan and observations are not product truth.                     |
| **Tools**             | Allowlisted by profile; typed inputs; target-side authorization; side-effect class visible.                              |
| **Checkpoints**       | Mandatory before high-cost, sensitive-data, external communication, privileged or side-effect operations.                |
| **Stop conditions**   | Goal met, limit reached, uncertainty threshold, repeated failure, policy denial, human stop or kill state.               |
| **Concurrency**       | Per-tenant/user/agent limits; race and duplicate-action protections.                                                     |
| **Multi-agent**       | No implicit trust; agent-to-agent messages are untrusted inputs with typed contracts and no authority transfer.          |
| **Recovery**          | Resume only from validated checkpoint; replay cannot repeat side effects without idempotency and receipt reconciliation. |

# 15 \| Tool Contracts, Capability Grants and Transaction Boundaries

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image97.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image77.png" />

***Figure 10 - AI tool authorization and transaction boundary.***

| **Side-effect class**                  | **Examples**                                                      | **Minimum control**                                                                                   |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **T0 Pure read**                       | Fetch allowed record, query index, retrieve evidence              | Tenant/purpose authorization, bounded result, provenance, rate/cost limit.                            |
| **T1 Derived computation**             | Aggregate, compare, simulate, draft query                         | Deterministic service, no persistent state, input/output evidence.                                    |
| **T2 Reversible internal write**       | Create draft, add private note, queue review                      | Human-visible draft state, idempotency, undo, audit and ownership.                                    |
| **T3 External communication**          | Send notification/draft externally, create ticket                 | Named approval or pre-approved template/scope; receipt and cancellation where possible.               |
| **T4 Customer-estate/security action** | Revoke token, quarantine, isolate, block                          | Response authority R0-R4, target attestation, approvals, rate ceilings, rollback and broker controls. |
| **T5 Irreversible/prohibited**         | Delete evidence, change authorization, sign claim, transfer funds | Not available to AI; deterministic named authority only or prohibited entirely.                       |

## 15.1 Capability grant

- Short-lived, non-transferable reference binding agent, human/service principal, tenant, purpose, tool, operation, resource scope, expiry and limits.

- Does not contain standing credentials and cannot be broadened by the model.

- Target service verifies current policy and state; possession of the grant is necessary but not sufficient.

- Revoked when role, session, case, tenant policy, kill switch or incident state changes.

- Every attempted use emits allow/deny reason, arguments hash, target, result and evidence reference.

# 16 \| Human Oversight, Autonomy and Decision Rights

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image98.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image78.png" />

***Figure 11 - Human oversight and AI decision-rights model.***

| **Decision area**                | **AI role**              | **Required human/deterministic authority**                                         |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Alert summarization**          | Assist                   | Analyst verifies sources before material disposition.                              |
| **Triage recommendation**        | Recommend                | Qualified analyst accepts/modifies/rejects; rationale recorded for material cases. |
| **Incident declaration**         | No authority             | Named SOC/customer authority under deterministic criteria.                         |
| **Detection candidate**          | Draft                    | Detection engineer tests, reviews, signs and publishes.                            |
| **Control/evidence mapping**     | Recommend                | Control owner/assessor approves; mapping version and rationale stored.             |
| **Compliance conclusion**        | No authority             | Deterministic evaluator plus accountable control owner/auditor.                    |
| **Executive narrative**          | Draft from facts         | Approver verifies scope, known limitations and source snapshot.                    |
| **Read-only investigation tool** | Bounded assist           | Target authorizes; analyst sees tool inputs/outputs.                               |
| **External response action**     | No independent authority | Tenant response policy, R-level approvals, action broker and customer attestation. |
| **Customer communication**       | Draft/translate          | Approved templates and named human/operational authority for material notices.     |
| **Risk acceptance/exception**    | No authority             | Named accountable authority with expiry and compensating controls.                 |
| **Release approval**             | No authority             | Engineering, Security, AI Risk, Privacy and release authority based on evidence.   |

## 16.1 Effective-review interface

- AI label and use-case name

- Sources and exact supporting spans

- Known missing, stale or conflicting evidence

- Confidence and uncertainty stated in calibrated terms

- Alternative hypotheses or actions

- Expected impact and reversibility

- Required authority and approvals

- Accept, modify, reject and escalate controls

- Recorded human decision and rationale

- Appeal/feedback route where customer-affecting

# 17 \| AI Use in Detection, Response, Evidence and Compliance

| **Domain**              | **Permitted**                                                                       | **Prohibited / gated**                                                                                |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Detection**           | Generate candidate rules, explain logic, suggest tests, cluster signals in sandbox. | Direct production rule publication; unversioned model-only detector as sole basis for material alert. |
| **Triage**              | Summarize events, propose hypotheses and queries, surface related records.          | Close alert/case, declare incident or suppress evidence without human/policy authority.               |
| **Response**            | Recommend playbook/action and explain blast radius.                                 | Authorize, sign or execute customer-estate action without deterministic response controls.            |
| **Evidence**            | Summarize artifacts, propose classification/mapping, identify gaps.                 | Alter original evidence, assert completeness, create hashes/signatures or hide failed collectors.     |
| **Controls/compliance** | Draft mappings and narratives from approved facts.                                  | Render PARTIAL/STALE/FAILED as compliant; claim certification or legal compliance.                    |
| **Risk**                | Explain factor contributions and scenarios.                                         | Create opaque risk truth or accept risk.                                                              |
| **Customer support**    | Draft grounded responses and route cases.                                           | Disclose another tenant, fabricate product behavior or commit to unsupported SLA/claim.               |
| **Engineering**         | Assist code/tests/docs in approved environment.                                     | Receive secrets/customer data in unapproved tools; bypass review, SBOM or supply-chain controls.      |

<col style="width: 100%" />

<p>AI may explain an evidence state. It cannot upgrade PARTIAL, STALE, COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY, PERMISSION_CHANGED or EVALUATOR_FAILED to COMPLETE.</p></th>
