# 12 \| Triage, Disposition and Escalation

| **Triage requirement**  | **Engineering contract**                                                                                                                   |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Ownership**           | Queue and analyst assignment are explicit; reassignment records reason and SLA impact.                                                     |
| **First review**        | Analyst confirms tenant, scope, data health, rule explanation and related activity before disposition.                                     |
| **Disposition**         | TRUE_POSITIVE, BENIGN_TRUE_POSITIVE, FALSE_POSITIVE, DUPLICATE, EXPECTED_ACTIVITY, INCOMPLETE_DATA, CUSTOMER_ACTION_REQUIRED or ESCALATED. |
| **Rationale**           | Structured reason code plus free-text evidence; AI text cannot substitute for analyst rationale.                                           |
| **Evidence**            | Relevant events, queries, screenshots/artifacts, context and communications linked with provenance.                                        |
| **Escalation**          | Severity, scope, customer impact, requested decision and response options are structured.                                                  |
| **SLA clocks**          | Start, pause, resume, breach and exception rules are machine-readable and evidence-logged.                                                 |
| **Quality review**      | Material dispositions and sampled closures require peer/supervisor review based on risk.                                                   |
| **Feedback**            | Disposition feeds detection tuning through a controlled dataset; it does not directly edit rule logic.                                     |
| **Customer visibility** | Customer-facing status and analyst-internal notes are separate, access-controlled fields.                                                  |

# 13 \| Case and Incident State Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image108.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image60.png" />

***Figure 6 - Case and incident state model.***

| **Object**               | **Creation threshold**                                                                   | **Required fields / invariants**                                                                                                           |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Case**                 | Investigation needs coordinated work, evidence, customer action or persistent ownership. | Tenant/scope, owner, severity, state, linked alerts, hypotheses, tasks, evidence, clocks, communications and decisions.                    |
| **Incident**             | Named authority declares material security incident under approved criteria.             | Incident severity, impact, start/awareness times, affected entities, command roles, notification clocks, legal/insurance flags and status. |
| **Major incident**       | Cross-tenant/platform/customer or severe impact threshold met.                           | Independent incident command, executive escalation, freeze consideration, customer/regulator communication governance.                     |
| **Post-incident review** | Incident or material case closure criteria met.                                          | Timeline, root cause, contributing controls, response effectiveness, evidence, actions, owners and deadlines.                              |

## 13.1 Transition controls

- Every transition records prior/new state, actor, reason, effective time, required evidence and policy version.

- Incident declaration and de-declaration require named authority; AI and rule engines may recommend only.

- CLOSED requires resolution basis, residual risk, customer communication status, evidence completeness and required review.

- Reopening creates a transition and preserves the prior closure decision.

- Legal hold prevents deletion but not necessary operational updates; sensitive legal notes use separately restricted fields.

- Case merges preserve source case IDs, timelines, approvals and exportability.

# 14 \| Investigation Workspace, Evidence and Chain of Custody

| **Workspace element**       | **Required behavior**                                                                                                              |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Timeline**                | Ordered events, findings, alerts, queries, decisions, approvals, actions, receipts and communications with source/effective times. |
| **Hypotheses**              | Explicit proposition, supporting/refuting evidence, owner, confidence and status; AI hypotheses are labeled.                       |
| **Tasks**                   | Owner, due time, dependency, required evidence, completion and reopen behavior.                                                    |
| **Queries**                 | Versioned query text, parameters, data scope, time range, result hash and retention policy.                                        |
| **Notes**                   | Author, visibility class, edits as new versions and links to evidence; no silent overwrite.                                        |
| **Artifacts**               | Hash, source, collector/uploader identity, custody, malware handling, retention and legal-hold state.                              |
| **Entity graph**            | Source-authority and confidence on every relationship; stale or inferred edges are visually distinct.                              |
| **Customer/internal split** | Customer-visible updates and internal analyst/security/legal material remain separately authorized.                                |
| **Chain of custody**        | Acquisition, transfer, access, transformation and export events are evidence-logged.                                               |
| **Export**                  | Case/incident package contains manifest, timelines, artifacts, decisions and integrity proofs under purpose-scoped access.         |

# 15 \| AI-Assisted Triage and Investigation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image109.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image61.png" />

***Figure 7 - AI-assisted investigation control plane.***

| **AI use**                   | **Permitted**                                         | **Required controls**                                                           | **Prohibited**                                         |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| **Alert summary**            | Summarize approved alert/event context.               | Citations, source scope, model/profile version, confidence and analyst review.  | Inventing missing facts or hiding incomplete coverage. |
| **Investigation hypothesis** | Propose hypotheses and next queries.                  | Grounding, alternative explanations, tool allowlist and human decision.         | Declaring incident truth or closing a case.            |
| **Query assistance**         | Generate bounded query proposals.                     | Read-only sandbox, cost/result limits, source visibility and analyst execution. | Unbounded production query or cross-tenant access.     |
| **Entity explanation**       | Explain relationships and risk factors.               | Source references, inference labeling and freshness.                            | Styling inference as fact.                             |
| **Response recommendation**  | Suggest governed actions.                             | Authority level, blast radius, policy references and human approval.            | Invoking action broker directly.                       |
| **Case narrative**           | Draft customer/executive updates from approved facts. | Fact whitelist, citation, review and communication-template controls.           | Automatic regulatory or legal notification.            |
| **Detection candidate**      | Draft rule/test ideas.                                | Sandbox, deterministic re-expression, replay and peer review.                   | Direct publication to production.                      |
| **Post-incident review**     | Assist timeline/root-cause synthesis.                 | Evidence citations, uncertainty and named human approver.                       | Replacing accountable root-cause decision.             |

## 15.1 AI release blockers

- Any cross-tenant retrieval or tool path.

- Any prompt-injection path that changes a recommendation, exposes restricted data or triggers a tool without authorization.

- Any AI output displayed as a system fact without source citations and human-review status.

- Any inability to disable a model, prompt, retrieval source, agent or tool independently.

- Any critical workflow that cannot continue through deterministic procedures when AI is unavailable.

- Any model/provider change without evaluation, data/region approval and controlled rollout.

# 16 \| Playbook Architecture and Execution Runtime

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image110.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image62.png" />

***Figure 8 - Playbook execution and step-level governance.***

| **Playbook field**  | **Requirement**                                                                                     |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **identity**        | Stable playbook_id and immutable version; owner and operational approver.                           |
| **purpose/scope**   | Use case, supported tenants/tier, environments, prerequisites and non-goals.                        |
| **mode**            | SIMULATION, ASSISTED or LIVE; mode is immutable for a run and prominently displayed.                |
| **inputs**          | Typed schema, source/provenance, required freshness and frozen values.                              |
| **steps**           | Typed step, actor, tool/action, precondition, timeout, retry, approval and expected output.         |
| **branching**       | Deterministic conditions or explicitly governed human/AI decision points.                           |
| **authority**       | Required R-level and tenant policy check for every side-effect step.                                |
| **compensation**    | Rollback/compensation step, eligibility, timing and residual-risk behavior.                         |
| **secrets**         | Vault references only; no embedded credentials or copied tokens.                                    |
| **evidence**        | Per-step input/output, approval, command, receipt, error and decision events.                       |
| **testing**         | Unit, simulation, connector sandbox, negative authorization, timeout, retry and compensation tests. |
| **release**         | Signed package, canary, kill switch, owner/on-call, compatibility and migration.                    |
| **terminal states** | COMPLETED, PAUSED, WAITING_APPROVAL, FAILED, COMPENSATING, CANCELLED or FROZEN.                     |

# 17 \| Response Authority R0-R4 and Policy Evaluation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image111.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image63.png" />

***Figure 9 - Response authority levels and enforcement.***

| **Level**                      | **Examples**                                                                       | **Minimum policy/approval**                                                                | **Engineering constraints**                                                                               |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R0 Observe**                 | Collect, query, enrich, notify, open case.                                         | Authenticated authorized actor/service.                                                    | No external customer-estate mutation.                                                                     |
| **R1 Recommend**               | Propose token revoke, isolation, block or disable.                                 | Named human approves each action.                                                          | Proposal and approval are separate objects; expiry enforced.                                              |
| **R2 Pre-authorized low risk** | Revoke session/token, quarantine known-malicious email, temporary indicator block. | Signed tenant policy, certified connector, reversible action, ceilings and red-team gate.  | Per-tenant signing and customer verification required; no privileged account/server isolation by default. |
| **R3 High impact**             | Disable privileged identity, isolate server, stop workload, block segment.         | Dual approval or named customer authority, simulation rehearsal and explicit blast radius. | Customer-side attestation; stricter TTL, rate and target controls.                                        |
| **R4 Emergency**               | Break-glass containment under severe active threat.                                | Time-boxed emergency authority, immediate escalation and post-review.                      | Hard ceilings, independent monitoring and automatic evidence; never a standing mode.                      |

## 17.1 Policy inputs and stable outcomes

| **Input family**           | **Examples**                                                                             |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant policy**          | Allowed actions, target classes, environments, blackout windows, contacts and max rates. |
| **Actor**                  | Identity, role, delegation, JIT elevation, step-up and SoD.                              |
| **Case context**           | Case/incident state, severity, evidence, authority request and legal/contract flags.     |
| **Action**                 | Type, parameters, reversibility, connector certification, target and blast radius.       |
| **Time/state**             | Approval age, policy version, freeze state, service health and customer change window.   |
| **Entitlement/obligation** | Technology entitlement versus human-service authorization and contract scope.            |
| **Decision**               | **Meaning**                                                                              |
| **ALLOW**                  | All mandatory conditions satisfied; issue a bounded authorization result.                |
| **ALLOW_WITH_CONDITIONS**  | Additional step-up, approval, simulation or parameter restriction required.              |
| **DENY**                   | Policy explicitly prohibits the action.                                                  |
| **INDETERMINATE**          | Required context or policy unavailable; fail closed.                                     |
| **FROZEN**                 | Safety control blocks the action regardless of ordinary authorization.                   |
| **EXPIRED**                | Approval/policy/token no longer valid; re-evaluation required.                           |

# 18 \| Action Broker, Per-Tenant Signing and Customer Attestation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image112.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image64.png" />

***Figure 10 - Isolated action broker and customer-side command attestation.***

| **Command field**    | **Mandatory binding**                                                                                        |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **identity**         | command_id, proposal_id, tenant_id, action type/version and regional cell.                                   |
| **target**           | Canonical target ID, target type, environment and connector endpoint.                                        |
| **authority**        | R-level, actor, approval references, tenant-policy version and entitlement result.                           |
| **parameters**       | Typed, allowlisted and canonicalized; free-form shell/script payloads prohibited unless separately approved. |
| **safety**           | Blast-radius estimate, rate bucket, idempotency key, simulation flag, reversibility/compensation profile.    |
| **time/replay**      | Issued time, expiry, nonce and command sequence.                                                             |
| **integrity**        | Per-tenant signature, signing-key ID/version and algorithm profile.                                          |
| **expected receipt** | Receipt schema, timeout, expected observed-state verification and rollback token behavior.                   |
| **evidence**         | Case/playbook references, reason, trace ID and immutable audit event.                                        |

## 18.1 Broker hard boundaries

- The core, AI gateway and connector runtime cannot invoke customer actions except through the broker contract.

- Broker workloads hold no exportable tenant private keys; signing is a scoped HSM/KMS operation under independent policy.

- Connector credentials remain tenant-scoped and cannot be reused by another tenant or action family.

- Customer-side integrations reject unsigned, expired, replayed, wrong-tenant, wrong-target or policy-incompatible commands.

- Global and per-tenant mass-action monitors operate independently from the normal broker request path.

- Production broker changes require canary tenants, red-team evidence and dual-controlled rollout.

# 19 \| Approvals, Simulation, Blast Radius, Rate Limits and Freeze

| **Control**                 | **Required behavior**                                                                                                                                |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Approval scope**          | Binds exact action type, target/target set, parameters, tenant, environment, case, expiry and permitted retry count.                                 |
| **Dual control**            | Required approvers must be distinct eligible principals; self-approval and hidden delegated equivalence are blocked.                                 |
| **Step-up**                 | Phishing-resistant reauthentication for R3/R4 and selected R2 actions; session age and device posture checked.                                       |
| **Simulation**              | Executes policy, target resolution and connector path without side effect; output includes expected commands, affected targets and rollback profile. |
| **Blast radius**            | Count, criticality, dependency and business-service impact; unknown target scope blocks R3+.                                                         |
| **Rate ceilings**           | Global, tenant, action, connector and target-class limits; ceilings cannot be raised within the same action transaction.                             |
| **Blackout/change windows** | Customer policy controls time restrictions; emergency override is separately authorized and evidenced.                                               |
| **Freeze switch**           | Out-of-band, dual-controlled ability to halt action issuance globally, regionally, by tenant, connector or action family.                            |
| **Freeze recovery**         | Root cause, integrity check, policy review, customer communication and staged re-enable; no automatic unfreeze.                                      |
| **Approval evidence**       | Decision, rationale, viewed blast radius, conditions, step-up receipt and policy version retained.                                                   |

<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>MASS-ACTION RULE</strong></p>
<p>No UI, API, playbook or AI tool may bypass blast-radius calculation and rate ceilings. Bulk response is a distinct high-risk action, not repeated low-risk calls.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>

# 20 \| Receipts, Rollback, Compensation and Reconciliation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image113.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image65.png" />

***Figure 11 - Response outcome, compensation and reconciliation.***

| **Action property**          | **Definition**                                                             | **Required UI/policy behavior**                                                     |
|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **REVERSIBLE**               | A tested inverse action can restore prior state within declared limits.    | Display rollback method, deadline and dependencies; capture rollback token/receipt. |
| **COMPENSABLE**              | No true inverse exists, but a separate action can reduce or offset impact. | Label as compensation, not rollback; require residual-risk review.                  |
| **IRREVERSIBLE**             | Action cannot be reliably undone.                                          | R3/R4 by default, heightened approval and explicit irreversible warning.            |
| **CONDITIONALLY_REVERSIBLE** | Rollback depends on timing/state/provider support.                         | Show conditions and verify at execution time.                                       |
| **READ_ONLY**                | No customer-estate mutation.                                               | R0; still audit access and query scope.                                             |
| **Receipt/outcome state**    | **Meaning**                                                                | **Required response**                                                               |
| **ACCEPTED**                 | Execution point accepted command but outcome not yet verified.             | Continue observed-state check.                                                      |
| **SUCCEEDED**                | Expected state observed and reconciled.                                    | Record completion and monitor.                                                      |
| **REJECTED**                 | Local policy, signature, expiry, target or provider rejected.              | Record reason; do not retry blindly.                                                |
| **FAILED**                   | Execution attempted and returned known failure.                            | Assess side effects; compensate if required.                                        |
| **PARTIAL**                  | Some targets/steps succeeded.                                              | Freeze further expansion; enumerate affected targets and reconcile.                 |
| **UNKNOWN**                  | No reliable receipt or observed state.                                     | Treat as material uncertainty; escalate and avoid duplicate side effects.           |
| **ROLLED_BACK**              | Verified inverse action restored declared prior state.                     | Retain original and rollback evidence.                                              |
| **COMPENSATED**              | Mitigating action completed but prior state not restored.                  | Record residual risk and customer decision.                                         |

# 21 \| Threat Intelligence and Indicator Operationalization

| **Control area**       | **Requirement**                                                                                                            |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source and license** | Record provider, TLP/license, redistribution rights, jurisdiction and customer-use restrictions.                           |
| **Confidence**         | Provider confidence, Zoiko assessment, corroboration and tenant relevance remain separate fields.                          |
| **Lifecycle**          | First/last seen, valid from/to, expiry, revocation, supersession and historical retention.                                 |
| **Normalization**      | Canonical indicator type/value with source-native preservation and normalization version.                                  |
| **Operationalization** | Indicator set version is bound to detection/replay; changes do not rewrite historical alerts.                              |
| **Action use**         | Blocking/quarantine requires stronger policy, confidence, freshness and false-positive controls than detection/enrichment. |
| **Privacy**            | Personal or sensitive indicators are minimized, purpose-bound and region-controlled.                                       |
| **Customer context**   | Customer allowlists and known infrastructure are tenant-scoped, expiring and evidence-backed.                              |
| **Quality**            | Hit rate, false positives, stale percentage and action outcomes monitored by source/set.                                   |
| **AI**                 | AI may summarize intelligence but cannot invent source confidence or remove licensing restrictions.                        |

# 22 \| Communications, Notification Clocks and Customer Visibility

| **Object/control**           | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                   |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Communication template**   | Versioned, audience-specific, severity-aware, legally/commercially reviewed and localization-ready.           |
| **Facts**                    | Generated from approved structured facts; AI draft remains review-required and cited.                         |
| **Clock**                    | Type, trigger event, start/awareness time, jurisdiction/contract, owner, target, pause rule and breach state. |
| **Delivery**                 | Channel, recipient, encryption, delivery state, acknowledgment and escalation path.                           |
| **Customer update**          | Case/incident scope, current status, actions, customer requests, limitations and next update time.            |
| **Internal notes**           | Separate visibility class; never accidentally exported to customer or auditor.                                |
| **Regulator/insurer/legal**  | Specialized access and approval; engineering supplies clocks/evidence but does not decide legal obligation.   |
| **Failure**                  | Delivery failure opens escalation; it does not mark notification complete.                                    |
| **Evidence**                 | Rendered content hash, template version, approver, delivery receipt and acknowledgment retained.              |
| **Status page/trust center** | Only approved service facts and claims; customer-specific incident data never leaks to public status.         |

# 23 \| SOC Handover, Quality and Human-Service Controls

| **Capability**            | **Required platform support**                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Shift handover**        | Structured open cases, commitments, watch items, pending approvals, degraded coverage and acknowledged transfer.                  |
| **Queue ownership**       | Region, certification, language, service tier, workload and conflict-of-interest aware assignment.                                |
| **Quality sampling**      | Risk-based sample of dispositions, closures, communications and response actions with findings and corrective action.             |
| **Supervisor review**     | Mandatory for selected severities, exceptions, R3/R4, customer disputes and high-risk closure.                                    |
| **Analyst certification** | Action and customer access constrained by current competence/certification and training status.                                   |
| **Service obligations**   | Technology events link to applicable human obligation, but software cannot invent or expand contracted coverage.                  |
| **Overflow partner**      | Delegated tenant scopes, approved tooling, handover, monitoring and no parallel uncontrolled stack.                               |
| **Performance metrics**   | MTTA/MTTR and throughput are contextual; quality, evidence completeness, customer impact and premature-closure controls dominate. |
| **Fatigue/safety**        | Rate and workload signals support staffing escalation; critical actions are never auto-approved due to backlog.                   |
| **Customer review**       | Service-review metrics reconcile detections, cases, actions, coverage gaps, obligations and improvement work.                     |

# 24 \| Failure, Degraded and Emergency Operating Modes

| **Failure**                          | **Required degraded behavior**                                                                             | **Prohibited behavior**                            |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| **AI gateway unavailable**           | Use deterministic queries, runbooks and human workflow; show AI unavailable.                               | Routing restricted data to an unapproved provider. |
| **Search unavailable**               | Continue durable ingestion and point detection where possible; queue investigations and expose limitation. | Dropping telemetry or showing no risk.             |
| **Enrichment unavailable**           | Evaluate only rules with declared fallback; mark context incomplete.                                       | Using stale cache as current without label.        |
| **Connector degraded**               | Mark coverage windows, pause unsupported actions and attempt backfill/reconciliation.                      | Rendering tenant healthy.                          |
| **Case service degraded**            | Persist commands/events durably; restrict actions requiring unavailable case authority.                    | Executing unlinked high-impact actions.            |
| **Authorization/policy unavailable** | Fail closed for external action; preserve observe-only paths where safe.                                   | Default-allow or cached indefinite privilege.      |
| **Action broker unavailable**        | Continue detection/investigation; queue no live action unless command validity can be preserved.           | Direct connector action from core.                 |
| **Receipt missing**                  | Outcome UNKNOWN; reconcile observed state and escalate.                                                    | Blind retry that may duplicate side effects.       |
| **Signing/HSM unavailable**          | No signed commands; R0/R1 remain.                                                                          | Fallback to unsigned command.                      |
| **Freeze activated**                 | Block scoped action issuance, display prominently, continue evidence and investigation.                    | Silent auto-unfreeze.                              |
| **Region outage**                    | Apply tested failover/residency policy; preserve accepted telemetry and evidence reconciliation.           | Cross-region transfer without approved mechanism.  |
| **Evidence ledger degraded**         | Block material response/closure assertions requiring missing audit evidence as defined by policy.          | Continue silently without auditability.            |

# 25 \| Crown-Jewel Threat Model and Abuse Cases

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image114.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image66.png" />

***Figure 12 - Crown-jewel threat and blast-radius control model.***

| **Threat / abuse case**                  | **Mandatory controls**                                                                              | **Release evidence**                                      |
|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cross-tenant alert/case access**       | Tenant context at every layer, RLS/index/object isolation, negative tests and scoped observability. | Automated cross-tenant test suite and penetration test.   |
| **Malicious rule or playbook**           | Signed content, review, tests, canary, kill switch and change evidence.                             | Content supply-chain verification and rollback rehearsal. |
| **Broker mass action**                   | Per-tenant signing, rate ceilings, customer verification and independent freeze.                    | External red team before R2 GA; mass-action simulation.   |
| **Approval bypass**                      | Target-side policy, step-up, SoD and immutable approval object.                                     | Negative authorization and replay tests.                  |
| **Command replay/substitution**          | Nonce, expiry, target binding, sequence and signature verification.                                 | Connector certification test.                             |
| **AI prompt injection/tool abuse**       | Retrieval controls, tool allowlist, target-side reauthorization and adversarial corpus.             | Per-release AI security evaluation.                       |
| **Connector credential theft**           | Tenant-scoped vault credentials, workload isolation, rotation and least privilege.                  | Connector threat model and credential-revocation test.    |
| **Insider concealment**                  | No silent mutation, immutable timeline, JIT access and independent audit evidence.                  | Privileged-access test and audit reconciliation.          |
| **Suppression abuse**                    | Scoped/expiring policy, approval, metrics and review.                                               | Suppression audit and stale-policy test.                  |
| **Supply-chain compromise**              | Signed/reproducible builds, SBOM/provenance and canary tenants.                                     | Admission and provenance verification.                    |
| **Denial of wallet/queue exhaustion**    | Quotas, budgets, backpressure, rate limits and cost telemetry.                                      | Load/cost test at reference envelope.                     |
| **Customer command endpoint compromise** | Local policy, pinned keys, signed receipts and target verification.                                 | Customer-side attestation conformance test.               |

# 26 \| Privacy, Residency, Retention and Legal Hold

| **Control**             | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                                |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Purpose limitation**  | Event use, investigation, AI, action, export and customer communication each carry an approved purpose.                    |
| **Minimization**        | Collect and display only fields needed; sensitive content is masked by default and revealed under purpose-scoped access.   |
| **Residency**           | Telemetry, case artifacts, AI processing, action routing and exports remain in approved regional paths.                    |
| **Legal hold**          | Cases/incidents/artifacts can be held without freezing necessary operational updates; hold access is restricted.           |
| **Retention**           | Rules by event, finding, alert, case, incident, action, receipt and communication; case closure is not immediate deletion. |
| **Deletion**            | Deletion/tombstone behavior respects evidence integrity, contract and hold; derived reports/AI memory are assessed.        |
| **AI data**             | Customer data cannot train models without explicit authority; prompts/outputs follow approved retention and region.        |
| **Sensitive artifacts** | Malware, credentials, personal data and privileged/legal content use separate storage/access profiles.                     |
| **Export**              | Purpose-scoped package with manifest, integrity, redaction and access evidence.                                            |
| **Support access**      | JIT, customer/owner approval where required, masking, session recording and evidence.                                      |

# 27 \| Observability, SLOs, Capacity and Unit Economics

| **Metric / SLO**                     | **Definition / target**                                                    | **Control use**                                                      |
|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **detection_latency_seconds{class}** | Durable acceptance to alert by point/windowed/sequence/batch class.        | Rule and platform SLO; customer claims only after measured evidence. |
| **replay_match_rate**                | Eligible historical alerts reproduced under frozen inputs.                 | Release gate for runtime/content changes.                            |
| **coverage_health**                  | Expected sources/events healthy, degraded, stale or unavailable by tenant. | Customer visibility and confidence.                                  |
| **alert_to_triage_seconds**          | Alert creation to qualified first triage by severity/tier.                 | Service operations and staffing.                                     |
| **case_mtta / mttr**                 | Acknowledgment and resolution with exclusions and severity.                | Operational planning; not sole quality measure.                      |
| **action_authorization_latency**     | Proposal to final policy/approval result.                                  | User experience and high-risk bottleneck monitoring.                 |
| **action_success_rate**              | Verified reconciled success, not API acceptance.                           | Connector and response quality.                                      |
| **unknown_outcome_rate**             | Actions without verified final state.                                      | P0/P1 reliability signal.                                            |
| **rollback/compensation_success**    | Verified restoration or mitigation by action class.                        | Action catalog eligibility.                                          |
| **AI grounded-output rate**          | Sampled outputs with valid citations and no material fabrication.          | Model/prompt release gate.                                           |
| **analyst_quality_rate**             | Risk-based review pass and corrective-action closure.                      | Service quality dominates throughput.                                |
| **cost per evaluated GB/event**      | Fully loaded analytics cost at reference envelope.                         | Release-blocking unit-economics guardrail.                           |
| **cases per analyst shift**          | Contextual workload measure by severity/complexity.                        | Staffing; never used alone to drive automation.                      |
| **broker_headroom**                  | Action throughput before configured ceilings and failure threshold.        | Capacity and mass-action safety.                                     |
| **freeze_test_success**              | Scheduled freeze activation and staged recovery pass.                      | Operational readiness.                                               |

# 28 \| Testing, Validation, Red Team and Release Gates

| **Test family**            | **Minimum coverage**                                                                | **Blocking condition**                                           |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Rule unit/contract**     | Positive, negative, missing data, late data, boundary and explanation.              | Any material false positive/negative outside approved threshold. |
| **Replay regression**      | Historical/synthetic corpus with exact context and runtime.                         | Nondeterminism or unexplained material change.                   |
| **Correlation scale**      | State size, window, out-of-order, burst and recovery.                               | Latency/cost beyond guardrail or state loss.                     |
| **Tenant isolation**       | API, DB, search, queue, cache, export, AI retrieval and observability.              | Any cross-tenant path.                                           |
| **Case state**             | All transitions, authorization, clocks, merge/reopen and legal hold.                | Unattributed or invalid transition.                              |
| **Playbook simulation**    | Branches, approvals, retries, timeout, compensation and freeze.                     | Unbounded loop or side effect in simulation.                     |
| **Action authorization**   | R0-R4, SoD, expiry, rate, blackout and policy failure.                              | Any allow on missing/indeterminate authority.                    |
| **Command attestation**    | Signature, nonce, expiry, target, replay, wrong tenant and key rotation.            | Any invalid command executes.                                    |
| **Outcome reconciliation** | Success, rejection, partial, unknown, rollback and compensation.                    | API success misclassified as outcome success.                    |
| **AI adversarial**         | Direct/indirect prompt injection, tool abuse, leakage, poisoning, denial of wallet. | Material unsafe output/tool path.                                |
| **Failure/chaos**          | Search, AI, policy, broker, HSM, connector, region and evidence outages.            | Silent healthy state or unsafe bypass.                           |
| **Security red team**      | Broker, tenant isolation, command endpoint and AI chain.                            | Critical/high unresolved before R2+.                             |
| **Accessibility/UX**       | All required states, non-color cues, keyboard/screen-reader and action clarity.     | Hidden authority, uncertainty or inaccessible high-risk control. |
| **Canary/rollback**        | Zoiko synthetic tenants then approved customer cohort.                              | Unable to stop/rollback content or deployment safely.            |
| **Cost/headroom**          | Reference scale and worst permitted tenant profile.                                 | Unit-economics or capacity guardrail breach.                     |

## 28.1 P0 release blockers

- Any cross-tenant access or action path.

- Any production rule, playbook or action package lacking signed provenance and required tests.

- Any alert or case decision that cannot be reconstructed from controlled inputs and versions.

- Any R2+ command without per-tenant signing and customer-side verification.

- Any external action allowed when authorization is unavailable or indeterminate.

- Any unbounded mass-action path or inoperative freeze control.

- Any AI tool path that bypasses target-service authorization.

- Any UI that hides incomplete data, authority level, blast radius, approval or rollback limitations.

- Any critical data/action outcome that cannot be reconciled after restore.

- Any unsupported public detection, response or assurance claim.

## 29.1 Mandatory states and UX doctrine

| **State**                     | **Required treatment**                                                                      |
|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Loading / resolving**       | Show scope and requested time; never display stale prior data as current.                   |
| **Empty / first use**         | Explain prerequisites and next action; distinguish no data from no findings.                |
| **Nominal / populated**       | Display tenant, environment, region, time, authority and evidence links.                    |
| **Partial / incomplete**      | Non-suppressible limitation and affected decisions/actions.                                 |
| **Stale / degraded**          | Age/source health and restricted functions visible.                                         |
| **Error / unavailable**       | Stable reason/correlation ID and safe recovery path.                                        |
| **Unauthorized / restricted** | Separate from system error; show request/escalation path without leaking sensitive content. |
| **Frozen / safety stop**      | Prominent scope/reason; live action affordances disabled; investigation remains available.  |

## 31.1 Definition of Ready

- Requirement IDs and acceptance criteria are approved and linked.

- Object/schema authority and owner are identified.

- Tenant, identity, privacy, residency, evidence and AI implications are resolved.

- Failure/degraded/unauthorized/frozen states are specified.

- Response authority and customer-policy impact are explicit.

- Experience contract and accessibility states exist where user-facing.

- Test data, replay corpus, connector sandbox and performance envelope are available.

- Relevant ADRs and exceptions are closed or time-bound.

## 31.2 Definition of Done

- Code/content is reviewed, signed and linked to controlled requirements.

- Unit, integration, replay, isolation, authorization, AI, performance and failure tests pass.

- All material decisions/actions emit required audit and evidence records.

- SLOs, dashboards, alerts and runbooks are operational.

- Rollback, compensation, kill/freeze and recovery paths are tested as applicable.

- Canary and staged rollout evidence is complete.

- Customer-visible uncertainty, authority and limitation states are verified.

- Release Evidence Register contains approvals, artifacts and residual risks.

- Documentation and machine-readable registries are current.

- No unsupported claim or unapproved customer-specific fork exists.

# Document Control and Navigation

| **Control**                  | **Value**                                                                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Normative language**       | MUST = mandatory; SHOULD = expected unless an approved exception exists; MAY = optional.                                                                                |
| **Implementation authority** | Approved evidence contracts, collector/evaluator packages, cryptographic profiles, retention policies and release manifests constrained by the parent masters and ADRs. |
| **Truth boundary**           | The ledger proves integrity and history of referenced records; it does not by itself prove semantic truth, completeness, certification or legal compliance.             |
| **Conflict rule**            | Stop affected work; do not choose between conflicting evidence schema, control content, retention, cryptographic, package or register entries.                          |
| **Change authority**         | Material schema, evaluator, anchoring, witness, retention, package or verifier changes require owner approval, compatibility/replay evidence and release traceability.  |
| **Distribution**             | Only current controlled copies through approved engineering repositories; key hierarchy, production witness topology and red-team details are separately gated.         |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                                                    | **Risk if uncorrected**                                                                                                          | **Required refinement**                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Integrity, completeness and truth are treated as one property.**             | A cryptographically intact artifact may still be false, irrelevant, stale or incomplete; a green status can overstate assurance. | Model integrity, provenance, completeness, freshness, semantic evaluation and approval as separate dimensions with independent states.     |
| **The evidence ledger is described as immutable without defining correction.** | Errors, privacy requests and schema fixes either force silent mutation or leave unusable data.                                   | Use append-only correction, supersession and tombstone records; never rewrite a frozen package or prior chain history.                     |
| **Hashing is presented as sufficient proof.**                                  | A platform operator could rewrite a full private chain and recompute hashes after compromise.                                    | Use per-tenant chains, HSM-signed Merkle roots, two independent witnesses and customer-held receipts.                                      |
| **Collection success is mistaken for control effectiveness.**                  | A connector can submit irrelevant or partial data and still appear healthy.                                                      | Separate collector health, expected-evidence coverage, evaluator result and control assessment.                                            |
| **Audit packages are live reports.**                                           | Later schema, enrichment or evaluator changes can alter a prior audit outcome and destroy reproducibility.                       | Freeze exact inputs, outputs, versions, proofs, limitations and rendered facts; supersede by new package only.                             |
| **The verifier is assumed to trust Zoiko services.**                           | An auditor cannot independently validate the platform that produced the assertion.                                               | Provide a standalone, reproducibly built verifier with public schemas, test vectors and offline operation.                                 |
| **AI-generated summaries are treated as evidence.**                            | Fabrication, prompt injection or provider drift can enter compliance assertions.                                                 | AI output is a derived artifact with full provenance; source evidence, completeness and compliance remain deterministic/human governed.    |
| **Retention and immutability are treated as absolute.**                        | Legal hold, contractual retention and deletion rights can conflict; uncontrolled retention creates privacy exposure.             | Resolve policy before deletion, retain minimal tombstone proof, use key destruction where appropriate and attest remaining backup windows. |
| **Restore procedures focus on availability.**                                  | A restore can create an internally consistent but externally divergent history.                                                  | Reconcile chain heads and package roots against independent witnesses before resuming normal writes.                                       |
| **Framework content is embedded directly in evaluator code.**                  | Licensing, update and interpretation drift become invisible software defects.                                                    | Reference licensed framework identifiers and versioned Zoiko control objectives; keep content rights and legal review in R12.              |

# 02 \| Executive Engineering Mandate

Build ZoikoShield so that every material security, governance and AI outcome can be reconstructed from attributable source artifacts, tamper-evident history, declared completeness, version-bound evaluation and explicit human authority; and so that a customer or auditor can independently verify a frozen package after platform change, outage or customer exit.

| **Mandate**                         | **Engineering consequence**                                                                                          |
|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Preserve source authority**       | Keep native bytes or a verifiable source reference, source identity, scope, time and collection receipt.             |
| **Separate proof dimensions**       | Integrity, truth, completeness, freshness, control effectiveness and approval are never collapsed into one flag.     |
| **Append, do not overwrite**        | Corrections, supersessions, deletion and reassessment produce new records linked to prior history.                   |
| **Make gaps first-class**           | Missing, stale, unauthorized, unhealthy or failed evidence remains visible and blocks unsupported green status.      |
| **Bind every conclusion**           | A control assessment stores exact evidence, mappings, context, evaluator version, limitations and reviewer decision. |
| **Anchor outside Zoiko**            | Externally witnessed roots and customer-held receipts make post-compromise rewriting detectable.                     |
| **Verify independently**            | Open formats and an offline verifier allow customers and auditors to check integrity without a live Zoiko account.   |
| **Use AI as assistance**            | AI may explain or propose; it may not originate source evidence, determine completeness or sign an assurance claim.  |
| **Treat economics as architecture** | Evidence retention, package duplication, search and verification costs remain measured and release-gated.            |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Disclosure Boundary

## 3.1 In scope

- Evidence artifacts, metadata, derived facts, evaluations, assessments, assertions, packages and verification results.

- Collector identity, permissions, source authority, collection scheduling, validation, quarantine and health.

- Expected-evidence rules, coverage reconciliation, gap classification, freshness and completeness states.

- Content-addressed evidence vault, WORM profiles, per-tenant ledger, Merkle aggregation and independent witnesses.

- Deterministic evaluator runtime, versioned mappings, human review, replay and supersession.

- Audit package build, freeze, approval, export, independent verification and offboarding portability.

- Privacy, residency, minimization, redaction, retention, legal hold, deletion and deletion attestation.

- AI-assisted classification, summarization, mapping and explanation under model-gateway controls.

- Failure, restore, chain reconciliation, operational monitoring, testing, release evidence and customer visibility.

## 3.2 Out of scope

- Certification, legal advice, regulator decisions or guarantees that a customer is compliant.

- Production private keys, HSM ceremonies, witness credentials and unresolved exploit details; these remain in EC-3 annexes.

- Full copyrighted standards text; evaluators consume licensed identifiers and approved control abstractions.

- Customer-specific evidence, credentials or live production data in the engineering document.

- Final commercial retention tiers, pricing or public claims; engineering implements register-controlled policy and measurement.

- An unbounded blockchain or public disclosure of tenant evidence. External anchoring publishes commitments, not customer content.

# 04 \| Binding Evidence and Assurance Principles

| **ID**    | **Principle**                   | **Binding consequence**                                                                                            |
|-----------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EA-01** | Evidence before assertion       | No material control, risk, incident or AI assertion completes without linked evidence and declared scope.          |
| **EA-02** | Independent verifiability       | A frozen package must be checkable without trusting Zoiko databases, staff or live services.                       |
| **EA-03** | Integrity is not truth          | Cryptography proves byte/history integrity; semantic truth and sufficiency require source and evaluation controls. |
| **EA-04** | Completeness is declared        | Coverage is measured against expected evidence; absence is never silently treated as compliant.                    |
| **EA-05** | No silent mutation              | Corrections, deletion, mapping changes and reassessment create new linked records.                                 |
| **EA-06** | Tenant context everywhere       | Tenant, environment, region, legal entity, purpose and data class bind every artifact and operation.               |
| **EA-07** | Source-native preservation      | Normalization never destroys the native source or its verifiable reference and parser provenance.                  |
| **EA-08** | Deterministic critical path     | Ledger append, integrity, completeness and control decisions do not depend on an LLM.                              |
| **EA-09** | Version-bound conclusions       | Every derived fact, test and assertion records the exact parser, mapping, evaluator, policy and input versions.    |
| **EA-10** | Failure is explicit             | Quarantine, stale, partial, unhealthy, anchor-delayed and integrity-incident states are distinct and visible.      |
| **EA-11** | Least evidence necessary        | Collect and retain only the data required for the declared purpose and assurance objective.                        |
| **EA-12** | Open exit                       | Customer exports preserve original artifacts, open metadata, package proofs and verifier compatibility.            |
| **EA-13** | Dual control for proof roots    | Anchor keys, package approval and integrity-incident closure require segregated authority.                         |
| **EA-14** | Economics are measurable        | Collection, vault, retention, search, package and verification cost are attributable by tenant and evidence type.  |
| **EA-15** | Claims follow verified evidence | Product, customer and public claims require current package or runtime evidence and Claim Register approval.       |

# 05 \| Source-of-Truth and Controlled Object Model

| **Object**                 | **Authority and mutable state**                                                                                      | **Mandatory distinction**                            |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| **Evidence artifact**      | Immutable bytes or verifiable external reference in the evidence vault; metadata may be superseded, not overwritten. | What was collected from a source.                    |
| **Evidence record**        | Ledger-bound metadata describing source, scope, time, hash, collector, retention and state.                          | Proof envelope, not the content itself.              |
| **Observed fact**          | Versioned parser/normalizer output linked to one or more artifacts.                                                  | Derived statement, not source evidence.              |
| **Expected-evidence rule** | Controlled declaration of what evidence should exist for a scoped control and period.                                | Basis for completeness/gap detection.                |
| **Evaluation run**         | Immutable execution record binding exact inputs, evaluator and output.                                               | Automated or manual test, not final assertion.       |
| **Control assessment**     | Versioned interpretation of evaluation results, evidence states and human decision.                                  | Conclusion with scope and limitations.               |
| **Assertion**              | Approved customer-facing statement linked to assessments and package/runtime snapshot.                               | May support a claim; never self-authorizing.         |
| **Audit package**          | Frozen manifest of artifacts, results, mappings, approvals, limitations and proofs.                                  | Portable audit snapshot.                             |
| **Anchor receipt**         | Signed root, inclusion/witness receipts and publication metadata.                                                    | Independent tamper-evidence.                         |
| **Verifier result**        | Independent check of package bytes, proofs, schemas and declared coverage.                                           | Verification outcome, not certification.             |
| **Deletion tombstone**     | Minimal append-only record of authorized content removal or key destruction.                                         | Proof of deletion without retaining deleted content. |
| **Claim record**           | Approved public or contractual claim with evidence, scope, expiry and wording.                                       | Governed outside engineering runtime authority.      |

## 5.1 Source-of-truth hierarchy

1.  Controlled masters and approved ADRs define architecture and assurance doctrine.

2.  Machine-readable registers define current evidence types, controls, collectors, evaluators, retention, SLOs and approved claims.

3.  Signed schemas, policies, evaluator packages and release manifests define executable behavior.

4.  The ledger and content vault are runtime authorities for immutable evidence history.

5.  Frozen packages and external witness receipts are authorities for historical audit snapshots.

6.  User interfaces are projections and may never become the only source of a material status or approval.

# 06 \| Evidence Lifecycle and State Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image118.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.02569in" alt="Image: image46.png" />

***Figure 3 - Evidence lifecycle and state transitions.***

| **State dimension** | **Allowed states**                                                          | **Required behavior**                                                                                         |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Intake**          | RECEIVED, AUTHENTICATED, VALIDATED, QUARANTINED, REJECTED                   | Invalid or unauthenticated artifacts never enter the authoritative ledger as usable evidence.                 |
| **Integrity**       | UNVERIFIED, VERIFIED, SIGNATURE_FAILED, HASH_MISMATCH, CHAIN_DIVERGED       | Integrity failure opens an incident and blocks affected assertions.                                           |
| **Coverage**        | NOT_EXPECTED, EXPECTED, COMPLETE, PARTIAL, MISSING, UNKNOWN                 | COMPLETE is computed only against a versioned expected set.                                                   |
| **Freshness**       | CURRENT, NEAR_EXPIRY, STALE, NOT_APPLICABLE                                 | Threshold and grace behavior are evidence-type and control scoped.                                            |
| **Collector**       | HEALTHY, DEGRADED, RATE_LIMITED, PERMISSION_CHANGED, UNAUTHORIZED, FAILED   | Collector health affects coverage and the applicable window; it never silently preserves prior green status.  |
| **Evaluator**       | QUEUED, RUNNING, PASSED, FAILED, PARTIAL, UNKNOWN, ERROR, NON_DETERMINISTIC | Operational error is distinct from control failure.                                                           |
| **Anchor**          | PENDING, PUBLISHED, WITNESS_PARTIAL, DELAYED, FAILED, RECONCILING           | Anchor delay is visible and measured; it does not change artifact bytes but weakens rewrite-detection timing. |
| **Retention**       | ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, HELD, EXPIRY_PENDING, DELETED, TOMBSTONED                 | Deletion and hold decisions are explicit and evidenced.                                                       |
| **Package**         | DRAFT, PRECHECK_FAILED, READY, FROZEN, APPROVED, SUPERSEDED, WITHDRAWN      | Frozen packages are immutable; correction creates a new package version.                                      |

# 07 \| Evidence Object Contract and Content Vault

| **Field group** | **Mandatory fields**                                                                          | **Engineering requirement**                                             |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**    | evidence_id, tenant_id, legal_entity_id, environment_id, region_id                            | Server-issued identifiers; tenant and region immutable after intake.    |
| **Source**      | source_system_id, source_object_id, source_authority, collector_id, collector_version         | Source and collector are separately attributable.                       |
| **Time**        | source_observed_at, source_period_start/end, received_at, trusted_time_receipt, clock_quality | Preserve source and platform time; record skew and uncertainty.         |
| **Scope**       | control_scope, asset/identity/resource refs, purpose, data_class, jurisdiction                | Scopes use canonical identifiers and support many-to-many links.        |
| **Content**     | content_hash, hash_algorithm, canonicalization_profile, media_type, size, vault_uri/reference | Vault URI is not a public locator; content hash is the durable address. |
| **Integrity**   | collector_signature, signing_key_id, ledger_sequence, entry_hash, prior_hash, anchor_batch_id | All cryptographic algorithms and key IDs are explicit and agile.        |
| **State**       | intake, integrity, freshness, completeness, retention and legal_hold states                   | State transitions append events and are auditable.                      |
| **Lineage**     | parent_artifact_ids, parser, normalizer, mapping and enrichment versions                      | Derived artifacts preserve full upstream lineage.                       |
| **Governance**  | retention_profile, deletion_due_at, hold_refs, access_policy, owner                           | Policy resolution is visible and versioned.                             |
| **Limitations** | known_gaps, source limitations, redactions, excluded fields, confidence notes                 | Limitations travel with packages and reports.                           |

## 7.1 Vault invariants

- Artifacts are immutable after successful commit; metadata correction creates a new evidence record linked by SUPERSEDES or CORRECTS.

- WORM/object-lock profiles are enabled by controlled retention class, not globally and irreversibly for every artifact.

- Large telemetry may remain in the security lakehouse until package freeze, but the evidence record must bind the exact immutable segment or snapshot; required bytes are copied into package storage before source retention expires.

- Encryption uses tenant and region context; keys and vault objects cannot be moved across regions by an application request.

- Deduplication may reuse identical content bytes within the same authorized tenant/key scope, but never merge tenant metadata or weaken deletion semantics.

- Preview and extraction services are sandboxed, malware-aware and unable to modify the authoritative artifact.

# 08 \| Collector Identity, Provenance and Collection Architecture

| **Control area**        | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                                                                            |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**            | Every collector instance has a short-lived workload identity bound to tenant, source, environment, region and approved evidence types.                               |
| **Permissions**         | Requested and granted scopes are stored separately; drift or permission loss changes collector state and affected coverage windows.                                  |
| **Version**             | Collector binary, configuration, schema, parser and source API version are recorded on every receipt.                                                                |
| **Source time**         | Original source timestamp, extraction time, receipt time and clock/skew quality are preserved.                                                                       |
| **Native preservation** | Source-native payload or a cryptographically bound immutable source segment is retained where contract and minimization permit.                                      |
| **Manifest**            | Batch/file collections include manifest, item count, byte count, hashes and completion receipt; partial batches do not appear complete.                              |
| **Replay**              | Collection requests and receipts use stable idempotency keys; duplicates are detected but remain attributable.                                                       |
| **Quarantine**          | Malformed, unsigned, out-of-scope, oversized, malware-bearing or residency-ineligible artifacts enter a tenant-isolated quarantine with expiry.                      |
| **Revocation**          | Collector credentials can be revoked per tenant without affecting unrelated tenants; revocation propagates within the approved SLO.                                  |
| **Health**              | Health combines authentication, permission, schema, rate, schedule, backlog and last-success state; a heartbeat alone is insufficient.                               |
| **Manual evidence**     | Uploader identity, source declaration, reason, review requirement, content hash and expiry are mandatory; manual evidence never masquerades as automated collection. |
| **External assessor**   | Third-party reports preserve assessor identity, contract/scope, version, signature where available, limitations and validity period.                                 |

## 8.1 Collector trust boundary

- A collector can submit evidence only for registered evidence types and source scopes; it cannot author control results, package approvals or public claims.

- Collector signing keys are unique by controlled identity scope and cannot sign ledger roots or response actions.

- Connector runtime is network-segmented from the evidence ledger writer and action broker; intake uses authenticated bounded APIs/events.

- Customer-side collectors expose a signed attestation and version report so customers can validate the active build.

- An unknown collector version is accepted only into quarantine unless a controlled compatibility rule explicitly permits it.

# 09 \| Expected-Evidence Model and Gap Detection

***Figure 4 - Expected-evidence and gap-detection flow.***

| **Expected-evidence field**          | **Requirement**                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Rule ID and version**              | Immutable version; changes create a new applicability window.                                                    |
| **Control and implementation scope** | Canonical control objective, tenant implementation, legal entity, environment and resources.                     |
| **Evidence types**                   | One or more required/alternative/supporting evidence types with relationship semantics.                          |
| **Coverage unit**                    | Account, user, privileged identity, endpoint, workload, repository, policy, period or other canonical unit.      |
| **Cadence and window**               | Collection frequency, evaluation window, grace period, late-data policy and expiration.                          |
| **Population expectation**           | Expected source objects or authoritative population query and reconciliation version.                            |
| **Health dependencies**              | Collectors, permissions, APIs, source systems and enrichment dependencies required for coverage.                 |
| **Threshold**                        | All, percentage, sample, risk-based or approved alternative; threshold rationale and authority stored.           |
| **Gap taxonomy**                     | MISSING, PARTIAL, PERMISSION_CHANGED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, EXCLUDED, NOT_APPLICABLE, ACCEPTED_EXCEPTION, UNKNOWN. |
| **Escalation**                       | Owner, notification, remediation SLA, exception path and customer visibility.                                    |
| **Assurance effect**                 | How each gap state affects evaluator and assessment state; no default-to-pass behavior.                          |

# 10 \| Cryptographic Integrity, Signatures and Trusted Time

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image120.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image48.png" />

***Figure 5 - Cryptographic integrity and anchoring stack.***

| **Control**             | **Required design**                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Hashing**             | Use an approved collision-resistant algorithm; store algorithm identifier, canonicalization profile and full digest. Baseline algorithms are controlled by E3 and cryptographic-agility ADRs. |
| **Canonicalization**    | Structured metadata has an explicit canonical serialization; raw content is hashed as received or after a declared, versioned canonical transformation.                                       |
| **Collector signature** | Signature binds artifact hash, tenant, source, evidence type, observed period, collector identity/version and nonce.                                                                          |
| **Trusted time**        | Use platform-receipt time plus an independently verifiable timestamp receipt for chain/anchor events; record source clock quality separately.                                                 |
| **Key separation**      | Collector, ledger, anchor, package and verifier-release signing keys are distinct with non-overlapping policy and operators.                                                                  |
| **Key custody**         | High-value signing operations use HSM/KMS policy, dual control for key lifecycle and immutable key-use audit.                                                                                 |
| **Rotation**            | New entries use current keys; historical verification resolves retired public keys and revocation/compromise intervals.                                                                       |
| **Algorithm agility**   | Every signed or hashed object records suite/version; verifier supports controlled overlap and explicit deprecation.                                                                           |
| **Compromise handling** | A compromised key produces a bounded incident interval, key revocation, new trust chain and package impact assessment; history is not silently re-signed.                                     |
| **Proof minimization**  | External witnesses receive signed commitments/root metadata, never customer evidence content or sensitive tenant names.                                                                       |

<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />

<th><p><strong>CRYPTOGRAPHIC HONESTY</strong></p>
<p>Verification confirms that the package bytes, ledger sequence and published commitments are consistent. It does not prove that a source system was truthful or that a control was legally sufficient.</p></th>
