# 11 \| Per-Tenant Ledger, Sequence and Append Semantics

| **Ledger element**   | **Mandatory semantics**                                                                                                                        |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Partition**        | One logical append history per tenant and regional cell; no global chain that leaks tenant activity or creates unnecessary blast radius.       |
| **Sequence**         | Monotonic sequence allocated server-side; gaps may exist only with an explicit reserved/aborted record.                                        |
| **Entry commitment** | entry_hash commits prior_hash, sequence, evidence_record_hash, event type, actor/workload identity, policy version and trusted time receipt.   |
| **Append result**    | Caller receives ledger sequence, entry hash, append receipt and pending anchor batch; response is idempotent by evidence ID.                   |
| **Concurrency**      | Single logical ordering per tenant via transactional append or consensus-backed sequencer; concurrent callers never choose sequence values.    |
| **Correction**       | CORRECTS or SUPERSEDES points to prior evidence/metadata; original remains discoverable and included in lineage.                               |
| **Deletion**         | TOMBSTONE commits authorized deletion action, policy, approvers and prior content hash without retaining deleted content.                      |
| **Fork detection**   | Multiple heads for one tenant/sequence range are an integrity incident, never an automatic merge.                                              |
| **Backpressure**     | If durable append cannot be guaranteed, evidence remains in authenticated intake with explicit PENDING state; it is not declared committed.    |
| **Read model**       | Search/index projections are rebuildable and not authoritative for history; read-model drift is reconciled against the ledger.                 |
| **Cross-region**     | Tenant history remains in its assigned regional cell; authorized migration creates a signed transfer checkpoint and dual-sided reconciliation. |
| **Access**           | No application role can update or delete existing ledger rows; privileged maintenance is separately controlled and evidenced.                  |

**Illustrative commitment construction - normative algorithm suite is controlled by the cryptography standard.**

<th>ledger_entry_commitment = HASH(<br />
canonical({<br />

policy_version, trusted_time_receipt_hash<br />
})<br />
)<br />

# 12 \| Merkle Aggregation, Anchoring and Independent Witnesses

| **Component**           | **Required behavior**                                                                                                                 |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Batch membership**    | Each anchor batch records region, tenant chain-head commitments, deterministic leaf ordering and complete inclusion-proof material.   |
| **Merkle root**         | Root is calculated with a versioned tree profile that prevents leaf/branch ambiguity and supports algorithm agility.                  |
| **Anchor signature**    | Root and batch metadata are signed by a dedicated HSM-backed anchor identity separate from ledger writers.                            |
| **Witness set**         | At least two independently operated witness channels with different administrative failure domains; selection is ADR-controlled.      |
| **Publication receipt** | Receipt records root, signature, witness identity, submission/acceptance time, external reference and retry state.                    |
| **Customer receipt**    | Frozen packages include root, inclusion proof, witness receipts and public keys so customers can retain independent proof.            |
| **Cadence**             | Target and maximum delay are register-controlled by service tier; actual publication delay is measured and surfaced.                  |
| **Partial witness**     | One-witness success is WITNESS_PARTIAL, not fully anchored; retries continue and affected package limitations are explicit.           |
| **Split view**          | Witness roots and package receipts are compared; inconsistent roots for the same batch/time open an integrity incident.               |
| **Privacy**             | Leaves use tenant commitment IDs/pseudonyms and reveal no artifact content, customer name or control result.                          |
| **Witness exit**        | Historical receipts and public keys remain available after provider exit; migration adds a continuity checkpoint and customer notice. |
| **Key change**          | Anchor-key rotation produces a signed continuity statement witnessed under old/new trust where feasible.                              |

# 13 \| Evidence Lineage, Facts and Control Mapping

| **Relationship**                         | **Required semantics**                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Artifact -\> fact**                    | Parser/normalizer version, field mapping, redactions, confidence and source offsets are recorded.                                        |
| **Fact -\> test input**                  | Evaluator input bundle references exact fact versions and upstream artifact hashes.                                                      |
| **Test -\> control objective**           | Mapping relationship (full, partial, supporting, alternative, conflict, not applicable) and rationale are versioned.                     |
| **Control implementation -\> objective** | Tenant implementation records owner, scope, configuration, exceptions and effective period.                                              |
| **Assessment -\> assertion**             | Assertion identifies assessment versions, reviewer, approval, scope, period, limitations and expiry.                                     |
| **Package -\> all objects**              | Manifest enumerates each object, hash, schema, version and inclusion status; omissions are explicit.                                     |
| **AI output -\> sources**                | Every AI statement points to exact evidence/facts/retrieval items and the model/prompt/tool provenance.                                  |
| **Correction -\> prior object**          | CORRECTS, SUPERSEDES or INVALIDATES is explicit; lineage remains navigable in both directions.                                           |
| **Framework version**                    | Control and requirement identifiers include framework/version and content-display rights; evaluator code does not embed unlicensed text. |
| **Human attestation**                    | Attestor identity, authority, exact statement, period, challenge/review, expiry and supporting evidence are recorded.                    |

## 13.1 Lineage query invariants

- From any customer-facing assertion, an authorized user can traverse to assessment, evaluator run, exact inputs, artifact hashes, source and integrity state without a dead end.

- From any artifact, an authorized user can identify every fact, test, assessment, package and claim that depends on it.

- Lineage respects tenant, purpose, legal hold and data-minimization policies; graph traversal cannot bypass authorization.

- Deleting content preserves minimal dependency/tombstone relationships needed to explain affected assessments without exposing deleted bytes.

# 14 \| Evaluator Runtime and Deterministic Replay

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image121.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image49.png" />

***Figure 6 - Deterministic control-evaluation and assurance flow.***

| **Evaluator contract** | **Mandatory requirement**                                                                                                                  |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity and owner** | Stable evaluator_id, semantic version, owner, control/test scope and approval state.                                                       |
| **Input declaration**  | Accepted evidence/fact schemas, required fields, expected-evidence state, enrichment references and time window.                           |
| **Execution package**  | Signed immutable artifact, dependency lock, runtime image/hash, deterministic settings and resource limits.                                |
| **Isolation**          | No ambient tenant/database/network access; inputs mounted/read-only; outputs written only through approved result API.                     |
| **Output**             | Result state, rationale, component facts, limitations, confidence where meaningful, exceptions and evidence references.                    |
| **Determinism**        | Same input bundle and evaluator version produces byte-equivalent normalized result or flags NON_DETERMINISTIC with divergence.             |
| **Human test**         | Manual procedures are versioned step sets with performer, reviewer, sampled population, artifacts and outcome.                             |
| **AI assistance**      | AI may suggest mapping or narrative but cannot set the authoritative result; AI artifacts are separately stored and reviewed.              |
| **Replay**             | Original input bundle and environment metadata remain available for the retention period; replay never uses current enrichment by default. |
| **Supersession**       | New evaluator version re-evaluates only under controlled campaign; prior results and packages remain immutable.                            |
| **Timeout/error**      | Operational ERROR is not FAIL or PASS; assessment becomes UNKNOWN/PARTIAL according to controlled rule.                                    |
| **Cost**               | CPU, memory, query, model and storage consumption are metered by evaluator and tenant for unit-economics review.                           |

# 15 \| Completeness, Freshness, Coverage, Confidence and Limitations

| **Dimension**            | **Definition**                                                                                        | **Prohibited shortcut**                                     |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Integrity**            | Referenced content and ledger history match cryptographic commitments.                                | “Stored in ZoikoShield” does not mean verified.             |
| **Provenance**           | Source, collector, identity, scope and transformation chain are attributable.                         | A filename or user label is not provenance.                 |
| **Completeness**         | Valid observed evidence covers the declared expected population/window.                               | No errors or high artifact count does not equal complete.   |
| **Freshness**            | Evidence remains within the controlled threshold for its use and control.                             | Last collection time alone ignores source period and grace. |
| **Coverage**             | Which assets, identities, environments, legal entities and controls the evidence actually represents. | Tenant-level presence does not imply fleet-wide coverage.   |
| **Confidence**           | Uncertainty in source, mapping or inference where the method supports a calibrated value.             | Never fabricate a percentage from subjective judgment.      |
| **Effectiveness**        | Evaluator and human conclusion about the control for the stated scope and period.                     | Evidence existence is not effectiveness.                    |
| **Limitation**           | Known exclusions, source gaps, sampling, redaction, unresolved conflicts or assumptions.              | Limitations cannot be buried in an appendix or tooltip.     |
| **Assurance level**      | Strength of evidence, method, independence and review under an approved methodology.                  | Do not label internal automation as external assurance.     |
| **Certification status** | Outcome issued by an authorized certification/examination body.                                       | ZoikoShield never self-declares customer certification.     |

# 16 \| Audit Package Build, Freeze, Approval and Supersession

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image122.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.85625in" alt="Image: image50.png" />

***Figure 7 - Audit package freeze and independent verification.***

| **Package component**        | **Mandatory content**                                                                                                         |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity and scope**       | package_id/version, tenant, legal entity, environments, framework/control set, period and purpose.                            |
| **Framework and mapping**    | Framework versions, licensed display mode, canonical controls, mapping versions and interpretation authority.                 |
| **Evidence inventory**       | Evidence IDs, content hashes, schemas, source/collector, periods, states, redactions and inclusion reason.                    |
| **Expected coverage**        | Expected-evidence rule versions, population, coverage result, gaps, exceptions and collector-health windows.                  |
| **Evaluation inventory**     | Evaluator IDs/versions, input bundle hashes, results, replay receipts, human review and limitations.                          |
| **Assessment and approvals** | Control assessment versions, reviewers, sign-offs, risk acceptances, exceptions and expiry.                                   |
| **Cryptographic proofs**     | Ledger ranges, chain proofs, package manifest hash, Merkle inclusion, root signature and witness receipts.                    |
| **Rendered facts**           | Frozen tables/narratives generated from approved structured facts; every number is traceable to manifest items.               |
| **Verifier material**        | Supported verifier version, schema bundle, public keys, test instructions and expected verification profile.                  |
| **Export formats**           | JSON/JSONL, original artifact formats, open event schemas where applicable and human-readable PDF/HTML as a projection.       |
| **Known limitations**        | Mandatory, prominent and machine-readable; package cannot be frozen while required limitation fields are unresolved.          |
| **Supersession**             | Prior package link, reason, changed objects and explicit statement that the earlier package remains independently verifiable. |

## 16.1 Freeze controls

- Freeze runs against an immutable snapshot and blocks live-query drift during package assembly.

- Pre-check failure prevents READY status but may allow an explicitly partial package where the methodology and approver permit it; limitations must be prominent.

- Package approval is segregated from evaluator authoring and package generation for material assurance scopes.

- After freeze, bytes, manifest and proofs are immutable. Typographical or factual correction creates a superseding package.

- Package downloads are purpose-scoped, logged and optionally customer-encrypted; a download does not grant ongoing platform access.

# 17 \| Independent Verifier Architecture and Verification Semantics

| **Verifier capability**    | **Required behavior**                                                                                                                                           |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Operation**              | Runs offline from a package directory/archive; optional online mode fetches published witness roots but is not required for core checks.                        |
| **Supply chain**           | Open-source source code, signed releases, SBOM, provenance, reproducible build instructions and published checksums.                                            |
| **Schema validation**      | Validates manifest and object schemas against embedded/signed schema versions; unsupported versions fail explicitly.                                            |
| **Content verification**   | Recomputes artifact/object hashes and reports missing, extra, altered or unreadable content.                                                                    |
| **Ledger verification**    | Checks sequence continuity, entry commitments, chain ranges, correction/tombstone relationships and declared gaps.                                              |
| **Anchor verification**    | Checks Merkle inclusion, root signature, key validity interval and independent witness receipts.                                                                |
| **Package signature**      | Validates package approval signature(s), scope, time and signing-key status.                                                                                    |
| **Coverage declaration**   | Verifies that the manifest’s expected-evidence and limitation declarations are internally complete; it does not independently discover unlisted source systems. |
| **Result**                 | Machine-readable and human-readable report with PASS, PASS_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITATIONS, FAIL or UNSUPPORTED, plus exact findings.                                 |
| **Privacy**                | No package content is transmitted by default; diagnostic bundles require explicit opt-in and redaction.                                                         |
| **Portability**            | Supports Windows, macOS and Linux or a portable runtime approved by ADR; no proprietary Zoiko service dependency.                                               |
| **Long-term verification** | Public keys, schemas and verifier source remain available after customer exit and product version retirement.                                                   |

# 18 \| Schema Evolution and Migration-Safe Reproducibility

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image123.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image51.png" />

***Figure 8 - Temporal lineage and migration-safe reproducibility.***

| **Change type**                     | **Required control**                                                                                                   |
|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Additive metadata field**         | Backward-compatible default/absence semantics; old hashes remain computed over the original canonical profile.         |
| **Canonicalization change**         | New profile ID and object version; never recompute old evidence hashes under the new profile.                          |
| **Evidence schema breaking change** | Dual-read/write or adapter with explicit version; migration creates new derived object, not rewritten source artifact. |
| **Parser/normalizer change**        | New fact versions linked to the same source artifact; dependent evaluations are not silently updated.                  |
| **Evaluator change**                | New signed version and replay campaign; differences recorded and reviewed before affecting current assessments.        |
| **Framework mapping change**        | Effective date, rationale, legal/SME review and affected controls/packages identified.                                 |
| **Retention policy change**         | Prospective by default; retroactive impact requires legal/privacy approval and recorded customer/contract analysis.    |
| **Cryptographic algorithm change**  | Overlap period, new keys/profiles, verifier compatibility and continuity proofs controlled by E3/ADR.                  |
| **Witness change**                  | Continuity checkpoint anchored to old and new witness sets; historical receipts preserved.                             |
| **Package schema change**           | Verifier supports controlled historical versions; package always embeds exact schema bundle/hash.                      |
| **Platform migration**              | Source and target chain heads, counts, hashes and witness checkpoints reconcile before cutover.                        |
| **Re-rendering**                    | Creates a new package/render version with prior link; original package bytes remain unchanged.                         |

# 19 \| Retention, WORM, Legal Hold and Verifiable Deletion

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image124.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.68889in" alt="Image: image52.png" />

***Figure 9 - Retention, legal hold and verifiable deletion.***

| **Policy area**          | **Required behavior**                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Retention resolution** | Evaluate evidence type, purpose, contract, control, jurisdiction, tenant choice and legal hold before storage tier and expiry.             |
| **WORM**                 | Apply only where required and for a controlled period; policy prevents accidental perpetual retention.                                     |
| **Legal hold**           | Named matter, authority, scope, start, review and release; hold overrides normal deletion but remains access-restricted.                   |
| **Conflict**             | Deletion request versus legal/contractual hold enters a legal-review queue with clock and customer-visible status where appropriate.       |
| **Content deletion**     | Delete bytes or destroy scoped encryption keys after approval; append tombstone with policy/approval and prior hash.                       |
| **Derived objects**      | Assess downstream facts, evaluations, packages and claims; mark invalid/limited or retain lawfully under separate policy.                  |
| **Backups**              | Declare backup expiry and restoration controls; deletion attestation identifies residual backup windows.                                   |
| **Package retention**    | Frozen packages follow contract/hold; customer export may transfer custody but does not silently extend Zoiko retention.                   |
| **Proof retention**      | Minimal non-personal commitments, tombstones and witness receipts may remain to prove integrity/deletion, subject to legal/privacy review. |
| **Attestation**          | Signed deletion report enumerates stores, key destruction, backups, exceptions, holds and completion/remaining dates.                      |
| **Testing**              | Quarterly synthetic-tenant deletion and legal-hold conflict test; failures block offboarding readiness claims.                             |

# 20 \| Privacy, Residency, Minimization and Redaction

| **Control**               | **Engineering requirement**                                                                                                                    |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Purpose**               | Collection, evaluation, package, export, AI use and auditor access each carry an approved processing purpose.                                  |
| **Minimization**          | Prefer source-side filtering; collect only fields needed for the evidence type and declared control test.                                      |
| **Classification**        | Artifact and extracted fields inherit/raise data classification; classification cannot be lowered by normalization.                            |
| **Residency**             | Region/provider route is resolved before durable storage, external model use or package processing.                                            |
| **Cross-border transfer** | Requires approved mechanism and provider eligibility; missing decision routes to quarantine, not default region.                               |
| **Redaction**             | Deterministic, versioned redaction produces a derived artifact; original is separately controlled and never overwritten.                       |
| **Tokenization**          | Use tenant-scoped tokens for identifiers where the evaluator does not require raw values; token mapping remains region/key scoped.             |
| **Auditor access**        | Purpose, package/scope, duration and download rights are explicit; access activity becomes evidence.                                           |
| **AI processing**         | Only approved derived/minimized inputs reach model providers; evidence content is never used for provider training without explicit authority. |
| **DSR/search**            | Evidence search supports lawful discovery without opening unrestricted analyst access; package/hold consequences are reviewed.                 |
| **Export**                | Customer exports preserve open metadata and proofs while excluding Zoiko internal notes, third-party restricted content or unrelated tenants.  |
| **Logs**                  | Operational logs avoid evidence content and personal data; identifiers are pseudonymized and reversible only under controlled access.          |

# 21 \| Access Control, Auditor, Support and Customer Visibility

| **Actor**                  | **Permitted capabilities**                                                                                                   | **Non-negotiable constraints**                                                                   |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Customer control owner** | View scoped evidence, coverage, tests, limitations; upload/attest where authorized; approve implementation/assessment roles. | Cannot edit prior evidence or anchor state.                                                      |
| **Customer auditor**       | Read approved packages/evidence, request clarification, comment, download package/verifier.                                  | Purpose/time scoped; no access to unrelated periods, tenants or internal notes.                  |
| **Zoiko analyst**          | View evidence required for assigned case/control; add derived notes and requests.                                            | No bulk export or standing cross-tenant access.                                                  |
| **Evidence engineer**      | Operate collectors/evaluators and diagnose metadata/health.                                                                  | Content masked by default; JIT access for customer bytes; cannot approve package they generated. |
| **Support engineer**       | Troubleshoot customer-authorized scope under JIT and recorded session.                                                       | No hidden support access; customer-visible activity evidence.                                    |
| **Compliance reviewer**    | Review mappings, tests, limitations and package approval.                                                                    | Cannot alter source artifacts or evaluator history.                                              |
| **Security/SRE**           | Operate ledger/anchor infrastructure, restore and reconciliation.                                                            | Key/anchor duties segregated; no customer-content need by default.                               |
| **AI assistant**           | Read only approved retrieval bundle and create a derived suggestion.                                                         | No ambient search, package approval, ledger signing or completeness decision.                    |
| **Partner/MSP**            | Delegated access to named managed tenants and functions.                                                                     | Non-transitive, revocable, fully tenant-scoped and customer-visible.                             |

## 21.1 Customer-visible proof surfaces

- Every evidence object shows source, collector, observed period, integrity, coverage, freshness, retention and limitation state.

- Every control status drills to expected evidence, actual coverage, evaluator version, result, reviewer and exceptions.

- Every package displays freeze time, scope, gaps, signatures, anchor receipts and independent-verifier instructions.

- Every privileged evidence access, export, redaction, hold and deletion operation is visible in the customer audit log where contractually appropriate.

# 22 \| AI-Assisted Evidence and Assurance Controls

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image125.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image53.png" />

***Figure 10 - AI-assisted evidence and assurance architecture.***

| **AI use**                  | **Permitted output**                                         | **Required controls**                                                                     | **Prohibited authority**                                         |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Artifact classification** | Candidate evidence type, sensitivity and routing suggestion. | Grounded inputs, deterministic validation, confidence, human review for material changes. | Cannot bypass residency/quarantine or lower classification.      |
| **Document extraction**     | Derived fields and source-offset citations.                  | Sandboxing, prompt-injection defense, exact page/offset links, extraction validation.     | Cannot replace original artifact or create source attestation.   |
| **Control mapping**         | Candidate control/evidence relationship and rationale.       | Approved framework IDs, legal display rules, human SME approval.                          | Cannot publish mapping or declare applicability.                 |
| **Gap explanation**         | Narrative explaining expected versus observed evidence.      | Uses deterministic coverage result; citations and limitations mandatory.                  | Cannot mark gap resolved.                                        |
| **Assessment narrative**    | Draft summary from approved structured facts.                | No new facts, visible AI label, reviewer approval, stored prompt/model provenance.        | Cannot set PASS/FAIL or sign package.                            |
| **Auditor Q&A**             | Scoped answer from frozen package content.                   | Package-bound retrieval, citations, no external memory, session logging.                  | Cannot answer beyond package scope or provide legal conclusions. |
| **Anomaly assistance**      | Candidate unusual collection/evaluation patterns.            | Separate detection version/evaluation, analyst review.                                    | Cannot alter evidence or suppress incidents.                     |
| **Remediation suggestion**  | Proposed next action for gaps.                               | Tool-free by default; any tool call independently authorized and recorded.                | Cannot execute response or accept risk.                          |

## 22.1 AI provenance contract

- initiating principal, tenant, purpose, use_case_id and approval state;

- model provider, model/version, region, prompt profile/version, deterministic parameters and safety policy;

- exact retrieval bundle IDs/hashes, evidence citations, tool calls and tool authorization results;

- input redaction/tokenization profile, output hash, confidence/uncertainty and human decision;

- latency, token/cost usage, retention and incident/evaluation linkage.

# 23 \| Failure Modes, Restore and Integrity Reconciliation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image126.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.74236in" alt="Image: image54.png" />

***Figure 11 - Failure, restore and integrity-reconciliation workflow.***

| **Failure**                       | **Required system response**                                                                                                                   |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Collector outage**              | Mark health and affected coverage window; continue unrelated sources; expose gap and remediation path.                                         |
| **Permission drift**              | Stop out-of-scope collection, record granted/requested mismatch, downgrade affected coverage and notify owner.                                 |
| **Vault unavailable**             | Accept only into bounded encrypted intake if durability and residency are guaranteed; do not issue ledger commit or evidence-ready status.     |
| **Ledger writer unavailable**     | Queue authenticated immutable intake with PENDING state; backpressure before loss; never fabricate sequence.                                   |
| **Search/read model unavailable** | Continue authoritative intake/append; UI shows degraded search; rebuild from ledger/vault projections.                                         |
| **Anchor witness unavailable**    | Publish to available witness, mark WITNESS_PARTIAL/DELAYED, retry and disclose package limitation.                                             |
| **Hash/signature mismatch**       | Quarantine artifact/result, open integrity incident, block dependent assertions and preserve forensic copies.                                  |
| **Chain fork/divergence**         | Freeze affected tenant append or isolate new branch, compare witnesses, declare integrity incident and require dual-controlled reconciliation. |
| **Evaluator outage**              | Result is ERROR/UNKNOWN; no pass-through to prior or optimistic status; queue controlled rerun.                                                |
| **AI gateway outage**             | Use deterministic workflows and human review; no evidence or assurance pipeline dependency.                                                    |
| **Restore**                       | Compare local heads to external witness roots and event/vault manifests before service resumption.                                             |
| **Clock anomaly**                 | Record skew, use trusted receipt time for platform ordering, mark source-time confidence and review affected windows.                          |
| **Package corruption**            | Verifier fails with exact missing/altered items; original package source remains immutable and incident assessed.                              |
| **Key compromise**                | Revoke/rotate, bound affected interval, preserve old verification material and assess every dependent package/claim.                           |

# 24 \| Threat Model and Abuse Cases

| **Threat / abuse case**                        | **Primary controls**                                                                           | **Required verification**                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Insider edits or deletes evidence**          | Append-only ledger, WORM profiles, JIT access, dual control, external witnesses.               | Attempt mutation/deletion; prove detection and immutable access evidence.          |
| **Collector spoofs source or scope**           | Workload identity, signed envelope, source allowlist, tenant/evidence-type contract.           | Forged identity, wrong tenant/source/type and replay tests.                        |
| **Full private-chain rewrite**                 | Dual witnesses, customer receipts, HSM root signature, split-view checks.                      | Alternate-history and mismatched witness-root simulation.                          |
| **Artifact substitution**                      | Content addressing, manifest hash, package verification.                                       | Replace same-name file with altered bytes; verifier must fail.                     |
| **Omission from package**                      | Expected-evidence pre-check, manifest inventory, limitations, approval.                        | Remove required item and verify pre-check/verifier result.                         |
| **Evaluator tampering**                        | Signed package, isolated runtime, release evidence, deterministic replay.                      | Modified binary/config/dependency and output-forgery tests.                        |
| **AI prompt injection in evidence**            | Treat content as data, deterministic redaction/extraction, tool isolation, adversarial corpus. | Indirect injection, citation substitution and tool-abuse tests.                    |
| **Cross-tenant evidence access**               | Tenant/key/store isolation, resource authorization, negative tests, pseudonymized logs.        | API, search, object, cache, queue, package, AI retrieval and support-access tests. |
| **Clock rollback or false source time**        | Trusted receipt/timestamp, clock-quality field, anomaly rules.                                 | Clock skew, duplicate time and out-of-order evidence tests.                        |
| **Legal hold bypass**                          | Policy engine, hold index, dual approval, tombstone/deletion evidence.                         | Deletion under active hold and conflicting policy test.                            |
| **Verifier supply-chain compromise**           | Reproducible builds, signatures, SBOM, independent test vectors.                               | Build reproduction, altered binary and key-rotation tests.                         |
| **Anchor-service compromise**                  | Key release policy, rate/cadence checks, independent witness comparison, freeze switch.        | Unauthorized root, batch omission and split-view simulation.                       |
| **Denial of wallet/storage**                   | Quotas, source filtering, evidence size limits, tiering, cost telemetry.                       | Oversized/burst collection, package duplication and AI-cost tests.                 |
| **Sensitive content leak through diagnostics** | Redacted logs, no-content telemetry, opt-in diagnostic bundles.                                | Log scanning and support-export negative tests.                                    |

# 25 \| Testing and Verification Architecture

| **Test family**                | **Minimum release evidence**                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Contract and schema**        | Evidence/collector/evaluator/package/verifier schema validation, compatibility and invalid-input rejection.                     |
| **Cryptographic known-answer** | Hash, canonicalization, signature, Merkle and witness receipt vectors across supported algorithms/versions.                     |
| **Ledger property tests**      | Append ordering, idempotency, concurrency, gaps, correction, tombstone, fork and replay invariants.                             |
| **Tamper tests**               | Alter, delete, insert, reorder, duplicate and substitute artifacts/entries/packages; every case detected and localized.         |
| **Collector certification**    | Identity, scope, permissions, source time, partial batches, rate limits, quarantine, revocation and health.                     |
| **Expected-evidence**          | Population, alternatives, partials, grace, missing, permission drift, exceptions and source outage.                             |
| **Evaluator**                  | Deterministic replay, isolation, timeout, error/pass/fail separation, malicious inputs and dependency pinning.                  |
| **Package/verifier**           | Offline verify, unsupported schema, missing bytes, altered proofs, witness partial, supersession and exit portability.          |
| **Tenant isolation**           | Database, vault, search, cache, queue, package, verifier temp files, AI retrieval and support access.                           |
| **Privacy/residency**          | Routing before storage/model use, redaction, minimization, retention, hold, deletion and backup-window attestation.             |
| **AI assurance**               | Prompt injection, retrieval poisoning, fabrication, citation validity, cross-tenant leakage, tool abuse and denial-of-wallet.   |
| **Migration/replay**           | Historical schema, parser/evaluator changes, package reproduction, anchor/witness continuity and rollback.                      |
| **Resilience/chaos**           | Vault, ledger, search, witness, KMS, identity and regional failure; backpressure, restore and integrity reconciliation.         |
| **Performance/cost**           | Ingest/append/anchor/package/verifier throughput, evidence volume, retention/search cost and tenant noisy-neighbor behavior.    |
| **Accessibility/usability**    | All evidence states, proofs, limitations and AI labels are perceivable without color alone; keyboard and assistive-tech checks. |
| **Independent review**         | External security review of cryptographic/anchor/verifier design before G1 and after material trust-model change.               |

## 25.1 Release blockers

- Any undetected cross-tenant evidence access or package leakage.

- Any path that mutates prior ledger/package history without a linked append-only record.

- Failed tamper, chain, witness, package or independent-verifier tests.

- Any non-COMPLETE or ERROR state rendered as compliant/verified.

- Non-reproducible evaluator result without approved, visible exception.

- AI output used as source evidence or authoritative compliance decision.

- Unreconciled restore divergence or unresolved signing-key compromise.

- Unlicensed standards content embedded in product or evaluator artifacts.

- No tested export/verifier path for the supported package version.

# 26 \| SLOs, Metrics, Cost and Operational Readiness

| **Metric**                          | **Definition / segmentation**                                                                            | **Release and operating use**                           |
|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| **evidence_intake_acceptance**      | Valid authenticated submissions durably accepted / eligible submissions, by region and collector.        | Availability and backpressure.                          |
| **evidence_commit_latency**         | Validated artifact to vault+ledger commit, excluding source polling delay.                               | Point SLO; percentiles by size/type.                    |
| **collector_coverage_state**        | Healthy, degraded, stale, permission-changed, unauthorized, failed by source and tenant.                 | Customer visibility and gap detection.                  |
| **expected_evidence_coverage**      | Valid current observed units / expected units, with explicit unknown/excluded counts.                    | Completeness and assurance.                             |
| **ledger_append_gap**               | Unexpected missing/duplicate/forked sequence events.                                                     | Integrity incident trigger; target zero unresolved.     |
| **anchor_publication_latency**      | Ledger cut-off to receipt from each witness.                                                             | Detect weakened rewrite window; tier-controlled target. |
| **ledger_verification_pass**        | Synthetic and sampled tenant chains/packages verified independently.                                     | Release and continuous canary.                          |
| **evaluator_determinism_rate**      | Replays producing normalized byte-equivalent result / eligible replays.                                  | Release gate and drift detection.                       |
| **evidence_freshness_rate**         | Expected evidence within threshold, segmented by control/evidence type.                                  | Assurance quality.                                      |
| **package_build_latency**           | Approved scope to frozen package, segmented by size and evidence count.                                  | Capacity and customer workflow.                         |
| **package_verifier_success**        | Supported valid packages passing core checks / attempted validations.                                    | Portability and support.                                |
| **restore_reconciliation_success**  | Restore exercises that match external roots/manifests before resumption.                                 | DR gate.                                                |
| **deletion_attestation_completion** | Approved deletion cases completed with store/backup evidence by target.                                  | Privacy/offboarding.                                    |
| **evidence_cost_per_unit**          | Fully loaded collection, vault, ledger, anchor, search, package and support cost per evidence/GB/tenant. | Unit-economics release gate.                            |
| **AI_grounding_pass_rate**          | Sampled AI outputs with valid cited support and no unsupported material statement.                       | Model/prompt release and monitoring.                    |

## 26.1 Required runbooks

- collector permission/schema drift and backfill;

- vault or ledger append outage and bounded intake recovery;

- anchor witness delay, partial witness and split-view investigation;

- chain fork/hash/signature mismatch integrity incident;

- evaluator failure and deterministic replay campaign;

- package corruption or verifier compatibility issue;

- signing-key compromise and historical package impact;

- restore and external-root reconciliation;

- legal hold/deletion conflict and deletion attestation;

- AI evidence-assistance kill switch and prompt-injection incident.

# 27 \| Change, Migration and Release Governance

| **Change**                  | **Minimum approval and evidence**                                                                            |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **New evidence type**       | Owner, source authority, purpose/data class, schema, integrity, expected use, retention, UI state and tests. |
| **New collector/version**   | Connector certification, permissions, source schema, scale, health, negative and backfill tests.             |
| **Expected-evidence rule**  | Compliance owner, population method, threshold, gaps, applicability/effective date and customer impact.      |
| **Evaluator change**        | Signed version, test corpus, deterministic replay, difference review and staged release.                     |
| **Ledger/canonicalization** | Architecture + Security ADR, compatibility proof, migration/replay and verifier support.                     |
| **Anchor/witness/key**      | Security ADR, key/witness continuity, customer/package impact and failover exercise.                         |
| **Package/verifier schema** | Backward support window, test vectors, customer notice and exit-portability evidence.                        |
| **Retention/hold policy**   | Privacy/Legal approval, contract/jurisdiction analysis, prospective/retroactive scope and deletion test.     |
| **AI use/model/prompt**     | AI Register approval, data/region, evaluation, adversarial tests, cost limit, disclosure and kill switch.    |
| **Framework/mapping**       | SME/legal review, licensing state, effective date, affected evaluators/packages and customer communication.  |
| **Exception**               | Named owner, risk, compensating controls, expiry, affected claims/packages and release visibility.           |
| **Emergency change**        | Time-bounded, segregated approval, immediate evidence capture, retrospective review and replay/verification. |

## 27.1 Stop-work triggers

- Conflicting evidence, retention, cryptographic or framework authority.

- Undefined integrity, completeness or failure-state behavior.

- Need to mutate frozen evidence/package history.

- Need to collect or transfer data without purpose/residency approval.

- Need to use AI for integrity, completeness, authoritative assessment or package approval.

- Unsupported schema/evaluator/package version with no controlled migration.

- Any unresolved chain divergence, witness inconsistency or signing-key incident.

# 30 \| Workstream Handoff, DoR and DoD

## 30.1 Minimum workstream handoff pack

| **Item**                    | **Required content**                                                                               |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Assigned requirements**   | R04 IDs, acceptance criteria, priority, gate and owning outcome.                                   |
| **Applicable contracts**    | Evidence types, collector/evaluator/package schemas, API/events and version rules.                 |
| **Authority and data**      | Source authority, tenant/region/purpose/data class, retention and access constraints.              |
| **Integrity model**         | Hash/canonicalization/signature/chain/anchor obligations and key references without secret values. |
| **Failure model**           | Applicable states, degraded behavior, stop-work triggers and customer-visible limitations.         |
| **Experience contracts**    | Applicable EV views with all required state classes and accessibility behavior.                    |
| **Tests**                   | Unit, contract, tamper, cross-tenant, replay, migration, failure, performance and cost tests.      |
| **Observability**           | Metrics, traces, audit events, alerts, runbooks and SLO measurement points.                        |
| **Release evidence**        | Required artifacts, approvers, register updates and independent verification result.               |
| **Restricted annex access** | Named EC-3 materials, owner, expiry and handling controls where necessary.                         |

## 30.2 Definition of Ready

- Requirement IDs and acceptance criteria are approved and traceable.

- Evidence/object/schema authority and tenant/region/purpose are unambiguous.

- Integrity, completeness, freshness, failure and correction behavior are specified.

- Applicable cryptographic profile and key references are approved without embedding secrets.

- Expected-evidence, evaluator and package/verifier contracts are versioned.

- Privacy, retention, hold and deletion consequences are approved.

- Wireframe states, APIs/events and negative tests are available.

- External dependency, witness, provider and licensing decisions are closed or defaulted by ADR.

- No unresolved conflict requires the engineer to invent assurance semantics.

## 30.3 Definition of Done

> 1\. Implementation satisfies linked requirements and controlled contracts.
>
> 2\. All source, tenant, region, purpose, data class, time, provenance and version fields are populated correctly.
>
> 3\. Append-only, correction, chain, anchor and package invariants pass automated tests.
>
> 4\. Completeness and failure states are visible and never default to pass.
>
> 5\. Cross-tenant, tamper, replay, migration, restore and verifier tests pass.
>
> 6\. AI assistance is gateway-controlled, grounded, labeled, overridable and non-authoritative.
>
> 7\. Privacy, retention, legal hold, deletion and export tests pass.
>
> 8\. Observability, audit events, metrics, alerts and runbooks are complete.
>
> 9\. Independent verifier validates the synthetic release package.
>
> 10\. R11/R12/R18/R19 and requirement traceability are current.
>
> 11\. Rollback/disablement exists and no unsupported assurance or certification claim is introduced.
>
> 12\. Required technical, Security, Compliance, Privacy and QA approvals are recorded.

# Document Control and Navigation

| **Control**                  | **Value**                                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Normative language**       | MUST = mandatory; SHOULD = expected unless an approved exception exists; MAY = optional.                                                  |
| **Implementation authority** | Approved executable policies, identity configurations and tenant/residency manifests constrained by controlled masters and ADRs.          |
| **Conflict rule**            | Stop affected work; do not choose between conflicting policy, code, schema, role map, tenant configuration or register entry.             |
| **Change authority**         | Material identity, authorization, isolation or residency changes require owner approval, negative-test evidence and release traceability. |
| **Distribution**             | Only current controlled copies through approved engineering repositories; EC-3 annexes are separately gated.                              |
| **Supersession**             | Superseded versions remain read-only historical evidence and are removed from active build navigation.                                    |

# 01 \| Critical Analysis and Refinements

| **Finding**                                                                                  | **Risk if uncorrected**                                                                                                         | **Required refinement**                                                                                                                                 |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity, authorization, tenancy and residency are often collapsed into one IAM diagram.** | Authentication success can be mistaken for resource authority, and region labels can be mistaken for enforceable residency.     | Specify each concern separately, then define their binding context at every enforcement point.                                                          |
| **A tenant_id field is treated as isolation.**                                               | Client-controlled or missing context can create cross-tenant access even when every table has a tenant column.                  | Resolve tenant server-side from identity, route and resource; enforce across application, data, object, search, queue, cache, AI and operations layers. |
| **Global administrator roles are convenient.**                                               | One credential or insider can reach every customer and bypass customer authority.                                               | No standing global super-admin. Use scoped JIT elevation, dual control, session evidence and emergency freeze/revocation.                               |
| **Role-only models are used until role explosion occurs.**                                   | Permissions drift, become opaque and cannot express resource relationships, purpose, region or action risk.                     | Use canonical actions plus RBAC, ABAC and relationship rules in versioned policy-as-code.                                                               |
| **ZoikoID is treated as infallible.**                                                        | An identity-control outage can halt the security platform or tempt insecure bypasses.                                           | Define bounded cached validation for low-risk existing sessions and fail closed for writes, privilege and response actions.                             |
| **Residency is defined only as storage region.**                                             | AI calls, support access, backups, search, keys, exports or processors can violate the intended boundary.                       | Model collection, processing, storage, backup, key, support, transfer and provider locations separately.                                                |
| **Support and partner access is modeled as an ordinary role.**                               | Delegated access can become transitive, invisible or effectively unlimited.                                                     | Represent delegation as a customer-revocable, non-transitive relationship with named principals, scope, expiry and customer-visible evidence.           |
| **AI agents inherit human sessions.**                                                        | Prompt injection or tool abuse can silently expand authority and break attribution.                                             | Give each agent a separate non-human identity and require on-behalf-of context plus tool-side reauthorization.                                          |
| **Permission denial and technical outage are conflated.**                                    | Users and operators cannot distinguish a policy decision from a broken service, undermining auditability and incident response. | Use distinct DENY, INDETERMINATE, UNAVAILABLE and RESTRICTED states with stable reason codes.                                                           |
| **Lifecycle controls focus on onboarding.**                                                  | Stale contractors, leavers, orphaned service accounts and delayed SCIM removal become persistent attack paths.                  | Engineer joiner, mover, leaver, expiry, revocation propagation and orphan detection as first-class SLOs and tests.                                      |

# 02 \| Executive Engineering Mandate

Build ZoikoShield so that every human, workload, partner, support process and AI agent is an attributable principal; every request is explicitly scoped to one tenant, environment, region, resource and purpose; every material decision is evaluated by versioned policy and enforced where the effect occurs; and every isolation or residency outcome is testable and evidenced.

| **Mandate**                   | **Engineering consequence**                                                                                        |
|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authenticate explicitly**   | No network location, email domain, API key presence or UI state is treated as identity proof.                      |
| **Authorize at the resource** | Domain services and data access paths validate action, ownership, relationship, policy and current resource state. |
| **Deny by default**           | Missing, stale, conflicting or indeterminate context never becomes implicit permission.                            |
| **Contain tenant scope**      | Cross-tenant operations are exceptional, explicitly modeled and independently approved.                            |
| **Keep privilege temporary**  | Privileged access is JIT, scoped, time-bound, separately authenticated and reviewable.                             |
| **Route before persistence**  | Residency and provider eligibility are decided before durable storage or external model processing.                |
| **Expose uncertainty**        | Unauthorized, degraded, stale and policy-indeterminate states remain visible and distinct.                         |
| **Prove the boundary**        | Negative tests, policy decisions, access evidence and release records support every assurance statement.           |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope and Disclosure Boundary

## 3.1 In scope

- Human identity federation, authentication, MFA/passkeys, session, recovery and lifecycle.

- Workload, service, connector, client and agent identities with short-lived credentials.

- RBAC, ABAC, relationship-based policy, purpose, entitlement and resource authorization.

- Tenant hierarchy, legal entity, business unit, environment and workspace scoping.

- Privileged access, step-up, JIT elevation, segregation of duties and break-glass.

- Delegated customer, partner, MSP and Zoiko support access.

- Multi-tenant isolation across all application, data and operational layers.

- Regional cells, data residency, provider eligibility, transfer and support-location rules.

- Degraded modes, lifecycle revocation, audit evidence, monitoring, tests and release gates.

- AI and agent principal boundaries, on-behalf-of context and tool authorization.

## 3.2 Out of scope or controlled elsewhere

| **Area**                                                 | **Boundary**                                                                          |
|----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Detailed cryptographic algorithms and key ceremonies** | Owned by E3; this document defines required context and interfaces only.              |
| **Full network and infrastructure topology**             | Owned by H1 and EC-3 production annexes.                                              |
| **Customer contract language and legal advice**          | Owned by G7/G8; engineering receives enforceable requirements only.                   |
| **Commercial entitlements and pricing**                  | Owned by B2/B3; authorization consumes entitlement state but does not expose pricing. |
| **Final UI designs**                                     | Owned by C11/W01-W38; this document defines required identity and state behavior.     |
| **Customer production identity data**                    | Never included in this document or test fixtures.                                     |
| **Sovereign and OT deployment details**                  | G4-gated and excluded until approved.                                                 |

## 3.3 Disclosure classes

| **Class**          | **Content in this document**                                                                                                         | **Access**                                            |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| **EC-2**           | Principals, flows, policy model, tenant hierarchy, data-store controls, tests and operational states.                                | Assigned engineering and review teams.                |
| **EC-3**           | Production IdP trust configuration, key hierarchy, admin endpoints, detailed attack paths, emergency controls and red-team findings. | Named Security/SRE/Identity leads under JIT approval. |
| **Never embedded** | Secrets, private keys, bearer tokens, recovery codes, customer identities or production tenant data.                                 | Vault/system references only.                         |

# 04 \| Binding Identity and Isolation Principles

| **ID**     | **Principle**                                    | **Binding consequence**                                                                                     |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **IAM-01** | Authentication is not authorization.             | Every resource operation re-evaluates authority after identity proof.                                       |
| **IAM-02** | Tenant context is mandatory and server-resolved. | Client-supplied tenant identifiers are hints, never sole authority.                                         |
| **IAM-03** | Default deny and deny on indeterminate.          | Missing policy, stale elevation, unknown region or unresolved relationship blocks the operation.            |
| **IAM-04** | No standing universal privilege.                 | Privileged effects require scoped JIT grants and fresh step-up.                                             |
| **IAM-05** | Policy is executable and versioned.              | Roles, attributes, relationships, obligations and precedence live in signed policy artifacts.               |
| **IAM-06** | Enforcement is local to the effect.              | UI, gateway and service checks supplement but never replace domain/data enforcement.                        |
| **IAM-07** | Actor and subject remain distinct.               | Delegation, impersonation, support and agent actions preserve both identities.                              |
| **IAM-08** | Workload identity is short-lived.                | Static shared service credentials are prohibited.                                                           |
| **IAM-09** | Residency precedes persistence.                  | No write, enrichment, AI call or export occurs before route and provider policy resolve.                    |
| **IAM-10** | No raw customer data in the global plane.        | Only approved bounded metadata and aggregate health are permitted.                                          |
| **IAM-11** | Support access is visible.                       | Customer-affecting support access is purpose-scoped, time-bound, audit-linked and customer-reviewable.      |
| **IAM-12** | AI has no ambient authority.                     | Agents use separate identities and tool-side reauthorization.                                               |
| **IAM-13** | Failure is explicit.                             | DENIED, RESTRICTED, INDETERMINATE and UNAVAILABLE are separate states.                                      |
| **IAM-14** | Lifecycle revocation is a security control.      | Suspension, expiry and leaver events propagate within controlled targets.                                   |
| **IAM-15** | Isolation is verified continuously.              | Cross-tenant negative tests cover every storage, query, cache, queue, export and AI path.                   |
| **IAM-16** | Access decisions are evidence.                   | Material decisions record policy, reason, obligations, actor, subject, tenant and resource without secrets. |

# 05 \| Source-of-Truth and Controlled Object Model

## 5.1 Authority map

| **Object / decision**               | **System of record**                                                                       | **Not authoritative**                                    |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Human identity proof**            | Customer IdP or approved Zoiko identity authority.                                         | Application profile, email string or local cache.        |
| **Tenant membership**               | ZoikoShield tenant membership service, synchronized from approved lifecycle sources.       | Token claim alone or UI-selected tenant.                 |
| **Role and permission definition**  | Signed policy catalog and approved register snapshot.                                      | Hard-coded UI checks or ad hoc database flags.           |
| **Resource ownership/relationship** | Owning domain module.                                                                      | Identity service copy or stale search projection.        |
| **Commercial entitlement**          | Entitlement service.                                                                       | Role assignment or product feature flag alone.           |
| **Authorization decision**          | Approved PDP using current context and policy, enforced by the PEP.                        | Client-side gating or cached permit beyond approved TTL. |
| **Tenant isolation profile**        | Signed tenant configuration.                                                               | Deployment naming convention.                            |
| **Residency/transfer outcome**      | Tenant/data-class/purpose policy resolved against current provider and region eligibility. | User preference text or source region alone.             |
| **Session and elevation**           | Session/JIT authority with revocation and expiry.                                          | Browser local storage or task ticket.                    |
| **Audit evidence**                  | Append-only audit/evidence pipeline.                                                       | Application logs alone.                                  |

# 06 \| Principal Classes, Trust Domains and Context

| **Principal class**     | **Examples**                                                 | **Required controls**                                                                               |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Human customer**      | Tenant admin, analyst, auditor, executive, responder.        | Federation/local approved auth, MFA/passkey, membership, session risk, resource authorization.      |
| **Zoiko workforce**     | Support, SOC analyst, SRE, security, engineering.            | Separate workforce IdP, managed device, JIT privilege, customer-purpose scope, stronger monitoring. |
| **Workload/service**    | shield-core module, ingest worker, BFF, scheduled evaluator. | Short-lived workload identity, mTLS, allowed peers, no human token reuse.                           |
| **Client application**  | Customer OAuth client, SDK automation.                       | Registered client, narrow scopes, owner, rotation, quotas and tenant binding.                       |
| **Connector**           | Vendor/source collector instance.                            | Per-tenant identity, isolated credentials, source/action separation, health and certification.      |
| **AI agent**            | Investigation assistant or workflow agent.                   | Registered non-human principal, on-behalf-of context, tool allowlist, memory and expiry.            |
| **Partner/MSP**         | Named human in a managing organization.                      | Explicit non-transitive delegation grant, customer visibility and revocation.                       |
| **Emergency principal** | Break-glass identity or process.                             | Offline custody, dual declaration, fresh step-up, restricted scope and immediate review.            |

## 6.1 Mandatory request context

- principal and actual actor; subject if acting on behalf of another principal;

- principal type, issuer/source, assurance and session/device risk;

- tenant, legal entity, environment and region;

- action, effect class, resource type, resource identifier and owning domain;

- purpose, case/change/approval reference where required;

- entitlement and service-obligation context where applicable;

- data class, retention and residency policy reference;

- policy bundle version, decision identifier and required obligations;

- correlation, causation and audit/evidence references.
