# 07 \| Tenant Hierarchy, Lifecycle and Resource Scoping

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image129.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.91597in" alt="Image: image46.png" />

***Figure 3 - Tenant and resource hierarchy.***

## 7.1 Hierarchy rules

| **Level**         | **Purpose**                                     | **Isolation meaning**                                                                          |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **group_account** | Commercial/group relationship across tenants.   | Not a data-isolation boundary; cross-tenant visibility requires explicit approved aggregation. |
| **tenant**        | Primary customer isolation boundary.            | Every durable object, event, policy, search and audit record is tenant scoped.                 |
| **legal_entity**  | Jurisdictional and accountability scope.        | May drive policies and reporting; cannot broaden tenant access.                                |
| **business_unit** | Organizational segmentation.                    | Policy/resource scope within one tenant.                                                       |
| **environment**   | Production, test or named operational boundary. | Controls access/effect; never substitutes for tenant isolation.                                |
| **workspace**     | Collaboration and workflow scope.               | May narrow access; cannot grant authority beyond tenant membership.                            |
| **resource**      | Domain-owned object.                            | Owning service resolves tenant and relationship from authoritative state.                      |

## 7.2 Tenant lifecycle

| **State**        | **Allowed behavior**                                                                          | **Required evidence**                                                        |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **PROVISIONING** | Configuration, region, keys, policies and bootstrap identities only. No production ingestion. | Approved order/entitlement, tenant profile, region and isolation validation. |
| **ACTIVE**       | Contracted capabilities within approved scope.                                                | Current owner, health, access reviews and release compatibility.             |
| **RESTRICTED**   | Limited due to security, legal, payment, risk or incident control.                            | Reason, authority, allowed operations and review/expiry.                     |
| **SUSPENDED**    | Interactive and external actions blocked; retention/monitoring behavior explicit.             | Approval, notification and preserved evidence.                               |
| **OFFBOARDING**  | Exports, holds, revocation and deletion workflow active.                                      | Manifest, access freeze, key/delete plan and customer approvals.             |
| **CLOSED**       | No active access; retained evidence/records only under policy.                                | Deletion attestation, hold state and archive ownership.                      |

## 7.3 Cross-tenant operations

- Cross-tenant reads are prohibited by default and never implemented as arbitrary admin queries.

- Approved aggregate reporting uses a governed data product containing only permitted de-identified or bounded metadata.

- Migrations, support, incident response and legal processes use explicit scoped operations with named authority and evidence.

- Batch jobs partition and checkpoint by tenant; one tenant failure cannot reveal or corrupt another tenant.

- Cross-tenant joins in operational databases and search are build-broken unless an ADR and dedicated aggregate model exist.

# 08 \| Human Identity Federation and Authentication

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image130.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image47.png" />

***Figure 4 - Human authentication, session and step-up flow.***

## 8.1 Supported authentication patterns

| **Pattern**                          | **Required behavior**                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Enterprise federation**            | OIDC or SAML through approved tenant configuration; issuer, audience, signature, time, recipient and tenant mapping validated. |
| **Lifecycle provisioning**           | SCIM or controlled directory synchronization for users/groups; provisioning never grants permissions without approved mapping. |
| **Passkey / phishing-resistant MFA** | Required for Zoiko privileged roles and high-impact customer actions where supported by policy.                                |
| **Password fallback**                | Only when approved; strong rate limiting, breach-resistant storage, recovery controls and step-up for sensitive actions.       |
| **Invitation/bootstrap**             | Single-use, short-lived, tenant-bound invitation with verified destination and explicit role/expiry review.                    |
| **Account recovery**                 | High-assurance, rate-limited, evidence-linked and incapable of bypassing tenant policy or privileged step-up.                  |
| **Session reauthentication**         | Fresh proof required for policy-defined high-risk actions, not inferred from an old session.                                   |
| **Emergency identity**               | Separate custody and path; not used for routine access or customer impersonation.                                              |

## 8.2 Federation validation controls

- Pin the approved issuer/metadata and reject algorithm, audience, recipient or clock anomalies.

- Resolve tenant from approved IdP configuration and membership, not from arbitrary email domain or untrusted claim.

- Treat group/role claims as inputs to controlled mapping; never grant platform permissions directly from an unknown group string.

- Prevent account linking by email alone; require issuer-subject continuity or an approved verified linking flow.

- Log federation configuration changes, certificate rollover, mapping changes and failed high-risk assertions.

- Use synthetic federation test tenants and negative assertion fixtures; production assertions are prohibited in development.

## 8.3 Authentication states

| **State**                  | **Meaning**                                                                  |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AUTHENTICATED**          | Identity proof accepted; no resource authority implied.                      |
| **STEP_UP_REQUIRED**       | Current assurance is insufficient for the requested effect.                  |
| **SESSION_RESTRICTED**     | Session valid for bounded low-risk operations only.                          |
| **IDENTITY_SUSPENDED**     | Principal cannot establish new sessions and existing sessions are revoked.   |
| **FEDERATION_UNAVAILABLE** | IdP or metadata path unavailable; not equivalent to unauthorized.            |
| **RISK_BLOCKED**           | Authentication blocked by approved risk policy with reason and review route. |
| **RECOVERY_PENDING**       | Recovery initiated but no normal authority restored until completed.         |

# 09 \| Workload, Service and Machine Identity

| **Identity type**          | **Required controls**                                                                                                      | **Prohibited**                                            |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Workload identity**      | Short-lived certificate/token, environment and service binding, mutual authentication, allowed peers and rotation.         | Shared static secret or human account reuse.              |
| **Scheduled job**          | Dedicated principal, tenant partition rules, purpose, limited datasets, checkpoints and owner.                             | Running as cluster admin or broad database owner.         |
| **Connector runtime**      | Per-tenant instance identity, source scopes, isolated credentials and no action-broker access unless separately certified. | One credential or identity shared across customers.       |
| **OAuth client**           | Registered owner, tenant scope, grant type, redirect/endpoint controls, secret/certificate rotation and quotas.            | Unbounded client credentials or wildcard redirects.       |
| **CLI/automation**         | Named human or registered client; explicit tenant/environment, safe token storage and non-interactive constraints.         | Embedding tokens in scripts, logs or command history.     |
| **Build/deploy identity**  | Environment-specific, protected pipeline, artifact provenance and narrow deployment authority.                             | Developer workstation directly assuming production admin. |
| **Data pipeline identity** | Read/write separated, store and partition scoped, lineage/audit and no interactive use.                                    | Ad hoc analyst access through pipeline credentials.       |

# 10 \| Sessions, Tokens, Devices and Risk Posture

| **Control**             | **Required behavior**                                                                                               |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Session issuance**    | Bind principal, tenant context, assurance, device/risk, policy version, issue/expiry and revocation state.          |
| **Access token**        | Short-lived, narrow audience and scopes; no long-lived bearer token for privileged or action paths.                 |
| **Refresh/renewal**     | Rotation and revocation; material risk, role, tenant or policy changes trigger re-evaluation.                       |
| **Tenant switching**    | New server-validated context and authorization; no client-only switch or cross-tenant carryover.                    |
| **Step-up**             | Separate fresh proof for high-impact actions; step-up age and method are policy inputs.                             |
| **Device posture**      | Managed-device or posture requirements for Zoiko workforce and restricted roles; posture loss can restrict session. |
| **Concurrent sessions** | Visible and revocable; risk-based limits for privileged users and suspicious geography/device changes.              |
| **Revocation**          | Immediate for termination/compromise and bounded propagation for ordinary changes; target in R19.                   |
| **Token storage**       | Secure client storage, no logs/URLs, no source control, no local plaintext export.                                  |
| **Session evidence**    | Issue, assurance, tenant selection, step-up, restriction, revocation and expiry events without token values.        |

## 10.1 Session risk inputs

- authentication method and assurance freshness;

- device management and security posture;

- network/geographic anomaly within lawful and approved use;

- identity lifecycle state and recent privilege changes;

- tenant sensitivity and requested action effect class;

- active incident, customer restriction or support-access context;

- behavioral risk signals that are explainable and reviewable.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>RISK DECISION BOUNDARY</strong></p>
<p>Risk signals may require step-up, session restriction or review. They do not silently grant authority, and an opaque score cannot be the only explanation for denial.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 11 \| Authorization Architecture and Policy Evaluation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image131.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image48.png" />

***Figure 5 - Authorization decision and obligation flow.***

## 11.1 Decision inputs and outputs

| **Element**        | **Required content**                                                                                   |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Subject/actor**  | Actual principal, on-behalf-of subject, principal type, source and assurance.                          |
| **Tenant context** | Tenant, legal entity, environment, region and delegated relationship.                                  |
| **Action**         | Stable action identifier and effect class: read, configure, export, privileged, response, destructive. |
| **Resource**       | Type, identifier, owning tenant, state, sensitivity, owner and relationships.                          |
| **Purpose**        | Approved purpose plus case/change/approval reference where required.                                   |
| **Entitlement**    | Capability availability and quantity/state; entitlement cannot override security policy.               |
| **Policy**         | Signed bundle version, effective time and applicable layers.                                           |
| **Decision**       | PERMIT, DENY, INDETERMINATE or NOT_APPLICABLE with stable reasons.                                     |
| **Obligations**    | Mask fields, filter results, step-up, dual approval, JIT, region, logging, rate limit or human review. |
| **Evidence**       | Decision ID, context hash, policy version, enforcement outcome and correlation.                        |

## 11.2 Policy evaluation layers and precedence

| **Order** | **Policy layer**              | **Rule**                                                                                                          |
|-----------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1**     | Platform safety prohibition   | Hard denies for cross-tenant, unsupported region, compromised identity, prohibited AI/tool or blocked action.     |
| **2**     | Residency and data protection | Processing, provider, support, export and transfer conditions.                                                    |
| **3**     | Tenant policy                 | Customer-selected restrictions, response authority, data access and approval rules within platform safety bounds. |
| **4**     | Entitlement/capability        | Confirms capability is purchased and active; does not create identity authority.                                  |
| **5**     | Role/attribute/relationship   | Evaluates permissions, principal/resource attributes and ownership/delegation.                                    |
| **6**     | Action-risk obligation        | Requires step-up, JIT, dual approval, rate ceiling, simulation or customer attestation.                           |
| **7**     | Emergency path                | Explicit break-glass policy with stronger evidence and bounded scope; never an implicit override.                 |

## 11.3 Enforcement-point requirements

- Every PEP validates tenant/resource binding after receiving the decision.

- Bulk operations authorize each item or a provably bounded homogeneous set; no blanket permit over mixed tenants/resources.

- Queries enforce tenant and field filters in the query plan, not only after results return.

- Exports reauthorize at creation and download; the export artifact is tenant, purpose, expiry and recipient scoped.

- Background jobs and event consumers use workload identity and explicit tenant partitioning.

- Cached decisions are signed/bound to context, short-lived and prohibited for privileged, destructive, response or residency-changing operations.

- Authorization failure produces stable reason codes without disclosing another tenant or sensitive resource existence.

# 12 \| Roles, Attributes, Relationships and Permission Governance

## 12.1 Canonical permission model

| **Dimension**           | **Requirement**                                                                                       |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Action**              | Stable verb such as case.read, case.update, evidence.export, connector.configure or response.execute. |
| **Resource type**       | Canonical domain type with owning service.                                                            |
| **Effect class**        | Read, write, configuration, export, privilege, external action, destructive or emergency.             |
| **Required context**    | Tenant, environment, purpose, case/change, step-up, approvals, region and data class.                 |
| **Obligations**         | Masking, filtering, dual control, logging, watermark, rate limit, simulation or review.               |
| **Incompatibilities**   | Segregation-of-duties conflicts and prohibited combinations.                                          |
| **Owner and lifecycle** | Named owner, version, effective/retirement dates and review cadence.                                  |
| **Tests**               | Positive, negative, cross-tenant, field-level and policy-diff tests.                                  |

## 12.2 Roles and attributes

- Roles are curated job bundles, not a replacement for resource relationships or context.

- Role creation is restricted; duplicate/near-duplicate roles trigger review to prevent role explosion.

- Attributes have an authoritative source, type, allowed values, freshness and missing-value behavior.

- User-controlled attributes cannot grant privilege without independent validation.

- Role assignment includes tenant, scope, source, approver, start, expiry and review owner.

- Dynamic group mappings are tested against over-broad grants and issuer changes.

## 12.3 Relationship-based authorization

| **Relationship** | **Example use**                                             | **Constraint**                                                   |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **member_of**    | Principal is a member of tenant/legal entity/business unit. | Cannot be inferred solely from email domain.                     |
| **owns**         | Principal or team owns an asset/control/case.               | Ownership source is the domain system of record.                 |
| **assigned_to**  | Analyst is assigned to case/queue.                          | Assignment narrows access; does not override data/tenant policy. |
| **auditor_for**  | External auditor can access approved package/scope.         | Read-only, purpose/time bound, package-specific.                 |
| **manages**      | MSP tenant manages named customer tenant.                   | Requires explicit delegation grant; no transitive manage.        |
| **approver_for** | Principal may approve named action class.                   | Subject to SoD and cannot approve own request.                   |
| **supports**     | Zoiko support principal has active support request.         | JIT, purpose, customer-visible and expires automatically.        |

## 12.4 Segregation of duties

| **Conflict**                                 | **Required control**                                              |
|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Author and approve policy**                | Separate approver for material policy publication.                |
| **Request and approve own privilege**        | Prohibited; independent approver required.                        |
| **Develop and promote to production**        | Protected pipeline and independent release approval.              |
| **Create and execute high-impact response**  | Customer/dual approval per R-level.                               |
| **Collect and attest evidence**              | Evidence owner cannot unilaterally attest own material exception. |
| **Create and approve price/entitlement**     | Commercial control; engineering consumes approved state only.     |
| **Support access and delete audit evidence** | Prohibited by architecture; audit/evidence path is independent.   |

# 13 \| Privileged Access, Step-Up, JIT and Break-Glass

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image132.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image49.png" />

***Figure 8 - Privileged access, JIT elevation and break-glass control.***

## 13.1 Privileged effect classes

| **Class**                   | **Examples**                                                            | **Minimum controls**                                                        |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **P1 Sensitive read**       | Customer evidence content, restricted logs, identity details.           | Purpose, JIT where workforce, enhanced audit, masking.                      |
| **P2 Configuration**        | Identity, connector, policy, retention or notification settings.        | Step-up, change reference, before/after, rollback.                          |
| **P3 Privilege/security**   | Role grants, key/credential actions, tenant isolation changes.          | JIT, dual control, fresh step-up, session recording.                        |
| **P4 External/high impact** | Account disablement, token revocation, workload isolation, bulk export. | Response authority, approvals, signing/attestation, blast-radius ceiling.   |
| **P5 Emergency**            | Break-glass during declared incident.                                   | Named declaration, bounded scope/time, immediate alert and post-use review. |

## 13.2 JIT grant requirements

- Named principal, not group-only or shared account;

- one tenant/environment or tightly bounded set;

- stable actions/resource types and data classes;

- purpose and incident/change/support reference;

- independent approver and SoD validation;

- fresh phishing-resistant authentication;

- start and hard expiry with no silent renewal;

- session indication, monitoring and customer-visible evidence where applicable;

- automatic revocation and post-use review for material access.

## 13.3 Break-glass constraints

| **Requirement** | **Control**                                                                                          |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Custody**     | Separate emergency identity/credential custody with periodic verification; no daily use.             |
| **Activation**  | Declared incident, named accountable authority and explicit scope.                                   |
| **Authority**   | Still subject to platform hard-deny, tenant boundary and regional/legal prohibitions.                |
| **Visibility**  | Immediate Security/SRE alert and customer notification where contractually/applicably required.      |
| **Evidence**    | Full session/action records, reason, timeline, affected tenants/resources and outcome.               |
| **Review**      | Mandatory post-use review within controlled time; credential/session rotation and corrective action. |

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>PRIVILEGED-ACCESS RULE</strong></p>
<p>JIT access reduces standing exposure; it does not remove the need for tenant, resource, purpose and action authorization at every privileged effect.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 14 \| Delegated Administration, Partners, MSPs and Support Access

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image133.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image50.png" />

***Figure 9 - Customer, partner, MSP and Zoiko support delegation.***

## 14.1 Delegation contract

| **Field**                 | **Requirement**                                                                                  |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Grantor**               | Customer authority or approved platform authority; recorded and reviewable.                      |
| **Managing organization** | Partner/MSP/Zoiko organization with no implicit access to managed tenants.                       |
| **Named principal/group** | Actual principal remains attributable; group membership has authoritative lifecycle.             |
| **Managed tenant/scope**  | Explicit tenant, legal entity/environment, resources and actions.                                |
| **Purpose**               | Service/support/implementation purpose and case/contract reference.                              |
| **Time**                  | Start, hard expiry, review cadence and emergency revocation.                                     |
| **Approvals**             | Customer/platform approvals and SoD checks.                                                      |
| **Transitivity**          | Prohibited unless a separate explicit grant exists; no delegated creation of further delegation. |
| **Visibility**            | Persistent delegated-session indicator and customer-accessible activity record.                  |
| **Revocation**            | Customer and platform can revoke; active sessions and tokens invalidated within target.          |
| **Data locality**         | Support/partner location and provider eligibility evaluated before access.                       |
| **Evidence**              | Grant, changes, sessions, material reads/actions and review outcomes.                            |

## 14.2 Zoiko support access

- No default content access for support roles; metadata-only diagnostics are preferred.

- Content access requires a customer support case, approved purpose, JIT grant and defined data class.

- Sensitive content is masked by default and revealed only where the grant explicitly allows it.

- Customer impersonation is prohibited; the user interface and audit trail display the Zoiko actor and customer context separately.

- Support access from an unapproved country, region, device or identity state is blocked or routed to an eligible responder.

- Every support session has an automatic expiry and customer-reviewable access summary.

# 15 \| Multi-Tenancy and Isolation Classes

| **Class**                | **Architecture**                                                                                                                                        | **Availability / constraints**                                               |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **T1 Pooled**            | Shared regional compute/data services with tenant-scoped schemas/partitions, search/object/cache/queue isolation and platform keys with tenant context. | G1 baseline; continuous isolation tests mandatory.                           |
| **T2 Enhanced**          | Dedicated namespace/node pool, dedicated schema/index and tenant-dedicated key where contracted.                                                        | G2/G3 demand-gated; same logical controls plus stronger resource separation. |
| **T3 Dedicated**         | Dedicated cluster/data services in a Zoiko-managed account; BYOK optional.                                                                              | G3; separate operational and recovery evidence.                              |
| **T4 Sovereign/Private** | Customer cloud/on-prem, customer key custody and constrained control-plane metadata.                                                                    | G4 only; no speculative commitment.                                          |

## 15.1 Isolation profile requirements

- Tenant identifier format and immutable ownership;

- regional cell and permitted failover regions;

- database/schema/partition and connection pattern;

- object storage prefix/bucket and retention/key context;

- search index/alias and mandatory filter enforcement;

- queue/topic/partition and dead-letter isolation;

- cache namespace and eviction behavior;

- analytics/lakehouse partition and query guard;

- vector/retrieval index namespace and AI eligibility;

- observability pseudonymization and customer data restrictions;

- support/partner access constraints;

- last isolation test, result, evidence and exceptions.

<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>ISOLATION-CLASS RULE</strong></p>
<p>A higher isolation class strengthens resource separation. It never weakens application authorization, audit, residency, lifecycle or customer-visibility requirements.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>

# 16 \| Data-Plane Isolation by Technology Layer

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image134.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image51.png" />

***Figure 6 - Multi-tenant isolation defense in depth.***

| **Layer**                   | **Mandatory isolation controls**                                                                                  | **Required negative tests**                                                        |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **API/BFF**                 | Server-resolved tenant, object authorization, field filtering, rate partition, explicit cross-tenant prohibition. | IDOR/BOLA, tenant switch, guessed ID, bulk mixed-tenant and export tests.          |
| **Relational data**         | Composite tenant keys, row-level or equivalent controls, domain-owned connections, constrained migrations.        | Direct query, join, missing filter, transaction/rollback and backup-restore tests. |
| **Object/evidence storage** | Tenant path/bucket, access point/policy, content hash, encryption context and signed export.                      | Prefix traversal, presigned URL, copy/move, lifecycle and legal-hold tests.        |
| **Search/hot analytics**    | Tenant index/alias or enforced filter, query templates, result count protection and reindex controls.             | Filter omission, alias bypass, wildcard, aggregation and cache tests.              |
| **Lakehouse/batch**         | Tenant partitions, catalog policy, job identity, output location and lineage.                                     | Cross-partition scan, temp table, spill/export and replay tests.                   |
| **Cache**                   | Tenant-prefixed keys, no shared sensitive values, bounded TTL and purge on revocation/offboarding.                | Collision, missing prefix, stale authz, eviction/repopulation tests.               |
| **Queues/events**           | Tenant context in envelope/partition, producer/consumer scopes, DLQ isolation and replay controls.                | Cross-topic publish, consumer group, replay and poison-event tests.                |
| **Observability**           | Tenant pseudonym, no secrets/raw customer data in labels, controlled support access.                              | Log injection, trace baggage, metric cardinality and dashboard boundary tests.     |
| **AI/retrieval**            | Tenant-scoped source authorization, index/namespace, prompt context, tool reauthorization and memory expiry.      | Cross-tenant retrieval, poisoned content, prompt scope expansion and cache tests.  |
| **Backups/DR**              | Region and tenant key policy, restore isolation and anchor/audit reconciliation.                                  | Restore to wrong tenant/region, alternate history and deletion-expiry tests.       |

# 17 \| Regional Cells, Residency and Transfer Enforcement

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image135.png" style="width:6.75in;height:3.80208in" alt="Image: image52.png" />

***Figure 7 - Residency routing before persistence.***

## 17.1 Controlled location dimensions

| **Dimension**             | **Meaning**                                                                 |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant home region**    | Default regional cell for tenant operational data.                          |
| **Source region**         | Location from which data is collected or received.                          |
| **Processing region**     | Where normalization, detection, evaluation, search or AI processing occurs. |
| **Storage region**        | Where durable data or evidence content is stored.                           |
| **Backup/archive region** | Where backups, replicas and archives reside.                                |
| **Key region/custody**    | Where keys are generated, held and used; tenant isolation tier applies.     |
| **Support-access region** | Where Zoiko/partner personnel may access data or systems.                   |
| **Provider region**       | External vendor/model/subprocessor processing location and eligibility.     |
| **Export destination**    | Approved recipient, destination and transfer basis for outbound data.       |
| **Failover region**       | Approved alternate region and allowed data classes/effects during failover. |

## 17.2 Residency policy function

**Controlled residency decision model**

<col style="width: 100%" />

<th>route = policy(<br />

## 17.3 Global control-plane boundary

| **Permitted**                                                  | **Prohibited**                                         |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant directory identifiers and region assignment.**        | Raw customer telemetry or evidence content.            |
| **Catalog and entitlement metadata.**                          | Secrets, credentials or private key material.          |
| **Deployment inventory and signed policy/version metadata.**   | Unrestricted personal or confidential customer data.   |
| **Bounded aggregate health/usage with approved minimization.** | Searchable customer event payloads or case content.    |
| **Feature and compatibility policy.**                          | AI prompts/retrieval content containing customer data. |
| **Incident routing metadata where approved.**                  | Hidden replication used to bypass residency.           |

## 17.4 Transfer and failover controls

- No transfer or failover occurs because the preferred region is unavailable unless policy explicitly permits the alternate route.

- Transfer decisions record source/destination, data class, purpose, mechanism, provider, approval and expiry.

- Failover rehearsals test residency, key access, DNS/routing, support access, audit continuity and customer communication.

- Blocked or unmatched routing enters a quarantined, visible state; it never falls back to a generic global store.

- Historical data is not silently moved when a tenant changes region; a controlled migration and reconciliation plan is required.

# 18 \| Data Classification, Purpose and Cryptographic Context

| **Control**             | **Requirement**                                                                                                            |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Data classification** | Every resource/event/evidence type has a controlled class used by authorization, residency, AI, support and export policy. |
| **Purpose**             | Material read, export, support, AI, investigation and administrative activity carries an approved purpose.                 |
| **Field authorization** | Sensitive fields are masked, tokenized or omitted according to principal, purpose and resource policy.                     |
| **Encryption context**  | Tenant, region, isolation tier, data class and object purpose bind key selection and access.                               |
| **Key separation**      | T1 tenant context; T2+ dedicated keys as defined. No shared application secret as data-encryption authority.               |
| **BYOK/HYOK**           | Only for approved tiers with lifecycle, availability, revocation, recovery and offboarding behavior.                       |
| **Secret references**   | Documents/config contain vault/key references, never secret values.                                                        |
| **Export cryptography** | Export artifact, manifest, recipient and expiry are bound and auditable.                                                   |
| **Deletion**            | Key destruction may support erasure only where design proves scope and retention/hold behavior.                            |
| **AI processing**       | Provider/region/data-use policy resolves before model call; no customer-data training without explicit authority.          |

## 18.1 Purpose vocabulary - starter set

| **Purpose**                | **Typical allowed effects**                                                     |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **security-monitoring**    | Collect, normalize, detect and create governed cases.                           |
| **security-investigation** | Read scoped events/assets/evidence linked to an authorized case.                |
| **incident-response**      | Execute approved response actions under R0-R4 authority.                        |
| **continuous-assurance**   | Collect/evaluate evidence and generate scoped control conclusions.              |
| **customer-support**       | Diagnose approved support issue under JIT and masking rules.                    |
| **audit-review**           | Read frozen package/evidence within auditor scope.                              |
| **platform-operations**    | Operate platform metadata/services; customer content only under separate grant. |
| **legal-hold**             | Preserve named records; does not create broad read authority.                   |
| **product-analytics**      | Approved minimized/aggregate data product only.                                 |
| **ai-assistance**          | Gateway-approved retrieval and model processing with human oversight.           |

# 19 \| Identity Lifecycle, Provisioning and Deprovisioning

| **Lifecycle event**    | **Required system behavior**                                                                                             |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Invite/create**      | Verify tenant, destination, source, role intent, expiry and approver; no default privileged role.                        |
| **Federate/link**      | Bind approved issuer-subject; prevent email-only takeover and duplicate identity ambiguity.                              |
| **Provision**          | Create membership/attributes from approved source; policy mapping validated before access.                               |
| **Activate**           | Require authentication and accepted terms/policies; record source and assurance.                                         |
| **Move/change**        | Recompute roles, relationships, SoD, tenant/environment and active sessions.                                             |
| **Suspend**            | Block new sessions and revoke existing sessions within target; preserve evidence.                                        |
| **Terminate/delete**   | Revoke memberships, clients, credentials, delegations, elevations and assigned approvals; retain required audit records. |
| **Contractor expiry**  | Automatic hard expiry independent of manual manager action.                                                              |
| **Orphan detection**   | Identify identities, clients, service accounts, grants and roles without current owner/source.                           |
| **Reinstate**          | Treat as new controlled activation with revalidation; do not silently restore old privilege.                             |
| **Tenant offboarding** | Freeze access, preserve export/legal-hold scope, revoke integrations, delete/attest under policy.                        |

## 19.1 SCIM/directory synchronization semantics

- Synchronization is idempotent, source-versioned and tenant bound.

- Delete/suspend events have higher operational priority than additive profile updates.

- Unknown groups, conflicting mappings and stale source state produce a visible review state rather than broad access.

- Group removal revokes derived role membership and triggers session re-evaluation.

- Manual overrides have owner, reason, expiry and precedence; permanent shadow overrides are prohibited.

- Reconciliation compares source population, membership, status and last processed cursor; API success is not enough.

## 19.2 Lifecycle evidence

| **Evidence**               | **Minimum content**                                                                         |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Provisioning event**     | Source, issuer, principal, tenant, change, mapping version and result.                      |
| **Role/membership change** | Before/after, source, approver, SoD result, effective/expiry.                               |
| **Session revocation**     | Reason, initiator, affected sessions/tokens, propagation and exceptions.                    |
| **Orphan review**          | Object, last owner/source, risk, action and closure.                                        |
| **Offboarding**            | All identities, clients, credentials, delegations and support grants reconciled and closed. |

# 20 \| Degraded Modes and Dependency Failure

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image136.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image53.png" />

***Figure 10 - Identity and policy dependency degraded modes.***

| **Failure**                             | **Allowed behavior**                                                                                                       | **Prohibited behavior**                                                      |
|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Customer IdP unavailable**            | Existing bounded sessions may continue per policy; show federation unavailable; new auth may fail.                         | Creating local bypass accounts or extending sessions beyond approved limits. |
| **ZoikoID control plane unavailable**   | Validate signed keys/config from bounded cache; existing authenticated sessions may remain read-operable.                  | Privileged, response, policy, entitlement or new delegation actions.         |
| **Policy decision service unavailable** | Use signed bounded cache only for approved low-risk reads; otherwise INDETERMINATE/DENY.                                   | Permit by default or use stale decisions for writes/exports/actions.         |
| **Key/KMS unavailable**                 | Protect keys, stop affected decrypt/write operations and expose degraded state.                                            | Fallback to plaintext or alternate unapproved key/region.                    |
| **SCIM/lifecycle source delayed**       | Flag stale lifecycle, prioritize disable signals and reconcile.                                                            | Assume all users/groups remain current indefinitely.                         |
| **Regional cell unavailable**           | Use only approved failover route or quarantine.                                                                            | Move data to an unapproved region.                                           |
| **Audit/evidence pipeline unavailable** | Queue only where durable/approved; block material privileged or external-effect operations if evidence cannot be captured. | Execute high-impact action with no attributable audit record.                |
| **Device posture service unavailable**  | Apply approved bounded fallback or restrict workforce session.                                                             | Treat unknown device posture as trusted for EC-3 access.                     |
| **Time source anomaly**                 | Reject/limit tokens, signatures and grants affected; open incident.                                                        | Extend expiry or accept assertions without controlled time.                  |

## 20.1 Explicit outcome states

| **State**          | **Meaning**                                                                                            |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **PERMIT**         | Policy allows the requested effect with all obligations satisfied.                                     |
| **DENY**           | Policy explicitly prohibits the effect.                                                                |
| **INDETERMINATE**  | Required context, policy or dependency cannot produce a safe decision; treated as deny for the effect. |
| **NOT_APPLICABLE** | Policy does not govern the request; another required policy layer may still apply.                     |
| **RESTRICTED**     | Session/tenant/resource is intentionally limited to a defined subset of operations.                    |
| **UNAVAILABLE**    | Technical service cannot currently complete the operation; distinct from policy denial.                |
| **STALE**          | Identity, membership, policy, device or region state exceeded freshness threshold.                     |
| **QUARANTINED**    | Request/data held from normal processing due to security, residency or integrity uncertainty.          |

# 21 \| AI and Agent Identity and Authorization

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image137.png" style="width:6.75in;height:4.19931in" alt="Image: image54.png" />

***Figure 11 - AI and agent identity boundary. AI may assist, but never authenticates, authorizes, attests evidence or approves response authority.***

## 21.1 Agent principal requirements

| **Control**                 | **Requirement**                                                                                            |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Registration**            | Every agent/use case has an owner, purpose, tenant eligibility, tool set, data classes, memory and expiry. |
| **Identity**                | Agent is a separate non-human principal; model/provider name is not the principal.                         |
| **On-behalf-of**            | Tool call carries originating principal, agent, tenant, purpose and current human-oversight state.         |
| **No ambient authority**    | Agent receives no broad platform token, database access or customer session cookie.                        |
| **Tool authorization**      | Each tool re-evaluates action/resource policy; prompt content cannot expand scope.                         |
| **Retrieval authorization** | Sources are authorized before retrieval and results remain tenant/data-class filtered.                     |
| **Memory**                  | Tenant/principal/use-case scoped, minimized, time-bounded and deletable; no cross-tenant memory.           |
| **Human decision**          | Material recommendation, control mapping and restricted action preserve required review/approval.          |
| **Provider routing**        | Region, data class, training/retention terms and cost policy resolved at gateway.                          |
| **Evidence**                | Prompt profile, retrieval set, model, tool requests/decisions, output, override and feedback are linked.   |
| **Kill switch**             | Agent, tool, prompt, provider or retrieval source can be disabled independently.                           |
| **Fallback**                | Deterministic workflow remains available; no-LLM-critical-path rule applies.                               |

## 21.2 AI authorization prohibitions

- AI must not authenticate a principal or infer identity from prose.

- AI must not decide final access, create roles, change tenancy or alter residency policy.

- AI must not attest evidence integrity or declare a control compliant.

- AI must not approve its own tool use, response action, export or privileged elevation.

- AI must not retrieve across tenants for convenience, benchmark generation or context expansion.

- AI must not persist secrets, tokens or unrestricted customer content in memory.

## 21.3 Prompt-injection boundary

<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>ATTACKER-CONTROLLED INPUT</strong></p>
<p>Logs, alerts, emails, file names, connector payloads, evidence and retrieved documents are untrusted data that may contain instructions. They must never alter identity, tenant scope, tool allowlist, approval requirement or residency policy.</p></th>
</tr>

# 22 \| Audit, Evidence, Monitoring and Customer Visibility

| **Event family**         | **Required events**                                                                                        |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication**       | Attempt, success/failure, issuer, assurance, MFA/passkey, recovery, risk restriction and session issuance. |
| **Authorization**        | Material permit/deny/indeterminate, policy version, reason, obligations, resource and enforcement outcome. |
| **Membership/role**      | Create, change, remove, mapping source, approver, SoD and effective/expiry.                                |
| **Delegation/support**   | Grant, session, material read/action, expiry, revocation and customer review.                              |
| **Privilege**            | Request, approval, step-up, elevation, action, expiry, break-glass and post-use review.                    |
| **Policy/configuration** | Draft, review, sign, publish, canary, rollback and retirement.                                             |
| **Tenant/isolation**     | Provision, region/isolation change, cross-tenant test, exception and offboarding.                          |
| **Residency/transfer**   | Route decision, provider, region, transfer approval, failover and blocked/quarantined outcome.             |
| **Workload/client**      | Credential issue/rotation/revocation, allowed peer/scope change and anomalous use.                         |
| **AI/agent**             | Agent initiation, on-behalf-of, retrieval authorization, tool permit/deny, human decision and kill switch. |
| **Lifecycle**            | Provision, suspend, terminate, orphan, reconciliation and revocation propagation.                          |
| **Access review**        | Scope, reviewer, findings, removals, exceptions and closure.                                               |

## 22.1 Audit record controls

- No token, secret, password, private key or unnecessary personal content in audit records.

- Actor, subject, tenant, resource, purpose, policy version, decision ID and correlation are preserved.

- High-volume read decisions may use governed sampling/aggregation only where material access remains reconstructable.

- Audit delivery is durable, append-only and independently monitored; missing material audit events are release blockers.

- Customer-facing audit views distinguish Zoiko, partner, customer, workload and AI actors.

- Exported audit records include integrity manifest, scope and known limitations.

## 22.2 Customer-visible controls

| **Surface**                | **Required visibility**                                                                 |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Session/access center**  | Active sessions, devices, last authentication, revocation and risk restrictions.        |
| **Role/access review**     | Membership, roles, relationships, source, approver, expiry and conflicts.               |
| **Support/partner access** | Active and historical delegation, actual actor, purpose, duration and material actions. |
| **Residency view**         | Home/processing/storage/backup/key/support/provider regions and current policy state.   |
| **Audit explorer**         | Filterable access and policy events with export/integrity context.                      |
| **Degraded banner**        | Identity, policy, connector, region or key degradation and its functional impact.       |
| **AI disclosure**          | Agent identity, human initiator, sources, tools, decision and oversight status.         |

# 23 \| Threat Model and Abuse Cases

| **Threat / abuse case**                   | **Primary controls**                                                                             | **Required tests**                                                       |
|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Broken object-level authorization**     | Server-side resource tenant/relationship checks, stable actions and negative tests.              | Guessed IDs, indirect references, bulk and export paths.                 |
| **Tenant context injection**              | Resolve tenant from trusted identity/membership and target resource; ignore body-only authority. | Header/body/path mismatch, token reuse and tenant-switch tests.          |
| **Confused deputy**                       | Actor/subject separation, purpose, delegated relationship and tool-side reauthorization.         | Support, partner, service and AI on-behalf-of tests.                     |
| **Token theft/replay**                    | Short lifetime, secure storage, revocation, step-up and risk controls.                           | Replay, expiry, audience, device and session revocation tests.           |
| **Federation assertion attack**           | Strict issuer/audience/recipient/time/signature validation and metadata control.                 | Malformed, wrapped, expired, wrong-tenant and key-rollover fixtures.     |
| **Role/claim overgrant**                  | Controlled mapping, allowlisted attributes, SoD and policy diff.                                 | Unknown group, wildcard, nested group and stale mapping tests.           |
| **Support insider abuse**                 | JIT, purpose, masking, session evidence, customer visibility and independent review.             | Unauthorized content access, scope extension and expiry tests.           |
| **Workload credential compromise**        | Short-lived workload identity, allowed peers, rotation and narrow scopes.                        | Cross-service, cross-environment and stolen-credential simulations.      |
| **Policy tampering**                      | Signed bundles, protected pipeline, dual approval, canary and rollback.                          | Signature failure, stale bundle, malicious diff and rollback tests.      |
| **Region/residency bypass**               | Pre-persistence routing, provider eligibility and fail-closed no-match.                          | Failover, provider outage, export and support-location tests.            |
| **Cross-tenant cache/search/object leak** | Namespace/index/prefix/access controls plus continuous isolation tests.                          | Collision, wildcard, presigned URL and stale cache tests.                |
| **AI prompt/tool scope expansion**        | Agent principal, tool reauthorization, untrusted input handling and kill switch.                 | Indirect injection, cross-tenant retrieval and tool abuse corpus.        |
| **Dormant/orphan identity**               | Expiry, reconciliation, owner, source and orphan workflow.                                       | Contractor expiry, deleted owner and inactive client tests.              |
| **Break-glass abuse**                     | Separate custody, declaration, hard scope, monitoring and post-use review.                       | Routine-use prevention, expired emergency access and notification tests. |

<p>A compromise of ZoikoShield identity or policy systems must not automatically grant customer-estate command authority. The action broker, per-tenant signing, customer-side attestation and rate ceilings remain independent controls.</p></th>

# 24 \| Testing and Verification Architecture

## 24.1 Test families

| **Family**                            | **Minimum scope**                                                                                           |
|---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication conformance**        | Federation, MFA/passkey, recovery, session, issuer/key rollover and negative assertions.                    |
| **Authorization unit/property tests** | Every action/resource policy, missing attributes, deny precedence, obligations and deterministic decisions. |
| **Domain integration**                | PEP/PDP/resource authority, field filtering, export and bulk behavior.                                      |
| **Cross-tenant negative tests**       | API, DB, object, search, cache, queue, analytics, observability, AI and support access.                     |
| **Residency matrix tests**            | Every supported region/data-class/purpose/provider/failover combination; unmatched fails closed.            |
| **Lifecycle tests**                   | Provision, group mapping, move, suspend, terminate, contractor expiry, orphan and session revocation.       |
| **Privileged/delegation tests**       | JIT, SoD, step-up, break-glass, support/partner visibility, revocation and no transitivity.                 |
| **Workload/client tests**             | Allowed peer/audience, environment, scope, rotation, expiry and stolen credential.                          |
| **AI authorization tests**            | On-behalf-of, retrieval filtering, tool reauthorization, prompt injection and memory isolation.             |
| **Chaos/degraded-mode tests**         | IdP, ZoikoID, policy, key, region, audit and posture dependency failures.                                   |
| **Performance/capacity**              | Authentication/session, policy decision, revocation propagation and cross-tenant test throughput.           |
| **Independent assessment**            | Tenant isolation, privileged/support paths, policy pipeline, action authority and AI agent boundary.        |

## 24.2 Verification levels

| **Level**                   | **Evidence required**                                                                    | **Gate**                                           |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| **V0 Static**               | Policy lint, schema, ownership, no wildcard/broad grant, dependency and secret scanning. | Every change.                                      |
| **V1 Unit**                 | Positive/negative policy and identity component tests with stable reason codes.          | PR/build.                                          |
| **V2 Integration**          | Identity, policy, domain, data and audit end-to-end tests.                               | Release candidate.                                 |
| **V3 Isolation**            | Automated cross-tenant suite across all stores and interfaces.                           | G1 and every material release.                     |
| **V4 Residency/resilience** | Routing matrix, failover, key, support location and dependency chaos tests.              | G1/G2 by capability.                               |
| **V5 Independent**          | External red team/assessment of identity, JIT, action, tenant and AI boundaries.         | Before R2 automation and annually/material change. |

## 24.3 Release blockers

- Any reproducible cross-tenant access or data disclosure path;

- any material operation that can proceed with missing or indeterminate authorization;

- any standing global privilege or unbounded support/partner access;

- any privileged, response, export or AI tool path without attributable actor/subject and audit evidence;

- any residency route that falls back to an unapproved region/provider;

- any session, elevation or delegation that cannot be revoked within its controlled target;

- any policy bundle that is unsigned, unreviewed, non-reproducible or not rollback-capable;

- any customer-facing healthy state while membership, policy, connector or region state is stale/degraded.

# 25 \| SLOs, Metrics and Operational Readiness

| **Metric**                         | **Definition / labels**                                                                              |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **authentication_success_rate**    | Eligible attempts succeeding by identity pattern, tenant and failure class; excludes policy denials. |
| **authn_latency**                  | Start to session result by IdP/method/region and cache path.                                         |
| **authorization_decision_latency** | PDP processing by action/effect/policy bundle; separate PEP/resource checks.                         |
| **authorization_denial_rate**      | Denials by stable reason; monitor unexpected shifts without treating denial as error.                |
| **indeterminate_rate**             | Requests lacking safe policy/context/dependency decision; must be near zero and investigated.        |
| **revocation_propagation**         | Suspend/terminate/grant revoke to rejection across sessions, clients, caches and services.           |
| **jit_expiry_enforcement**         | Grant expiry to privilege rejection and active session termination.                                  |
| **identity_sync_freshness**        | Directory/SCIM cursor age, reconciliation gap and disable-event latency.                             |
| **tenant_isolation_test_pass**     | Automated negative tests passed by layer, release and tenant class.                                  |
| **residency_route_compliance**     | Approved/quarantined/denied routes by data class, purpose, provider and region.                      |
| **support_access_volume**          | Active grants, content-access sessions, duration, customer review and exceptions.                    |
| **orphan_identity_count**          | Principals/clients/grants without active owner/source or beyond expiry.                              |
| **policy_bundle_adoption**         | Runtime decisions by version; stale/unknown bundle usage.                                            |
| **identity_dependency_health**     | ZoikoID, customer IdP, PDP, key, posture and audit path status.                                      |
| **ai_tool_denial/override**        | Agent tool denials, human overrides, cross-tenant blocks and kill-switch events.                     |

## 25.1 SLO governance

| **SLO class**    | **Measurement rule**                                                                                   |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Availability** | Measure eligible authentication/policy/session operations separately from policy denial.               |
| **Latency**      | Define start/end and cache path; report p95/p99 by region and effect class.                            |
| **Revocation**   | Measure end-to-end across tokens, caches, sessions, workload credentials and delegations.              |
| **Freshness**    | SCIM, policy, device, key and region states have explicit thresholds that change system state.         |
| **Correctness**  | Isolation and residency correctness are independent from availability and latency.                     |
| **Security**     | High-risk denial, break-glass, policy tamper and support-access anomalies page the appropriate team.   |
| **Cost**         | Identity-provider, policy decision, logging and cross-region control costs are attributed and bounded. |
| **Claims**       | No public access/isolation/residency claim until measured evidence supports approved wording.          |

## 25.2 Operational runbooks

- customer IdP outage and metadata/certificate rollover;

- ZoikoID/policy service degradation;

- identity compromise and mass session revocation;

- cross-tenant isolation alarm;

- privileged/support-access misuse;

- residency route or provider-policy violation;

- key-service outage and tenant key revocation;

- SCIM backlog/orphan spike;

- policy rollback and emergency hard deny;

- AI agent/tool authorization incident.

# 26 \| Change, Migration and Policy Release Governance

## 26.1 Change classes

| **Change**                         | **Required governance**                                                                                |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **New identity provider/protocol** | Threat/privacy review, tenant mapping, negative assertions, recovery and operational runbook.          |
| **New permission/action**          | Owner, effect class, required context/obligations, role impact, tests and documentation.               |
| **Role change**                    | Policy diff, grant impact, SoD, migration and access-review plan.                                      |
| **Attribute/source change**        | Authority/freshness/missing-value behavior, migration and rollback.                                    |
| **Policy engine/bundle change**    | Signed artifact, deterministic tests, canary, runtime version telemetry and rollback.                  |
| **Tenant hierarchy change**        | Data migration, authorization, audit and UI impact; no silent resource reassignment.                   |
| **Isolation-tier change**          | Provision/migration/cutover/rollback, key/store/search/queue verification and customer evidence.       |
| **Region/residency change**        | Legal/privacy approval, route matrix, data migration, key/backup/support/provider and customer notice. |
| **Delegation/support change**      | Customer authority, scope, visibility, revocation and contract impact.                                 |
| **AI agent/tool change**           | Use-case approval, identity/tool policy, adversarial tests, memory and kill switch.                    |
| **Emergency hard deny**            | Security authority, immediate publication, customer/operations communication and follow-up ADR.        |

## 26.2 Policy release pipeline

7.  Author change against controlled requirement and permission catalog.

8.  Run static lint, policy unit/property tests and SoD checks.

9.  Generate affected principals, roles, tenants, resources and effect classes.

10. Review by owner and independent Security/Privacy approver as classified.

11. Sign the policy/configuration artifact and record provenance.

12. Deploy to synthetic tenants and canary region/tenant cohort.

13. Compare decisions and denials against baseline; verify no cross-tenant or residency regression.

14. Publish gradually with runtime policy-version telemetry.

15. Rollback automatically or manually on controlled thresholds.

16. Archive bundle, diff, approvals, test evidence and deployment result in R20.

## 26.3 Migration safeguards

- Expand-contract for identity and membership schema changes; old/new policy compatibility is explicit.

- Never rewrite historical authorization or audit decisions; new policy applies prospectively with effective time.

- Resource tenant reassignment is a controlled migration with source/destination authorization, reconciliation and evidence.

- Role/permission migration includes grant inventory, user communication, temporary overlap only if risk-approved and expiry enforced.

- Region migration preserves evidence integrity, key ownership, backups, exports and audit lineage.

# 27 \| Required Wireframe Views and Diagrams

The final specification must contain the following controlled views. A text-only policy document is insufficient because reviewers must be able to see trust boundaries, decision precedence, tenant scope, degraded modes and operational evidence.

| **View** | **Controlled view**                     | **Minimum purpose**                                                                          |
|----------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **V01**  | Authority and source-of-truth hierarchy | Master/register/policy/config/runtime evidence precedence.                                   |
| **V02**  | Identity trust-domain context           | Customer IdP, ZoikoID, workload authority, edge, PDP/PEPs, data, broker and audit.           |
| **V03**  | Principal-class matrix                  | Human, workforce, workload, client, connector, agent, partner and emergency controls.        |
| **V04**  | Tenant hierarchy and resource scoping   | Group, tenant, legal entity, BU, environment, workspace and domain resource.                 |
| **V05**  | Human sign-in and session flow          | Discovery, federation, MFA/passkey, session, step-up, authorization, denial and revocation.  |
| **V06**  | Authorization decision flow             | Inputs, layers, precedence, obligations, enforcement and evidence.                           |
| **V07**  | Permission/role/relationship catalog    | Actions, effect classes, resource types, attributes, relationships and SoD.                  |
| **V08**  | Privileged and break-glass flow         | Request, approvals, step-up, elevation, session, expiry, review and alert.                   |
| **V09**  | Delegation and support-access flow      | Grant, named actor, scope, customer visibility, revocation and no transitivity.              |
| **V10**  | Isolation-class matrix                  | T1-T4 controls, availability, keys, stores and verification evidence.                        |
| **V11**  | Data-plane isolation matrix             | API, DB, object, search, lakehouse, cache, queues, observability, AI and backups.            |
| **V12**  | Residency decision matrix               | Data class/purpose/provider/processing/storage/backup/key/support/failover outcomes.         |
| **V13**  | Identity lifecycle state model          | Invite, active, move, suspend, terminate, orphan, reinstate and offboard.                    |
| **V14**  | Degraded-mode matrix                    | IdP, ZoikoID, PDP, KMS, region, audit and posture failures with allowed/prohibited behavior. |
| **V15**  | AI agent identity boundary              | Initiator, model gateway, agent, on-behalf-of, tools, memory, human oversight and evidence.  |
| **V16**  | Threat and negative-test matrix         | Threat, trust boundary, control, test, cadence, owner and evidence.                          |
| **V17**  | SLO and operational dashboard           | Authentication, authorization, revocation, sync, isolation, residency and policy adoption.   |
| **V18**  | Requirement-to-runtime traceability     | Requirement, policy, config, tests, release, decision, evidence and claim.                   |

## 27.1 Visual-state requirements

| **State**                     | **Required treatment**                                                                    |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **LOADING / RESOLVING**       | Show identity/policy/region resolution and timeout; do not show false empty/denied state. |
| **EMPTY / FIRST USE**         | Explain required federation, membership, role or policy setup.                            |
| **NOMINAL / POPULATED**       | Show current tenant, role/relationship, policy version and region.                        |
| **PARTIAL / INCOMPLETE**      | Enumerate missing claims, mappings, sources, regions or review states.                    |
| **STALE / DEGRADED**          | Show last healthy time, impacted decisions and restricted behavior.                       |
| **ERROR / UNAVAILABLE**       | Stable technical error, correlation and retry/support path.                               |
| **UNAUTHORIZED / RESTRICTED** | Explicit policy outcome and safe request/review path; distinct from outage.               |

prohibited_tools: [response.execute, role.grant, evidence.attest]<br />
on_behalf_of: required<br />
memory: {scope: tenant_and_case, ttl: controlled-value}<br />
provider_region_policy: approved-only<br />
human_review: required_for_material_output<br />
kill_switch: enabled</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>

# 29 \| Workstream Handoff, Definition of Ready and Definition of Done

## 29.1 Definition of Ready

- Controlling requirement, release scope and relevant ADRs are approved.

- Principal class, tenant/resource context and source authorities are identified.

- Canonical actions, roles/attributes/relationships and effect classes exist.

- Authorization inputs, decision states, obligations and enforcement point are defined.

- Identity provider/session/workload credential flow and lifecycle behavior are defined.

- Tenant isolation profile and every affected data-store control are identified.

- Residency, provider, key, support-location and failover outcomes are defined.

- Privileged, delegated, support or AI authority is classified and approved.

- Degraded-mode behavior, audit events, metrics and runbooks are defined.

- Positive, negative, cross-tenant, lifecycle and residency tests exist.

- No unresolved authority conflict, broad wildcard grant or missing owner blocks design.

## 29.2 Definition of Done

- Executable policy/configuration matches the approved specification and register views.

- Human, workload, client, connector and agent identities are separately attributable.

- Every material operation resolves tenant/resource/purpose/region and enforces the current policy.

- Positive, deny, indeterminate, unauthorized and unavailable paths are tested and observable.

- Cross-tenant negative tests pass across every affected storage, queue, cache, search, export and AI path.

- Residency routing and no-match quarantine pass the controlled matrix.

- JIT, SoD, step-up, delegation, support visibility, expiry and revocation are proven where applicable.

- Lifecycle suspend/terminate/orphan and session/credential revocation meet approved targets.

- AI agents use separate principals, on-behalf-of context and tool-side reauthorization.

- No standing global privilege, shared service credential, secret in documents or production data in fixtures exists.

- Policy artifacts are signed, canaried, rollback-capable and runtime version telemetry is visible.

- R20 contains approvals, tests, signed artifacts, dashboards/runbooks and exception status.

## 29.3 Workstream handoff package

| **Package item** | **Required content**                                                                       |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope**        | Principal/resource/tenant/region/action scope, requirements, exclusions and owners.        |
| **Policy**       | Actions, roles/attributes/relationships, precedence, obligations, signed bundle and diff.  |
| **Identity**     | IdP/workload/client/agent configuration without secrets; lifecycle and session rules.      |
| **Isolation**    | Tenant profile and store-by-store controls.                                                |
| **Residency**    | Routing matrix, providers, keys, support/failover and blocked outcomes.                    |
| **Security**     | Threat model, privileged/delegated controls and negative tests.                            |
| **Operations**   | Metrics, SLOs, dashboards, alerts, runbooks, degradation and revocation.                   |
| **Evidence**     | ADRs, approvals, test reports, policy/config hashes, release and runtime decision samples. |
