# 11 \| Physical Data Model and Persistence Topology

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image149.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.7125in" alt="Image: image30.png" />

***Figure 3 — Data-store authority and projection topology.***

## 11.1 Physical schema requirements

- One schema namespace per shield-core module, enforced by database roles and CI architecture tests.

- Tenant-aware row-level security or equivalent mandatory on pooled authoritative tables; bypass roles restricted, monitored and JIT.

- Primary and unique indexes include tenant partition context where required to prevent cross-tenant collision and query leakage.

- Large immutable artifacts remain in content-addressed object storage, never base64-embedded in transactional rows.

- Outbox/inbox tables use bounded retention, idempotency keys, replay status and correlation/causation context.

- Search, analytical and graph projections include source version, last-reconciled time and rebuild status.

- Cache keys include tenant and environment context; cache contents are classified, encrypted where required and never sole authority.

- Every physical store declares backup, restore, integrity verification, retention, deletion and offboarding behavior.

## 11.2 Storage decision matrix

| **Data type**                                    | **Primary store**                             | **Projection/secondary store** | **Authority rule**                                                               |
|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant/commercial/configuration**              | Relational                                    | Cache/reporting                | Relational is authoritative.                                                     |
| **Cases, risks, controls and evidence metadata** | Relational                                    | Search/reporting               | Relational is authoritative; projections rebuildable.                            |
| **Evidence content**                             | Encrypted object vault                        | Package export cache           | Content hash and ledger metadata bind authority.                                 |
| **Raw and normalized telemetry**                 | Object lakehouse + event backbone             | Hot analytics/search           | Source-native and normalized objects retained per contract; indexes rebuildable. |
| **Detection/query state**                        | Relational + analytics engine                 | Search/cache                   | Published rules/policies authoritative in relational registry.                   |
| **AI prompts, runs and outputs**                 | Relational metadata + approved object storage | Analytics                      | Gateway record authoritative; provider logs never sole source.                   |
| **Metrics/traces/logs**                          | Observability stores                          | Aggregates                     | Operational evidence only where explicitly promoted and retained.                |

# 13 \| Commands, Events, Snapshots and Temporal Semantics

## 13.1 Temporal fields

| **Time**                          | **Meaning**                                          | **Use**                                                            |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **occurred_at**                   | When the source event occurred.                      | Security event ordering and incident timeline.                     |
| **observed_at**                   | When ZoikoShield or the collector observed the fact. | Latency and freshness calculation.                                 |
| **effective_from / effective_to** | Business-valid period.                               | Policy, entitlement, mapping, authority and control applicability. |
| **recorded_at**                   | When the platform committed the record.              | Audit and system-time reconstruction.                              |
| **ingested_at**                   | When durable ingestion acceptance completed.         | Ingestion SLO and replay.                                          |
| **evaluated_at**                  | When a detection/control/model evaluation executed.  | Reproducibility and assessment history.                            |
| **anchored_at**                   | When evidence chain head was externally witnessed.   | Tamper-evidence boundary.                                          |

## 13.2 Event rules

- Domain events are past-tense facts and immutable once published.

- Commands identify requested authority, actor, purpose, tenant scope and idempotency key.

- Events carry schema version, producer version, correlation, causation, ordering key, source provenance and integrity state.

- Late and out-of-order data behavior is declared by contract; windowed detections declare watermark semantics.

- Snapshots store references to exact mutable-context versions used, not merely a current foreign key.

- Replay may rebuild projections but must never duplicate external response actions, notifications, metering or evidence conclusions.

## 13.3 Bitemporal requirements

Bitemporal storage is mandatory for entitlements, policy applicability, control mappings, asset criticality where it affects historical decisions, identity privilege context, risk acceptance and any fact whose later correction must not alter the record of what the platform knew at decision time.

# 14 \| Data Authority, Lineage, Provenance and Reconciliation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image151.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.53889in" alt="Image: image32.png" />

***Figure 5 — Source-to-assertion lineage spine.***

## 14.1 Authority states

| **State**         | **Meaning**                                                              | **Allowed use**                                             |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AUTHORITATIVE** | Owning source is current and successfully reconciled.                    | May drive governed decisions subject to policy.             |
| **DERIVED**       | Calculated from named authoritative inputs and versioned transformation. | May support decisions with provenance and confidence.       |
| **CACHED**        | Temporary representation of an authority.                                | Never sole basis for irreversible action.                   |
| **DISPUTED**      | Sources conflict or ownership is unresolved.                             | Surface conflict; do not silently choose.                   |
| **STALE**         | Authority exceeds freshness threshold.                                   | Degrade affected controls/detections/reports.               |
| **UNAVAILABLE**   | Source cannot be accessed or permission changed.                         | Expose coverage gap and retry/escalate.                     |
| **QUARANTINED**   | Failed security, schema, residency or integrity validation.              | Not available to normal consumers.                          |
| **REDACTED**      | Value intentionally hidden under policy.                                 | Preserve redaction reason and original authority reference. |

## 14.2 Reconciliation requirements

- Reconciliation compares source counts, checksums, watermarks, expected-object inventories and permissions, not only successful API responses.

- Field-level merges retain source, precedence rule, confidence and last-reconciled time.

- Conflicts open a reviewable reconciliation item with owner and service impact.

- Reports and AI retrieval bundles include lineage to the frozen source versions used.

- Any assertion lacking an unbroken lineage chain is labeled unsupported and blocked from approved claims.

# 15 \| Multi-Tenancy, Isolation and Residency Data Rules

| **Layer**                   | **Mandatory tenant boundary**                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Relational**              | RLS/partition policy, tenant-inclusive uniqueness, scoped roles, cross-tenant negative tests.                      |
| **Object storage**          | Tenant and region prefixes/buckets, policy conditions, tenant-context encryption and inventory reconciliation.     |
| **Event backbone**          | Authenticated producer, tenant partition/headers, authorization at publish/consume, replay scope.                  |
| **Search/analytics**        | Tenant-filter enforcement below application query layer, index strategy, query audit and negative tests.           |
| **Cache**                   | Tenant/environment in key, bounded TTL, no sensitive unencrypted payload, flush/rebuild plan.                      |
| **AI retrieval/embeddings** | Tenant-isolated indexes or cryptographically enforced namespaces; source ACL and purpose filter at retrieval time. |
| **Observability**           | Tenant identifiers pseudonymized where possible; sensitive attributes prohibited or redacted.                      |
| **Export/backup**           | Tenant-scoped manifests, region and legal-hold behavior, integrity proof and deletion schedule.                    |

## 15.1 Residency routing contract

The route is computed before durable persistence from tenant region, source region, data class, purpose, provider eligibility, transfer mechanism, contract and key policy. An unmatched or conflicting route fails closed to quarantine and creates a visible operational and customer coverage state.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>ISOLATION BLOCKER</strong></p>
<p>Any code path, query, index, cache key, object prefix, AI retrieval or support tool capable of omitting tenant scope is a P0 release blocker unless the operation is a specifically approved platform-wide control with independent authorization and audit.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 16 \| Data Classification, Privacy Purpose and Minimization

| **Class**                   | **Examples**                                                                    | **Required control posture**                                         |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **DC-0 Public**             | Approved public product metadata.                                               | Normal integrity controls.                                           |
| **DC-1 Internal**           | Non-public operating and engineering data.                                      | Workforce access by role.                                            |
| **DC-2 Confidential**       | Customer configuration, cases, controls, commercial and service data.           | Tenant scoped, encrypted, purpose bound.                             |
| **DC-3 Personal**           | Identifiers, account and user activity data.                                    | Privacy purpose, minimization, DSR and transfer controls.            |
| **DC-4 Sensitive Security** | Telemetry, vulnerabilities, secrets metadata, response actions, threat details. | Restricted access, strong logging, egress and support controls.      |
| **DC-5 Evidence / Legal**   | Audit artifacts, approvals, legal hold, incident and assurance evidence.        | Integrity, retention, access and package controls.                   |
| **DC-6 Secret Material**    | Passwords, tokens, private keys and recovery codes.                             | Never stored in documents or normal databases; vault reference only. |

## 16.1 Processing-purpose contract

- Every collection, privileged access, export, AI call and secondary use references an approved processing purpose.

- Purpose incompatible with the original collection requires explicit approval, contract/legal basis and updated register entries.

- Source-side filtering and field suppression are preferred over collecting then masking.

- Personal and sensitive data fields identify masking, tokenization, indexing, logging and model-input rules.

- Customer data is never used for model training absent explicit contractual authorization and AI Register approval.

# 17 \| Evidence Ledger and Audit-Package Data Model

| **Object**             | **Required fields / behavior**                                                                                                                                     |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **evidence_object**    | evidence_id, tenant, source, collector identity/version, collection/coverage times, content hash, scope, classification, retention, hold, freshness, completeness. |
| **evidence_content**   | Content-addressed encrypted object; WORM/object-lock where required; malware and format validation; no silent overwrite.                                           |
| **ledger_entry**       | Tenant chain sequence, previous hash, record hash, trusted timestamp reference, signer and integrity state.                                                        |
| **anchor_batch**       | Merkle root, included tenant chain heads, signing key ID, external witness reference, publication time and proof.                                                  |
| **evaluator_run**      | Evaluator/version, input evidence IDs/hashes, policy/mapping versions, output, limitations, failure state and runtime receipt.                                     |
| **control_assessment** | Control/scope, status, evidence basis, completeness/freshness, confidence, owner, decision time and supersession.                                                  |
| **audit_package**      | Frozen manifest, package scope, evidence hashes, chain/Merkle proofs, framework versions, evaluator versions, known limitations and verifier version.              |

## 17.1 Immutability and correction

Evidence metadata and frozen packages are immutable. Corrections use a new object or assessment linked through supersedes/corrects relationships. Deletion under policy creates a tombstone and signed deletion evidence where retention and legal hold permit; an old package remains verifiable against its manifest even when later access to content is lawfully restricted.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>COMPLETENESS RULE</strong></p>
<p>Cryptographic integrity proves that retained material is unaltered; it does not prove that all expected material was collected. Completeness is modeled separately and may be COMPLETE, PARTIAL, STALE, COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY, PERMISSION_CHANGED or EVALUATOR_FAILED.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 18 \| Detection Replay and Analytical Reproducibility

- Every alert records detection version, event set/watermarks, enrichment snapshot references, policy version, threat-intel set and engine/runtime version.

- Windowed rules declare window, ordering, late-arrival, missing-data and watermark behavior.

- Replay uses original versions and snapshots; current asset or identity context is never substituted silently.

- A replay mismatch records NON_DETERMINISTIC with the exact divergent input, engine or serialization identified.

- AI-assisted candidates are not reproducible production detections until deterministically expressed or explicitly governed as advisory.

- Analytical queries used in material reports are versioned, parameterized, tenant scoped and linked to the output snapshot.

## 18.1 Snapshot classes

| **Snapshot**                | **Minimum contents**                                                                     |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Asset context**           | Identity, owner, criticality, environment, exposure, source and reconciliation state.    |
| **Identity context**        | Account/person mapping, privileges, groups, authentication state, source and confidence. |
| **Threat-intelligence set** | Indicators, relationships, confidence, TLP, validity window and feed/version.            |
| **Control context**         | Applicable objectives, implementation, exceptions, mappings and evaluator policy.        |
| **Response policy**         | Authority, approvals, action allowlist, limits and customer attestation requirements.    |
| **AI retrieval bundle**     | Source IDs/versions, chunks, permissions, freshness, poisoning checks and purpose.       |

# 20 \| Retention, Legal Hold, Deletion, Export and Offboarding

| **Lifecycle control**     | **Required model behavior**                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Retention assignment**  | Applied from data class, purpose, tenant tier, contract, jurisdiction and object type; versioned policy reference stored.   |
| **Legal hold**            | Hold scope, authority, start/end, reason and review are explicit; deletion is suspended and conflict is visible.            |
| **Deletion request**      | Identity, authority, scope, reason, stores, dependencies and outcome recorded.                                              |
| **Cryptographic erasure** | Permitted only where key scope and backup behavior make erasure complete and demonstrable.                                  |
| **Backup expiry**         | Deletion attestation states backup retention and final expiry rather than claiming immediate deletion where untrue.         |
| **Export**                | Open documented formats, schema versions, manifests, evidence proofs, source provenance and known limitations.              |
| **Offboarding**           | Configuration, cases, controls, risks, evidence, packages and approved telemetry exports; post-export deletion attestation. |
| **Derived data**          | Indexes, embeddings, caches, projections and analytics rows are included in deletion and rebuild logic.                     |

## 20.1 Evidence/privacy conflict handling

Where deletion rights, contractual retention, security evidence and legal hold conflict, the data model must represent the conflict, decision owner, applicable authority, restricted-access state and review deadline. Silent retention and silent deletion are both prohibited.

# 21 \| Schema Evolution, Migration, Compatibility and Rollback

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image153.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.53889in" alt="Image: image34.png" />

***Figure 7 — Schema evolution and migration safety model.***

## 21.1 Compatibility rules

| **Change**                         | **Default classification** | **Required control**                                                          |
|------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Add optional field/table/index** | Backward compatible        | Version, defaults, performance and export behavior tested.                    |
| **Add required field**             | Potentially breaking       | Expand with nullable/default, backfill, verify, then enforce.                 |
| **Rename field**                   | Breaking                   | Add new field, dual-write/adapter, migrate consumers, deprecate old.          |
| **Change type/unit/semantics**     | Breaking                   | New version and explicit conversion; never silent reinterpretation.           |
| **Delete field/table**             | Breaking/destructive       | Zero-consumer proof, retention/legal review, backup and rollback plan.        |
| **Repartition/rekey**              | High risk                  | Shadow copy or online migration, tenant reconciliation and rollback.          |
| **Change encryption/key scope**    | High risk                  | Cryptographic design review, staged re-encryption and integrity verification. |
| **Change AI embedding model**      | Semantic breaking          | New index/version, retrieval evaluation, dual-run and deletion policy.        |

## 21.2 Migration manifest requirements

- Migration ID, owner, dependency order, affected tenants/regions/stores and requirement/ADR references.

- Preconditions, lock/availability behavior, expected duration, resource/cost envelope and observability.

- Forward steps, idempotency, backfill checkpoints, validation queries and integrity checks.

- Rollback or compensation strategy with data-loss statement.

- Tenant-by-tenant reconciliation and failure isolation.

- Post-cutover consumer proof and old-contract retirement criteria.

- Release evidence and approval record.

<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>EMERGENCY DATA FIX</strong></p>
<p>Direct production data correction is prohibited. Emergency repair uses an approved, peer-reviewed, idempotent repair job with scoped authorization, dry run, before/after evidence, rollback/compensation and post-use review.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

# 22 \| Data Quality, Freshness, Completeness and Health States

| **Dimension**         | **Definition**                                         | **Required state behavior**                                      |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Validity**          | Conforms to schema and semantic constraints.           | Invalid data quarantined with reason and source feedback.        |
| **Completeness**      | Expected required facts/objects are present.           | Partial is visible and propagates to dependent decisions.        |
| **Freshness**         | Within approved age for purpose.                       | Stale state appears at threshold; no green status.               |
| **Accuracy**          | Matches authoritative source within defined tolerance. | Disputes and confidence recorded.                                |
| **Consistency**       | Related authorities and projections reconcile.         | Drift opens reconciliation item.                                 |
| **Uniqueness**        | No unintended duplicate semantic object.               | Deduplication preserves source records and rationale.            |
| **Integrity**         | Hashes, signatures, chain or checksums verify.         | Failed integrity is quarantined and incidented.                  |
| **Coverage**          | Expected sources/assets/periods are represented.       | Coverage gaps affect controls, detections and reports.           |
| **Permission health** | Collector retains required access.                     | Permission changes immediately degrade evidence/telemetry state. |

## 22.1 Health-state propagation

The specification must define how source and contract health propagates to normalized data, context snapshots, detections, control assessments, dashboards, AI retrieval and reports. A dependent output may not present greater certainty or health than its material inputs unless an approved compensating source exists and is disclosed.

# 24 \| Lakehouse, Search, Graph and Reporting Projections

| **Projection**                       | **Authority source**                  | **Required reconstruction control**                                        |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Normalized telemetry lakehouse**   | Raw source payloads + mapping/version | Reprocess by mapping version and replay manifest.                          |
| **Hot detection/search index**       | Normalized events + context snapshots | Index generation/version, checkpoint and tenant reconciliation.            |
| **Asset/exposure relationship view** | Asset/identity/exposure authorities   | Projection timestamp, source versions, confidence and stale state.         |
| **Attack-path graph**                | Relationship projection               | Rebuildable; graph engine not authoritative; stale inputs visibly degrade. |
| **Alert/case search**                | Relational alert/case authority       | Outbox checkpoint and row/index count/hash reconciliation.                 |
| **Control posture dashboard**        | Assessments/evidence authorities      | Snapshot scope, completeness and evaluator versions.                       |
| **Executive/Board report**           | Approved frozen snapshot              | Immutable render, manifest, limitations and drill-down references.         |
| **AI retrieval index**               | Approved source objects/chunks        | Source/version/ACL/embedding model lineage and deletion propagation.       |

## 24.1 Projection prohibitions

- No business-state update writes directly to a search, graph, cache or reporting projection without the authoritative write first succeeding.

- No projection may erase source uncertainty, completeness or authorization state.

- No AI retrieval index may outlive the source or retain content after a required deletion beyond approved technical latency.

- No report or dashboard number may be irreproducible from a versioned snapshot and query/evaluator definition.

<td>Role/workstream access, synthetic data, audited query tooling, no shared accounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Production support read</strong></td>
<td>JIT, ticket/case purpose, tenant scope, masking, session audit and expiry.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><strong>Production mutation</strong></td>
<td>Exceptional only; dual approval, repair job, dry run, evidence and post-use review.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Database administration</strong></td>
<td>Separate identity, JIT, monitored session, no unrestricted application impersonation.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><strong>Evidence vault administration</strong></td>
<td>Dual control, HSM/KMS policy, no content browsing by default, ledger-audited access.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>AI data access</strong></td>
<td>Gateway only, approved purpose/model/region, retrieval provenance and cost cap.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><strong>Export</strong></td>
<td>Named authority, purpose, scope, manifest, encryption, expiry and download audit.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="2"><p><strong>NO SECRETS IN DATA MODELS</strong></p>
<p>Schemas and documents may store a secret reference, key ID, vault path or rotation state. Passwords, tokens, private keys and recovery material are never valid business fields.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

# 27 \| Automated Data-Architecture Fitness Functions

| **ID**     | **Automated rule**                                                                                           |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **DAF-01** | All tenant-owned tables/events/objects include approved tenant context and negative tests.                   |
| **DAF-02** | Cross-module direct table access fails CI.                                                                   |
| **DAF-03** | Every published contract has owner, version, compatibility, classification and consumers.                    |
| **DAF-04** | Breaking schema change without migration manifest and consumer proof fails release.                          |
| **DAF-05** | Material state changes emit an outbox event and audit event.                                                 |
| **DAF-06** | Evidence records without content hash, collector/version, scope, time and completeness fail validation.      |
| **DAF-07** | Compliance/control status cannot be COMPLETE/healthy when required evidence is non-COMPLETE.                 |
| **DAF-08** | AI run without tenant, purpose, model/prompt version, retrieval provenance and disposition fails validation. |
| **DAF-09** | Search/graph/report projections expose source version and reconciliation health.                             |
| **DAF-10** | Raw production customer data is rejected from development/test environments.                                 |
| **DAF-11** | Retention/deletion policy coverage is complete for every classified object.                                  |
| **DAF-12** | Residency routing has an explicit test for every supported region/data-class/purpose combination.            |
| **DAF-13** | Replay of golden detections and control evaluations is deterministic or explicitly records divergence.       |
| **DAF-14** | Every migration includes forward, validation and rollback/compensation tests.                                |
| **DAF-15** | Export round-trip preserves semantics, evidence proofs and stable identifiers.                               |
| **DAF-16** | No schema stores raw secret material outside approved vault interfaces.                                      |
| **DAF-17** | No composite risk/report value lacks component factors, policy/evaluator version and source snapshot.        |
| **DAF-18** | Orphaned entities, fields, events, migrations and contracts fail traceability reconciliation.                |

# 28 \| Testing and Verification Strategy

| **Test family**            | **Minimum required tests**                                                                                      |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Schema and semantic**    | Type, constraints, enum evolution, unit/timezone, null/unknown semantics and documentation lint.                |
| **Contract compatibility** | Producer/consumer, backward/forward compatibility, deprecation and SDK/code generation.                         |
| **Tenant isolation**       | Cross-tenant API, DB, object, queue, search, cache, analytics, export and AI retrieval negative tests.          |
| **Migration**              | Expand/contract, idempotency, backfill, resume, tenant isolation, rollback and large-volume behavior.           |
| **Lineage/replay**         | Source-to-assertion trace, deterministic detection/control replay and package reproduction.                     |
| **Evidence integrity**     | Hash/signature, chain continuity, Merkle proof, external root and offline verifier.                             |
| **Privacy lifecycle**      | Purpose, minimization, DSR, hold, deletion, backup expiry and export.                                           |
| **AI data**                | Prompt injection via data, retrieval poisoning, cross-tenant leakage, memory expiry, tool receipt and deletion. |
| **Projection recovery**    | Drop/rebuild search, graph, dashboard and embedding indexes from authorities.                                   |
| **Performance/cost**       | Reference envelope, hot partitions, query concurrency, retention and unit-cost guardrails.                      |
| **DR/restore**             | Backup restore, event replay, projection rebuild and anchor reconciliation.                                     |

## 28.1 Required test evidence

- Test ID linked to requirement, contract, schema version, migration and release.

- Environment, dataset/source, tenant/region configuration and tool versions.

- Expected and actual result, including negative and degraded states.

- Failure artifacts, risk/exception link and retest evidence.

- Performance and cost results against the current Scale Envelope Register.

- Signed release evidence manifest stored in R20.

# 30 \| Definition of Ready and Definition of Done

## 30.1 Definition of Ready

72. Domain owner, requirements, users/consumers and current-release scope are approved.

73. Aggregate boundary, authority and material invariants are defined.

74. Tenant, region, legal-entity, data-class and processing-purpose rules are resolved.

75. Logical object and field semantics, temporal behavior and source authority are complete.

76. Physical store, partition, encryption, retention, backup and projection decisions are approved.

77. Contracts, compatibility, migration and deprecation strategy are defined.

78. Evidence, AI, lineage, quality and degraded-state requirements are included where applicable.

79. Tests, observability, capacity and release evidence are defined.

80. No unresolved architecture, privacy, security or licensing conflict remains.

## 30.2 Definition of Done

81. Executable schema and contract artifacts are reviewed, versioned and published.

82. Code respects module ownership and passes architecture fitness functions.

83. Migrations and backfills are idempotent, tested and reconciled.

84. Tenant isolation, authorization, privacy lifecycle and negative tests pass.

85. Lineage, audit events, evidence and AI decision records are complete.

86. Quality/freshness/coverage states propagate correctly to dependent surfaces.

87. Projections can be rebuilt from authoritative data within the approved recovery window.

88. Performance, capacity and unit-economics tests meet the current envelope.

89. Export/offboarding and deletion behavior pass applicable tests.

90. Operational dashboards, alerts and runbooks are active.

91. Release evidence is complete in R20 and no blocking exception remains.

92. Document, catalogs and generated documentation are current.

# 00 \| Critical Review and Refined Architecture Decision

The prior Document-04 concept correctly identified architecture doctrine and system context as a separate engineering control. It was not yet sufficient for a distributed team because it could still become a diagram repository rather than an enforceable engineering authority. The refined design below closes the gaps that most often cause architecture drift: unclear view ownership, hidden failure paths, absent fitness functions, stale ADRs, uncontrolled technology choices, unbounded regional data movement and AI components escaping the deterministic control plane.

| **ID**    | **Finding**                                             | **Risk**                                                                                                 | **Required refinement**                                                                                                                               |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AR-01** | Doctrine without automated enforcement                  | Principles become advisory language.                                                                     | Every material doctrine item receives an invariant ID, implementation consequence, test or policy control and release evidence reference.             |
| **AR-02** | Context diagrams without trust-boundary semantics       | Engineers can connect systems without understanding authority, data class, region or failure behavior.   | Every edge declares protocol, direction, identity, tenant context, data class, persistence, timeout, retry and audit requirement.                     |
| **AR-03** | Logical and deployment views conflated                  | Teams infer that every bounded context is a separate microservice.                                       | Separate product layers, logical planes, domain modules and deployables; extraction requires measured criteria and an ADR.                            |
| **AR-04** | No temporal or source-authority model                   | Mutable enrichment and duplicated stores produce irreproducible decisions.                               | Name write authority, projection status, event time, processing time, version and replay semantics for every material data product.                   |
| **AR-05** | Happy-path architecture                                 | Failure, staleness, partial coverage and authorization denial are discovered during implementation.      | Every component and interaction defines nominal, partial, stale, unauthorized, unavailable and recovery behavior.                                     |
| **AR-06** | AI shown as a general intelligence layer                | Engineers may place LLMs on authorization, evidence or response paths.                                   | Gateway-only AI, no-LLM-critical-path, bounded tools, cited outputs, human authority and deterministic fallback are explicit architecture invariants. |
| **AR-07** | Security detail either overexposed or withheld entirely | Teams either receive sensitive attack detail they do not need or miss controls required to build safely. | Main document states full invariant and acceptance test; EC-3 annex holds exploit paths, production topology and key hierarchy.                       |
| **AR-08** | Architecture decisions detached from release truth      | A diagram can remain approved while code and deployment drift.                                           | Architecture fitness functions, topology manifests and R20 reconciliation become release gates.                                                       |

| **REFINED DECISION** | ZS-ENG-ARCH-001 will be the current-release engineering projection of the approved Tier-0 architecture. It will bind system context, boundaries, interaction patterns, invariants, failure behavior, technology decision envelopes and architecture fitness functions. It will not duplicate detailed data, API, AI, security or infrastructure specifications. |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 01 \| Document Control, Authority and Approval

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image155.png" style="width:6.8in;height:3.30278in" alt="Five-level hierarchy from legal and contractual authority to controlled architecture, registers and implementation evidence." />

***Figure 1 — Architecture authority, derivation and implementation precedence.***

| **Control field**         | **Required value**                                                                                                               |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Accountable owner**     | CTO / Chief Architect.                                                                                                           |
| **Operational owner**     | Architecture Enablement Lead or delegated Staff/Principal Architect.                                                             |
| **Control co-owners**     | CISO, Head of Engineering, Data Architect, AI Systems Lead and SRE Lead for applicable sections.                                 |
| **Approvers**             | CTO, CISO, Head of Engineering and Product Engineering authority.                                                                |
| **Review cadence**        | Quarterly; before each release baseline; and on any trigger in Section 26.                                                       |
| **Implementation status** | Only APPROVED + CURRENT versions are valid. DRAFT, OVERDUE, SUPERSEDED and WITHDRAWN states cannot authorize new implementation. |
| **Restricted annexes**    | EC-3; separately approved and distributed under ZS-ENG-GOV-001.                                                                  |
| **Primary evidence**      | R20 approval record, current ADR digest, architecture fitness-function results and recipient acknowledgment.                     |

## 1.1 Source precedence

**1.** Applicable law, executed contract and approved regulatory obligation for the specific tenant or service.

**2.** Current controlled master documents, led by C1 and A7.

**3.** Approved ADRs and current machine-readable register values for the specific decision.

**4.** Current approved ZS-ENG-ARCH-001 and its applicable restricted annex.

**5.** Current workstream delivery pack and signed interface contracts.

**6.** Issue tracker, code comment, meeting note, email or chat instruction.

| **STOP-WORK RULE** | A lower authority never resolves a conflict with a higher authority. The affected implementation stops until the controlling owner records a decision and updates the dependent artifacts. |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 02 \| Executive Engineering Mandate

| **MANDATE** | Build one horizontal, evidence-first, AI-centric security and assurance platform for the approved current release. Preserve domain boundaries inside a modular monolith, isolate ingestion, AI, response and evidence anchoring where their risk or scale requires it, and make every material decision reproducible, tenant-scoped and release-verifiable. |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| **Mandate dimension** | **Engineering interpretation**                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Market boundary**   | Regulated-first and high-assurance; no industry-specific core forks.                                                                                                   |
| **Entry offers**      | Managed Defense and Continuous Assurance may land independently but share one platform spine.                                                                          |
| **Core moat**         | Evidence ledger, independently verifiable audit packages, control evaluation, cross-tool context and governed response.                                                |
| **AI posture**        | AI assists; deterministic controls authorize. No LLM on authentication, authorization, entitlement, integrity, compliance state or privileged response approval paths. |
| **Runtime posture**   | Modular monolith first; bounded satellites only for divergent scale, trust or failure domains.                                                                         |
| **Data posture**      | Regional by default; tenant, environment, region, purpose and data class travel with every request, event and object.                                                  |
| **Security posture**  | Assume ZoikoShield itself is the crown jewel and bound blast radius accordingly.                                                                                       |
| **Scope posture**     | Current release only. Deferred sector, sovereign, OT and Zoiko-built EDR capability remains out of build scope.                                                        |

# 03 \| Purpose, Applicability and Disclosure Boundary

## 3.1 Purpose

Define the controlled document architecture and minimum-complete engineering content for ZoikoShield system doctrine, context, boundaries and integration rules. The document tells each engineering workstream what the system is, what it is not, where authority resides, how components interact, how failure is represented and which architectural facts must be enforced automatically.

## 3.2 Applies to

- Every ERB-01 module, satellite, interface, data store, connector, AI surface, evidence flow, experience contract and deployment cell.

- All engineers, architects, QA, SRE, security, AI, data and managed-service tooling teams producing or reviewing implementation.

- All technical ADRs, architecture changes, service extraction proposals, technology introductions and cross-boundary data flows.

- All build, integration, release and operational evidence used to demonstrate conformity to C1.

## 3.3 Deliberately excludes

- Full market strategy, pipeline, pricing, customer identities, Board financials and negotiated partner terms.

- Detailed logical/physical schemas, API payloads, event definitions and connector implementation contracts owned by Documents 05–06.

- Complete threat trees, production key hierarchy, live network coordinates, unresolved exploit detail and emergency secrets held in EC-3 annexes.

- Future G3/G4 sector, sovereign and OT designs not approved into the current release baseline.

# 04 \| Binding Architecture Doctrine

| **ID**    | **Doctrine**                   | **Binding engineering consequence**                                                                                                                             |
|-----------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **AD-01** | Evidence before assertion      | No material conclusion, response, risk score, control state, AI recommendation or privileged change completes without attributable evidence and an audit event. |
| **AD-02** | Tenant context everywhere      | Tenant, environment, region, legal entity, purpose and data class are mandatory context at all trust boundaries.                                                |
| **AD-03** | No silent mutation             | Material history is versioned or corrected through compensating records; overwrite without trace is prohibited.                                                 |
| **AD-04** | Human-in-command               | Automation is bounded by policy, confidence, authority, approval, reversibility and blast radius.                                                               |
| **AD-05** | Integrate before duplicate     | Connect existing effective controls; do not recreate EDR, email security, scanners or generic awareness engines without Board-level authorization.              |
| **AD-06** | Policy is executable           | Authorization, residency, retention, response, entitlement, evidence and AI rules are machine-evaluable and versioned.                                          |
| **AD-07** | Failure is explicit            | Partial, stale, unauthorized, unavailable and recovery states are first-class; unknown is never treated as healthy or compliant.                                |
| **AD-08** | No LLM critical path           | Critical detection, identity, authorization, evidence integrity, compliance state and action approval continue deterministically without a model.               |
| **AD-09** | Regional persistence by design | Residency is decided before durable storage; the global plane carries bounded metadata only.                                                                    |
| **AD-10** | Economics are architecture     | Scale and cost guardrails are measurable release constraints, not post-release FinOps aspirations.                                                              |
| **AD-11** | Modular monolith first         | Domain boundaries are enforced in code; service extraction follows measured need.                                                                               |
| **AD-12** | Claims follow proof            | No public or customer-facing claim is enabled until R17 and R20 carry approved evidence.                                                                        |
| **AD-13** | Independent verifiability      | Auditors can validate frozen evidence packages without trusting Zoiko runtime or personnel.                                                                     |
| **AD-14** | Reversibility by default       | High-consequence decisions, migrations and actions require rollback, compensation or explicitly approved irreversibility.                                       |
| **AD-15** | Architecture as code           | Boundaries, dependencies, policies, schemas, topology and fitness functions are versioned and checked in CI.                                                    |

# 05 \| Source Authority, Decision Precedence and Conflict Rules

| **Source**                      | **Owns**                                                                                                 | **Does not own**                                        |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| **C1 Back-End Architecture**    | Tier-0 decisions, canonical layers, topology doctrine, major invariants, gates and strategic boundaries. | Current implementation detail or register field values. |
| **R02 ADR/Gate Register**       | Specific approved decisions, deadlines, defaults, consequences and supersession.                         | Unapproved options or implementation tasks.             |
| **R06 Service/Module Catalog**  | Current module ownership, APIs/events, dependencies, SLO, tier and deployment.                           | Code-level internals.                                   |
| **R09 Data Register**           | Data authority, classification, purpose, region, retention and lineage.                                  | Schema implementation mechanics.                        |
| **R10/R11 Interface Registers** | Approved API, webhook, event and schema identities and versions.                                         | Business requirement intent.                            |
| **R19 SLO/Scale Register**      | Current quantitative targets, scale envelope and cost ceilings.                                          | Test execution results.                                 |
| **R20 Release Evidence**        | Observed conformity for a release.                                                                       | Architecture intent or exception approval.              |

## 5.1 Conflict classes

| **Class**                 | **Example**                                                             | **Required action**                                       |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authority conflict**    | Architecture document permits a flow prohibited by privacy or contract. | Stop; escalate to Legal/Privacy and architecture owner.   |
| **Decision conflict**     | Current code follows a superseded ADR.                                  | Block merge/release; migrate or approve exception.        |
| **Interface conflict**    | Wireframe, API and event contract disagree on state or field.           | Resolve source authority; regenerate dependent artifacts. |
| **Topology conflict**     | Deployment manifest contains an unapproved service or data store.       | Reject deployment until ADR and catalog update.           |
| **Failure conflict**      | Component returns nominal status while upstream coverage is partial.    | Treat as P0 control defect.                               |
| **AI authority conflict** | Agent can invoke a tool beyond approved decision rights.                | Disable path; Security/AI review required.                |

# 06 \| Required Document Architecture and Controlled View Set

| **Context section**    | Actors, external systems, trust boundaries, data classes, authority and major flows.                                   |
| **Logical views**      | Product layers, planes, domains, module ownership and dependency direction.                                            |
| **Deployment views**   | Deployables, regional cells, stores, networks at approved abstraction and failure domains.                             |
| **Dynamic views**      | Commands, events, evidence, response actions, AI calls, retries, timeouts and compensation.                            |
| **Data views**         | Sources of truth, projections, lineage, persistence and regional authority.                                            |
| **Failure views**      | Nominal, partial, stale, unauthorized, unavailable, recovery and disaster states.                                      |
| **Fitness functions**  | Automated boundary, topology, policy, dependency, cost and resilience checks.                                          |
| **Governance**         | ADR triggers, service extraction, exception, review and supersession.                                                  |
| **Annexes**            | Controlled templates, matrices, view catalog, restricted detail references and machine-readable metadata.              |

## 9.1 Dependency rule

Logical planes do not authorize direct database access or cyclic domain dependencies. Each domain names its write authority, published interface, emitted events and permitted dependencies in R06. Architecture tests must fail any direct table or internal-package dependency that violates the approved direction.

# 10 \| Day-One Deployment Topology and Module Boundaries

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image158.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.57292in" alt="Central shield-core modular monolith with isolated ingestion, AI gateway, action broker and evidence anchoring satellites." />

***Figure 4 — Day-one deployables and enforced domain boundaries.***

| **Deployable**             | **Day-one responsibility**                                                                                                                 | **Isolation rationale**                                                             | **Prohibited**                                                                                                      |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **shield-core**            | Tenant/commercial control; asset/exposure; detections/alerts/cases; controls/evidence metadata; assessments/risk/reporting; authorization. | Transactional integrity and one operational surface while domain boundaries mature. | Cross-module direct table access; connector credentials; model-provider SDKs; standing customer action credentials. |
| **shield-ingest**          | Connector runtime, source authentication, routing, validation, normalization, quarantine and replay.                                       | Bursty throughput, untrusted source data and independent scaling/failure.           | Business source-of-truth state; action broker invocation.                                                           |
| **shield-ai-gateway**      | Provider routing, redaction, prompt profiles, retrieval, tool policy, evaluation hooks and spend controls.                                 | Distinct egress, data terms, adversarial surface and cost profile.                  | Direct authorization, compliance assertion or privileged action approval.                                           |
| **shield-action-broker**   | External response policy, approvals, per-tenant signing, rate ceilings, receipts, compensation and freeze.                                 | Highest-consequence blast radius and independent kill path.                         | General business logic; standing global customer credentials.                                                       |
| **shield-evidence-anchor** | Tenant chain-head aggregation, Merkle roots, external witness publication and verification receipts.                                       | Independent integrity boundary and separate key custody.                            | Evidence content evaluation or mutable business state.                                                              |

## 10.1 Internal module boundary contract

- Each module owns a schema namespace and published in-process API mirroring a future service contract.

- Cross-module direct table access fails static architecture tests and database grants.

- All state changes that publish events use the transactional outbox pattern.

- Cross-module reads use interfaces, projections or governed data products; cache never becomes authority.

- Each module declares owner, dependencies, SLIs, threat model, runbook and extraction status in R06.

# 11 \| Regional Cells and Global Control-Plane Boundary

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image159.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.78056in" alt="Global metadata control plane connected to three regional data cells, each holding core runtime and regional stores." />

***Figure 5 — Regional-cell architecture and bounded global control plane.***

| **Plane/cell**                    | **May contain**                                                                                                                     | **Must not contain**                                                                             | **Failure posture**                                                                        |
|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Global control plane**          | Tenant directory, catalog metadata, deployment inventory, feature policy, signed configuration and approved aggregate health/usage. | Raw telemetry, evidence content, secrets, unrestricted personal data or regional search indexes. | Regional cells continue under cached signed policy; privileged global changes fail closed. |
| **Regional data cell**            | Regional API/ingest, shield-core, search/lakehouse, evidence vault, regional keys and operational telemetry.                        | Data assigned to another residency region unless approved transfer applies.                      | Multi-AZ continuity; queue/backpressure; customer-visible degraded state.                  |
| **Cross-region standby**          | Encrypted backups, replication manifests and minimum recovery state under approved residency.                                       | Active unrestricted customer access or hidden analytics.                                         | Failover only through tested runbook and reconciliation.                                   |
| **Customer-side execution point** | Scoped connector/agent, pinned verification key and local command validation.                                                       | Global Zoiko credentials or unrestricted tenant authority.                                       | Reject unsigned, expired or replayed commands.                                             |

## 11.1 Required regional invariants

| **ID**    | **Invariant**                                                                           | **Fitness function / evidence**                                                          |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **RG-01** | Residency route is resolved before first durable write.                                 | CI policy tests for every supported data-class/region pair; unmatched route quarantines. |
| **RG-02** | Global stores reject raw telemetry and evidence content schemas.                        | Schema allowlist + DLP test + storage inventory reconciliation.                          |
| **RG-03** | Tenant key and region binding are immutable without controlled migration.               | Database constraint + migration approval record.                                         |
| **RG-04** | Cross-region transfer requires approved mechanism and purpose.                          | Policy decision log + R09 reference.                                                     |
| **RG-05** | Restore reconciles transactional state, event replay and last external evidence anchor. | Quarterly restore evidence in R20.                                                       |

# 12 \| Interaction, Command and Event Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image160.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.78056in" alt="Three rows showing user commands, telemetry events and response actions through validation, persistence, streams, policy and receipts." />

***Figure 6 — Canonical interaction patterns for commands, events and governed actions.***

| **Interaction type**          | **Required pattern**                                                                                                  | **Idempotency / ordering**                                                     | **Failure behavior**                                                                              |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **User/API command**          | Authenticate → authorize → validate → persist intent/state → emit outbox event → return stable result/correlation ID. | Idempotency key for retriable writes; optimistic concurrency where applicable. | Reject before side effects; expose machine error; do not report success until authority persists. |
| **Telemetry/event**           | Authenticate source → validate/residency route → normalize/enrich → publish → consume idempotently.                   | Partition key and deduplication key declared; late-data semantics explicit.    | Quarantine invalid/unauthorized data; backpressure before loss; coverage marked partial.          |
| **Cross-module domain event** | Commit source state and outbox atomically → publish canonical event → inbox/dedup at consumer.                        | At-least-once transport, idempotent consumer, no hidden exactly-once claim.    | Retry with bounded poison-message path; source remains authority.                                 |
| **Response action**           | Create proposal → policy/authority/approval → sign per tenant → execute → receipt → verify → compensate/rollback.     | Nonce, expiry and replay prevention; rate ceilings.                            | Fail closed; no unsigned action; uncertain result enters reconciliation state.                    |
| **Evidence collection**       | Schedule/trigger → collect → hash/sign → append metadata → evaluate → update completeness.                            | Collector run ID and covered period prevent duplication.                       | No artifact or failed evaluator yields explicit incomplete state.                                 |
| **AI request**                | Gateway policy → minimize/redact → retrieve with provenance → model → evaluate → disclose/cite → human decision.      | Request trace and prompt/model versions; no replay of privileged tools.        | Deterministic fallback or unavailable state; never silent provider substitution.                  |

# 13 \| Data Authority, Persistence and Lineage Boundaries

| **Data class / product** | **Write authority**                                     | **Permitted projections**                             | **Persistence boundary**                               | **Replay / migration rule**                                                       |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant/configuration** | Tenant/commercial module.                               | Experience/BFF, reporting and signed regional policy. | Transactional regional store; bounded global metadata. | Versioned changes; no direct mutation by consuming modules.                       |
| **Telemetry**            | Source-native payload + shield-ingest normalized event. | Lakehouse, hot analytics, detections and case links.  | Regional event backbone/lakehouse/search.              | Raw and normalized versions retained per policy; parser mapping version recorded. |
| **Alert/case**           | Detection/alert/case modules.                           | Dashboards, reports, audit packages.                  | Regional transactional store + search projection.      | State transitions evented; correction through new event.                          |
| **Evidence**             | Evidence service metadata; content vault for artifacts. | Control assessments and frozen packages.              | Regional WORM-capable vault + ledger metadata.         | Original never rewritten; superseding package preserves old proofs.               |
| **Control/risk**         | Control/assessment/risk modules.                        | Executive reporting and audit workspace.              | Regional transactional store; approved snapshots.      | Evaluator, mapping and input versions frozen.                                     |
| **AI interaction**       | AI gateway audit record.                                | Quality/evaluation and user decision history.         | Region/policy-controlled store with minimized content. | Prompt/model/tool/retrieval versions retained; memory expiry enforced.            |
| **Usage/SLO/cost**       | Metering/SRE sources.                                   | Customer usage, FinOps and release gates.             | Approved regional/aggregate telemetry.                 | Reconciliation to source totals; corrections versioned.                           |

## 13.1 Source-of-truth rule

Every data product is classified as authoritative, projection, cache, evidence snapshot or external source. A projection may be rebuilt; a cache may be discarded; an evidence snapshot is immutable; an external source remains authoritative only for the fields explicitly assigned to it. The architecture document must not use the generic word “database” where authority matters.

## 13.2 Temporal contract

| **Time concept**               | **Required use**                                                               |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source/observed time**       | When the source says the fact/event occurred.                                  |
| **Ingest/acceptance time**     | When ZoikoShield durably accepted it.                                          |
| **Processing/evaluation time** | When normalization, enrichment or control evaluation occurred.                 |
| **Effective period**           | Business or control interval covered by the fact/evidence.                     |
| **Version time**               | When a schema, rule, mapping, policy or model version became effective.        |
| **Anchor time**                | When an evidence root was externally witnessed.                                |
| **Supersession time**          | When a later fact/package replaced a prior interpretation without deleting it. |

# 14 \| Tenant, Identity, Authorization and Residency Context

| **Context element**   | **Architecture requirement**                                                                                             | **Default failure**                                                        |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant**            | Primary isolation boundary on every persistent object, request, event, search, cache key, queue message and audit event. | Reject/quarantine when missing or mismatched.                              |
| **Environment**       | Separates production, staging, development and customer-defined environments.                                            | No implicit default on privileged or evidence paths.                       |
| **Human identity**    | ZoikoID/federated identity with MFA/passkey and step-up for sensitive actions.                                           | Cached validation may preserve bounded read; privileged paths fail closed. |
| **Workload identity** | Short-lived, mutually authenticated credentials with service/workload scope.                                             | No static service credential fallback.                                     |
| **Authorization**     | RBAC + ABAC + relationship rules; purpose and case/change reference for sensitive actions.                               | Deny with auditable decision.                                              |
| **Delegation**        | Explicit partner/support scope, tenant-bound and time-limited.                                                           | No inherited cross-tenant access.                                          |
| **Residency**         | Policy resolved from tenant, source region, data class, purpose, provider eligibility and transfer mechanism.            | Quarantine and alert on unmatched route.                                   |
| **Break-glass**       | JIT, dual-controlled where required, session recorded and post-use reviewed.                                             | No permanent emergency role.                                               |

| **ARCHITECTURE BOUNDARY** | Identity-provider availability is a dependency, not an excuse to bypass authorization. Degraded operation may preserve bounded read; configuration, privilege and response actions remain fail-closed. |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 15 \| Evidence-First Architectural Spine

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image161.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.89097in" alt="Six-stage evidence flow from source and collector through immutable record, evaluator, assessment and audit package, anchored externally." />

***Figure 7 — Evidence-first spine from source artifact to independently verifiable assertion.***

| **Stage**                    | **Required architecture fact**                                                              | **Failure / integrity state**                          |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source acquisition**       | Source identity, scope, permissions, source-native artifact and covered period.             | UNAUTHORIZED, PERMISSION_CHANGED, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.  |
| **Collection**               | Collector workload identity, version, configuration hash, run ID and signature.             | COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY, FAILED, PARTIAL.                  |
| **Evidence record**          | Tenant/region, content hash, provenance, retention, legal hold, freshness and completeness. | HASH_MISMATCH, STALE, PARTIAL.                         |
| **Ledger append**            | Per-tenant sequence, prior hash, record hash and trusted timestamp.                         | CHAIN_GAP, DUPLICATE, ANCHOR_PENDING.                  |
| **Evaluation**               | Evaluator/rule/mapping version plus exact input/enrichment snapshots.                       | EVALUATOR_FAILED, NON_DETERMINISTIC, INCOMPLETE_INPUT. |
| **Assessment/assertion**     | Transparent conclusion, confidence, scope, limitations and owner.                           | UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE; never compliant by default.        |
| **Package/freeze**           | Manifest, chain proofs, Merkle inclusion, source versions and known gaps.                   | FREEZE_BLOCKED if required evidence or proofs fail.    |
| **Independent verification** | Offline verifier validates content, chain, timestamps and published roots.                  | VERIFICATION_FAILED opens integrity incident.          |

## 15.1 Architecture fitness checks

- Synthetic tenant produces a complete package each release and the standalone verifier passes without privileged Zoiko access.

- Restore test reconciles ledger chain heads against the last external witness and event-replay manifest.

- Any connector degradation automatically changes affected evidence windows and downstream control states.

- Schema migration does not mutate frozen packages; a re-render produces a superseding package with both versions verifiable.

- No report or API can render a non-COMPLETE material control as compliant.

# 16 \| Detection, Correlation and Deterministic Replay Context

| **Architecture element** | **Required declaration**                                                                          |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Detection identity**   | Stable ID, owner, version, status, data prerequisites, ATT&CK mapping and severity policy.        |
| **Detection class**      | Point, windowed, sequence, behavior, batch or intel-match; latency SLO follows class.             |
| **Input set**            | Canonical event/schema versions, required fields, allowed missing-data behavior and tenant scope. |
| **Enrichment**           | Asset, identity, intel and policy snapshot references used at original evaluation.                |
| **Time semantics**       | Window, watermark, ordering, allowed lateness, event time vs processing time.                     |
| **Decision output**      | Alert, risk factor contributions, confidence and incomplete-data state.                           |
| **Replay**               | Exact rule/version/input/enrichment/watermark reconstruction; divergence is NON_DETERMINISTIC.    |
| **Publication**          | Signed content bundle, staged rollout, canary tenants and rollback.                               |
| **Cost**                 | Estimated and measured compute/query/data cost against R19 guardrail.                             |
| **Evidence**             | Test corpus, precision/noise, replay result, reviewer and release reference.                      |

| **CRITICAL RULE** | AI may propose a detection candidate. A blocking production detection must be deterministic or carry an explicitly approved exception with a bounded use and evaluation plan. |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 17 \| Cases, SOAR and Governed Response Context

| **Object**               | **Authority**                        | **Required controls**                                                                                  |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Alert**                | Detection/alert module.              | Immutable source references, risk factors, confidence, disposition rationale and SLA state.            |
| **Case**                 | Case module.                         | State machine, owner, timeline, evidence, tasks, communications, legal hold and closure criteria.      |
| **Playbook run**         | Playbook module.                     | Version, simulation/live mode, step inputs/outputs, approvals, errors and compensation.                |
| **Action proposal**      | shield-core/case workflow.           | Target, blast radius, authority level, policy and required approvers.                                  |
| **Response command**     | shield-action-broker.                | Per-tenant signature, nonce, expiry, approval references, rate ceiling and customer-side verification. |
| **Execution receipt**    | Customer integration/agent + broker. | Result, timestamp, target, verification, uncertainty state and rollback availability.                  |
| **Post-incident review** | Case/incident process.               | Root cause, effectiveness, control changes, lessons, owners and evidence.                              |

## 17.1 Authority levels

| **Level**                      | **Meaning**                                       | **Architecture gate**                                                           |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R0 Observe**                 | Collect, enrich, query, notify and open case.     | No external estate change.                                                      |
| **R1 Recommend**               | Human approval required before action.            | Default production posture for current release.                                 |
| **R2 Pre-authorized low risk** | Bounded reversible actions under customer policy. | Independent broker red team, per-tenant signing and measured rollback required. |
| **R3 High impact**             | Dual approval or named customer authority.        | Customer-side attestation, simulation rehearsal and blast-radius limit.         |
| **R4 Emergency**               | Time-boxed break-glass.                           | Immediate escalation, out-of-band review and mandatory PIR.                     |
