| **Evaluation service** | Grounding, factuality, injection, tool-abuse, leakage, cost and regression tests.                      | Self-approval of model release.                                                            | Dataset/version, metrics, threshold, reviewer and finding state.   |
| **User disclosure**    | Labels, citations, confidence, human-review state and override.                                        | Styling AI output as system fact.                                                          | Rendered disclosure and human decision event.                      |

# 20 \| Failure, Degradation and Recovery Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image163.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.94653in" alt="Five source states mapped to controlled outcomes including scope continuation, degraded assertions, fail-closed action paths and deterministic fallback." />

***Figure 9 — Explicit failure and degradation architecture.***

| **Dependency failure**      | **Must continue**                                                               | **Must degrade or stop**                                                       | **Visible state / evidence**                            |
|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| **ZoikoID control plane**   | Bounded read for valid cached sessions within approved lifetime.                | Privilege, configuration and response actions fail closed.                     | IDENTITY_DEGRADED; window and affected actions logged.  |
| **AI provider/gateway**     | Deterministic detection, cases, evidence, control evaluation and authorization. | AI assistance unavailable or reduced; no provider substitution outside policy. | AI_UNAVAILABLE / FALLBACK_ACTIVE.                       |
| **Search/hot analytics**    | Ingestion, durable event transport and transactional case/evidence writes.      | Interactive search and some correlations delayed.                              | SEARCH_DEGRADED; queue lag and recovery ETA.            |
| **Event backbone**          | Bounded source buffering/backpressure and transactional intents.                | New async processing after buffer; reject before data loss ceiling.            | INGESTION_DEGRADED / BACKPRESSURE.                      |
| **Connector/source**        | Other sources and verified scope continue.                                      | Affected coverage/evidence/control claims become partial/stale.                | CONNECTOR\_\* state with gap window.                    |
| **Action broker**           | Detection, triage and recommendation.                                           | All external response actions stop.                                            | ACTION_FREEZE / BROKER_UNAVAILABLE.                     |
| **Evidence anchor witness** | Evidence collection and local chain append.                                     | New packages show ANCHOR_PENDING; freeze may block by policy.                  | Anchor latency and last confirmed root.                 |
| **Primary region**          | Approved standby and recovery workflow.                                         | New writes/actions until failover authority and reconciliation.                | REGION_INCIDENT; RTO/RPO clock.                         |
| **Cost/usage guardrail**    | Existing contracted safe workload.                                              | Unbounded query/model/data expansion; release of cost-regressing changes.      | BUDGET_GUARD / RATE_LIMIT with no silent coverage loss. |

## 20.1 Fail-open / fail-closed decision record

Every material dependency must explicitly state whether each operation fails open, fails closed, queues, retries, degrades to read-only, uses deterministic fallback or enters reconciliation. “Graceful degradation” without operation-level behavior is rejected.

# 21 \| Nonfunctional and Scale Constraints

| **Constraint family** | **Architecture requirement**                                                                                                  | **Source of current value** |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Availability**      | Control-plane, ingestion and premium-recovery objectives are separated by capability and phase.                               | R19.                        |
| **Latency**           | Point, windowed and batch detection classes have distinct SLO semantics.                                                      | R19 + C8.                   |
| **Scale**             | Every benchmark uses the current tenant, endpoint/identity, event, GB/day, connector, case, evidence and model-call envelope. | R19 Scale Envelope.         |
| **Durability**        | Accepted telemetry is durably replayable; transactional RPO is not misrepresented as telemetry loss.                          | R19 + E6/H4.                |
| **Security**          | Tenant isolation, action signing, key custody and supply-chain controls are release-blocking.                                 | E1–E5 + R20.                |
| **Privacy/residency** | Data-class routes, minimization, deletion and legal hold are policy-enforced.                                                 | R09 + G6.                   |
| **Accessibility**     | Experience contracts represent status without color alone and support keyboard/screen-reader operation.                       | C11 + R04.                  |
| **Operability**       | Every deployable/module has owner, SLIs, alerts, runbook, dependency and recovery behavior.                                   | R06 + H5.                   |
| **Cost**              | Ingestion, retention, AI and query changes remain within approved cost ceilings and gross-margin guardrails.                  | R19.                        |
| **Portability/exit**  | Open export formats and independently verifiable evidence survive offboarding.                                                | C4 + B5.                    |
| **Maintainability**   | Module boundaries, contracts, architecture tests and migration/deprecation rules remain current.                              | R06/R10/R11/R20.            |

| **Active tenants**                     | 3–10 design partners.             | Single regional cell may serve launch; isolation tests remain fleet-wide. |
| **Protected endpoints/identities**     | 2,000–10,000 fleet.               | No premature service extraction; benchmark peak/burst.                    |
| **Telemetry**                          | 0.5–2 TB/day; ~15K events/s peak. | shield-ingest isolated; durable backbone and backpressure mandatory.      |

| **Model calls/day**                    | ~5,000.                           | Gateway budget, caching and deterministic fallback.                       |

# 22 \| Build-vs-Integrate and Technology Decision Envelope

| **Capability**                       | **Canonical decision**                          | **Engineering boundary**                                                                        |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Evidence ledger/verifier**         | BUILD.                                          | Core differentiation; open verifier; cryptographic design controlled.                           |
| **Control/evaluation/risk**          | BUILD.                                          | Canonical control model and evidence-linked transparent outcomes.                               |
| **Detection/correlation/cases/SOAR** | BUILD core.                                     | Own normalized context, rules, workflows and governed actions.                                  |
| **EDR/email/vulnerability engines**  | INTEGRATE/PARTNER.                              | Connector and response certification; no Zoiko agent in plan horizon.                           |
| **Threat intelligence**              | BUILD thin + integrate feeds.                   | Differentiate through context/operationalization, not raw feed ownership.                       |
| **AI models**                        | INTEGRATE behind gateway.                       | Provider-neutral contracts, no direct SDK, no customer-data training.                           |
| **Event backbone**                   | Managed Kafka-compatible per ADR.               | Vendor-neutral contracts and export/replay.                                                     |
| **Hot analytics**                    | Managed approved engine per benchmark/ADR.      | No engine-specific business authority.                                                          |
| **Graph**                            | Relational/analytics projection first.          | Dedicated graph only with benchmarked need.                                                     |
| **Policy engine**                    | Approved OPA/Cedar-class engine.                | Policy language/version is controlled; business logic not scattered.                            |
| **Identity**                         | ZoikoID/federation with governed dependency.    | Fallback bounded read; no authentication rewrite in product team.                               |
| **Cloud/runtime**                    | Managed Kubernetes-class and portable services. | No cloud-specific business logic; portability is pragmatic, not theoretical multi-cloud parity. |

| **Problem**          | Measured problem or mandatory requirement; not preference.                               |
| **Options**          | At least maintain current design, managed service and build alternatives where credible. |
| **Scale/cost**       | Benchmark at R19 envelope and forecasted next gate.                                      |
| **Security/privacy** | Threat, data class, region, identity, key and supply-chain implications.                 |
| **Operations**       | On-call, upgrade, backup, restore, observability and staffing impact.                    |
| **Lock-in/exit**     | Data and contract export, replacement path and switching cost.                           |
| **Compatibility**    | API/event/schema/deployment changes and migration.                                       |

# 23 \| Service Extraction Criteria and Architecture Anti-Patterns

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image164.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.66597in" alt="Workflow from observed production constraint through measured criteria and ADR to approve, defer or reject extraction." />

***Figure 10 — Architecture change and service-extraction decision workflow.***

| **Extraction criterion**        | **Evidence threshold / condition**                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Resource-profile divergence** | Module scaling distorts shield-core capacity by at least 30% or repeatedly forces unrelated overprovisioning/rollback. |
| **Independent cadence**         | Module needs at least twice the release frequency and shared deployment causes measurable delay/risk.                  |
| **Isolation class**             | A contracted tenant tier requires physical/data/compute separation not achievable safely inside current deployable.    |
| **Team topology**               | Dedicated team owns the capability end-to-end and coordination cost exceeds separation cost.                           |
| **Blast-radius reduction**      | Independent process/identity/freeze boundary materially limits a crown-jewel threat and cannot be achieved in-process. |
| **Regulatory/contractual**      | Approved obligation requires separate key custody, region, audit or operational boundary.                              |

## 23.1 Prohibited architecture theater

| **Anti-pattern**                   | **Why rejected**                                                   | **Approved alternative**                                                |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Microservice per noun**          | Operational and consistency cost without measured need.            | Enforced module boundary inside shield-core.                            |
| **Shared database integration**    | Destroys ownership, isolation and migration control.               | Published API/event/projection.                                         |
| **Service mesh as business logic** | Couples policy to infrastructure implementation.                   | Workload identity and versioned policy independent of mesh.             |
| **Graph database by aspiration**   | Adds operational specialty before query need is proven.            | Relational/analytics projection benchmark.                              |
| **Event-driven everything**        | Hides simple transactional invariants behind eventual consistency. | Synchronous transaction for authority; events for propagation.          |
| **LLM as universal orchestrator**  | Non-deterministic authority, injection and cost risk.              | Bounded AI gateway + deterministic workflow engine.                     |
| **Data lake as source of truth**   | Weak transactional and governance semantics.                       | Relational authority plus lakehouse analytics.                          |
| **Global active-active promise**   | High complexity and false SLA before tested capability.            | Multi-AZ regional active-active plus honest warm standby.               |
| **Generic “zero trust” label**     | No implementation consequence.                                     | Named identities, policy decisions, least privilege and negative tests. |

## 24.1 Diagram quality rule

Every diagram must declare scope, release, view type, owner, source snapshot, legend, trust boundaries and deferred elements. Every arrow must be directional and meaningful. A decorative cloud, database cylinder or double-headed arrow without an edge contract is prohibited.

# 25 \| Architecture Fitness Functions and Automated Enforcement

| **ID**    | **Fitness function**      | **Enforcement**                                                                                   | **Frequency**             | **Owner**                |
|-----------|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------|
| **AF-01** | Module dependency         | Static analysis fails disallowed package/module dependency or cyclic boundary.                    | Every build               | Engineering Architecture |
| **AF-02** | Database ownership        | DB grants and query scan fail cross-module direct writes.                                         | Every migration/build     | Data Platform            |
| **AF-03** | Tenant context            | Contract/schema lint rejects persistent/event/API objects without required tenant/region context. | Every build               | Platform Security        |
| **AF-04** | Interface registry        | API/event versions in code reconcile to R10/R11 and approved deprecation state.                   | Daily + release           | Platform                 |
| **AF-05** | Topology manifest         | Deployed services/stores/egress match approved R06 + ADR inventory.                               | Every deploy              | SRE                      |
| **AF-06** | Global-plane data         | Schema/DLP test rejects prohibited raw/customer data in global stores.                            | Every build + continuous  | Data/Privacy             |
| **AF-07** | No direct model SDK       | Dependency and egress policies block model providers outside shield-ai-gateway.                   | Every build/deploy        | AI Systems               |
| **AF-08** | No action bypass          | Only action broker identity may invoke certified customer action endpoints.                       | Every deploy + continuous | Security                 |
| **AF-09** | Response signing          | Synthetic customer endpoint rejects unsigned, expired and replayed commands.                      | Every release             | Response Engineering     |
| **AF-10** | Evidence verification     | Synthetic package passes offline verifier and anchor proof.                                       | Every release             | Evidence Engineering     |
| **AF-11** | Failure-state propagation | Connector/identity/search/model fault injection produces approved degraded states.                | Release + quarterly       | QA/SRE                   |
| **AF-12** | Replay determinism        | Recorded detection replay reproduces decision or explicitly flags divergence.                     | Every content release     | Detection Engineering    |
| **AF-13** | Residency policy          | Supported data-class/region matrix has explicit pass/quarantine result.                           | Every policy change       | Privacy/Platform         |
| **AF-14** | Cost envelope             | Benchmark remains inside R19 ingestion, retention, search and AI cost thresholds.                 | Material change + release | FinOps/SRE               |
| **AF-15** | Claim guard               | Customer-visible claim/disclosure IDs reconcile to approved R17 evidence.                         | Every release             | Product/Compliance       |

| **RELEASE RULE** | A failed P0/P1 architecture fitness function blocks merge or deployment. A manual waiver is not sufficient; an approved, time-bounded exception with compensating control must be linked to R20. |
|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| **New deployable, store, queue, model provider or external dependency** | ADR + R06/R18/R02 update + threat/privacy/operability review.                 |
| **New data class, region, transfer or residency topology**              | ADR + R09 + privacy/legal review + routing tests.                             |
| **New cross-module dependency or source of truth**                      | ADR + domain/data review + migration and fitness-function update.             |
| **Breaking API/event/schema change**                                    | ADR or approved compatibility plan + R10/R11 deprecation and consumer impact. |
| **New AI tool, memory, agent authority or provider**                    | AI register update + D2/D3 review + adversarial tests.                        |
| **New response authority or action type**                               | Security/customer policy review + broker certification + red-team gate.       |
| **Service extraction or merge**                                         | Measured extraction criteria + cost/operability/rollback ADR.                 |
| **SLO, scale or cost change**                                           | R19 update + benchmark/test impact + contractual/claim review.                |
| **Material incident/red-team finding**                                  | Threat model/architecture review; controls and fitness functions updated.     |
| **Parent architecture superseded**                                      | Derivative invalidation and complete impact reconciliation.                   |

## 26.1 ADR minimum fields

| **Field**            | **Required content**                                                       |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Decision**         | Specific decision and scope.                                               |
| **Context**          | Measured problem, constraints, current design and affected gates.          |
| **Options**          | Credible alternatives, including no change.                                |
| **Consequences**     | Security, privacy, data, AI, cost, operations, compatibility and exit.     |
| **Evidence**         | Benchmark, threat model, prototype, design-partner or control evidence.    |
| **Owner/approvers**  | Accountable decision owner and mandatory reviewers.                        |
| **Deadline/default** | Forcing date and safe default if unresolved.                               |
| **Implementation**   | Migration, rollback, feature flag, verification and documentation updates. |
| **Revisit trigger**  | Metric, phase, date or condition that reopens the decision.                |

## 27.1 Handoff rule

An architecture handoff is complete only when the receiving team can identify its source of truth, allowed dependencies, prohibited flows, failure behavior, required tests and escalation route. A meeting or diagram review without a versioned delivery pack is not a handoff.

# 28 \| Definition of Ready and Definition of Done

## 28.1 Architecture Definition of Ready

**1.** Current release and requirement IDs are approved and traceable.

**2.** Relevant system context, module and deployment views are current.

**3.** Write authority, dependencies, APIs/events and data classifications are identified.

**4.** Tenant, identity, authorization, region and residency behavior is explicit.

**5.** Nominal, partial, stale, unauthorized, unavailable and recovery behavior is defined.

**6.** AI authority, tools, data, fallback and human oversight are defined where applicable.

**7.** Applicable threat, privacy, evidence, SLO, scale and cost constraints are linked.

**8.** ADRs are closed or have deadline/default; no load-bearing decision is silently open.

**9.** Architecture fitness functions and test owners are assigned.

**10.** The workstream delivery pack is acknowledged and not expired.

## 28.2 Architecture Definition of Done

**1.** Implementation conforms to approved module/dependency and topology manifests.

**2.** API/event/schema and data-authority registers reconcile to code and deployment.

**3.** All applicable fitness functions pass; exceptions are approved, bounded and unexpired.

**4.** Tenant-isolation, residency, failure/degradation and rollback tests pass.

**5.** Evidence and audit events exist for material decisions and changes.

**6.** AI evaluations and deterministic fallback pass for AI surfaces.

**7.** SLO/scale/cost tests satisfy R19 for the release envelope.

**8.** Runbook, observability and ownership are current in R06/H5.

# 00 \| Critical Review and Refined Requirements Decision

The initial Document-03 concept correctly required approved requirements, acceptance criteria and traceability. It remained too close to a conventional backlog specification and did not yet control the failure modes that make requirements estates untrustworthy in remote, compartmentalized engineering: duplicated sources, untestable acceptance, silent scope expansion, orphaned controls, ticket drift and incomplete negative-state coverage.

| **ID**    | **Finding**                                                                                                  | **Refined control**                                                                                                                            |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **CR-01** | A Word document was at risk of becoming the primary requirement store.                                       | Use R04 as the structured authority; this document governs schema, quality and rendered views.                                                 |
| **CR-02** | “Requirement”, “acceptance criterion”, “test” and “evidence” were not sufficiently separated.                | Define distinct artifact types, owners, states and links. A test is not a requirement; a ticket is not acceptance evidence.                    |
| **CR-03** | Happy-path criteria could pass while partial, stale, unauthorized or recovery behavior remained unspecified. | Make seven state classes mandatory where applicable and require negative-state evidence.                                                       |
| **CR-04** | Traceability could degrade into a single spreadsheet hyperlink.                                              | Use a bidirectional graph from obligation/outcome through requirement, design, test, evidence, release and claim.                              |
| **CR-05** | AI requirements could be mixed with ordinary feature behavior.                                               | Add explicit AI use-case class, model/data/tool authority, human decision rights, citations, fallback and adversarial tests.                   |
| **CR-06** | Nonfunctional requirements were likely to be generic adjectives.                                             | Require measurable observation point, load/scale envelope, threshold, window, exclusions, owner and evidence.                                  |
| **CR-07** | Change control did not automatically invalidate downstream artifacts.                                        | A material requirement change triggers impact traversal and stale-state propagation to tests, wireframes, delivery packs and release evidence. |
| **CR-08** | Issue trackers could silently override the controlled baseline.                                              | Treat them as execution projections with synchronization and drift detection.                                                                  |
| **CR-09** | Remote-team compartmentalization could hide implementation-critical constraints.                             | Apply minimum-complete disclosure: all assigned security, data, evidence, AI, failure and acceptance requirements must be present.             |
| **CR-10** | No formal linting or quality dashboard was defined.                                                          | Add automated quality rules, orphan detection, coverage metrics and release-blocking reconciliation.                                           |

| **REFINED DECISION** | Create ZS-ENG-REQ-001 as the controlled requirements method and human-readable specification, backed by R04 as the structured source. Authorize implementation only from approved, baselined, quality-passing requirements with linked acceptance criteria, verification method and required evidence. |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

## 1.2 Source authority and conflict precedence

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image165.png" style="width:6.8in;height:3.13333in" alt="Hierarchy from applicable law and contracts to controlled masters, registers and ADRs, ZS-ENG-REQ-001, and workstream projections." />

***Figure 1 — Requirement authority and implementation precedence.***

**1.** Applicable law, executed customer contract and approved regulatory obligation.

**5.** Current approved workstream delivery pack.

**6.** Issue tracker, meeting note, email or chat instruction.

| **STOP-WORK** | Where two authorities conflict, the affected implementation stops. Engineers do not choose the “most recent message.” The source owner resolves the conflict and updates R04 before work resumes. |

# 02 \| Executive Engineering Mandate

Build the current ZoikoShield release only from requirements that are controlled, current, assigned, measurable and traceable. Every material behavior must identify its tenant and data scope, authority, failure behavior, AI status, evidence obligation, acceptance criteria, verification method and release evidence. Engineering may refine implementation detail within approved boundaries; it may not create product scope, weaken controls or convert an assumption into behavior without controlled approval.

| **Mandate**                     | **Binding engineering consequence**                                                                                                                                      |
|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **One horizontal platform**     | Requirements may vary by governed configuration or sector pack; core behavior must not fork into industry-specific products.                                             |
| **Independent entry offers**    | Managed Defense and Continuous Assurance requirements must be independently satisfiable unless a dependency is explicit and approved.                                    |
| **Evidence before assertion**   | Any displayed conclusion, control state, response outcome, AI recommendation or claim links to attributable evidence.                                                    |
| **No-LLM critical path**        | Authentication, authorization, entitlement, evidence integrity, compliance state and response approval remain deterministic authorities.                                 |
| **Failure is explicit**         | Partial, stale, degraded, unauthorized and error states are specified and tested, not inferred from absent success.                                                      |
| **Minimum-complete disclosure** | Assigned engineers receive all implementation-critical constraints and tests, while unrelated strategy, pricing, customer and restricted threat detail remains withheld. |
| **No release by ticket status** | Release requires trace reconciliation and valid evidence, not “Done” labels.                                                                                             |

# 03 \| Purpose, Applicability and Disclosure Boundary

## 3.1 Purpose

Define the controlled architecture for capturing, decomposing, approving, baselining, distributing, changing, verifying and retiring ZoikoShield engineering requirements. Provide the exact document sections, register schema, acceptance patterns, trace rules, review gates and operational templates required to create the later production specification.

## 3.2 Applies to

- All ERB-01 functional, quality, security, privacy, evidence, AI, data, interface, experience, operational and commercial-enablement requirements that affect engineering behavior.

- All employees, contractors, approved partners and service providers producing or consuming controlled requirements.

- All modules, connectors, APIs, events, data stores, AI surfaces, wireframes, tests, infrastructure and managed-service tooling governed by the current release.

- All requirement changes capable of affecting G0, G1 or a subsequent release gate.

## 3.3 Does not disclose

- Named pipeline, design-partner identities, account economics, negotiated terms or Board forecasts.

- Full price books, discount authorities, vendor rates or unrelated commercial strategy.

- Unrestricted attack trees, live credentials, private keys, production secrets or unresolved exploit detail.

- Licensed standards text beyond legally permitted identifiers, paraphrases and implementation requirements.

- Future-sector requirements not approved into the current release baseline.

# 04 \| Binding Requirements-Control Principles

| **ID**    | **Principle**                  | **Required consequence**                                                                                                        |
|-----------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **RQ-01** | Atomicity                      | One requirement expresses one necessary behavior or constraint. Compound statements split unless verification is inseparable.   |
| **RQ-02** | Necessity                      | Every requirement traces to an approved outcome, obligation, architecture invariant, risk treatment or operational need.        |
| **RQ-03** | Unambiguity                    | Actors, scope, trigger, expected result, conditions and exceptions are explicit; undefined adjectives are prohibited.           |
| **RQ-04** | Verifiability                  | A qualified observer can determine pass/fail using a named method and evidence artifact.                                        |
| **RQ-05** | Feasibility                    | Engineering confirms the requirement is implementable within the approved architecture and scale envelope.                      |
| **RQ-06** | Traceability                   | Bidirectional links exist from origin through design, tests, evidence, release and applicable claim.                            |
| **RQ-07** | Tenant and data scope          | Tenant, environment, region, legal entity, data class and processing purpose are stated where applicable.                       |
| **RQ-08** | Failure completeness           | Material non-nominal states and recovery are explicit.                                                                          |
| **RQ-09** | Authority visibility           | Human, system and AI decision rights are explicit before action.                                                                |
| **RQ-10** | Evidence integrity             | The record required to prove behavior is specified with source, timing, integrity and retention.                                |
| **RQ-11** | Version immutability           | Baselined requirements are never silently edited; change creates a new version with impact analysis.                            |
| **RQ-12** | Economics and operability      | Requirements that materially change compute, storage, model, vendor or human cost identify the applicable cost/scale guardrail. |
| **RQ-13** | No hidden implementation rule  | Any assigned security, privacy, AI, evidence or acceptance condition affecting code must appear in the workstream pack.         |
| **RQ-14** | No shadow authority            | Tickets, documents and diagrams reference R04 IDs; they never create parallel requirement truth.                                |
| **RQ-15** | No public claim by implication | Engineering output does not create certification, compliance, uptime, detection or AI claims unless R17/R20 authorizes them.    |

# 05 \| Source of Truth, Precedence and Register Architecture

R04 is the authoritative structured graph. ZS-ENG-REQ-001 defines the governance and rendered human views. The issue tracker receives controlled projections for execution. The documentation repository stores approved snapshots and annexes. CI/CD and release tooling consume machine-readable control fields and report evidence back to R20.

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image166.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.32222in" alt="Graph linking market or obligation triggers to outcomes, capabilities, requirements, design contracts, verification, release evidence and claims, with feedback loops." />

***Figure 2 — Closed-loop traceability graph.***

| **System**                      | **Authoritative content**                                                                             | **May not become authority for**                                        |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R04 requirements register**   | Requirement identity, version, state, owner, metadata, links, acceptance and verification references. | Design implementation, test results or evidence content.                |
| **Controlled master documents** | Strategy, architecture, policy, service and control intent.                                           | Current field values held in registers.                                 |
| **ZS-ENG-REQ-001**              | Approved method, quality rules, views and templates.                                                  | Unregistered feature requirements.                                      |
| **Issue tracker**               | Execution task, assignee, iteration, code/PR links and current delivery status.                       | Scope, acceptance wording, control exceptions or release authorization. |
| **Test management / CI**        | Test definitions, execution, results and artifacts.                                                   | Requirement intent or risk acceptance.                                  |
| **R20 release evidence**        | Release-specific evidence, approvals and reconciliation result.                                       | Requirement authoring or product priority.                              |

## 5.1 Synchronization controls

- R04 changes emit a versioned change event or digest consumed by delivery-pack and issue-tracker integrations.

- Projected tickets display requirement ID, version and baseline; stale projections are visibly marked and blocked from release.

- Links are stable identifiers, not file paths or paragraph numbers.

- A daily reconciliation detects orphaned, stale, duplicated or contradictory artifacts.

- Human-readable exports state the register snapshot and generation timestamp.

# 06 \| Requirement Taxonomy and Decomposition Model

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image167.png" style="width:6.8in;height:3.71181in" alt="Hierarchy from business or customer outcome through capabilities and requirement classes to acceptance criteria, verification and release evidence." />

***Figure 3 — Controlled decomposition from outcome to verifiable implementation.***

| **Artifact type**                       | **Prefix** | **Purpose**                                                                         | **Mandatory parent**                              |
|-----------------------------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Outcome / objective**                 | OBJ        | Measurable customer, service, risk or operational result.                           | Approved strategy, obligation or release mandate. |
| **Capability**                          | CAP        | Coherent platform ability delivered through one or more bounded contexts.           | OBJ.                                              |
| **Use case / journey**                  | UC         | Actor goal and interaction flow, including alternate paths.                         | OBJ or CAP.                                       |
| **Functional requirement**              | FR         | Required observable behavior.                                                       | CAP or UC.                                        |
| **Quality / nonfunctional requirement** | NFR        | Measurable quality property or service condition.                                   | CAP, system or interface.                         |
| **Constraint**                          | CON        | Binding limit from architecture, law, contract, security, privacy, AI or economics. | Authority source.                                 |
| **Data requirement**                    | DR         | Data authority, structure, classification, lifecycle and lineage.                   | FR/NFR/CON.                                       |
| **Interface requirement**               | IR         | API, event, webhook, connector or UI contract behavior.                             | FR/NFR/CON.                                       |
| **Acceptance criterion**                | AC         | Specific pass/fail condition for a requirement version.                             | FR/NFR/CON/DR/IR.                                 |
| **Verification case**                   | VC         | Method and executable or manual test definition.                                    | AC.                                               |
| **Evidence requirement**                | ER         | Artifact and integrity conditions required to prove outcome.                        | AC or control.                                    |
| **Decision / exception**                | ADR/EXC    | Approved design decision or temporary deviation.                                    | Affected requirements and risk.                   |

## 6.1 Decomposition rules

**1.** An outcome may have multiple capabilities; each capability has one accountable product owner and one technical owner.

**2.** Functional and quality requirements are peers. A feature is incomplete if its applicable quality, security, privacy, evidence, AI and operability requirements are absent.

**3.** Constraints may govern many requirements and must be linked rather than copied into inconsistent prose.

**4.** Acceptance criteria bind to an exact requirement version. Rewording a baselined requirement invalidates the old criteria until reviewed.

**5.** Implementation tasks may be many-to-many with requirements; a task can never substitute for the requirement graph.

|--------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Requirement**          | ZS-{DOMAIN}-{TYPE}-{NNNN}   | ZS-EVID-FR-0042       |
| **Acceptance criterion** | {REQ-ID}-AC-{NN}            | ZS-EVID-FR-0042-AC-03 |
| **Verification case**    | VC-{DOMAIN}-{NNNN}          | VC-EVID-0117          |
| **Evidence requirement** | ER-{DOMAIN}-{NNNN}          | ER-EVID-0061          |

| **Change request**       | RCR-{YYYY}-{NNNN}           | RCR-2026-0048         |

## 7.2 Mandatory requirement metadata

| **Metadata group**   | **Required fields**                                                                                       |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**         | id, type, title, version, state, baseline, supersedes, created_at, effective_from.                        |
| **Authority**        | origin_type, origin_id, parent_ids, applicable_ADRs, obligation/control references.                       |
| **Scope**            | release, product/offer, tenant class, region, environment, legal entity, data class, actor.               |
| **Ownership**        | product_owner, technical_owner, control_reviewers, approver, delivery_team.                               |
| **Requirement**      | normative statement, rationale, assumptions, exclusions, dependencies, priority, criticality.             |
| **Quality**          | quality_characteristic, metric, threshold, observation_point, window, scale profile, exclusions.          |
| **Security/privacy** | threat/control IDs, processing purpose, minimization, retention, residency, audit events.                 |
| **AI**               | use_case_id, risk class, model/tool authority, human review, citations, confidence, fallback, cost limit. |
| **Acceptance**       | AC IDs, state coverage, verification method, test IDs, evidence IDs.                                      |
| **Trace**            | design/API/event/data/UX IDs, code/PR links, release evidence, claim/disclosure IDs.                      |
| **Change**           | change reason, impact summary, affected nodes, migration, compatibility, notification and expiry.         |
