# 08 \| Requirement Quality Standard and Automated Linting

| **Rule**  | **Quality test**        | **Release consequence**                                                                                                |
|-----------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **QL-01** | Atomic                  | No uncontrolled “and/or” combining independently verifiable behavior.                                                  |
| **QL-02** | Normative               | Uses MUST for mandatory behavior; SHOULD only with exception route; MAY only for explicit optionality.                 |
| **QL-03** | Actor and scope         | Names the system/actor and tenant/environment/data scope.                                                              |
| **QL-04** | Trigger and result      | States triggering condition and observable outcome.                                                                    |
| **QL-05** | No vague adjectives     | Blocks “fast”, “secure”, “intuitive”, “real time”, “robust”, “scalable” without measurable definition.                 |
| **QL-06** | No solution leakage     | Avoids implementation choice unless the choice is an approved constraint or ADR.                                       |
| **QL-07** | Testable                | Has at least one AC, verification method and evidence requirement before BASELINED.                                    |
| **QL-08** | Negative-state coverage | Applicable partial, stale, degraded, unauthorized, error and recovery states are addressed.                            |
| **QL-09** | No hidden default       | Unknown or missing data behavior is explicit; absence is never silently treated as healthy, low risk or compliant.     |
| **QL-10** | No undefined reference  | Every external term, interface, state and policy is linked to a controlled definition.                                 |
| **QL-11** | No duplicate authority  | Semantic duplicate detection identifies overlapping or contradictory requirements.                                     |
| **QL-12** | Current parent          | All parent requirements, ADRs and register values are current.                                                         |
| **QL-13** | Risk proportionality    | P0/P1 and high-impact AI/response requirements require independent control review.                                     |
| **QL-14** | Cost/scale completeness | Material workload requirements identify the scale envelope and cost guardrail.                                         |
| **QL-15** | Accessible experience   | User-facing requirements identify keyboard, screen-reader, focus, non-color and language obligations where applicable. |

## 8.1 Quality disposition

| **Disposition** | **Meaning**                                                         | **Allowed next state**                                    |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **PASS**        | All mandatory lint and reviewer checks pass.                        | Review, approval or baseline.                             |
| **WARNING**     | Non-blocking improvement; rationale and owner recorded.             | Approval only where no control or ambiguity risk exists.  |
| **FAIL**        | Ambiguous, untestable, orphaned, conflicting or control-incomplete. | Return to draft; implementation authorization prohibited. |
| **WAIVED**      | Specific lint rule waived by approved, expiring exception.          | Only under the exception authority matrix.                |
| **STALE**       | Source, parent, design or acceptance dependency changed.            | Impact review before further delivery or release.         |

# 09 \| Outcome, Persona, Use-Case and Capability Architecture

Requirements begin from an approved outcome, not from a screen or technology preference. The document must expose enough user and operational context for engineering while withholding named customer and pipeline information.

| **Layer**              | **Required content**                                                                  | **Engineering view**                                          |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Outcome**            | Target condition, measurement, time horizon, owner, disqualifying result.             | Anonymized and release-specific.                              |
| **Persona / actor**    | Role, decision rights, expertise, access context, risk and accessibility needs.       | Role archetype; no named customer person.                     |
| **Journey / use case** | Trigger, preconditions, main flow, alternates, failure states, evidence and handoff.  | Current release only.                                         |
| **Capability**         | Boundary, owner, dependencies, interfaces, data, operational model and exit evidence. | Full assigned workstream context.                             |
| **Story / task**       | Iteration-level implementation slice.                                                 | Generated from approved requirement links; not authoritative. |

## 9.1 Required launch archetypes

| **Archetype**                        | **Primary outcome**                                                   | **Requirement consequence**                                                           |
|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Security operations buyer/user**   | Detect, investigate and govern response with evidence.                | Alert/case/action requirements must stand without Continuous Assurance entitlement.   |
| **Assurance / GRC buyer/user**       | Monitor controls, manage evidence and support audit.                  | Control/evidence requirements must stand without Managed Defense entitlement.         |
| **Auditor / assessor**               | Independently inspect scope, evidence and limitations.                | Read-only, purpose-bound, verifiable packages and activity logging.                   |
| **Platform administrator**           | Configure tenant, identities, connectors, policies and entitlements.  | Strong SoD, approval, rollback and audit requirements.                                |
| **Executive / Board viewer**         | Understand material risk and control posture without false precision. | Transparent factors, drill-down, stale/partial degradation and approved snapshotting. |
| **SOC analyst / incident commander** | Operate queues, cases, playbooks and communications.                  | Service clocks, handovers, authority and customer-visible evidence.                   |

# 10 \| Functional Requirement Wireframe

| **Field**                       | **Mandatory content**                                                                        |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Header**                      | Requirement ID, title, version, state, baseline, criticality, release, owner.                |
| **Normative statement**         | One atomic MUST statement with actor/system, scope, trigger and observable result.           |
| **Rationale**                   | Why the behavior is necessary; links to outcome, obligation, risk or architecture invariant. |
| **Preconditions**               | Required configuration, entitlement, authority, data and dependencies.                       |
| **Main behavior**               | State transition or outcome; no implementation detail unless constrained.                    |
| **Alternative behavior**        | Valid alternate paths and boundary conditions.                                               |
| **Failure behavior**            | Partial, stale, degraded, unauthorized, error, recovery and rollback as applicable.          |
| **Evidence behavior**           | Required audit events, evidence object, lineage, integrity, retention and visibility.        |
| **Data and interface links**    | Controlled data objects, APIs, events, schemas, connectors and UX contracts.                 |
| **Acceptance and verification** | ACs, verification method, test cases, evidence and release gate.                             |
| **Dependencies and exclusions** | Named dependencies, out-of-scope behavior and deferrals.                                     |
| **Change history**              | Version reason, impact, supersession and recipient notification.                             |

## 10.1 Illustrative functional requirement

| **ILLUSTRATIVE — NOT AUTHORITY** | ZS-EVID-FR-0042: When a collector expected by an active control test has no reconciled artifact for an in-scope evidence window, the platform MUST mark that window PARTIAL, identify the missing expectation, prevent the affected assessment from rendering compliant, and create an attributable gap event. |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| **Acceptance slice**   | **Required observation**                                                                               |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Nominal**            | Expected artifact arrives and reconciles; window may become COMPLETE only after evaluator success.     |
| **Partial**            | Expected artifact absent at deadline; state becomes PARTIAL and affected conclusion cannot be green.   |
| **Permission changed** | Connector loses required permission; state identifies PERMISSION_CHANGED and affected period.          |
| **Recovery**           | Backfill succeeds; new assessment version is produced without rewriting the original partial record.   |
| **Evidence**           | Gap event, connector health state, evaluator version, assessment version and UI/API result are linked. |

# 11 \| Quality and Nonfunctional Requirement Architecture

Every NFR must identify metric, unit, observation point, workload or population, threshold, measurement window, percentile or aggregation, exclusions, target phase, owner, evidence source and failure response. “Best effort” and unqualified adjectives are prohibited.

| **Quality domain**     | **Required requirement dimensions**                                                                        |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Security**           | Threat/control, trust boundary, attack resistance, failure mode, logging and negative test.                |
| **Privacy**            | Purpose, minimization, lawful/contractual authority, region, retention, access and deletion.               |
| **Reliability**        | SLI, eligible population, availability/latency target, error budget, degraded behavior and recovery.       |
| **Performance**        | Operation, start/end observation points, load profile, percentile, concurrency, data size and environment. |
| **Scalability**        | Reference envelope, headroom, horizontal/vertical behavior, bottleneck and cost effect.                    |
| **Operability**        | Telemetry, alert, runbook, ownership, support access, rollback and maintenance.                            |
| **Maintainability**    | Module boundary, testability, migration, compatibility, documentation and change isolation.                |
| **Interoperability**   | Protocol/schema version, conformance, error handling, deprecation and certification.                       |
| **Portability / exit** | Export format, completeness, proof portability, deletion, restore and vendor-exit behavior.                |
| **Accessibility**      | Keyboard, focus, semantics, screen reader, non-color status, zoom, motion and language.                    |
| **AI quality**         | Grounding, citation, confidence, consistency, drift, latency, cost, fallback and human review.             |
| **Economics**          | Cost driver, reference volume, threshold, alert, customer transparency and release consequence.            |

## 11.1 Measurable NFR pattern

| **Element**              | **Example structure**                                                                 |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Operation**            | Point-rule detection evaluation.                                                      |
| **Population**           | Valid, durably accepted events mapped to an enabled point-rule.                       |
| **Observation interval** | Durable acceptance timestamp to alert creation timestamp.                             |
| **Target**               | p95 within the current R19 threshold for ERB-01.                                      |
| **Exclusions**           | Declared batch sources and replay jobs, reported separately.                          |
| **Evidence**             | OpenTelemetry metric, rule class, release version and synthetic scale-run result.     |
| **Failure response**     | Error-budget burn alert; release blocked where regression exceeds approved threshold. |

# 12 \| Security, Privacy, Tenancy and Residency Requirements

| **Control family**    | **Requirement must state**                                                                                |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authentication**    | Identity type, assurance level, federation/local route, MFA/passkey, session and recovery.                |
| **Authorization**     | Actor, resource, action, tenant/environment scope, policy, purpose, decision and denial evidence.         |
| **Privileged access** | JIT duration, approver, step-up, recording, break-glass, review and revocation.                           |
| **Tenant isolation**  | Isolation layer, partition key, negative tests, support/delegation path and failure behavior.             |
| **Cryptography**      | Data state, key scope, algorithm/profile reference, rotation, signing, verification and failure.          |
| **Secrets**           | Vault reference, workload identity, rotation and prohibition on documents/code/logs.                      |
| **Privacy**           | Data class, purpose, minimization, redaction/tokenization, access, retention, deletion and DSR impact.    |
| **Residency**         | Decision point before persistence, permitted region/provider, transfer mechanism and quarantine behavior. |
| **Auditability**      | Material event, actor, time, tenant, purpose, policy, result, evidence and retention.                     |
| **Supply chain**      | Dependency provenance, SBOM, signature, admission, vulnerability and update behavior.                     |

## 12.1 Security acceptance minimum

- Positive authorization is tested alongside cross-tenant, wrong-region, wrong-purpose, expired, replayed and privilege-escalation attempts.

- Unauthorized behavior returns a stable machine result without disclosing sensitive existence or content.

- Privileged actions are attributable and cannot be completed through undocumented support paths.

- Customer data never appears in test artifacts unless an approved, controlled test-data process applies.

- A security requirement without a named negative test is not baseline-ready.

# 13 \| Evidence, Assurance and Auditability Requirements

| **Requirement element**  | **Mandatory content**                                                                                                       |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Evidence subject**     | What fact, action, configuration, assessment or service delivery is being proven.                                           |
| **Source and collector** | Authoritative source, collector identity, permission scope and version.                                                     |
| **Time semantics**       | Collection time, source time, period covered, clock confidence and freshness threshold.                                     |
| **Integrity**            | Content hash, signature, chain/anchor reference, storage immutability and verification state.                               |
| **Completeness**         | Expected population/window and COMPLETE, PARTIAL, STALE, COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY, PERMISSION_CHANGED or EVALUATOR_FAILED state. |
| **Lineage**              | Source → fact → test → assessment → assertion/report.                                                                       |
| **Access**               | Tenant, purpose, role, auditor scope, export and access logging.                                                            |
| **Retention**            | Retention class, legal hold, deletion, package portability and supersession.                                                |
| **Reproducibility**      | Input versions, evaluator/mapping version, enrichment snapshot and frozen output.                                           |
| **User presentation**    | Evidence link, freshness, limitations and no-green-without-COMPLETE behavior.                                               |

| **NON-NEGOTIABLE** | Integrity and completeness are separate. A cryptographically intact artifact can still be incomplete, stale or inapplicable. The requirement model must preserve both dimensions. |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 14 \| AI, Agentic and Human-Oversight Requirements

| **AI requirement group** | **Mandatory content**                                                                                    |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Use-case authority**   | Approved use-case ID, risk class, permitted purpose, excluded decisions and affected users.              |
| **Model/provider**       | Approved model profile, region, data terms, version policy and fallback.                                 |
| **Input/data**           | Allowed data classes, redaction, tenant isolation, retrieval sources, freshness and poisoning controls.  |
| **Prompt/retrieval**     | System prompt/profile version, retrieval boundary, citations, source authority and injection handling.   |
| **Agent/tool use**       | Tool allowlist, read/write scope, transaction boundary, budget, timeout, rate limit and human approval.  |
| **Memory**               | Permitted memory type, tenant scope, purpose, retention, correction, deletion and no-secret rule.        |
| **Output**               | Label, citations, confidence, limitations, structured facts, uncertainty and prohibited styling as fact. |
| **Human oversight**      | Reviewer role, decision point, accept/modify/reject/override behavior and recorded rationale.            |
| **Fallback**             | Deterministic behavior when provider/model/retrieval is unavailable or disallowed.                       |
| **Evaluation**           | Grounding, hallucination, injection, cross-tenant, tool abuse, denial-of-wallet, drift and cost tests.   |
| **Incident control**     | Disablement, kill switch, rollback, evidence preservation and customer notification input.               |
| **Disclosure**           | Customer-facing AI notice, review status, data-use statement and challenge path.                         |

## 14.1 AI requirement prohibitions

- No model output is the sole authority for authentication, authorization, entitlement, evidence integrity, compliance status, control effectiveness or R2–R4 response approval.

- No direct provider SDK use outside the approved gateway.

- No cross-tenant retrieval, memory or tool context.

- No AI-generated assertion without source citations and recorded prompt/model/retrieval versions.

- No silent provider fallback to an unapproved region, model or data term.

- No “AI confidence” presented as calibrated probability unless the calibration method and validation evidence are approved.

# 15 \| Data, Event, API, Webhook and Connector Requirements

| **Contract class** | **Requirement dimensions**                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Data object**    | Authority, owner, key, tenant/region scope, lifecycle, classification, lineage, retention and invariants.                                |
| **Event**          | Name, version, producer, consumers, trigger, payload, ordering, deduplication, replay, late data, privacy and retention.                 |
| **API**            | Actor, authorization, method/resource, request/response, idempotency, pagination, rate limit, errors, audit and deprecation.             |
| **Webhook**        | Event, subscription scope, signing, timestamp/nonce, retry, replay defense, delivery evidence and secret rotation.                       |
| **Connector**      | Source, permissions, collection mode, scope, credential reference, health, backfill, rate limits, quarantine, version and certification. |
| **Export**         | Scope, format, manifest, evidence proofs, completeness, legal holds, timing, deletion and attestation.                                   |

## 15.1 Interface acceptance rules

- Every retriable write identifies idempotency behavior and duplicate outcome.

- Every asynchronous flow identifies ordering, watermark, retry, dead-letter and replay semantics.

- Every breaking change has deprecation, migration, compatibility and customer/partner notification requirements.

- Every connector health failure states its downstream coverage and assurance impact.

- Every error response uses a stable machine code and correlation identifier without leaking restricted detail.

# 16 \| Experience, Accessibility and Disclosure Requirements

| **Experience requirement** | **Mandatory content**                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Context**                | Visible tenant, environment, region, role and data/coverage state.                                                                     |
| **States**                 | Loading/resolving, empty, nominal, partial/incomplete, stale/degraded, error/unavailable and unauthorized/restricted where applicable. |
| **Evidence drill-down**    | Any risk, control, compliance, response or executive assertion links to source evidence and freshness.                                 |
| **Action authority**       | Authority level, target, blast radius, approvals, attestation, rollback and live/simulation state before confirmation.                 |
| **AI disclosure**          | Distinct AI styling, citations, confidence/limitations, review status and override/feedback.                                           |
| **Transparent numbers**    | Component factors, policy version, scope and incomplete-input behavior.                                                                |
| **Accessibility**          | Semantic structure, keyboard path, focus order, labels, screen reader, non-color cues, zoom/reflow and motion controls.                |
| **Localization**           | Locale, timezone, date/number format, language fallback and legally controlled wording.                                                |
| **Notifications**          | Severity, acknowledgment, escalation, quiet hours, evidence link and delivery state.                                                   |
| **Audit**                  | User decision, configuration, export and privileged-view events captured without invasive content logging.                             |

| **EXPERIENCE RULE** | A happy-path wireframe is not an acceptance specification. Each applicable state must identify data authority, user action, API/event dependency, audit event, test and evidence. |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 17 \| Failure, Degraded, Unauthorized and Recovery States

| **State class**               | **Requirement questions**                                                    | **Required evidence**                                         |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Loading / resolving**       | What is known, unknown, cancellable or time-bounded?                         | Start/end metric; timeout or cancellation event.              |
| **Empty / first use**         | Is absence expected, newly configured or a collection gap?                   | Source/coverage state and onboarding context.                 |
| **Nominal**                   | What complete evidence supports success?                                     | Successful result plus control/audit record.                  |
| **Partial / incomplete**      | What expected data or operation is missing and what conclusions are blocked? | Gap enumeration and affected scope/window.                    |
| **Stale / degraded**          | What threshold was exceeded; what deterministic capability remains?          | Health/freshness event and degradation start/end.             |
| **Error / unavailable**       | What failed, what was committed, retried, compensated or quarantined?        | Stable error, correlation, state and recovery record.         |
| **Unauthorized / restricted** | Which policy denied access without revealing protected content?              | Decision, actor, scope, policy and denial audit.              |
| **Recovery / rollback**       | How is integrity reconciled and prior state preserved?                       | Restore/replay/compensation evidence and new version.         |
| **Unknown / indeterminate**   | How is insufficient confidence represented?                                  | Explicit UNKNOWN state; never silently low/healthy/compliant. |

## 17.1 Cross-state acceptance matrix

| **Requirement ID** | **Nominal** | **Partial**          | **Stale**            | **Error**            | **Unauthorized**     | **Recovery**         | **Evidence** |
|--------------------|-------------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------|
| **Template**       | AC link     | AC / N/A + rationale | AC / N/A + rationale | AC / N/A + rationale | AC / N/A + rationale | AC / N/A + rationale | ER link      |

# 18 \| Acceptance Criteria Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image168.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.32222in" alt="Acceptance criteria structure showing precondition, trigger, observable result and evidence, with nominal, partial, unauthorized and recovery state coverage." />

***Figure 4 — Acceptance-criteria contract for material states.***

| **Criterion style**   | **Use when**                                          | **Required syntax**                                                                                         |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Behavioral / BDD**  | Actor/system behavior from a known state.             | Given \[controlled precondition\], when \[trigger\], then \[observable result\], and \[evidence\].          |
| **Invariant**         | A condition must always or never hold.                | For all \[scope\], \[invariant\] MUST hold; violation produces \[state/event\].                             |
| **Quantitative**      | Performance, availability, quality or cost threshold. | Under \[profile\], \[metric\] measured at \[point\] MUST meet \[threshold/window\].                         |
| **State transition**  | Lifecycle or workflow behavior.                       | From \[state\], on \[event\], transition to \[state\] only when \[guard\]; emit \[record\].                 |
| **Negative security** | Unauthorized, malicious or invalid behavior.          | Given \[attack/invalid condition\], system MUST deny/quarantine/fail closed and record \[evidence\].        |
| **Recovery**          | Rollback, replay, restore or compensation.            | After \[failure\], system MUST restore/reconcile \[invariants\] within \[target\] and preserve \[history\]. |
| **Human oversight**   | AI or high-impact decision.                           | System presents \[evidence/limitations\]; named role accepts/modifies/rejects before \[effect\].            |

## 18.1 Acceptance-criterion quality rules

- One criterion proves one observable condition; do not bundle unrelated outcomes.

- Use controlled states and terms; avoid subjective wording such as “looks correct.”

- Name the observation point and required evidence.

- Do not prescribe an implementation unless an approved architecture constraint requires it.

- Criteria must be independently reviewable by QA and the relevant control owner.

- P0/P1, tenant-isolation, evidence-integrity, privileged-action and high-impact AI criteria require negative tests.

# 19 \| Verification, Test and Release-Evidence Contract

| **Verification method**    | **Appropriate evidence**                                                                               |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Inspection**             | Approved design, schema, configuration, policy, code or documentation review record.                   |
| **Analysis**               | Model, calculation, static analysis, threat model, privacy analysis or formal reasoning artifact.      |
| **Demonstration**          | Controlled end-to-end demonstration with captured inputs, outputs and operator acknowledgment.         |
| **Test**                   | Automated/manual result with environment, version, dataset, expected outcome, actual outcome and logs. |
| **Measurement**            | SLI/metric query, population, interval, threshold, raw source and reproducible calculation.            |
| **Simulation / replay**    | Versioned input set, rule/evaluator version, enrichment snapshot and deterministic result.             |
| **Independent assessment** | Pen test, red team, audit, certification or specialist review with scope and remediation evidence.     |

## 19.1 Test linkage minimum

| **Requirement criticality**                                              | **Minimum verification**                                                                                   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **P0 / safety, tenant isolation, evidence integrity, privileged action** | Independent reviewer; automated positive and negative tests; release evidence; rollback/containment proof. |
| **P1 / material customer or service behavior**                           | Automated unit/contract/integration or E2E test as appropriate; owner acceptance; failure-state coverage.  |
| **P2 / normal product behavior**                                         | Appropriate automated test and acceptance evidence.                                                        |
| **P3 / low-risk presentation or convenience**                            | Documented verification; automation where regression risk justifies it.                                    |

| **EVIDENCE RULE** | A passing test link is insufficient if the test ran against the wrong version, environment, tenant model, scale profile or requirement baseline. Evidence must be scoped and attributable. |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 20 \| End-to-End Traceability Graph and Reconciliation

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image166.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.32222in" alt="Traceability graph from origin and outcome through design and verification to release evidence and claims." />

***Figure 5 — Required bidirectional traceability graph.***

| **Trace edge**                        | **Cardinality** | **Required validation**                                                               |
|---------------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Origin → outcome**                  | 1..n            | Every outcome has an approved origin; withdrawn origin triggers impact review.        |
| **Outcome → capability**              | 1..n            | Capabilities collectively cover outcome without unauthorized expansion.               |
| **Capability → requirement**          | 1..n            | Every capability has complete functional and applicable quality/control requirements. |
| **Requirement → design contract**     | 0..n            | Before implementation, every affected module/API/event/data/UX contract is linked.    |
| **Requirement → acceptance criteria** | 1..n            | Baselined requirement has complete applicable state coverage.                         |
| **Acceptance → verification case**    | 1..n            | Method and expected evidence are defined.                                             |
| **Verification → result/evidence**    | 1..n            | Current release execution and artifact integrity are valid.                           |
| **Evidence → release**                | n..1            | Release reconciliation confirms all blockers resolved or approved.                    |
| **Release → claim/disclosure**        | 0..n            | Public/customer statement only where claim register authorizes it.                    |

## 20.1 Orphan and drift rules

- No P0/P1 requirement may be orphaned from design, acceptance, verification or release evidence.

- No production test may claim coverage for a superseded requirement version.

- No release evidence may remain valid after a material source requirement or design contract changes without revalidation.

- No customer-facing claim may outlive its supporting release evidence or approved scope.

- Orphans and stale edges are release blockers unless a named, expiring exception exists.

# 21 \| Requirement Lifecycle, Baselines and Version Control

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image169.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.08056in" alt="Requirement states from proposed to verified, with rejected, withdrawn and superseded side states." />

***Figure 6 — Requirement lifecycle with controlled side states.***

| **State**              | **Entry condition**                                          | **Permitted action**                          | **Exit evidence**                              |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| **PROPOSED**           | Identified need with origin and sponsor.                     | Triage only.                                  | Triage decision.                               |
| **TRIAGED**            | Need, scope and owner understood.                            | Prioritize, reject, defer or draft.           | Disposition and rationale.                     |
| **DRAFT**              | Structured requirement and metadata present.                 | Review and refine; no build authority.        | Quality lint result.                           |
| **REVIEW**             | Required reviewers assigned and no blocking lint failures.   | Comment, approve or return.                   | Reviewer decisions.                            |
| **APPROVED**           | Product and applicable control/technical approvals complete. | Baseline assignment.                          | Approval record.                               |
| **BASELINED**          | Included in named release baseline.                          | Authorize implementation under delivery pack. | Baseline manifest.                             |
| **IMPLEMENTED**        | Code/configuration/documentation complete and linked.        | Verification.                                 | PR/build/provenance links.                     |
| **VERIFIED**           | All required tests/evidence pass for release scope.          | Release reconciliation or supersession.       | R20 evidence.                                  |
| **REJECTED/WITHDRAWN** | No longer authorized.                                        | Retain history; remove active projection.     | Decision and impact review.                    |
| **SUPERSEDED**         | New version replaces old.                                    | Historical reference only.                    | Supersession link and affected artifact state. |

## 21.1 Baseline rules

- A baseline is an immutable manifest of exact requirement versions and applicable constraints.

- Adding, removing or changing a baselined requirement creates a new baseline revision; history remains intact.

- Each delivery pack and issue-tracker projection names its baseline.

- Release evidence reconciles against the release baseline, not the latest draft state.

- An emergency change follows H2 and creates retrospective requirement and evidence updates within the approved window.

# 22 \| Change Impact, Conflict and Stop-Work Control

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image170.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.38611in" alt="Flow from change proposal through impact analysis, reviews, decision, regeneration of delivery packs and release evidence, with stop-work on conflict." />

***Figure 7 — Controlled requirement change and impact-analysis workflow.***

| **Change class**            | **Examples**                                                                            | **Minimum review**                                                         |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Editorial**               | Typographical correction with no semantic effect.                                       | Custodian; automated diff; version note.                                   |
| **Clarification**           | Removes ambiguity without changing approved intent.                                     | Owner, engineering and QA.                                                 |
| **Behavioral**              | Changes observable behavior, state or acceptance.                                       | Product, architecture, engineering, QA and applicable control owners.      |
| **Control-impacting**       | Security, privacy, AI, evidence, tenancy, response or claims effect.                    | Named control owner and release authority.                                 |
| **Breaking interface/data** | API/event/schema/data migration or compatibility impact.                                | Architecture, affected teams, migration and customer/partner notice owner. |
| **Scope/gate**              | Adds/removes capability, region, tenant class, connector, framework or authority level. | ADR and phase-gate authority.                                              |
| **Emergency**               | Immediate production containment or legal/security need.                                | Emergency change authority; retrospective full trace and review.           |

## 22.1 Impact traversal

**1.** Identify the changed requirement version and reason.

**2.** Traverse parents, children, design contracts, data, APIs/events, wireframes, tests, evidence, releases, claims and delivery packs.

**3.** Mark affected nodes STALE until reviewed or revalidated.

**4.** Assess security, privacy, AI, service, cost, compatibility and customer impact.

**5.** Approve, reject or time-bound the change; issue a new baseline where required.

**6.** Regenerate projections and notify named recipients.

**7.** Reconcile open work and release evidence before resuming or shipping.

# 23 \| Risks, Assumptions, Dependencies and Exceptions

| **Artifact**   | **Required fields**                                                                            | **Control rule**                                                      |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Risk**       | ID, cause, event, impact, likelihood, controls, owner, residual risk, review/expiry.           | Links to affected requirements and tests.                             |
| **Assumption** | Statement, basis, owner, validation date, consequence if false.                                | Cannot silently become a requirement; must be validated or converted. |
| **Dependency** | Provider/module/team, required capability/version/date, failure mode, fallback, owner.         | Dependency health and change trigger are explicit.                    |
| **Constraint** | Binding source, scope, requirement effect and exception authority.                             | Cannot be overridden in a ticket.                                     |
| **Exception**  | Exact requirement/version, reason, risk, compensating controls, approver, expiry and evidence. | No permanent exception; auto-escalate before expiry.                  |
| **Decision**   | Context, options, decision, consequences, owner, date and supersession.                        | Architectural decisions live in R02/ADR, not requirement prose.       |

| **ASSUMPTION RULE** | Any assumption that affects security, tenant isolation, data authority, evidence completeness, AI behavior, capacity or service obligation must be validated before the requirement is BASELINED. |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 24 \| Gate Binding and Release Authorization

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image171.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.6875in" alt="Release flow from baselined requirement through implementation, verification, control evidence and approval, with blocking checks." />

***Figure 8 — Traceability-based release authorization.***

| **Gate**                                          | **Requirements evidence required**                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **G0 — Build Authorization**                      | Approved requirement method; current R04 schema; release baseline; owners; data model; evidence design; AI controls; crown-jewel requirements; test strategy; no unresolved P0 ambiguity.                                        |
| **G1 — Design-Partner Readiness**                 | All in-scope requirements baselined; assigned W01–W29 experience contracts complete; security/privacy/AI reviews; negative-state tests; tenant-isolation and evidence verification; customer-data handling; operational handoff. |
| **G2 — Commercial GA**                            | Contractual service and SLA requirements; 24/7 operating requirements; incident/communication workflows; measured SLOs; release evidence; Trust Center/claims alignment; tenant exit tested.                                     |
| **G3 — Enterprise / Sector Scale**                | Enhanced isolation, scale, dedicated topology and sector-pack requirements; procurement assurance; partner certification; exercised recovery.                                                                                    |
| **G4 — Sovereign / OT / Critical Infrastructure** | Explicit Board authorization, contracted demand, sovereign/OT controls, deployment and operations evidence; no inherited assumption from earlier gates.                                                                          |

## 24.1 Release reconciliation result

| **Result**         | **Meaning**                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **PASS**           | All required trace nodes current; tests/evidence valid; no unapproved blockers.                                            |
| **CONDITIONAL**    | Only permitted where gate authority approves specific, expiring non-material conditions and customer impact is controlled. |
| **FAIL**           | Orphan, stale, failed, conflicting or unapproved requirement/control blocks release.                                       |
| **NOT APPLICABLE** | Criterion excluded by an approved scope rationale, not by omission.                                                        |

# 25 \| Issue Tracker, Delivery Pack and Agile Projection

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image172.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.81111in" alt="Workstream package containing assigned requirements, ADRs/register views, design contracts, acceptance/tests/evidence, risks, release target and change digest." />

***Figure 9 — Workstream delivery-pack architecture.***

| **Issue field**               | **Required value**                                                                 |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Requirement links**         | Exact IDs and versions; no free-text replacement.                                  |
| **Baseline**                  | Current release baseline identifier.                                               |
| **Delivery type**             | Feature, control, defect, migration, test, documentation, runbook or evidence.     |
| **Acceptance links**          | AC IDs and relevant experience-state contract.                                     |
| **Design links**              | Module, API/event/data/UX contract and ADR.                                        |
| **Test/evidence links**       | Verification cases and expected evidence.                                          |
| **Security/privacy/AI flags** | Applicable review and control owner.                                               |
| **Dependencies**              | Named requirement/module/team/provider dependencies.                               |
| **Definition of Ready**       | Current requirement, owner, design boundary, acceptance and no unresolved blocker. |
| **Definition of Done**        | Implementation, review, tests, audit, documentation, rollback and R20 evidence.    |

## 25.1 Synchronization and drift

- Tickets are generated or validated against R04; a manual ticket without a requirement reference cannot authorize product behavior.

- Requirement version changes mark linked tickets stale and notify the assignee and reviewer.

- Closing a ticket does not change requirement state to VERIFIED; verification evidence controls that transition.

- Issue comments may explain execution but do not amend acceptance criteria or constraints.

- Sprint completion metrics must not incentivize bypassing trace or test obligations.

# 26 \| Workstream Ownership, Reviews and Segregation of Duties

| **Workstream**             | **Primary requirement ownership**                                            | **Mandatory reviewers**                                           |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Platform / tenancy**     | Tenant, commercial control, module boundaries and shared platform behavior.  | Architecture, Security, Data, QA.                                 |
| **Ingestion / connectors** | Collection, normalization, health, backfill, OCSF and connector permissions. | Security, Privacy, Data, SRE, QA.                                 |
| **Evidence / GRC**         | Ledger, collectors, controls, evaluations, audit packages and verifier.      | Compliance, Security, Data, QA.                                   |
| **Detection / analytics**  | Rules, correlation, replay, risk factors and search.                         | SOC lead, Security, Data, SRE, QA.                                |
| **Case / response**        | Cases, playbooks, authority, broker, attestation and receipts.               | CISO, Service Ops, Customer authority model, QA.                  |
| **AI systems**             | Gateway, retrieval, agents, tools, memory, evaluation and disclosure.        | AI Risk, Security, Privacy, Product, QA.                          |
| **Experience / reporting** | Shell, workflows, states, accessibility, reporting and notifications.        | Product, Security, Compliance, AI Risk, Accessibility.            |
| **Infrastructure / SRE**   | Environments, deployment, observability, resilience, cost and operations.    | Security, Architecture, QA, FinOps.                               |
| **QA / release**           | Verification architecture, evidence reconciliation and gate outcome.         | Independent of primary implementer; control owners as applicable. |

## 26.1 Segregation rules

- No engineer may author, approve and independently verify a P0/P1 requirement they implement.

- Product approval cannot waive security, privacy, AI or evidence requirements.

- Control owners cannot unilaterally create product scope.

- Release authority cannot rewrite acceptance to fit an implementation.

- Requirement custodians manage records but do not replace accountable owners.

# 27 \| Metrics, Quality Assurance and Control Monitoring

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image173.png" style="width:6.9in;height:3.57083in" alt="Dashboard categories covering coverage, orphans, volatility, ambiguity, verification and drift." />

***Figure 10 — Requirements quality and traceability dashboard.***

| **Metric**                     | **Definition**                                                                          | **Control expectation**                               |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| **Trace coverage**             | Approved requirements with current parent, design, AC, verification and evidence links. | 100% for P0/P1; target defined for lower criticality. |
| **Orphan count**               | Requirements, tests, design contracts or evidence without valid trace parent.           | Zero release-blocking orphans.                        |
| **Quality pass rate**          | Drafts passing automated lint and required review.                                      | Trend by team/domain; failures aged and owned.        |
| **Ambiguity age**              | Time from clarification/stop-work opening to controlled resolution.                     | Target by criticality.                                |
| **Baseline volatility**        | Approved requirement versions changed after baseline.                                   | Measured with reason and rework impact.               |
| **Stale projection age**       | Time tickets/delivery packs remain on superseded versions.                              | Zero at release.                                      |
| **State coverage**             | Applicable failure/unauthorized/recovery states with AC and tests.                      | 100% for material states.                             |
| **Verification coverage**      | Requirements with valid release-specific result/evidence.                               | 100% for release baseline.                            |
| **Escaped requirement defect** | Production/design-partner defect caused by missing/incorrect requirement.               | Root cause and corrective action required.            |
| **Change impact completeness** | Changed trace nodes reviewed or revalidated.                                            | 100% before release.                                  |
| **Review SLA**                 | Required reviewers completing within target.                                            | Monitored; does not justify auto-approval.            |
| **Exception hygiene**          | Exceptions current, owned and within expiry.                                            | Zero expired active exceptions.                       |

## 27.1 Assurance activities

- Automated daily orphan, duplicate, stale-link and quality-lint checks.

- Weekly workstream requirement health review during ERB-01.

- Release-baseline reconciliation before every candidate promotion.

- Monthly sample of requirement-to-production evidence by QA and control owners.

- Quarterly taxonomy, metadata and access review after GA.

- Post-incident and escaped-defect analysis of requirement causes and corrective controls.

# 28 \| Document Page and Visual Architecture

The operational document must remain readable at engineering speed while preserving controlled authority. It should be approximately 40–55 pages for the ERB-01 baseline, excluding generated requirement catalogs and register exports. Requirements themselves should be rendered as filtered, generated views rather than manually copied pages.

| **Document zone**               | **Required content**                                                                                       |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cover**                       | Brand, title, ID, version, state, classification, baseline, parents, premise and non-authorization notice. |
| **Front matter**                | Approvals, change record, distribution, normative language, sources, contents and executive mandate.       |
| **Control architecture**        | Principles, taxonomy, metadata, lifecycle, quality, trace and change rules.                                |
| **Requirement-class chapters**  | Functional, NFR, security/privacy, evidence, AI, data/interface, experience and failure-state patterns.    |
| **Acceptance and verification** | Criterion patterns, test/evidence contract and gate reconciliation.                                        |
| **Operational controls**        | Issue-tracker integration, workstream roles, metrics, exceptions and stop-work.                            |
| **Annexes**                     | Templates, schemas, matrices, examples, lint rules and approval forms.                                     |
| **Generated views**             | Requirement catalogs and trace matrices produced from R04; snapshot and timestamp displayed.               |

## 28.1 Visual treatment

| **Element**            | **Controlled treatment**                                                                               |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Heading**            | Stable numbered hierarchy; no decorative ambiguity.                                                    |
| **Control statement**  | Stable ID, bold title, mandatory consequence and required evidence.                                    |
| **Requirement card**   | ID/version/state/owner header; normative statement; source, scope, AC, tests and evidence.             |
| **Table**              | Repeating header, non-color cues, compact wording, no split critical row where avoidable.              |
| **Diagram**            | Caption, alt text, source, version and no unlabeled decorative line.                                   |
| **Status**             | Text label plus shape/icon; color never the only signal.                                               |
| **Restricted content** | Separate controlled annex or redacted reference; main requirement remains complete for implementation. |
| **Generated content**  | “Generated from R04 snapshot …” label and checksum/version.                                            |

# 31 \| Definition of Ready, Done and Approval Gate

## 31.1 Requirement Definition of Ready

| **\#** | **Requirement Ready condition**                                                                                                 |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1**  | Unique ID, type, version, state and accountable owner assigned.                                                                 |
| **2**  | Approved origin, outcome/capability parent and current release scope linked.                                                    |
| **3**  | Atomic normative statement, rationale, scope, assumptions, dependencies and exclusions complete.                                |
| **4**  | Applicable functional, quality, security, privacy, evidence, AI, data/interface, experience and operational constraints linked. |
| **5**  | Material failure, degraded, unauthorized and recovery behavior specified.                                                       |
| **6**  | Acceptance criteria, verification method, tests and evidence requirements defined.                                              |
| **7**  | Architecture/data/API/event/UX dependencies linked and reviewed.                                                                |
| **8**  | No blocking quality-lint failure, unresolved conflict or unvalidated material assumption.                                       |
| **9**  | Required reviewers identified; classification and workstream disclosure approved.                                               |

## 31.2 Requirement Definition of Done

| **\#** | **Requirement Done condition**                                                                  |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1**  | Approved and baselined requirement version implemented without unexplained divergence.          |
| **2**  | Code/configuration/schema/content reviewed under segregation-of-duties rules.                   |
| **3**  | All linked acceptance criteria verified in the applicable state classes.                        |
| **4**  | Security, privacy, tenant-isolation, evidence and AI controls pass where applicable.            |
| **5**  | Observability, audit events, documentation, runbook, migration and rollback are complete.       |
| **6**  | API/event/data/UX documentation and generated register views are current.                       |
| **7**  | Release evidence is attributable to the correct baseline, build, environment and scale profile. |
| **8**  | No unresolved P0/P1 defect, stale edge, orphan or expired exception.                            |
| **9**  | Owner and control reviewers accept the evidence; R20 records the result.                        |

## 31.3 Document-03 approval decisions

| **Decision**                  | **Required closure**                                                                     |
|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R04 platform and schema**   | Tooling, API/export, identity, versioning, graph links, audit and backup approved.       |
| **Identifier and taxonomy**   | Prefixes, domains, artifact types and ownership approved.                                |
| **Quality lint**              | Blocking rules, warning policy and waiver authority implemented.                         |
| **Trace graph**               | Required nodes/edges, stale propagation and orphan detection implemented.                |
| **Issue tracker integration** | Projection, version sync, stale markers and reconciliation tested.                       |
| **Review model**              | Product, architecture, control, QA and release approvals defined.                        |
| **Baseline model**            | Immutable manifests, change flow and emergency path implemented.                         |
| **Evidence integration**      | Test/evidence systems can write attributable links to R20.                               |
| **Access model**              | Workstream filtering and restricted content behavior comply with ZS-ENG-GOV-001.         |
| **Pilot**                     | At least one complete vertical requirement slice passes authoring-to-release simulation. |

| **FINAL CONTROL SENTENCE** | No build from an orphaned requirement. No acceptance without observable evidence. No AI behavior without authority and fallback. No release with stale trace. No ticket, message or deadline may silently override the controlled baseline. |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# 32 \| Reference Methods and Controlled Use

The operational specification may use the following methods as design inputs. Standards content must be licensed or referenced by identifier; this document does not reproduce protected standards text and does not claim conformance by citation alone.

| **Reference**                        | **Controlled use**                                                                                                     |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018**          | Requirements-engineering process and information-item guidance.                                                        |
| **ISO/IEC 25010:2023**               | Product quality model used to structure measurable quality requirements.                                               |
| **ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026**          | Software life-cycle process framework used to align requirements, development, verification, operation and retirement. |
| **NIST SP 800-218, SSDF v1.1**       | Final secure software development practices; the 1.2 revision remains draft at this document date.                     |
| **NIST SP 800-218A (2024)**          | Final community profile for secure development of generative AI and dual-use foundation models.                        |
| **Gherkin / BDD conventions**        | Readable behavioral acceptance pattern; not a substitute for the controlled requirement and evidence graph.            |
| **OCSF**                             | Canonical security event normalization reference used by C3.                                                           |
| **OpenAPI / AsyncAPI / JSON Schema** | Machine-readable interface and schema contracts where approved by C3/C4.                                               |

Authoritative reference versions must be tracked in the applicable standards or architecture register. A newer publication does not silently alter a baselined requirement; impact review and controlled adoption are required.

# 00 \| Critical Review and Refined Scope Decision

The earlier Document-02 outline correctly identified the need for a current build mandate, but it did not yet establish a precise release identity, scope-state model, product/offer/sector-pack separation, decision-dependency contract, or gate-evidence structure. Those omissions would allow backlog drift, hidden coupling and informal scope expansion. This refinement converts the outline into a release-control architecture that an engineering organization can execute and audit.

<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th></th>
<th><p><strong>REFINED ARCHITECTURE DECISION</strong></p>
<p>Issue one controlled scope document for ERB-01. It defines the minimum complete G0-to-G1 build boundary, names every committed and conditional capability, records exclusions, binds workstreams to one vertical slice, and prevents informal scope growth. It does not expose customer identities, pricing, pipeline or executive strategy.</p></th>

<th><p><strong>BUILD MANDATE</strong></p>
<p>Deliver ERB-01 as one secure, multi-tenant, evidence-first platform that can onboard a design-partner tenant, integrate approved security and assurance sources, produce traceable detections and control evaluations, support human-reviewed AI-assisted investigation, preserve independently verifiable evidence, freeze an audit package and export the tenant’s portable proof.</p></th>

| **Mandate**                                   | **Binding engineering consequence**                                                                                                                                 |
|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **One platform**                              | Build one horizontal platform core. Do not create separate finance, SaaS, healthcare, telecom or AI products.                                                       |
| **Two entry offers**                          | Managed Defense and Continuous Assurance must each land independently; shared platform services may not create a commercial or operational dependency between them. |
| **Regulated-first, not regulated-only**       | Engineering must support organizations under regulatory, contractual, customer, insurer, investor, supply-chain or Board proof pressure.                            |
| **Evidence as product behavior**              | Every material conclusion, response proposal, AI recommendation and privileged change must produce attributable evidence.                                           |
| **AI assists; deterministic controls decide** | No LLM controls authentication, authorization, entitlement, evidence integrity, compliance status, response approval or critical recovery.                          |
| **Human-in-command**                          | ERB-01 supports R0/R1 and simulation. Higher response authority remains gate-controlled.                                                                            |
| **Integrate before duplicate**                | Connect Tier-1 security and business systems; build the evidence, policy, correlation, orchestration and assurance core.                                            |
| **Failure is visible**                        | Partial, stale, degraded, unauthorized and unknown states must be explicit in APIs, events, operations and screens.                                                 |
| **No speculative scope**                      | No work enters the active release without a source requirement, owner, acceptance evidence and capacity allocation.                                                 |

# 03 \| Purpose, Applicability and Disclosure Boundary

## 3.1 Purpose

Define the exact engineering outcome, capability boundary, deployment assumptions, quality envelope, workstream responsibilities, decision dependencies, exclusions and gate evidence for ERB-01. The document answers: what must be built now, what may be built only after a named decision, what must not be built, and what evidence proves completion.

## 3.2 Applies to

- All ZoikoShield engineering, platform, data, AI, QA, SRE, security, service-operations and experience teams assigned to ERB-01.

- Employees, contractors, approved engineering partners and service providers working under a controlled workstream pack.

- All repositories, environments, interfaces, schemas, wireframes, tests, release artifacts and runbooks governed by ERB-01.

- All changes whose behavior can affect a G0 or G1 gate condition.

## 3.3 Does not disclose

- Customer and design-partner identities, pipeline details, negotiation history or account economics.

- Complete price books, discount bands, partner margins, investment model or Board forecasts.

- Unrelated future-sector strategy, acquisition plans or speculative product hypotheses.

- Unrestricted crown-jewel attack trees, live credentials, private keys, production secrets or unresolved exploit details.

- Licensed standards text beyond the legally permitted implementation extract.

# 04 \| Scope-Control Principles and Non-Waivable Rules

| **ID**    | **Principle**                  | **Controlled consequence**                                                                                     |
|-----------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **SC-01** | Authoritative scope only       | Only COMMITTED scope in the current manifest authorizes implementation.                                        |
| **SC-02** | One horizontal core            | Sector requirements are configuration and governed content, never product forks.                               |
| **SC-03** | Independent landing            | Managed Defense and Continuous Assurance cannot require each other’s commercial entitlement.                   |
| **SC-04** | Minimum complete slice         | The release is accepted only when the full vertical slice works; isolated module completion is insufficient.   |
| **SC-05** | Decision visibility            | Conditional scope names the decision, owner, deadline, default and implementation consequence.                 |
| **SC-06** | No hidden customer specificity | Customer-specific work is parameterized or captured as a controlled configuration; no tenant fork.             |
| **SC-07** | No LLM critical path           | AI failure must not stop deterministic security, evidence, authorization or recovery paths.                    |
| **SC-08** | Evidence before assertion      | No healthy, secure or compliant state without the required evidence state and evaluator version.               |
| **SC-09** | Tenant context everywhere      | Tenant, environment, region, actor, purpose and trace context propagate across every material operation.       |
| **SC-10** | Authority before action        | Response level, approvals, attestation, rollback and blast radius are resolved before execution.               |
| **SC-11** | Economics are constraints      | Scale and cost are measured during the release, not deferred to post-GA optimization.                          |
| **SC-12** | Quality is part of scope       | Tests, telemetry, documentation, rollback and operational evidence are deliverables, not follow-on tasks.      |
| **SC-13** | No informal expansion          | Tickets, chats, demos and customer requests cannot enlarge committed scope without source change.              |
| **SC-14** | Stop on ambiguity              | Material ambiguity in tenant isolation, data authority, AI authority, response or evidence triggers stop-work. |
| **SC-15** | Gate evidence over schedule    | Dates do not close gates. Current evidence does.                                                               |

# 05 \| Scope Taxonomy, States and Source Authority

## 5.1 Six-level scope taxonomy

| **Scope layer**          | **Meaning**                                                                               | **Authority**                     |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Platform scope**       | Horizontal capabilities and invariants shared by all offers and sector packs.             | A5, B1, C1, R06                   |
| **Offer scope**          | Managed Defense or Continuous Assurance outcomes and service behavior.                    | A5, B1, F1/F2, R06/R08            |
| **Sector-pack scope**    | Mappings, evidence expectations, detections, workflows and reports layered over the core. | B1, G2, R14                       |
| **Release scope**        | Capabilities and quality evidence committed to ERB-01.                                    | A6, R02/R04/R05/R19/R20           |
| **Workstream scope**     | Subset assigned to a named team with interfaces and tests.                                | R04, R06 and workstream pack      |
| **Tenant configuration** | Approved entitlements, region, connectors, policies and settings for a customer.          | R08/R09/R12; never a product fork |

## 5.2 Controlled scope states

| **State**       | **Engineering meaning**                                                                                                                       |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **PROPOSED**    | Candidate only; discovery and design may occur in a sandbox. No production implementation commitment.                                         |
| **CONDITIONAL** | May enter design behind a disabled flag only when a named ADR, partner, legal or gate dependency is open. Cannot be represented as committed. |
| **COMMITTED**   | Approved, owned, funded, capacity-allocated, requirements-linked and release-tested.                                                          |
| **DELIVERED**   | Acceptance evidence exists and is recorded; remains subject to gate decision.                                                                 |
| **DEFERRED**    | Explicitly excluded until a named later gate or unlock condition.                                                                             |
| **PROHIBITED**  | Must not be designed or implemented in the current planning horizon without a new Board/architecture decision.                                |
| **WITHDRAWN**   | Previously proposed or committed scope removed through controlled change and impact reconciliation.                                           |
