# 07 \| Product, Offer and Market Boundary

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image177.png" style="width:6.55in;height:3.19306in" alt="One platform core supports independently landable Managed Defense and Continuous Assurance offers with sector packs as governed configuration." />

*Figure 4 — Horizontal platform, independent entry offers and governed sector packs.*

## 7.1 Shared horizontal platform

- Tenant, identity, policy, entitlement and regional control.

- Integration, ingestion, canonical events and connector health.

- Asset, identity, exposure and transparent risk context.

- Detection, alert, case, playbook and response-proposal workflows.

- Evidence ledger, control evaluation, risk, exception and audit-package workflows.

- AI gateway, retrieval, agent runtime, evaluation and disclosure controls.

- APIs, events, experiences, observability, release evidence and tenant exit.

## 7.2 Independent-offer boundary

| **Offer**                            | **Required engineering outcome**                                                                                                                                                | **Boundary**                                                                  |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **ZoikoShield Managed Defense**      | Security-led entry. Requires telemetry, detection, alerts, case workflows and evidence of service activity. May operate without a Continuous Assurance commercial entitlement.  | No implied certification or full framework coverage.                          |
| **ZoikoShield Continuous Assurance** | Assurance-led entry. Requires control library, evidence, evaluation, risk, exception and audit-package workflows. May operate without a Managed Defense commercial entitlement. | No implied 24/7 monitoring or response service.                               |
| **Combined deployment**              | Shares tenant, identity, evidence, asset context and reporting. Bundle validation prevents double charging or duplicate operating ownership.                                    | Shared platform does not erase separate entitlements and service obligations. |

## 7.3 Market information exposed to engineering

| **Category**                | **Controlled treatment**                                                                                                             |
|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Expose**                  | Functional needs: evidence pressure, fragmented tools, small security/compliance teams, cloud/API estates, audit and Board scrutiny. |
| **Do not expose**           | Named pipeline, account value, win/loss notes, negotiated terms, buyer politics, pricing or Board market assumptions.                |
| **Engineering consequence** | Build configurable capabilities for both launch archetypes and validate with approved anonymized design-partner profiles.            |
| **Prohibition**             | Do not hard-code “regulated customer” eligibility or a single-industry data model into the platform core.                            |

# 08 \| ERB-01 End-to-End Outcome and Release Increments

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image178.png" style="width:6.8in;height:2.30417in" alt="Tenant onboarding through source connection, detection or control testing, investigation, response proposal, evidence, audit package and offboarding." />

*Figure 5 — ERB-01 release-defining end-to-end proof.*

## 8.1 Release-defining acceptance narrative

A controlled tenant is created in an approved region; identity and authorization are configured; approved data sources are connected with declared permissions; events and evidence are authenticated, normalized and attributed; a point detection and a control evaluation execute against versioned inputs; a case is opened; the AI assistant produces a cited, human-reviewed recommendation without direct action authority; an R1 response proposal is created in simulation; material events and conclusions are written to the evidence ledger; an audit package is frozen and verified offline; the tenant’s records and evidence are exported in open formats; and every step is traceable to requirements, tests and release evidence.

## 8.2 Controlled increments

| **Increment**                           | **Gate**  | **Committed outcome**                                                                                                                                                                                                     | **Boundary**                                                    |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **F0 — Engineering foundation**         | G0        | Identity skeleton, tenant context, module boundaries, regional environments, CI/CD, event and data contracts, evidence ledger/verifier skeleton, model gateway skeleton, synthetic tenants and release evidence pipeline. | No real customer data; no customer-facing claims.               |
| **DP1 — Design-partner vertical slice** | G1        | P0 connectors, normalized events, point detection, control evaluation, alerts/cases, R1 proposal, AI assistance, evidence operations, audit package, G1 experience contracts, support and synthetic exit.                 | Controlled real customer data only after G1 approval.           |
| **GA0 — Commercial readiness**          | Future G2 | 24/7 operating model, measured SLOs, R2 red-team gates, G2 experience contracts, contracts/Trust Center, sector packs and commercial commitments.                                                                         | Not part of ERB-01; interfaces may be preserved, not delivered. |

# 11 \| Deferred, Prohibited and Non-Goals

| **Capability**                                    | **State**             | **Controlled reason / unlock**                                             |
|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Custom ZoikoShield EDR agent**                  | PROHIBITED            | Board-level ADR only; integration is the canonical position.               |
| **Standalone Managed SIEM service**               | DEFERRED G2/G3        | Requires unit-economics and operating-model proof.                         |
| **R2–R4 live automation**                         | DEFERRED G2+          | Requires independent red team, customer attestation and authority gates.   |
| **T3 dedicated / T4 sovereign or private planes** | DEFERRED G3/G4        | Demand-funded topology and specialized assurance required.                 |
| **OT-heavy critical infrastructure**              | DEFERRED G4           | Specialist safety/threat model and Board authorization required.           |
| **Full privacy/DSR product suite**                | DEFERRED              | Privacy controls required internally; customer product module not ERB-01.  |
| **Customer AI-governance workspace**              | DEFERRED G2/G3        | Internal AI governance is required; customer product is not.               |
| **Marketplace or app directory**                  | DEFERRED              | Connector catalog is sufficient for ERB-01.                                |
| **Mobile-native applications**                    | DEFERRED              | Responsive web experience only.                                            |
| **Custom dashboard builder**                      | DEFERRED              | Controlled standard views and reports only.                                |
| **Full multi-region active-active**               | DEFERRED              | Multi-AZ regional operation plus documented recovery.                      |
| **Tier-1 global-bank bespoke requirements**       | NON-GOAL              | No customer-specific architecture branch.                                  |
| **General microbusiness self-service product**    | NON-GOAL              | Not the initial support/economics model.                                   |
| **Reproduction of licensed standards text**       | PROHIBITED            | Use identifiers and rights-cleared Zoiko-authored objectives.              |
| **Use of customer data to train models**          | PROHIBITED by default | Requires explicit contractual and governance authorization outside ERB-01. |

# 12 \| Runtime, Deployment and Regional Boundary

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image179.png" style="width:6.65in;height:3.15833in" alt="Modular core with isolated ingestion, AI, action and evidence anchoring satellites in a regional data plane." />

*Figure 6 — ERB-01 runtime topology and trust boundaries.*

| **Boundary**                 | **ERB-01 position**                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Topology**                 | Modular monolith plus four satellites. No general microservice decomposition.                                     |
| **Production isolation**     | T1 pooled regional cells with tenant-scoped database, object, search, cache, queue and observability controls.    |
| **Availability pattern**     | Multi-AZ within an activated region. Cross-region recovery follows approved H1/H5 design; no active-active claim. |
| **Global control plane**     | Tenant directory, catalog metadata, feature policy, deployment inventory and approved aggregate health only.      |
| **Prohibited global data**   | Raw telemetry, evidence content, customer secrets, unrestricted personal data and response credentials.           |
| **Environment path**         | Local/synthetic → development → integration → staging → production. Customer data is prohibited before G1.        |
| **Infrastructure authority** | H1 infrastructure-as-code only; no manual shadow environments.                                                    |
| **Secrets**                  | Vault references only. No secret values in documents, code, tickets or logs.                                      |
| **Egress**                   | Controlled and allowlisted. AI/provider and connector egress is policy-governed.                                  |
| **Feature exposure**         | Disabled by default; tenant and gate eligibility evaluated before activation.                                     |

# 13 \| Identity, Data, Tenant and Evidence Boundary

## 13.1 Tenant and identity boundary

| **Control**                | **Committed behavior**                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant hierarchy**       | group_account → tenant → legal_entity → business_unit → environment → workspace; tenant is the isolation boundary.      |
| **Human identity**         | ZoikoID federation via OIDC/SAML; MFA/passkey; step-up for privileged or response actions.                              |
| **Workload identity**      | Short-lived workload identity and mTLS; static service credentials prohibited.                                          |
| **Authorization**          | RBAC + ABAC + relationship rules; purpose, tenant, environment, case/change and approval context for sensitive actions. |
| **Privileged access**      | JIT, time-bound, approved, recorded and ticket-linked; break-glass creates immediate evidence and review.               |
| **Degraded identity mode** | Bounded read capability may continue; privileged and response paths fail closed.                                        |

## 13.2 Data and evidence boundary

| **Data/evidence area**           | **Required boundary**                                                                                                                      |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source authority**             | Every material field records its system of authority or confidence; ZoikoShield does not silently become authoritative for external facts. |
| **Residency**                    | Region is resolved before durable persistence. Unmatched policy routes to quarantine and alerting.                                         |
| **Development data**             | Synthetic or approved anonymized data only. No raw customer data on local devices.                                                         |
| **Raw and normalized telemetry** | Raw source retained only where contract/privacy permit; normalized events preserve mapping provenance.                                     |
| **Evidence integrity**           | Canonicalized content hash, collector identity/version, tenant chain, checkpoint, witnesses and verifier contract.                         |
| **Completeness**                 | COMPLETE, PARTIAL, STALE, COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY, PERMISSION_CHANGED and EVALUATOR_FAILED are explicit states.                                |
| **Audit packages**               | Freeze inputs, mappings, evaluators, outputs, gaps and proofs; never regenerate silently against current data.                             |
| **Exit**                         | Open-format records and evidence with manifest/proofs; deletion attestation follows legal-hold and backup rules.                           |

# 14 \| AI and Response-Authority Boundary

## 14.1 AI use cases permitted in ERB-01

| **Permitted use**                        | **Mandatory controls**                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Alert and case summarization**         | Citations to source events and evidence; visible confidence; analyst review for material cases. |
| **Investigation assistance**             | Read-only allowlisted tools; tenant-bound retrieval; no direct action broker authority.         |
| **Control/evidence mapping suggestions** | Human owner accepts, modifies or rejects; decision recorded.                                    |
| **Detection candidate drafting**         | Sandbox only; deterministic re-expression and testing before publication.                       |
| **Executive narrative draft**            | Generated from approved structured facts; known limitations and human approval required.        |
| **Support and documentation assistance** | Approved non-sensitive knowledge only; no customer secret or production credential exposure.    |

## 14.2 AI prohibited authorities

- Authentication or session authority.

- Authorization, entitlement, segregation-of-duties or key-release decisions.

- Evidence integrity, ledger verification or completeness-state mutation.

- Final compliance or certification conclusion.

- Unreviewed customer-facing risk assertion.

- Approval or execution of response actions.

- Direct cross-tenant retrieval or unrestricted memory.

- Silent fallback to an unapproved provider or region.

## 14.3 Response authority in ERB-01

| **Level**                        | **ERB-01 state** | **Boundary**                                                              |
|----------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R0 — Observe**                 | COMMITTED        | Collect, enrich, query, notify and open cases; no external change.        |
| **R1 — Recommend**               | COMMITTED        | Human-approved recommendation; simulation and evidence receipt.           |
| **R2 — Pre-authorized low risk** | CONDITIONAL G2   | Interfaces disabled; independent red-team and attestation gates required. |
| **R3 — High impact**             | DEFERRED         | Dual customer authority and production command attestation required.      |
| **R4 — Emergency**               | DEFERRED         | Break-glass, immediate escalation and post-action review; not ERB-01.     |

# 15 \| Integration and Connector Boundary

| **Category**                | **ERB-01 source set**                                                                   | **Boundary**                                                                         |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity/productivity**   | Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 family.                                            | Read/collect at G1; permissions displayed and health monitored.                      |
| **Endpoint security**       | One certified EDR partner selected through ADR; additional BYO EDR read-only ingestion. | Response actions only after connector certification; R1 in ERB-01.                   |
| **Cloud**                   | AWS and Azure baseline.                                                                 | Cloud account/tenant audit and posture sources; least-privilege cross-account roles. |
| **Generic security events** | Authenticated webhook and TLS syslog/CEF/LEEF.                                          | Schema validation, replay protection, source identity and quarantine.                |
| **Ticketing**               | One approved ticketing integration.                                                     | Case/task synchronization with idempotency and source authority.                     |
| **Vulnerability**           | One approved vulnerability source.                                                      | Findings and asset linkage; no scanner engine built.                                 |
| **Threat intelligence**     | Approved feed adapter and STIX/TAXII-compatible intake where licensed.                  | Source/TLP/licensing and expiry preserved.                                           |
| **Email security**          | Read-only integration if required by a design partner and capacity approved.            | Conditional; not a reason to expand the P0 connector matrix silently.                |

## 15.1 Connector contract requirements

- Declared source permissions and purpose before consent.

- Per-tenant vaulted credentials and short-lived tokens where supported.

- Authentication, timestamp validation, schema validation, idempotency and replay protection.

- Regional routing before persistence.

- Explicit healthy, delayed, degraded, unauthorized, rate-limited, schema-drifted and failed states.

- Backfill, reconciliation, quarantine and source-native payload rules.

- Versioned connector contracts, negative tests, scale tests and deprecation policy.

- No connector identity may invoke the action broker directly.

# 16 \| Experience-Contract and Interface Boundary

ERB-01 includes the G1-blocking experience contracts because design-partner readiness is not achieved by back-end APIs alone. Each experience contract is an annotated engineering specification linked to requirements, permissions, data authority, API/event contracts, audit events, AI controls, accessibility and tests.

| **Group**                          | **Contracts**             | **ERB-01 treatment**                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|------------------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Shell, identity and operations** | W01–W05                   | Application shell; sign-in; JIT access; notifications; operational command center.                                                                                                                               |
| **Onboarding and administration**  | W06–W12                   | Tenant onboarding; connectors; health; users/SoD; entitlements/usage; audit explorer; configuration approval.                                                                                                    |
| **Security operations**            | W13–W18                   | Alert queue/detail; case workspace; response proposal; playbook simulation; detection content.                                                                                                                   |
| **Assurance and evidence**         | W21–W28                   | Control library/detail; evidence queue/object; package builder; auditor workspace; risk; exceptions.                                                                                                             |
| **AI patterns**                    | W33–W35                   | AI assistant; AI proposal decision card; internal model/agent operations.                                                                                                                                        |
| **G2-only interfaces**             | W19–W20, W29–W32, W36–W38 | Incident command, SOC handover, exposure/executive views, export developer and trust/support surfaces; interfaces may be anticipated but are not G1 completion unless specifically moved through change control. |

## 16.1 Mandatory state classes

| **State**                     | **Required behavior**                                                             |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Loading / resolving**       | Progress and source resolution are visible; no false zero state.                  |
| **Empty / first use**         | Guidance and next permitted action; not confused with missing data.               |
| **Nominal / populated**       | Current data with provenance and applicable confidence.                           |
| **Partial / incomplete**      | Missing coverage and affected scope are enumerated.                               |
| **Stale / degraded**          | Freshness or dependency threshold exceeded; non-suppressible.                     |
| **Error / unavailable**       | System or dependency failure with correlation ID and recovery path.               |
| **Unauthorized / restricted** | Permission state distinct from system failure; access request or escalation path. |

# 17 \| Nonfunctional, Scale and Quality Boundary

## 17.1 Hard invariants

| **Invariant**                       | **Release rule**                                                         |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cross-tenant access**             | Zero known paths; any finding is a P0 release blocker.                   |
| **Evidence integrity**              | No undetected mutation; verifier and witness consistency tests pass.     |
| **Material audit events**           | Missing high-impact event is P0; active reconciliation required.         |
| **Privileged and response actions** | Bounded, attributable, policy-evaluated and evidence-linked.             |
| **AI critical-path authority**      | Prohibited.                                                              |
| **Restore integrity**               | Restored state reconciles with event manifests and evidence checkpoints. |
| **Customer-data use**               | Approved purpose, region, classification and access only.                |
| **Release provenance**              | Signed artifact, SBOM, build provenance and approved promotion evidence. |

## 17.2 Internal engineering objectives

| **Objective**                       | **ERB-01 treatment**                                                                                 |
|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Control-plane API availability**  | 99.95% monthly at GA; ERB-01 must measure the same indicator without contractual claim.              |
| **Telemetry durable acceptance**    | 99.90% launch objective for valid authenticated events.                                              |
| **Point detection latency**         | p95 ≤60 seconds from durable acceptance to alert.                                                    |
| **Windowed detection latency**      | p95 ≤ declared window + 60 seconds.                                                                  |
| **Connector failure visibility**    | p95 ≤5 minutes from platform-observed failure.                                                       |
| **Material audit reconciliation**   | ≥99.99% sampled operations within 5 minutes; any missing high-impact event is P0.                    |
| **Evidence checkpoint publication** | ≤24 hours to both witnesses; missed cadence degrades integrity state.                                |
| **Transactional recovery**          | RTO 4 hours / RPO 15 minutes standard; accepted telemetry replayed.                                  |
| **Accessibility**                   | Applicable WCAG-aligned keyboard, focus, semantics, contrast and non-color status behavior verified. |
| **Economics**                       | Cost telemetry and per-tenant attribution operational; no release claim without measured headroom.   |

## 17.3 Reference scale envelope

| **Dimension**                            | **ERB-01 envelope**                                                      |
|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Active tenants**                       | 3–10                                                                     |
| **Protected resources**                  | 2,000–10,000                                                             |
| **Telemetry TB/day**                     | 0.2 low / 0.8 nominal / 2 high                                           |
| **Peak events/second**                   | 15,000                                                                   |
| **Connector instances**                  | 50–200                                                                   |
| **Alerts / cases per day**               | 200 / 30                                                                 |
| **Evidence objects/month**               | 50,000                                                                   |
| **Concurrent investigations / searches** | 10 / 50                                                                  |
| **AI calls/day**                         | 5,000                                                                    |
| **Concurrent agent runs**                | 10                                                                       |
| **Response commands/day**                | 25 simulation / 5 live maximum; live limited to approved R0/R1 semantics |

## 18.1 Workstream scope-card fields

- Scope-card ID and version.

- Release and gate.

- Accountable lead and named reviewers.

- In-scope requirements and explicit exclusions.

- Owned modules, repositories and schemas.

- Consumed and published APIs/events.

- Data classes, regions and environments.

- Applicable experience contracts.

- Security, privacy, AI and evidence controls.

- Dependencies and service-level expectations.

- Required tests and release evidence.

- Definition of ready and done.

- Open decisions and exception expiry.

- Capacity allocation and displaced work.

| **2**     | Moat contracts                   | C7 evidence ledger/verifier, C2 data model and C3 event schema established before broad feature code.            |
| **3**     | Platform and identity foundation | C6 tenant/identity/authorization and H1/H2 environments/release pipeline.                                        |
| **4**     | AI boundary and API contracts    | D1/D2 and C4 establish model, tool, retrieval and interface contracts.                                           |
| **5**     | P0 ingestion                     | C5 connectors and normalization against synthetic sources; health and replay proven.                             |
| **6**     | Detection/control vertical slice | C8 point detection plus C7 control evaluation against versioned inputs.                                          |

| **9**     | Integrated verification          | End-to-end vertical slice, tenant-isolation, AI adversarial, ledger verifier, restore and synthetic offboarding. |

## 19.1 Integration checkpoints

| **ID**    | **Checkpoint**     | **Acceptance**                                                                                    |
|-----------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **IC-01** | Tenant + event     | Authenticated event enters the correct regional tenant scope and is queryable with provenance.    |
| **IC-02** | Event + detection  | Point rule produces deterministic alert and replay result.                                        |
| **IC-03** | Evidence + control | Collector/evaluator produces explicit evidence and control state with verifier-compatible record. |
| **IC-04** | Alert + case + AI  | Case opens; AI summary cites inputs; human decision is recorded.                                  |
| **IC-05** | Response proposal  | R1 proposal shows authority, approvals, blast radius, rollback and simulation receipt.            |
| **IC-06** | Audit package      | Frozen package verifies offline and exposes known gaps.                                           |
| **IC-07** | Exit               | Open-format export verifies and deletion workflow produces synthetic attestation.                 |
| **IC-08** | Restore            | Restored state reconciles to event manifest and evidence checkpoint.                              |

# 20 \| Release Configuration Manifest

The operational Document 02 must contain a machine-readable Release Configuration Manifest. Narrative statements are explanatory; the manifest is the authoritative release-scoping view consumed by repositories, issue templates, feature policy, test selection and release evidence.

|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| **release_id**              | Unique release baseline, e.g., ERB-01.                       |
| **version**                 | Semantic version of the scope manifest.                      |
| **state**                   | draft / approved / review-required / superseded / withdrawn. |
| **gate_from / gate_to**     | Authorized gate movement.                                    |
| **effective_date / expiry** | Validity window.                                             |
| **parent_sources**          | Exact master/register/ADR versions.                          |
| **offers**                  | Enabled offer IDs and independent-landing rules.             |
| **sector_packs**            | Committed, conditional and deferred packs.                   |
| **deployment_tiers**        | Authorized topology and isolation classes.                   |
| **regions**                 | Activated, conditional and prohibited regions.               |
| **response_authority**      | Maximum enabled level by environment.                        |
| **ai_use_cases**            | Approved profiles, data classes, tools and human review.     |
| **connectors**              | Approved categories/versions and action certification.       |
| **frameworks**              | Rights-safe identifiers and mapping versions.                |
| **experience_contracts**    | Required W IDs and states.                                   |
| **scale_envelope**          | R19 snapshot identifier.                                     |
| **slos**                    | Internal objective snapshot identifier.                      |
| **requirements_snapshot**   | R04 release query/version.                                   |
| **open_decisions**          | Conditional item, owner, deadline and default.               |
| **exclusions**              | Deferred/prohibited scope.                                   |
| **approvals**               | Named role and evidence reference.                           |
| **release_evidence**        | R20 package identifier.                                      |

# 22 \| Scope Change, ADR and Stop-Work Control

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image181.png" style="width:6.7in;height:2.56181in" alt="A source change is assessed, approved, republished and reconciled before implementation continues." />

*Figure 8 — Controlled release-scope change workflow.*

## 22.1 Change classes

| **Class**                                     | **Trigger**                                                                               | **Required control**                                                        |
|-----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **S0 — Clarification**                        | No behavioral, control, interface or acceptance change.                                   | Owner records clarification; no version change if non-normative.            |
| **S1 — Local compatible change**              | Behavior within an existing requirement and interface; no gate or cross-team effect.      | Requirement/test update and patch manifest version.                         |
| **S2 — Cross-workstream change**              | API/event/schema/dependency/experience impact.                                            | Architecture review, impact plan and minor manifest version.                |
| **S3 — Material architecture/control change** | Tenant, data, AI, evidence, response, cryptography, topology, region or SLO change.       | ADR, risk review, source-master/register update and major manifest version. |
| **S4 — Gate/market/offer change**             | Offer, sector pack, deployment tier, customer-data authorization or gate outcome changes. | Executive/product/security/legal approval; rebaseline release.              |
| **S5 — Emergency containment**                | Security or integrity risk requires immediate disablement.                                | Feature freeze/kill switch; retrospective controlled update and evidence.   |

## 22.2 Stop-work triggers

- Scope manifest is expired, superseded or REVIEW REQUIRED for the affected capability.

- Requirement, API, event, wireframe or source authority conflicts.

- Tenant isolation, data purpose, residency or source authority is ambiguous.

- AI tool, provider, memory or output authority exceeds D1–D4 approval.

- Response action lacks authority, attestation, approval, rollback or evidence contract.

- Evidence completeness or integrity behavior is undefined.

- Customer-specific request would create a fork or bypass the entitlement model.

- A conditional item is being treated as committed without unlock evidence.

- An exclusion or prohibited capability appears in an active sprint.

# 23 \| Release Exit Criteria and Gate Evidence

| **Evidence domain**        | **Required exit evidence**                                                                                                                 |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope control**          | Approved ERB-01 manifest; all committed requirements resolved; conditional/deferred/prohibited states reconciled.                          |
| **Architecture**           | Current ADRs; module boundaries; regional topology; data/event/API contracts; no unauthorized forks.                                       |
| **Tenancy and security**   | Cross-tenant negative tests pass; privileged paths bounded; secrets and workload identity controls pass.                                   |
| **Evidence**               | Synthetic and design-partner package verifies offline; witness consistency and restore reconciliation pass.                                |
| **Detection and response** | Point and selected windowed detections meet contract; replay deterministic; R1/simulation receipts complete.                               |
| **AI**                     | Approved provider/profile; grounding/adversarial tests pass; tool boundaries and deterministic fallback verified; disclosures implemented. |
| **Privacy and residency**  | Purpose, data classes, region routing, retention and access controls approved; customer data not used before G1.                           |
| **Experience**             | All G1-blocking experience contracts signed off in applicable seven states and accessibility tests.                                        |
| **Scale and reliability**  | ERB-01 envelope exercised; latency, acceptance, connector visibility, restore and cost telemetry measured.                                 |
| **Operations**             | Runbooks, on-call, support, service handoff, connector/evidence operations and incident paths rehearsed.                                   |
| **Exit and portability**   | Synthetic export, verifier, deletion workflow and legal-hold exception tested.                                                             |
| **Supply chain**           | Signed artifacts, SBOM, provenance, dependency policy and release approvals complete.                                                      |
| **Documentation**          | Admin, API, analyst, auditor and known-limitations material current.                                                                       |
| **Release evidence**       | R20 package binds source versions, manifest, tests, artifacts, deployment and approvals.                                                   |
| **Gate approval**          | CTO/Product/Architecture/Security/QA/SRE/Privacy/Service Operations accept G1 readiness.                                                   |

# 24 \| Risks, Assumptions, Constraints and Dependencies

| **Type**       | **Statement**                                                | **Control / owner response**                                                                  |
|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Risk**       | Dual-buyer scope becomes a “build everything” program.       | Independent landing with shared core; ERB-01 vertical slice; deferred list and capacity test. |
| **Risk**       | Design-partner customization creates forks.                  | Configuration model, anonymized profiles and architecture review trigger.                     |
| **Risk**       | Evidence moat delayed behind visible features.               | C7/C2/C3 first in build sequence; verifier is a G0/G1 gate.                                   |
| **Risk**       | AI assistant becomes unreviewed authority.                   | Gateway-only, citations, human decision, tool limits, fallback and D3 tests.                  |
| **Risk**       | Connector breadth overwhelms engineering.                    | P0 category cap; one certified EDR; BYO read-only; new connector requires scope change.       |
| **Risk**       | SOC/service operating needs arrive late.                     | Service Operations workstream from week one; runbook validation in integration checkpoints.   |
| **Risk**       | Telemetry economics invalidate GA.                           | R19 scale/cost telemetry in ERB-01; standalone SIEM deferred.                                 |
| **Assumption** | ZoikoID can meet the internal dependency SLA.                | Degraded read mode and fail-closed privileged paths; dependency tracked.                      |
| **Assumption** | Approved model providers support required region/data terms. | Provider-neutral gateway; deterministic fallback; conditional provider selection.             |
| **Constraint** | No sector-specific product fork.                             | Sector content and workflows remain governed pack configuration.                              |
| **Constraint** | No live R2+ in ERB-01.                                       | Broker interfaces disabled; security gate required.                                           |
| **Dependency** | Standards licensing and mapping review.                      | Core Assurance uses rights-safe identifiers/objectives; R14 controls versions.                |
| **Dependency** | Design-partner technical access and source permissions.      | Onboarding readiness checklist; no bypass of least privilege.                                 |
| **Dependency** | Managed infrastructure and analytics decisions.              | Defaults and deadlines in R02; vendor-neutral contracts.                                      |

# 25 \| Engineering Use, Authorization and Acknowledgment

## 25.1 What every assigned engineer receives

- The current release scope summary and manifest version.

- Assigned R04 requirements and acceptance criteria.

- Applicable architecture, domain, data, API, event and connector contracts.

- Applicable security, privacy, evidence, AI, response and failure-state controls.

- Assigned experience contracts and test obligations.

- Open decisions affecting the workstream and the rule for conditional work.

- Definition of ready, done and release evidence expectations.

## 25.2 What remains withheld by default

- Customer identities and pipeline.

- Price book, discount authority and margin model.

- Board financial, valuation and investment material.

- Unrelated future-sector strategy.

- Unrestricted red-team findings, production topology and cryptographic secret material.

- Negotiated legal positions and customer-specific incident evidence.

## 25.3 Required acknowledgment

| **Acknowledgment**      | **Required statement**                                                                        |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Current scope**       | I verified the release ID, version, state and source lineage before implementation.           |
| **Assignment**          | I will implement only the committed scope assigned to my workstream.                          |
| **Conditional work**    | I will not enable or represent conditional scope as delivered.                                |
| **Exclusions**          | I will not introduce a deferred, prohibited or customer-specific fork.                        |
| **Control obligations** | I understand applicable tenant, data, evidence, AI, security and response constraints.        |
| **Change**              | I will use the controlled change process rather than informal instructions.                   |
| **Stop-work**           | I will stop and escalate material ambiguity or conflict.                                      |
| **Confidentiality**     | I will use the information only through approved systems and for the assigned responsibility. |

# 26 \| Detailed Document Wireframe and Page Architecture

The final operational ZS-ENG-SCOPE-001 should render as approximately 32–42 controlled pages, excluding machine-generated register extracts and release evidence. The page architecture below is binding for authoring and review; exact pagination may vary without removing a required content block.

| **Page/block** | **Required content**                                                                    | **Review focus**                                      |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cover**      | Identity, title, release baseline, status, classification, authority, control sentence. | No commercial slogan or customer detail.              |
| **1–2**        | Document control, approvals, change record and source authority.                        | Current versions and decision owners.                 |
| **3**          | Executive mandate and release one-page.                                                 | Single-page usable build boundary.                    |
| **4–5**        | Critical review, scope principles and taxonomy.                                         | Why the boundary exists and how states work.          |
| **6–7**        | Release identity, gates, offers and market boundary.                                    | Regulated-first/high-assurance; independent landing.  |
| **8–10**       | End-to-end outcome, increments and capability matrix.                                   | Release-defining vertical slice.                      |
| **11–12**      | Conditional decisions, deferrals and prohibitions.                                      | No ambiguous backlog.                                 |
| **13–15**      | Runtime, regional, identity, data and evidence boundary.                                | Architecture without restricted exploit detail.       |
| **16–17**      | AI and response authority.                                                              | Permitted/prohibited uses and deterministic fallback. |
| **18**         | Connector/integration boundary.                                                         | P0 cap and certification.                             |
| **19–20**      | Experience contracts and mandatory states.                                              | G1 interface scope.                                   |
| **21–22**      | Nonfunctional objectives and scale envelope.                                            | Measurable engineering boundary.                      |
| **23–25**      | Workstreams, dependencies and integration checkpoints.                                  | One outcome; named ownership.                         |
| **26–27**      | Release manifest and traceability.                                                      | Machine-readable authority.                           |
| **28–29**      | Change, stop-work, exit evidence and gate.                                              | Fail-closed scope governance.                         |
| **30**         | RAID, engineering use and acknowledgment.                                               | Operational ownership.                                |
| **Annexes**    | Templates, matrices and approval records.                                               | Reusable controlled artifacts.                        |

## 26.1 Section opening pattern

- Objective and gate relevance.

- Authoritative sources and register snapshots.

- Committed, conditional and excluded scope.

- Owner and consuming workstreams.

- Required controls and failure behavior.

- Acceptance evidence and release blockers.

- Restricted annex reference, where applicable.

# 27 \| Visual Component and Controlled-Table Library

| **Component**                | **Required use**                                                                                            |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Release identity banner**  | Release ID, version, state, gate and effective date on every controlled release view.                       |
| **Scope-state badge**        | Text + icon + controlled color for COMMITTED, CONDITIONAL, DEFERRED, PROHIBITED, DELIVERED and WITHDRAWN.   |
| **Scope card**               | Capability, owner, state, requirements, dependencies, tests, gate and exclusions.                           |

| **Vertical-slice diagram**   | Inputs, state transitions, evidence outputs and acceptance endpoint.                                        |
| **Capability matrix**        | Domain × increment × offer × state, with no merged ambiguous cells.                                         |
| **Interface contract table** | Producer/consumer, authority, schema, security, error and version behavior.                                 |
| **Release objective table**  | Metric, measurement point, target, qualification and claim status.                                          |
| **Traceability strip**       | Requirement → work item → code → test → artifact → release evidence.                                        |
| **Risk/assumption card**     | Statement, impact, owner, trigger, response and expiry.                                                     |
| **Gate evidence checklist**  | Evidence owner, status, record ID, reviewer and blocking condition.                                         |
| **Restricted-detail marker** | Indicates that implementation detail is available only in an approved annex; main control remains complete. |
| **Change-impact panel**      | Old/new scope, affected requirements/interfaces/tests, decision and rollout action.                         |

## 27.1 Status treatment

| **State**           | **Visual and semantic treatment**                                        |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **COMMITTED**       | Green accent + check icon + “authorized for ERB-01 implementation.”      |
| **CONDITIONAL**     | Amber accent + dependency icon + decision and deadline.                  |
| **DEFERRED**        | Violet accent + target gate/unlock condition.                            |
| **PROHIBITED**      | Red accent + no-entry icon + approval level required to reconsider.      |
| **DELIVERED**       | Blue accent + acceptance-evidence ID; not synonymous with gate approved. |
| **WITHDRAWN**       | Strike/supersession treatment + impact-reconciliation record.            |
| **REVIEW REQUIRED** | Persistent red/amber banner; affected implementation paused.             |

| **ID**     | **Completion condition**                                                                  |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **DOD-01** | Document authority, release ID and owners approved.                                       |
| **DOD-02** | ERB-01 manifest is machine-readable and published.                                        |
| **DOD-03** | Every committed capability links to R04 and a workstream owner.                           |
| **DOD-04** | Conditional items name evidence, deadline, default and disabled behavior.                 |
| **DOD-05** | Deferred/prohibited scope is reconciled with active backlogs and repositories.            |
| **DOD-06** | Independent-offer and no-product-fork rules are reflected in domains and entitlements.    |
| **DOD-07** | Runtime, region, identity, data, evidence, AI and response boundaries are unambiguous.    |
| **DOD-08** | P0 connector set and certification boundary are approved.                                 |
| **DOD-09** | G1 experience contracts and state requirements are mapped.                                |
| **DOD-10** | Internal objectives and reference scale envelope are linked to R19.                       |
| **DOD-11** | Workstream scope cards, dependency map and integration checkpoints exist.                 |
| **DOD-12** | Change, stop-work and withdrawal workflows are operational.                               |
| **DOD-13** | Gate evidence checklist maps to R20.                                                      |
| **DOD-14** | Security, Privacy, AI Risk, QA, SRE and Service Operations approve applicable sections.   |
| **DOD-15** | Document contains no production secret, customer identity or unapproved licensed content. |
| **DOD-16** | Rendered Word document passes visual and accessibility review.                            |

# Annex A \| ERB-01 One-Page Release Scope

| **Scope dimension**   | **Controlled ERB-01 position**                                                                                                                                                              |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Mandate**           | Deliver a G1 design-partner vertical slice from onboarding and integration through detection/control evaluation, human-reviewed AI assistance, evidence, audit package and portable export. |
| **Offers**            | Managed Defense and Continuous Assurance independently landable.                                                                                                                            |
| **Architecture**      | shield-core + shield-ingest + shield-ai-gateway + shield-action-broker + shield-anchor.                                                                                                     |
| **Tenant/deployment** | T1 pooled regional cell; exact activated regions from R02/R09.                                                                                                                              |
| **Response**          | R0/R1 and simulation only.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **AI**                | Gateway-only assistive uses; citations, human review, deterministic fallback.                                                                                                               |
| **Connectors**        | Microsoft identity/productivity, one certified EDR, AWS/Azure, generic webhook/syslog, one ticketing and one vulnerability source.                                                          |
| **Assurance**         | Core Assurance Baseline; evidence ledger/verifier; control/evidence/audit-package flows.                                                                                                    |
| **Experience**        | All G1-blocking contracts W01–W18, W21–W28 and W33–W35.                                                                                                                                     |
| **Scale**             | 3–10 tenants; 2K–10K resources; 0.2–2 TB/day; 15K events/sec peak.                                                                                                                          |
| **Excluded**          | R2+, standalone SIEM, custom EDR, dedicated/sovereign, OT, customer AI-governance workspace, marketplace and mobile apps.                                                                   |
| **Exit**              | Offline-verifiable package, synthetic offboarding, current release evidence and recorded G1 decision.                                                                                       |

| **Primary register**          | R01 Document Estate, Ownership and Review Register                                                                                     |
| **Supporting registers**      | R02 ADR and Phase-Gate; R05 Risk and Exception; R15 AI Register; R18 Vendor/Subprocessor; R20 Release Evidence and Production Approval |
| **Applies to**                | Employees, contractors, consultants, vendors, SOC partners and engineering service providers                                           |
| **Gate relevance**            | G0-G4                                                                                                                                  |

# 02 \| Executive Control Summary

| **BINDING CONTROL OBJECTIVE**                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Protect ZoikoShield technical and commercial information without withholding any directly applicable requirement needed to build, test, secure, operate or recover the assigned component. |

| **Control area**                                 | **Decision**                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **What engineering receives**                    | Current requirements, interfaces, data rules, security constraints, evidence obligations, failure behavior, wireframes, tests, SLOs and approved ADRs for the assigned responsibility. |
| **What engineering does not receive by default** | Board strategy, customer identities, pipeline, price books, negotiation positions, compensation, unrestricted attack paths, production secrets or unrelated architecture.              |
| **How access is decided**                        | Intersection of role, workstream, sensitivity, environment, time, device posture, contract status and named approval.                                                                  |
| **How authority is preserved**                   | Every derivative carries source versions, register snapshots, ADR references, exclusions, approvers, checksum and expiration/review triggers.                                          |
| **How drift is prevented**                       | Source changes trigger impact assessment, derivative suspension where necessary, regeneration, recipient notice and release-impact review.                                             |
| **How misuse is contained**                      | DLP, download controls, audit logging, automatic expiry, JIT restricted access, incident response and verified offboarding.                                                            |
| **How engineering remains productive**           | Common baseline plus scoped delivery packs; no directly applicable technical constraint may be hidden behind confidentiality classification.                                           |

# 03 \| Purpose, Scope, Applicability and Exclusions

## 3.1 Purpose

Define the controlled architecture for deriving, approving, distributing, using, monitoring, changing, superseding and revoking ZoikoShield engineering information across a remote, multi-entity and mixed employee/contractor workforce.

## 3.2 In scope

- All controlled ZS-ENG documents and workstream delivery packs.

- Engineering-accessible views of masters, registers, ADRs, schemas, APIs, wireframes, threat mitigations and release evidence.

- Repository, identity, device, DLP, approval, acknowledgment, expiry, audit and offboarding controls.

- Use of controlled information in source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, collaboration, AI-assisted engineering and support workflows.

- Employees, contractors, consultants, engineering partners, SOC partners and approved subcontractors.

## 3.3 Out of scope

- Detailed feature architecture and implementation behavior, which are defined in ZS-ENG Documents 02-16.

- Production secrets, customer credentials and private keys, which remain in approved vaults and are never document content.

- Board, investment, pricing, customer-pipeline and legal-strategy materials unless an executive role explicitly requires them.

- General workforce productivity monitoring. This standard governs information security and accountable access only.

## 3.4 Normative language

| **Term**                | **Meaning**                                                                                 |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **MUST / MUST NOT**     | Mandatory control; deviation requires an approved exception unless explicitly non-waivable. |
| **SHOULD / SHOULD NOT** | Expected control; deviation requires documented rationale and owner approval.               |
| **MAY**                 | Permitted option within stated constraints.                                                 |
| **CONTROLLED**          | Approved, versioned, access-governed and auditable.                                         |
| **DERIVATIVE**          | A controlled extract that inherits authority and cannot override its source.                |
| **WORKSTREAM PACK**     | A time- and scope-bounded implementation package for an assigned team.                      |

# 04 \| Governing Principles and Non-Waivable Rules

| **Control ID** | **Principle**                       | **Binding consequence**                                                                                                                |
|----------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EDC-PR-001** | Authoritative source first          | No derivative may invent, weaken or silently reinterpret a master requirement, register value or approved ADR.                         |
| **EDC-PR-002** | Minimum complete disclosure         | Least privilege must not hide any directly applicable security, privacy, AI, evidence, failure-state, testing or rollback requirement. |
| **EDC-PR-003** | Need-to-know by intersection        | Seniority alone never grants platform-wide access.                                                                                     |
| **EDC-PR-004** | Individual accountability           | Shared identities, generic repository accounts and unattributed acknowledgments are prohibited.                                        |
| **EDC-PR-005** | No secrets in documents             | Credentials, tokens, private keys, recovery codes and customer secrets remain in approved secret systems.                              |
| **EDC-PR-006** | Technical enforcement               | Material handling requirements must be technically enforced where reasonably possible and otherwise have a named manual control owner. |
| **EDC-PR-007** | Visible health state                | Draft, active, overdue, suspended, superseded, withdrawn and archived states must be machine-readable and visually unmistakable.       |
| **EDC-PR-008** | Stop on conflict                    | Engineers do not choose between conflicting authorities; affected implementation stops until resolved.                                 |
| **EDC-PR-009** | Segregation of duties               | No person independently controls specification, implementation approval and production promotion for a material change.                |
| **EDC-PR-010** | Time-bound access                   | Access ends automatically when role, assignment, device compliance, contract or approved duration ends.                                |
| **EDC-PR-011** | Lawful and proportionate monitoring | Access monitoring is disclosed, purpose-limited, retained only as required and never converted into covert productivity surveillance.  |
| **EDC-PR-012** | Evidence of operation               | Access, approval, publication, acknowledgment, review, exception, incident and revocation events produce auditable records.            |

| **NON-WAIVABLE CONTROLS**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| No exception is permitted for shared identities; secrets embedded in controlled documents; unlogged break-glass access; use of public/unapproved AI tools with confidential content; bypass of tenant-isolation requirements; or use of a superseded/withdrawn specification for production authorization. |

# 05 \| Information Object Model and Source-of-Truth Hierarchy

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image182.png" style="width:6.75in;height:2.62292in" alt="Diagram showing controlled masters, living registers and ADRs feeding engineering derivatives and workstream packs." />

*Figure 1. Controlled authority hierarchy.*

| **Object**                   | **Purpose**                                                                                                       | **Authority rule**                                                   |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Controlled master**        | Normative policy, architecture, product, security, operations or assurance authority.                             | May only be changed by its named owner and approval route.           |
| **Living register**          | Machine-readable current state such as ADR, requirement, schema, model, connector, SLO, risk or release evidence. | Register value prevails over a stale prose copy.                     |
| **Approved ADR**             | Binding decision with context, consequences, owner and supersession.                                              | Must be referenced by affected derivative and implementation.        |
| **ZS-ENG derivative**        | Curated engineering standard or specification derived from controlled sources.                                    | Cannot override source; invalidated by material source mismatch.     |
| **Restricted annex**         | Segregated technical detail such as attack paths, key hierarchy or production topology.                           | Named JIT access; main document retains full mitigation requirement. |
| **Workstream delivery pack** | Assigned release/workstream extract including requirements, interfaces, tests and wireframes.                     | Expires with assignment/release; no broader authority.               |
| **Record / evidence**        | Proof that a control, review, test, approval or action occurred.                                                  | Immutable or reconstructable; retained by policy.                    |

## 5.1 Conflict precedence

131. Applicable law, contract and approved regulatory obligation.

132. Current controlled master document.

133. Current living register value.

134. Approved ADR specific to the decision.

135. Current ZS-ENG derivative.

136. Current workstream delivery pack.

137. Issue tracker, meeting note, email or chat instruction.

| **CONFLICT RULE**                                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Lower-level content never silently overrides higher authority. A conflict creates a stop-work record, not an informal interpretation. |

# 06 \| Detailed Document Wireframe and Page Architecture

The final operational standard should render as a 32-40 page controlled document, excluding machine-generated recipient and access records. The page map below is binding for authorship unless an approved layout change preserves every content block.

| **Page range** | **Content block**                        | **Mandatory content**                                                                      |
|----------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1**          | Controlled cover                         | Brand, title, ID, version, state, authority, classification, governing premise.            |
| **2**          | Document control                         | Owners, approvers, sources, review cadence, gate relevance.                                |
| **3**          | Approval and change record               | Approval signatures/evidence references; version history.                                  |
| **4**          | Controlled contents                      | Static, internally linked contents generated from heading structure.                       |
| **5-6**        | Critical review and executive decision   | Findings, refined decisions, approval position.                                            |
| **7-8**        | Purpose, scope and principles            | Applicability, exclusions, normative language, non-waivable rules.                         |
| **9-10**       | Authority and object model               | Source hierarchy, conflict precedence, derivative classes.                                 |
| **11-13**      | Classification and access architecture   | Sensitivity classes, need-to-know dimensions, role/workstream bundles.                     |
| **14-16**      | Repository and tooling architecture      | Logical repositories, capability requirements, integrations and evidence.                  |
| **17-19**      | Derivation, publication and distribution | Source manifests, completeness review, approval, checksum, acknowledgment.                 |
| **20-22**      | Access lifecycle and handling            | Request, approval, provisioning, recertification, remote controls and prohibited channels. |
| **23-24**      | Restricted annexes and AI tools          | Segmentation, JIT, AI-assisted engineering, external service controls.                     |
| **25-27**      | Lifecycle, conflicts and exceptions      | Health states, source-change triggers, stop-work, break-glass and risk acceptance.         |
| **28-30**      | Monitoring, incidents and offboarding    | Metrics, control tests, misuse response, contractor chain and revocation.                  |
| **31-32**      | Records, SDLC and implementation         | Retention, legal hold, release integration, RACI and rollout.                              |
| **33-40**      | Controlled annexes                       | Matrices, schemas, request/acknowledgment/conflict/exception/review/offboarding templates. |

# 07 \| Information Classification and Handling Model

| **Class** | **Name**                   | **Typical content**                                                                                         | **Default audience**                     | **Default handling**                                                  |
|-----------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EC-0**  | Public / approved external | Published developer documentation, public schemas, approved security summaries.                             | Public channels after claim approval.    | No internal annotations or unpublished roadmap.                       |
| **EC-1**  | Engineering General        | Coding standards, approved general architecture principles, common runbooks, non-sensitive schemas.         | Authorized engineering workforce.        | External sharing prohibited unless separately approved.               |
| **EC-2**  | Engineering Controlled     | Requirements, internal APIs, data models, wireframes, test plans, non-production topology.                  | Assigned workstreams and approved leads. | Managed identity; acknowledgment; controlled download.                |
| **EC-3**  | Engineering Restricted     | Crown-jewel threats, cryptographic internals, red-team details, production topology, privileged procedures. | Named specialists only; JIT/time-bound.  | Managed device; no offline copy by default; enhanced logging and DLP. |
| **EC-4**  | Executive Restricted       | Customer identities, pipeline, pricing, Board finance, legal strategy, acquisitions.                        | Executive/Legal/Commercial roles.        | Not a normal engineering entitlement.                                 |

## 7.1 Mandatory classification metadata

- Class and rationale.

- Allowed roles and workstreams.

- Prohibited recipients and external-sharing rule.

- Device and geographic requirements.

- Download, print, screenshot and offline-copy permissions.

- Access duration and recertification cadence.

- Owner, reviewer and escalation route.

- Retention and legal-hold treatment.

## 7.2 Minimum complete disclosure test

| **Test area**        | **Approval question**                                                                                                    |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope**            | Does the recipient understand the exact component, release, tenant/region context and explicit exclusions?               |
| **Interfaces**       | Are applicable APIs, events, data contracts, dependencies and version rules present?                                     |
| **Security**         | Are all directly applicable authentication, authorization, isolation, cryptographic and secure-failure controls present? |
| **Privacy and data** | Are purpose, classification, residency, minimization, retention, deletion and test-data rules present?                   |
| **AI**               | Are gateway, model/provider, data, tool, human-oversight, injection and fallback rules present?                          |
| **Evidence**         | Are required audit events, evidence objects, provenance, integrity and retention rules present?                          |
| **Failure behavior** | Are partial, stale, unauthorized, degraded, error and recovery states defined?                                           |
| **Quality**          | Are acceptance criteria, negative tests, performance targets and release blockers present?                               |
| **Operations**       | Are observability, rollback, support, runbook and escalation requirements present?                                       |

# 08 \| Need-to-Know and Role-Based Access Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image183.png" style="width:6.75in;height:2.62292in" alt="Diagram of role, workstream, classification, environment, time and device posture intersecting to grant access." />

*Figure 2. Access decision model.*

| **ACCESS FORMULA**                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ACCESS = approved role x assigned workstream x information class x environment need x time window x compliant device/location x valid contract/status. Any failed term denies or narrows access. |

| **Level** | **Role class**                           | **Permitted scope**                                                       | **Constraint**                                               |
|-----------|------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EL-1**  | Authorized engineer                      | Assigned requirements, interfaces, wireframes, tests and common controls. | No platform-wide access; no EC-3 by default.                 |
| **EL-2**  | Engineering lead / architect             | Cross-domain dependencies, technical ADRs, broader non-production design. | Does not automatically grant EC-3 or production access.      |
| **EL-3**  | Restricted security / AI assurance / SRE | Named EC-3 materials required for operational responsibility.             | JIT/time-bound; enhanced evidence; periodic recertification. |
| **EL-4**  | Executive / Legal / Commercial           | EC-4 materials based on corporate role.                                   | Not inherited through engineering seniority.                 |

| **EB-AI**         | AI systems and assurance | Gateway, retrieval, agents, tools, memory, evaluations, red team, drift and kill switches.              |
| **EB-EXPERIENCE** | Front-end and design     | Experience contracts, state patterns, accessibility, evidence drill-down and disclosure.                |
| **EB-PLATFORM**   | Platform / SRE           | Infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, recovery, capacity and controlled production operations.          |
| **EB-QA**         | Quality engineering      | Requirements traceability, test suites, negative controls, release evidence and defect gates.           |

|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
