# 10 \| Derivation, Validation and Publication Architecture

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image185.png" style="width:6.75in;height:2.62292in" alt="Flow from controlled sources through extraction, validation, approval, publication, acknowledgment and use." />

*Figure 4. Controlled derivative publication flow.*

## 10.1 Mandatory derivation manifest

| **Metadata field**              | **Required content**                                                 |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **derivative_id**               | Unique ZS-ENG identifier.                                            |
| **title**                       | Approved title.                                                      |
| **version / state**             | Current controlled version and health state.                         |
| **parent_documents**            | Exact IDs and source versions.                                       |
| **source_register_snapshots**   | Register identifiers and snapshot timestamps/versions.               |
| **applicable_adrs**             | Approved ADRs governing the extract.                                 |
| **release / workstream scope**  | Exact implementation boundary.                                       |
| **extract_owner**               | Accountable person for completeness and correctness.                 |
| **exclusions**                  | Information intentionally omitted and why.                           |
| **restricted_annexes**          | Annex IDs and access level.                                          |
| **validation**                  | Product/architecture/security/privacy/AI/QA reviewers as applicable. |
| **checksum**                    | SHA-256 or repository-native immutable version reference.            |
| **effective / review / expiry** | Dates and event triggers.                                            |
| **recipient policy**            | Allowed roles, bundles and acknowledgment requirement.               |

## 10.2 Source change impact classes

| **Class**               | **Definition**                                                                                                       | **Required response**                                                                                                     |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **S0 Editorial**        | No requirement, interface, control or meaning change.                                                                | Derivative remains active; metadata update at next release.                                                               |
| **S1 Minor controlled** | Clarification or additive detail with no breaking behavior.                                                          | Notify owner; update within five business days; assess open work.                                                         |
| **S2 Material**         | Requirement, schema, access, security, data, AI, SLO or test change.                                                 | Mark derivative UNDER REVIEW; block affected release until updated/accepted.                                              |
| **S3 Critical**         | Tenant isolation, evidence integrity, privileged action, privacy, cryptography, active exploit or legal prohibition. | Suspend affected derivative immediately; notify recipients; stop affected work and release; regenerate before resumption. |

## 10.3 Publication package

- Controlled DOCX or repository-native editable source.

- Controlled PDF/HTML read view where required.

- Machine-readable metadata (YAML/JSON).

- Derivation manifest and checksum/version reference.

- Approval evidence and distribution manifest.

- Restricted annex links, never embedded where access classes differ.

- Supersession notice for prior versions.

- Applicable release and requirement links.

# 11 \| Access Request, Approval, Provisioning and Recertification

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image186.png" style="width:6.75in;height:2.62292in" alt="Diagram showing requested, approved, provisioned, active, reviewed, expired and revoked access states." />

*Figure 5. Access lifecycle and recertification.*

| **Request field**       | **Required detail**                                                                   |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**            | Name, corporate identity, legal entity, employment/contract status and sponsor.       |
| **Role and workstream** | Current role, assigned team, component and release.                                   |
| **Requested objects**   | Document, chapter, annex, register view or bundle.                                    |
| **Class / environment** | Requested information class and environment relevance.                                |
| **Justification**       | Specific engineering task and why existing access is insufficient.                    |
| **Duration**            | Start, expiry and renewal condition.                                                  |
| **Control readiness**   | MFA, device compliance, training, confidentiality/IP status and location eligibility. |
| **Approvals**           | Manager, owner, Security/Legal/Executive as required.                                 |
| **Conflict check**      | SoD and prior entitlement conflicts.                                                  |
| **Evidence reference**  | Ticket/approval ID and provisioned policy result.                                     |

## 11.1 Approval authority

| **Scope**            | **Minimum approval**                                                                       |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EC-0 / EC-1**      | Engineering manager or automated role policy where approved.                               |
| **EC-2**             | Engineering manager plus document/technical owner.                                         |
| **EC-3**             | Document owner plus Security and accountable executive delegate; self-approval prohibited. |
| **Break-glass EC-3** | Incident commander or delegated executive plus Security; auto-expiry and post-use review.  |
| **EC-4**             | Executive owner and Legal/Commercial owner as applicable.                                  |

## 11.2 Provisioning verification

- Policy grants only approved repository objects, not broad inherited groups.

- Expiry is set at provisioning time.

- Device, location and MFA conditions are evaluated before access.

- Recipient acknowledgment is required before EC-2/EC-3 use.

- Provisioning result is independently reconciled to the approved request.

- Failed or excessive grants are automatically revoked and investigated.

# 12 \| Distribution, Handling and Remote-Team Controls

| **Control ID**  | **Rule**                     | **Requirement**                                                                                                                             |
|-----------------|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EDC-HND-001** | Approved channels only       | Controlled content is accessed through approved repositories; external email, personal cloud storage and consumer messaging are prohibited. |
| **EDC-HND-002** | No shared accounts           | All access, review and acknowledgment events are individually attributable.                                                                 |
| **EDC-HND-003** | No secrets or customer data  | Documents and issue trackers reference vault objects or synthetic datasets; they do not contain live secrets or unnecessary customer data.  |
| **EDC-HND-004** | Local copy control           | EC-2 local copies require encrypted managed workspace and expiry; EC-3 offline copies are prohibited by default.                            |
| **EDC-HND-005** | Print/screenshot control     | Printing disabled by default for EC-2/3; EC-3 screenshots prohibited unless approved for an incident or evidence purpose.                   |
| **EDC-HND-006** | Meeting controls             | Unapproved recording, transcription and meeting-assistant services may not process controlled content.                                      |
| **EDC-HND-007** | External collaboration       | Vendor or partner sharing requires approved recipient entity, DPA/confidentiality terms, scoped access and expiry.                          |
| **EDC-HND-008** | Current-version verification | Recipients must use active navigation; downloaded copies do not establish authority.                                                        |

## 12.1 Remote access baseline

| **Area**           | **Baseline**                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity**       | Company-approved identity and phishing-resistant MFA for EC-2/3.                                                                    |
| **Device**         | Managed or explicitly approved device; disk encryption; supported OS; current patches; endpoint security; automatic lock.           |
| **Administration** | Restricted local administrator rights; no shared/family device use; no unmanaged browser profiles for EC-3.                         |
| **Network**        | Approved secure access path where required; no access from prohibited jurisdictions or anonymizing infrastructure without approval. |
| **Workspace**      | Reasonable visual/privacy controls for EC-3; no public/shared-space display of restricted material.                                 |
| **Data**           | No production customer data in local environments; synthetic or approved anonymized data only.                                      |
| **Reporting**      | Immediate report of device loss, suspicious access, accidental sharing or policy bypass.                                            |
| **Contractors**    | Sponsor, legal entity and contract-end date mandatory; access automatically expires; subcontracting requires prior approval.        |

## 12.2 Monitoring safeguards

| **WORKFORCE SAFEGUARD**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Monitoring is limited to access security, document control, system integrity and incident response. It must be disclosed, proportionate, purpose-limited, retained under policy and reviewed for local legal requirements. Keystroke, screenshot, webcam or covert productivity surveillance is outside this standard and prohibited unless separately lawful, necessary and explicitly approved. |

# 13 \| Restricted Annex and Content-Segmentation Model

| **Content object**               | **Contains**                                                                                                      | **Audience**                       |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Main engineering document**    | Required behavior, invariant, interface, error handling, evidence, acceptance test and operational constraint.    | All assigned implementers.         |
| **Restricted technical annex**   | Precise attack path, exploit detail, key hierarchy, production topology, red-team finding or emergency procedure. | Named EL-3 recipients only.        |
| **Role-filtered register view**  | Only relevant rows/fields from risk, connector, AI, vendor or SLO register.                                       | Approved workstream roles.         |
| **Redacted finding brief**       | Risk, affected component, mitigation, test and severity without exploit chain or sensitive customer context.      | Assigned remediation team.         |
| **Time-limited incident packet** | Specific evidence and procedures required for an active incident.                                                 | Incident team; break-glass expiry. |

## 13.1 Restricted annex rules

- Every annex has a separate ID, owner, classification, access list, expiry and checksum.

- The main document must still provide the complete mitigation and acceptance criteria.

- Annex access is not inherited from access to the parent document.

- Copy/paste and download restrictions apply independently.

- Access events and exports are logged and reviewed.

- Annex withdrawal does not remove the implementation requirement unless the source authority changes.

# 14 \| AI-Assisted Engineering and External Tool Controls

| **Control ID** | **Rule**                            | **Mandatory behavior**                                                                                                                |
|----------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EDC-AI-001** | Approved services only              | Only providers and workspaces approved in R15/R18 may process ZoikoShield controlled information.                                     |
| **EDC-AI-002** | Data-class policy                   | EC-3/EC-4 and customer data are prohibited unless the specific provider, use case, region and contract are explicitly approved.       |
| **EDC-AI-003** | No training use                     | Approved contracts must prohibit provider training on submitted ZoikoShield content unless separately authorized.                     |
| **EDC-AI-004** | No direct authority                 | AI output does not approve requirements, security exceptions, releases, access or production actions.                                 |
| **EDC-AI-005** | Human verification                  | Generated code, tests, summaries and documentation undergo normal review, security scanning, license checks and acceptance testing.   |
| **EDC-AI-006** | Prompt-injection awareness          | Repository content, logs, tickets and documentation are attacker-controlled inputs; agents/tools must be allowlisted and scope-bound. |
| **EDC-AI-007** | Provenance                          | Material generated artifacts identify tool/model use where required and retain review evidence.                                       |
| **EDC-AI-008** | Secret and customer-data prevention | DLP and pre-submit controls block secrets and prohibited data from prompts.                                                           |
| **EDC-AI-009** | Meeting assistants                  | Transcription and note-taking bots require approved provider, participant notice, retention and data-class eligibility.               |
| **EDC-AI-010** | Kill switch                         | Security may immediately disable a provider, extension or agent when risk, provider change or incident requires it.                   |

## 14.1 Engineering assistant decision table

| **Content**         | **Default AI use**                          | **Required control**                                                         |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EC-0 public**     | Permitted with approved tools.              | Normal review and license checks.                                            |
| **EC-1 general**    | Permitted in approved enterprise workspace. | No secrets/customer data; provider no-training terms.                        |
| **EC-2 controlled** | Case-by-case approved workspace/use case.   | DLP, region/provider eligibility, prompt/output governance and human review. |
| **EC-3 restricted** | Prohibited by default.                      | Explicit Security + owner approval and isolated provider configuration.      |
| **EC-4 executive**  | Prohibited for engineering assistants.      | Executive/Legal-approved use case only.                                      |

# 15 \| Document Lifecycle, Health, Review and Supersession

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image187.png" style="width:6.75in;height:2.62292in" alt="Diagram showing draft, review, active, under-review, overdue, superseded, withdrawn and archived states." />

*Figure 6. Engineering document health-state model.*

| **State**        | **Meaning**                                              | **Required treatment**                                        |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| **DRAFT**        | Not valid for implementation.                            | Draft banner; limited review access.                          |
| **IN REVIEW**    | Controlled comments; not yet valid.                      | Reviewer list and decision deadline.                          |
| **ACTIVE**       | Approved and effective.                                  | Current version in active navigation.                         |
| **UNDER REVIEW** | Still valid unless specifically suspended.               | Review reason and target date visible.                        |
| **OVERDUE**      | Review date missed; controlled defect.                   | Owner escalation and release impact assessment.               |
| **SUSPENDED**    | Temporarily invalid for affected use.                    | Stop-work scope, interim control and resolution owner.        |
| **SUPERSEDED**   | Replaced by a newer active version.                      | Archive only; active navigation removed; recipients notified. |
| **WITHDRAWN**    | Invalid due to risk, error, legal or authority decision. | Access blocked except archive/incident roles.                 |
| **ARCHIVED**     | Historical record only.                                  | Read-only retention and legal hold support.                   |

## 15.1 Review triggers

- Parent master, register or ADR changes.

- New product phase, jurisdiction, provider, model, data class or response authority.

- Material incident, vulnerability, red-team finding or audit finding.

- Repository, identity, DLP, device, offboarding or monitoring control change.

- Applicable law, contract, workforce policy or vendor term change.

- Scheduled review date or persistent metrics breach.

## 15.2 Supersession controls

138. Approve the replacement version and record checksum/version reference.

139. Mark prior version SUPERSEDED and remove it from active navigation.

140. Notify active recipients and owners of open work.

141. Compare changed control IDs and create required implementation tasks.

142. Assess in-flight releases and production behavior.

143. Revoke or expire restricted annex links where changed.

144. Retain prior version read-only for audit and legal hold.

# 16 \| Conflict, Stop-Work, Break-Glass and Exception Controls

## 16.1 Stop-work triggers

| **Trigger**               | **Condition**                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authority conflict**    | Two controlled sources or a derivative and register disagree.                                                 |
| **Missing requirement**   | Security, privacy, AI, evidence, failure or test behavior required for implementation is absent or ambiguous. |
| **Prohibited data flow**  | Implementation appears to require disallowed region, provider, storage or customer-data handling.             |
| **Isolation uncertainty** | Tenant, environment, identity or authorization boundary is unclear.                                           |
| **Privileged action gap** | Material response or administrative action lacks authority, approval, receipt or rollback.                    |
| **Document health**       | Governing document is suspended, withdrawn, materially overdue or source-mismatched.                          |
| **Control infeasibility** | A mandatory control cannot be implemented or tested as specified.                                             |

## 16.2 Conflict record fields

- Conflicting IDs, versions and exact clauses.

- Affected component, release, tenant/region and work items.

- Security, privacy, evidence, AI, commercial and customer impact.

- Interim containment and work paused.

- Decision owner, approvers and deadline.

- Resolution, source updates, tests and release evidence.

## 16.3 Break-glass access

| **Control**      | **Requirement**                                                                         |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Trigger**      | Active incident, outage, recovery or time-critical investigation with no standard path. |
| **Approval**     | Incident commander or delegated executive plus Security; no self-approval.              |
| **Scope**        | Minimum objects and duration; default maximum 4 hours.                                  |
| **Evidence**     | Incident ID, reason, grant, access events, exports, actions and revocation.             |
| **Restrictions** | No broad group grant; no unlogged local copy; no onward sharing.                        |
| **Review**       | Post-use review within one business day; corrective action for any control gap.         |

## 16.4 Exception architecture

| **Field**                 | **Required content**                                            |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope**                 | Specific control ID, component, release and duration.           |
| **Risk**                  | Threat, likelihood, impact and affected customers/obligations.  |
| **Compensating controls** | Measurable temporary safeguards.                                |
| **Owner**                 | Named accountable owner.                                        |
| **Approvals**             | Correct authority; requester cannot self-approve.               |
| **Expiry**                | Automatic expiration and pre-expiry escalation.                 |
| **Evidence**              | Linked tests, monitoring and release visibility.                |
| **Closure**               | Control restored, exception withdrawn or new approved decision. |

# 17 \| Monitoring, Evidence, Metrics and Control Tests

| **Metric**                                                         | **Threshold**          | **Measurement**                           |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **Shared engineering identities**                                  | 0                      | Continuous identity audit.                |
| **EC-3 access with named owner and expiry**                        | 100%                   | Daily reconciliation.                     |
| **Contractor access with automatic contract-end expiry**           | 100%                   | Daily joiner/mover/leaver reconciliation. |
| **EC-2/3 recipients acknowledging before first use**               | 100%                   | Per publication.                          |
| **Active navigation pointing to current version**                  | 100%                   | Automated per release.                    |
| **Secrets detected in controlled documents**                       | 0                      | Pre-publication and continuous scanning.  |
| **Superseded active copies accessible through primary navigation** | 0                      | Daily check.                              |
| **Material source mismatch unresolved at release**                 | 0                      | Release gate.                             |
| **Access reviews completed by due date**                           | \>= 99%; 100% for EC-3 | Monthly/quarterly.                        |
| **High-risk offboarding completed within target**                  | 100%                   | Per event.                                |
| **Unapproved external-sharing attempts**                           | 100% investigated      | Continuous DLP alert review.              |
| **Break-glass sessions reviewed within one business day**          | 100%                   | Per incident.                             |

## 17.1 Mandatory recurring control tests

| **Test** | **Name**                   | **Expected result**                                                                  |
|----------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **T-01** | Source mismatch test       | Change a test source version and verify derivative warning/suspension.               |
| **T-02** | Access expiry test         | Verify contractor and JIT access automatically expires.                              |
| **T-03** | Offboarding test           | Synthetic leaver loses documents, code, CI/CD, cloud and vault access within target. |
| **T-04** | External sharing block     | Attempt prohibited share/download/print route and verify block/evidence.             |
| **T-05** | Restricted annex isolation | Verify parent-document users cannot access annex without separate approval.          |
| **T-06** | Break-glass test           | Exercise grant, logging, expiry, revocation and post-review.                         |
| **T-07** | AI DLP test                | Attempt prohibited secret/customer-data prompt in approved and unapproved tools.     |
| **T-08** | Audit-log export/restore   | Export evidence, validate integrity and restore access history.                      |
| **T-09** | Supersession test          | Publish replacement and verify old version removal, notification and work impact.    |
| **T-10** | Minimum-disclosure review  | Sample workstream pack against completeness checklist and build tasks.               |

# 18 \| Information Misuse and Security Incident Response

| **Stage**     | **Mandatory action**                                                                                                                                        |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Report**    | Unauthorized access, accidental forwarding, lost device, suspicious export, public AI use, customer data exposure, access after role end or bypass attempt. |
| **Contain**   | Suspend access, revoke sessions/tokens, block sharing, isolate device or disable provider/integration.                                                      |
| **Preserve**  | Retain repository, IAM, DLP, endpoint, ticket, AI-gateway and communication evidence.                                                                       |
| **Assess**    | Classify information, recipients, geography, customer/contract impact and exploitation risk.                                                                |
| **Notify**    | Security, document owner, Legal/Privacy, People and affected customer/regulator owners as required.                                                         |
| **Remediate** | Recover or delete copies where lawful, rotate secrets if exposed, correct access policy and update controls.                                                |
| **Review**    | Root cause, control failure, disciplinary/process separation, lessons learned and CAPA.                                                                     |
| **Close**     | Evidence complete; access restored or terminated; claims/notifications reconciled.                                                                          |

| **FAIR PROCESS**                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| The control system records objective access and handling events. It must not presume malicious intent. Security containment, factual investigation, employment decisions and legal conclusions remain separate governed processes. |

# 19 \| Role Change, Contractor Chain and Offboarding

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image188.png" style="width:6.75in;height:2.62292in" alt="Diagram of trigger, identity, access, assets, ownership, verification and closure." />

*Figure 7. Role change and offboarding control chain.*

| **Trigger**                   | **Required control**                                                                                                                                |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **High-risk / involuntary**   | Immediately revoke EC-3, privileged, production, vault and active sessions; complete remaining access removal within the approved emergency target. |
| **Normal termination**        | Remove all access by end of final working period; pre-stage ownership transfer and session/token revocation.                                        |
| **Role or workstream change** | Recalculate access intersection; remove prior bundles before adding new ones where SoD risk exists.                                                 |
| **Contractor end**            | Automatic expiry from authoritative contract date; sponsor certifies extension before renewal.                                                      |
| **Subcontractor**             | Prime supplier remains accountable; no downstream access without prior identity, contract and security approval.                                    |
| **Leave / suspension**        | Suspend or narrow access based on risk and business need; retain evidence and avoid unnecessary personal-data processing.                           |

## 19.1 Closure checklist

- Identity, sessions, tokens and MFA factors resolved.

- Document, code, issue tracker, CI/CD, cloud, database, observability and vault access removed.

- Managed device returned, locked or securely wiped under policy.

- Local controlled copies and offline exports addressed where technically and legally possible.

- Open approvals, incidents, risks, documents and work items reassigned.

- Customer/partner delegated access removed.

- Final access reconciliation and closure evidence stored.

- Continuing confidentiality and IP obligations restated.

# 20 \| Records, Retention, Legal Hold and Privacy

| **Record**                                  | **Retention rule**                                                              |
|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Approved document versions**              | Per document/assurance retention schedule; historical versions read-only.       |
| **Derivation manifests and checksums**      | At least for the life of the affected product/release plus assurance retention. |
| **Distribution and acknowledgment records** | Per employment/contract, security and audit requirements.                       |
| **Access requests, approvals and reviews**  | Per security and compliance schedule; restricted to control roles.              |
| **Repository and DLP logs**                 | Purpose-limited retention aligned to threat detection and legal obligations.    |
| **Exceptions and risk acceptance**          | Through expiry/closure plus required assurance period.                          |
| **Incidents and investigations**            | Per incident, legal, insurer, regulator and litigation-hold requirements.       |
| **Offboarding evidence**                    | Per employment/contract and security-control retention.                         |
| **AI tool use evidence**                    | Per approved AI use case, provider terms and data-governance policy.            |

## 20.1 Privacy requirements

- Collect only identity, role, access, device-compliance and event data necessary for the stated control purpose.

- Disclose monitoring and retention in appropriate workforce/contractor notices.

- Restrict investigation data to authorized Security, Legal and People roles.

- Apply regional storage and transfer rules before centralizing logs.

- Support correction, access and deletion rights where applicable, subject to security records and legal hold.

- Do not repurpose access telemetry into performance scoring without a separately approved lawful process.

# 21 \| SDLC, Change and Release-Gate Integration

| **Lifecycle point**        | **Required document-control evidence**                                                         |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Requirement assignment** | R04 requirement ID; current derivative/workstream-pack version; owner and acceptance criteria. |
| **Design review**          | Applicable architecture, security, data, AI, evidence and experience controls referenced.      |
| **Implementation**         | Code/branch/issue linked to requirement and ADR IDs; no secrets or shadow specifications.      |
| **Peer review**            | Reviewer verifies current document version and directly applicable control IDs.                |
| **CI/CD**                  | Tests, scans, policy checks, SBOM/provenance and document/version metadata captured.           |
| **Release review**         | R20 includes requirements, document versions, tests, exceptions, rollback and approvers.       |
| **Production change**      | SoD enforced; current operational runbook and access entitlement verified.                     |
| **Post-release**           | Monitoring, incidents, drift and source changes feed back into registers and derivatives.      |

| **RELEASE BLOCKER**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A release is blocked when a material requirement is linked to an expired, suspended, withdrawn or source-mismatched engineering document; when required EC-3 review is missing; or when the release evidence cannot identify the exact controlled versions used. |

## 22.1 Rollout phases

| **Phase**                         | **Scope**                                                                                                     | **Exit condition**                                                 |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Phase 0 - Decisions**           | Close repository, identity, device, DLP, monitoring, retention, JIT and offboarding ADRs.                     | All owners named; residual risks recorded.                         |
| **Phase 1 - Control-plane pilot** | Implement four repositories, metadata, active-version navigation, SSO/MFA, access workflows and audit export. | Pilot with one engineering workstream and synthetic content.       |
| **Phase 2 - Engineering rollout** | Migrate current derivatives, create access bundles, train recipients and activate acknowledgments/expiry.     | 100% active engineering work uses controlled packs.                |
| **Phase 3 - Restricted controls** | Enable EC-3 JIT, DLP, watermarking, break-glass and advanced offboarding.                                     | Security tests pass; no broad EC-3 groups remain.                  |
| **Phase 4 - Assurance**           | Automate source mismatch, recertification, metrics, control tests and R20 linkage.                            | Quarterly control review and independent audit evidence available. |

## 23.1 Metadata validation rules

- No publication without exact parent versions and source register references.

- No ACTIVE state without complete approval evidence and checksum/version reference.

- No EC-3 access without allowed roles, expiry and separate annex metadata.

- No release use after next review date without a recorded validity decision.

- Any parent version mismatch emits a controlled health event and impact assessment.

# 24 \| Definition of Done and Approval Gate

| **Gate area**     | **Approval condition**                                                                                                       |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Authority**     | Derivative class, parent authority, owners, approvers and register relationships approved.                                   |
| **Content**       | All sections and annex specifications present; stable control IDs assigned.                                                  |
| **Repository**    | Selected platform demonstrably supports required identity, access, version, expiry, DLP, audit and legal-hold controls.      |
| **Identity**      | SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, lifecycle integration, JIT and session revocation tested.                                       |
| **Segmentation**  | Chapter/annex access and workstream-filtered register views tested.                                                          |
| **Derivation**    | Source manifest, checksum, source-change impact and regeneration workflow tested.                                            |
| **Handling**      | Download, print, screenshot, external share and prohibited-channel controls validated.                                       |
| **AI**            | Approved tool policy, data-class enforcement, DLP and provider kill switch validated.                                        |
| **Remote work**   | Device posture and contractor expiry controls operational.                                                                   |
| **Monitoring**    | Workforce notice, purpose limitation, retention and local legal review complete.                                             |
| **Operations**    | Access requests, recertification, break-glass, conflict, exception, incident and offboarding workflows operational.          |
| **Assurance**     | Metrics collected; mandatory control tests pass; evidence exportable to R20.                                                 |
| **Usability**     | Engineering pilot confirms controls do not prevent legitimate build activity and directly applicable truth remains complete. |
| **Residual risk** | All unresolved gaps recorded in R05 with owner, treatment and expiry.                                                        |

## 24.1 Decisions required before operational approval

| **Decision**   | **Required closure**                                                  |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **ADR-GOV-01** | Controlled repository platform and data region.                       |
| **ADR-GOV-02** | Identity, SCIM and phishing-resistant MFA enforcement.                |
| **ADR-GOV-03** | Managed-device and geographic conditions by class.                    |
| **ADR-GOV-04** | Download, print, screenshot and offline-copy model.                   |
| **ADR-GOV-05** | DLP, watermarking and external-sharing enforcement.                   |
| **ADR-GOV-06** | EC-3 JIT and break-glass implementation.                              |
| **ADR-GOV-07** | Contractor/subcontractor sponsor and automatic expiry model.          |
| **ADR-GOV-08** | Access and audit-log retention; legal-hold integration.               |
| **ADR-GOV-09** | Workforce monitoring notice and regional legal controls.              |
| **ADR-GOV-10** | Offboarding targets and authoritative trigger source.                 |
| **ADR-GOV-11** | Approved engineering AI assistants and data-class policy.             |
| **ADR-GOV-12** | Source-change synchronization and derivative invalidation automation. |

| **FINAL CONTROL SENTENCE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| No engineering document without an authoritative source. No access without a defined operational need. No restricted detail without named, time-bound approval. No directly applicable technical constraint withheld. No superseded specification in active use. No exception, emergency access or release without an owner, expiry and evidence. |

# 00 \| Critical Review, Authority and Change Control

## 0.1 Critical assessment of the prior engineering-disclosure proposal

| **ID**   | **Finding**                                         | **Risk**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **Controlled correction**                                                                                        |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **C-01** | Correct direction, wrong artifact class             | The prior proposal treated the pack as a new standalone controlled document. Under the 53-master estate, this must be a controlled annex under A7/H6, otherwise the disclosure process creates the document inflation it was designed to prevent. | Classified as a controlled annex; source masters and registers remain authoritative.                             |
| **C-02** | Policy and build content were mixed                 | It described repositories and permissions but did not define a repeatable pack-generation contract for each workstream.                                                                                                                           | Separates the common baseline, restricted annexes and scoped workstream delivery packs.                          |
| **C-03** | Access levels were too broad                        | Granting engineering leads the complete C1-C11 estate by default would overexpose unrelated architecture and customer-impact information.                                                                                                         | Access is purpose-, role- and workstream-bound; platform-wide access requires named approval.                    |
| **C-04** | No formal derivative lineage                        | A filtered document can drift from its masters unless every extract has source version, extraction date and regeneration trigger.                                                                                                                 | Every pack carries source lineage and becomes invalid when a controlling source changes.                         |
| **C-05** | No executable requirement-to-release chain          | The proposal did not bind requirements, issues, code changes, tests and production approvals into one traceable workflow.                                                                                                                         | R04 requirement IDs and R20 release evidence are mandatory from assignment through deployment.                   |
| **C-06** | No Definition of Ready                              | Remote engineers could receive under-specified tasks and resolve ambiguity through informal channels.                                                                                                                                             | Work may not start until the controlled DoR is satisfied or an exception is approved.                            |
| **C-07** | Security-withholding boundary needed precision      | Withholding attack details is valid only when the engineer still receives all applicable mitigations, tests and residual-risk instructions.                                                                                                       | Applicable security truth is mandatory; unrestricted attack trees and exploit chains remain restricted.          |
| **C-08** | Production custody needed stronger segregation      | Low trust is not solved by document restrictions alone. The build and release path needs code ownership, independent review and no unilateral production promotion.                                                                               | Dual custody, protected branches, signed artifacts, JIT access and R20 approval are binding.                     |
| **C-09** | Remote-device and local-copy rules were incomplete  | Documents can be controlled centrally yet leak through unmanaged devices, personal storage, screenshots or local production data.                                                                                                                 | Managed-device, vault, DLP, download, retention and offboarding controls are specified.                          |
| **C-10** | No expiry and revocation mechanism                  | A former workstream member could retain valid-looking packs after role or source changes.                                                                                                                                                         | Packs expire, access is reviewed, and superseded copies are revoked and marked invalid.                          |
| **C-11** | Insufficient feedback channel                       | When chat and issue comments become de facto architecture, control is lost.                                                                                                                                                                       | A formal clarification/ADR path is defined; informal messages never override controlled sources.                 |
| **C-12** | The team needed a minimum common technical baseline | Over-compartmentalization can cause incompatible implementations across squads.                                                                                                                                                                   | This annex defines common invariants every authorized engineer receives, while detailed contracts remain scoped. |

## 0.2 Authority hierarchy

| **Priority** | **Authority**                           | **Rule**                                                                                                   |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **1**        | Controlled masters and living registers | Normative source of architecture, requirements, controls, decisions and current operational facts.         |
| **2**        | This engineering annex                  | Controls what is disclosed, how it is packaged and how the remote team must deliver.                       |
| **3**        | Approved workstream delivery pack       | Filtered requirements, technical contracts, wireframes, tests and decisions for a named scope and release. |
| **4**        | Issue tracker and source repository     | Execution and evidence systems; they may reference authority but cannot create unapproved requirements.    |
| **5**        | Chat, email and meetings                | Coordination only. A decision is not binding until entered into the appropriate controlled source.         |

| **CONFLICT RULE**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Where an issue, wireframe, API definition or instruction conflicts with a controlled master or register, stop the affected work, preserve evidence and raise a controlled clarification. The most recent authoritative source wins only after its applicability is confirmed. |

## 0.3 Change control

- Changes to this annex require the A7 change process and approval by the Chief Architect, CISO and Head of Engineering.

- Changes to workstream packs require the pack owner and relevant domain/control owner; material architecture changes require an ADR.

- A source-master change automatically places affected derivatives into REVIEW REQUIRED until regenerated or explicitly confirmed unaffected.

- No engineer may locally edit a controlled pack and represent the edited copy as authoritative.

# 01 \| Executive Engineering Decision

| **ENGINEERING DECISION**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Use one controlled common baseline for all authorized engineers, restricted annexes for high-consequence security and production details, and time-bound workstream packs for implementation. Do not distribute the full 53-master estate to the remote engineering team. |

## 1.1 Engineering mission

Build ZoikoShield as one horizontal, evidence-first cybersecurity, trust, compliance and digital-risk platform. The initial platform must support ZoikoShield Managed Defense and ZoikoShield Continuous Assurance as independently operable offers. Sector requirements are governed configuration packs over the common core; they are not separate product forks.

## 1.2 Current build boundary

| **Boundary**                            | **Controlled position**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|-----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Build now**                           | Multi-tenant control plane; modular monolith; ingestion, AI, action and evidence-anchor satellites; identity and authorization; evidence ledger/verifier; event normalization; detection/replay; cases; governed response; control/evidence operations; APIs; G1 experience contracts; secure delivery foundation. |
| **Integrate**                           | Tier-1 EDR, identity, cloud, email, vulnerability, ticketing, threat-intelligence and analytics technologies through governed connectors.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Do not build in the initial horizon** | Zoiko-built EDR agent; speculative sovereign/private deployments; OT-heavy critical-infrastructure functionality; sector-specific product forks; uncontrolled autonomous response; direct model-provider integrations outside the AI gateway.                                                                      |
| **Phase-gated**                         | Additional sector packs, dedicated tenancy classes, broader managed SIEM, partner/MSP surfaces and high-impact automation.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Evidence required**                   | Every material decision, action, assertion, privileged change and release must produce attributable, tenant-scoped, time-stamped evidence.                                                                                                                                                                         |

## 1.3 Information-control objective

The organization will not use secrecy as a substitute for engineering control. Engineers receive every applicable requirement, trust boundary, failure mode, data restriction, acceptance test and rollback condition. Information is withheld only when it is unrelated to the assigned responsibility or when full disclosure would expose commercial, customer, credential, production or unrestricted offensive-security material.

# 02 \| Information Classification and Distribution Model

| **Class**                | **Authorized audience**                                              | **Typical content**                                                                                                                                                 | **Control**                                                                   |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **ENG-COMMON**           | All authorized ZoikoShield engineers                                 | Common architecture doctrine, delivery controls, secure coding, AI rules, data-handling principles, testing, auditability and shared experience patterns.           | Individual authenticated access; no public links.                             |
| **ENG-WORKSTREAM**       | Named squad and reviewers                                            | Scoped requirements, models, schemas, API/event contracts, wireframes, tests, applicable risks and ADRs.                                                            | Purpose-bound; expires at workstream end or role change.                      |
| **ENG-RESTRICTED**       | Named leads in Security, SRE, AI Assurance, Release and Architecture | Crown-jewel details, sensitive topology, key-management design, unresolved high risks, red-team findings, recovery implementation and production operations.        | JIT where practicable; managed device; enhanced logging; periodic reapproval. |
| **EXECUTIVE-RESTRICTED** | Board, executives, Legal, Finance, Commercial and named owners       | Price books, financial model, pipeline, customer negotiation history, acquisition/funding strategy, salaries, unrestricted legal advice and Board risk acceptances. | Not distributed through engineering repositories.                             |
| **SECRET / CREDENTIAL**  | Vault-controlled systems only                                        | Passwords, tokens, private keys, recovery codes, customer secrets and live service credentials.                                                                     | Never embedded in documents, tickets, source code or chat.                    |

## 2.1 Binding distribution principles

| **ID**   | **Principle**                                                                                                                                       |
|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **P-01** | Need-to-know is role- and purpose-based, never based on personal favor or informal trust.                                                           |
| **P-02** | Deny by default; grant the smallest sufficient scope for the shortest sufficient period.                                                            |
| **P-03** | No applicable security, privacy, AI, resilience, evidence or failure requirement may be withheld from the engineer responsible for implementing it. |
| **P-04** | Customer and production data are not engineering documentation and are never distributed as examples.                                               |
| **P-05** | Registers are filtered by row and field; complete register access is exceptional.                                                                   |
| **P-06** | A controlled pack is a derivative view. It cannot override the masters and registers from which it was generated.                                   |
| **P-07** | Source changes, role changes, offboarding and incident response trigger immediate access review and pack revocation.                                |
| **P-08** | Unmanaged local copies, personal storage and uncontrolled forwarding are prohibited.                                                                |
| **P-09** | All access and material changes are attributable to an individual identity.                                                                         |
| **P-10** | Every production change has independent review, machine-verifiable evidence and named release authority.                                            |

## 2.2 Repository model

| **Repository**                                | **Content**                                                                   | **Access**                                | **Rule**                                                     |
|-----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Corporate controlled estate**               | Full masters, registers, legal/commercial and Board materials                 | Executive owners and document controllers | Authoritative; not an engineering shared drive.              |
| **Engineering baseline repository**           | This annex and approved ENG-COMMON artifacts                                  | All authorized engineers                  | Read-only controlled specifications; versioned.              |
| **Workstream repository**                     | Scoped delivery packs, code, test fixtures and implementation evidence        | Named squad, reviewers and owners         | Separate permissions and code ownership per bounded context. |
| **Restricted security/operations repository** | Threat models, key design, red-team evidence, production and recovery details | Named ENG-RESTRICTED users                | JIT/controlled export; enhanced monitoring.                  |
| **Secret vault**                              | Credentials, private keys and sensitive configuration values                  | Workloads and approved JIT operators      | Not a document repository; all use is logged and rotated.    |

# 03 \| Source-of-Truth and Derivative-Pack Control

## 3.1 Mandatory metadata on every engineering pack

| **Required metadata**           | **Controlled content**                                                      |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Pack identifier and version** | Unique ID; semantic version; effective and expiry dates.                    |
| **Scope**                       | Release, bounded context, repositories and environments covered.            |
| **Recipients**                  | Named role groups and named approvers; no generic “engineering team” grant. |
| **Source lineage**              | Exact master/register IDs and versions; extraction timestamp.               |
| **Requirements**                | R04 identifiers and acceptance criteria in scope.                           |
| **Interfaces**                  | R10/R11/R12 identifiers and approved versions.                              |
| **Data authority**              | R09 classification, purposes, regions, retention and deletion rules.        |
| **Risks and exceptions**        | Applicable R05 records; expiry and compensating controls.                   |
| **AI controls**                 | Applicable R15/R16 versions and release thresholds.                         |
| **Tests and evidence**          | Required test suites and R20 evidence fields.                               |
| **Owner and approvals**         | Pack owner, domain owner, security/privacy/AI approvers as applicable.      |
| **Supersession**                | Previous pack replaced; invalidation and regeneration triggers.             |

## 3.2 Pack validity states

| **State**           | **Rule**                                                                                                   |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **CURRENT**         | Sources are current; scope and recipients remain valid; work may proceed.                                  |
| **REVIEW REQUIRED** | A source, risk, recipient or release changed; only unaffected work may continue after owner confirmation.  |
| **SUSPENDED**       | Material conflict, security concern or expired exception; affected work must stop.                         |
| **SUPERSEDED**      | A newer approved pack replaces this version; no new work may use it.                                       |
| **REVOKED**         | Access or artifact invalidated because of role change, incident, offboarding or unauthorized distribution. |

## 3.3 Informal-instruction prohibition

| **NO SHADOW REQUIREMENTS**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A chat message, call, email, issue comment or verbal instruction may clarify coordination, but it cannot change scope, architecture, data handling, permissions, AI authority, acceptance criteria or release controls. The decision must be recorded in R04, R02, the applicable specification or an approved exception before implementation. |

# 05 \| Common Engineering Build Mandate

## 5.1 Canonical runtime position

| **Deployable / plane**     | **Engineering contract**                                                                                                                                                                               |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **shield-core**            | Modular monolith with enforced bounded contexts for tenant/commercial control, assets/exposure, detections, alerts/cases, controls, evidence metadata, assessments, risk, reporting and authorization. |
| **shield-ingest**          | Isolated ingestion and connector runtime for authentication, validation, regional routing, normalization, enrichment, quarantine and publication.                                                      |
| **shield-ai-gateway**      | Only permitted path to approved model providers; enforces tenant, data, region, prompt, retrieval, tool, cost and evaluation policy.                                                                   |
| **shield-action-broker**   | Isolated, policy-gated outbound response authority with per-tenant signing, approvals, receipts, compensation, rate ceilings and freeze controls.                                                      |
| **shield-evidence-anchor** | Separates tenant-chain/Merkle anchoring and independent witness publication from the transactional application path.                                                                                   |
| **Regional data plane**    | Raw telemetry, evidence content, search and regulated data remain in approved regional planes; the global control plane contains bounded metadata only.                                                |

## 5.2 Non-negotiable invariants

| **ID**   | **Invariant**                                                                                                                                |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **I-01** | Tenant, environment, region, actor, purpose and trace context must propagate across requests, events, records and audit logs.                |
| **I-02** | No material threat decision, response, control conclusion, AI recommendation or privileged change completes without attributable evidence.   |
| **I-03** | Non-COMPLETE evidence states never render or evaluate as compliant or healthy.                                                               |
| **I-04** | LLMs are not authorities for authentication, authorization, entitlement, evidence integrity, compliance state, signing or response approval. |
| **I-05** | AI failure degrades to deterministic workflows; it does not stop core detection, evidence, authorization or response controls.               |
| **I-06** | Response authority is explicit R0-R4, policy-bound, approval-aware, reversible where possible and independently auditable.                   |
| **I-07** | Cross-domain writes occur only through owned interfaces; direct table access across bounded contexts is prohibited and CI-enforced.          |
| **I-08** | Asynchronous processing is idempotent, replayable and explicit about ordering, late data, missing data and quarantine.                       |
| **I-09** | Immutable history is corrected by compensating/superseding records, not silent mutation.                                                     |
| **I-10** | Existing customer security tools are integrated before replacement is considered; no Zoiko-built EDR is authorized in the initial horizon.   |
| **I-11** | Data residency is decided before durable persistence; unmatched routes fail closed to quarantine.                                            |
| **I-12** | Unit cost, capacity and operability are release constraints recorded in R19, not deferred optimization work.                                 |
| **I-13** | Every customer-facing assertion drills to evidence, evaluator version, freshness/completeness and known limitations.                         |
| **I-14** | No production change bypasses protected branches, required tests, signed artifacts, canary validation and R20 approval.                      |

## 5.3 Required failure behavior

| **Condition**                 | **Required behavior**                                                                                                     |
|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity outage**           | Existing bounded sessions may remain read-capable within policy; privileged and response actions fail closed.             |
| **Connector failure**         | Coverage becomes degraded/incomplete; affected time windows are visible; no healthy/compliant inference.                  |
| **AI provider outage**        | Deterministic path continues; restricted data is never rerouted to an unapproved provider.                                |
| **Search outage**             | Ingestion and evidence preservation continue; investigation/search surfaces declare degradation.                          |
| **Event backlog**             | Backpressure and explicit lag states; no silent event loss; response actions remain idempotent.                           |
| **Evidence-anchor failure**   | Evidence collection may continue with UNANCHORED state; claims requiring external anchoring are blocked until reconciled. |
| **Action broker anomaly**     | Command issuance freezes or rate-limits; core investigation remains available; no direct connector bypass.                |
| **Authorization ambiguity**   | Deny and audit; do not infer permission from UI state or client input.                                                    |
| **Region/residency mismatch** | Quarantine before persistence and alert the owning control path.                                                          |
| **Schema incompatibility**    | Reject/quarantine with explicit reason; do not coerce fields in a way that destroys provenance.                           |

# 06 \| Mandatory Engineering Pack Modules

The common baseline is supplemented by a workstream delivery pack. The pack owner must include every applicable module below and may omit a module only with a recorded “not applicable” rationale. Source masters remain authoritative.

| **ID**    | **Module**                                     | **Sources**                 | **Must include**                                                                                                                                                              | **Withhold**                                                                                          | **Acceptance evidence**                                        |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **EP-00** | Control, scope and handling                    | A7; R01-R02                 | Pack ID/version; release and bounded context; recipients; source lineage; classification; effective/expiry dates; owner/approvers; change and conflict process.               | Full estate inventory; unrelated owners; commercial approval history.                                 | Pack acknowledgment and current-version check.                 |
| **EP-01** | Requirements and acceptance                    | A5; R04                     | Requirement IDs; actors; preconditions; normal/degraded/error flows; security/privacy/evidence/AI obligations; acceptance criteria; linked tests, APIs/events and wireframes. | Unapproved backlog ideas; future-phase requests; customer negotiation notes.                          | 100% of assigned work linked to R04.                           |

## 7.1 Workstream isolation rules

- Each repository and delivery pack is mapped to one or more bounded contexts and named CODEOWNERS.

- Cross-workstream access is granted only for an explicit integration dependency and is removed when the dependency closes.

- An engineer may not obtain production or restricted-security access merely because the engineer contributes to the related feature.

- Common schemas, libraries and design-system components remain centrally governed; workstreams cannot fork them locally.

- Synthetic tenants and approved fixtures are the default for development and testing.
