## **15.1 Evidence Object Model**

| **Field Group**           | **Required Content**                                                                                                                        |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Identity and scope**    | evidence_id, tenant, cell, legal entity, environment, control/test/case scope and producing service.                                        |
| **Source and collection** | source system/object, collector identity/version, collection method, observed/collected time, period covered and permission state.          |
| **Content binding**       | media type, byte length, canonicalization profile, content hash, object locator, encryption/key class and source signature where available. |
| **Evaluation lineage**    | evaluator/rule/model/prompt version, input evidence IDs, enrichment snapshot, policy/mapping version, output and limitations.               |
| **Assurance state**       | integrity, freshness, completeness, review, attestation, exception, legal-hold and retention state.                                         |
| **History**               | sequence, previous-record commitment, correction/supersession links, checkpoint inclusion and witness proofs.                               |

## **15.2 Cryptographic Construction**

| **Layer**                     | **v1.2 Design**                                                                                                                                                                  | **Guarantee**                                                                                                      |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Canonicalization**          | A versioned canonical byte representation for ledger metadata; binary artifacts hashed as stored. Canonicalization profile is embedded in every record.                          | The same record produces the same commitment across implementations and time.                                      |
| **Content digest**            | Algorithm-agile multihash profile; SHA-256 baseline, with algorithm identifier and migration policy.                                                                             | Artifacts are bound without locking the platform permanently to one digest.                                        |
| **Tenant append log**         | Per-tenant ordered log where each entry commits to prior entry, canonical record digest, sequence and checkpoint epoch.                                                          | Deletion, reordering and insertion are detectable.                                                                 |
| **Signed checkpoint**         | shield-anchor signs tenant log heads and a cell-level Merkle root using HSM-protected, rotated keys with public key history.                                                     | A bounded, verifiable statement of ledger state at a point in time.                                                |
| **Independent witnesses**     | Checkpoint roots published within 24 hours to two logically independent witnesses: one public append-only transparency service and one separately operated/time-stamped witness. | Zoiko cannot silently rewrite history or present divergent views without detection beyond the unanchored interval. |
| **Anti-equivocation monitor** | Customers/auditors may gossip/compare checkpoint receipts; Zoiko monitoring compares witness consistency and previously published roots.                                         | Split-view and rollback attempts surface as integrity incidents.                                                   |
| **Content vault**             | Encrypted content-addressed object storage; object lock/WORM where required; access separately authorized from ledger metadata.                                                  | Evidence bytes remain immutable/controlled without putting large artifacts in the transactional store.             |

## **15.3 Integrity Is Not Completeness**

| **State**                | **Meaning**                                                                                                 | **Presentation Rule**                                                             |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **COMPLETE**             | All evidence expected by the collection/test manifest arrived and reconciled for the declared scope/window. | May support a control conclusion subject to evaluator and review.                 |
| **PARTIAL**              | Known missing sources, objects, permissions, time ranges or fields are enumerated.                          | Cannot render as fully effective/compliant.                                       |
| **STALE**                | Freshness threshold exceeded.                                                                               | Visible warning; prior conclusion is time-bounded and cannot be shown as current. |
| **COLLECTOR_UNHEALTHY**  | Connector or collector health invalidates confidence for an affected window.                                | Retroactively marks affected evidence windows and opens remediation.              |
| **PERMISSION_CHANGED**   | Collection access changed or became insufficient.                                                           | Coverage gap and customer action required.                                        |
| **EVALUATION_FAILED**    | Evidence exists but evaluation did not complete deterministically.                                          | No conclusion; retry/engineering path.                                            |
| **INTEGRITY_UNVERIFIED** | Hash/signature/checkpoint/witness proof missing or failed.                                                  | Quarantine; may not support a claim.                                              |

## **15.4 Reproducible Audit Package**

- A frozen manifest lists every evidence object, content digest, collection/evaluation metadata, framework/control/mapping version, completeness state, limitation and reviewer/attestation.

- Package proofs include the tenant chain segment, signed checkpoint, Merkle inclusion proof, witness receipts and key history required for offline validation.

- Inputs and enrichment snapshots used for each material conclusion are frozen by immutable reference. Live queries are not the historical source of truth.

- Schema or mapping migration never rewrites a frozen package. Re-rendering creates a new version with an explicit supersession link; the original remains verifiable.

- The package includes an open, documented format and verifier instructions. Customer export preserves proofs after tenant offboarding.

## **15.5 Independent Verifier**

| **Property**       | **Requirement**                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Operation**      | CLI and library validate hashes, canonicalization, chain continuity, signatures, inclusion proofs, witness receipts, key rotation and manifest references. |
| **Trust**          | Runs offline after the package and public checkpoint/key material are obtained; requires no Zoiko credentials or production access.                        |
| **Distribution**   | Open-source, signed, reproducibly built, SBOM/provenance published and independently testable.                                                             |
| **Versioning**     | Package embeds minimum/known verifier versions and algorithms. Compatibility tests cover historical packages.                                              |
| **Negative tests** | Tampered bytes, missing entry, reordered chain, forged checkpoint, expired/revoked key, divergent witness and incomplete manifest must fail distinctly.    |

#  **16 \| Cases, SOAR, MDR and Incident Response**

## **16.1 Case and Incident Lifecycle**

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th>NEW → TRIAGED → INVESTIGATING → CONTAINMENT_PENDING → CONTAINED → REMEDIATING → MONITORING → RESOLVED → CLOSED<br />
Alternates: DUPLICATE • FALSE_POSITIVE • ACCEPTED_RISK • CUSTOMER_ACTION_REQUIRED • THIRD_PARTY_DEPENDENCY • LEGAL_HOLD</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

| **Object**               | **Mandatory Evidence**                                                                                                               |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Alert**                | Source events, detection/version, enrichments, severity/priority, confidence, suppression and creation path.                         |
| **Case**                 | Tenant, owners, queue, SLA clock, timeline, hypotheses, queries, notes, communications, evidence, decisions and disposition.         |
| **Incident**             | Impact, affected assets/identities/data, chronology, severity, command structure, legal/regulatory clocks, containment and recovery. |
| **Playbook run**         | Version, trigger, policy, inputs, steps, branching, approvals, tool calls, retries, output and termination reason.                   |
| **Response action**      | Tenant, target, action type, authority, approvals, signature, expiry, nonce, receipt, outcome, rollback/compensation and evidence.   |
| **Post-incident review** | Root/contributing causes, control failures, detection gaps, actions, owners, deadlines and verification.                             |

## **16.2 Response Authority Levels**

| **Level**                      | **Authority**                                                                                                     | **Shipping Gate**                                                                                                   |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R0 Observe**                 | Collect, enrich, query, notify and open case; no external state change.                                           | Baseline.                                                                                                           |
| **R1 Recommend**               | Human approval required for suggested containment/reset/block/disable/isolate.                                    | Baseline; recommendation is evidence-linked.                                                                        |
| **R2 Pre-authorized low risk** | Automatic only for customer-approved, reversible and narrowly scoped actions.                                     | Independent red team; per-tenant signing; customer-side verification; rate ceilings; simulation and rollback proof. |
| **R3 High impact**             | Named customer authority or dual approval for privileged account, server, network or production workload actions. | Customer-side command attestation; per-playbook rehearsal; time-bound approval and enhanced monitoring.             |
| **R4 Emergency**               | Contracted break-glass with immediate escalation and mandatory post-action review.                                | Explicit emergency authority, time box, customer notification and review within 72 hours.                           |

## **16.3 Action Safety Envelope**

- shield-core never holds standing customer command credentials; shield-action receives narrowly scoped credentials or token exchange for the approved action.

- Every command carries tenant signature, target, authority, approval references, policy version, expiry, nonce, rate class and expected receipt schema.

- Customer execution points verify signature, expiry, target scope and replay state. High-assurance tenants can pin verification keys and enforce local policy.

- Global, cell, tenant, connector, action-type and target-class rate ceilings bound mass action. A two-person out-of-band freeze stops issuance; customers have a tenant kill switch.

- Retries are idempotent. A receipt distinguishes accepted, executed, verified, failed, partially executed and unknown. Unknown never equals success.

- Rollback is proven where technically possible; otherwise a compensating-action and customer-risk statement is required before approval.

## **16.4 IR Retainer and Legal-Sensitive Work**

IR retainers store annual term, included hours/services, response window, readiness obligations, exclusions, overage and rollover. Activation creates a restricted incident work order and consumption ledger. Legal privilege, insurer, regulator, law-enforcement and breach-notification fields use purpose-bound access and jurisdictional controls; ZoikoShield does not represent that privilege automatically exists.

# **17 \| GRC Control Plane and Standards Content Supply Chain**

<th><p><strong>CONTROL-PLANE RULE</strong></p>
<p>The GRC layer is not a reporting veneer over security tools. It is the versioned policy and evidence authority defining which obligations apply, how controls are implemented/tested, what gaps exist, what response is permitted, and what may be asserted.</p></th>

## **17.1 Canonical Governance Objects**

| **Object**                 | **Definition**                                                                                                         |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **obligation**             | A legal, regulatory, contractual, policy or customer requirement with jurisdiction, applicability and effective dates. |
| **framework_requirement**  | A versioned source reference; licensed text displayed only where permitted.                                            |
| **control_objective**      | Zoiko-authored, outcome-oriented control intent shared across frameworks.                                              |
| **control_implementation** | Tenant-specific people, process and technology implementation with owner and scope.                                    |
| **control_test**           | Machine/manual procedure, evidence manifest, cadence, threshold and evaluator.                                         |
| **control_assessment**     | Time-bounded conclusion with inputs, gaps, reviewer, confidence and limitation.                                        |
| **risk / exception**       | Scenario, likelihood/impact basis, treatment, control links, approver, expiry and review.                              |
| **audit_package**          | Frozen, independently verifiable collection of scoped evidence, conclusions, limitations and proofs.                   |

## **17.2 Mapping Model**

Framework requirements map many-to-many to canonical control objectives. Tenant implementations map to objectives rather than duplicating implementation for every framework sentence. Each mapping records source/target versions, relationship (full, partial, supporting, alternative, not applicable or conflict), rationale, author, reviewer, legal review, effective dates and supersession. A mapping is guidance, not a legal conclusion.

## **17.3 Standards Content Supply Chain**

| **Control**                  | **Requirement**                                                                                                                                                   |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Licensing Register**       | Framework, edition, licensor/source, territory, permitted text/display mode, renewal, attribution and redistribution restrictions.                                |
| **Display enforcement**      | If rights are not cleared, show source identifier plus Zoiko-authored objective/paraphrase only; never copy controlled standard text into UI, prompts or exports. |
| **Author/reviewer chain**    | Qualified content engineer authors; compliance SME reviews; Legal reviews jurisdictional claims and license treatment; all identities stored on version.          |
| **Update intake**            | Monitor source changes, corrections, regulatory technical standards and national transpositions; create impact assessment and customer migration plan.            |
| **Effective-version policy** | Tenant can see current, superseded and contracted versions; assessment never silently moves to a new framework edition.                                           |
| **AI use**                   | Models may suggest mappings only from licensed/approved content and must cite source/version; human owner approves publication.                                   |
| **Claim language**           | Product and contracts state that controls/mappings support assurance and do not themselves constitute certification, legal advice or regulatory approval.         |

## **17.4 Initial Framework Set**

Phase 1 supports SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria-oriented evidence and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 control objectives under approved content treatment. One sector overlay is selected by signed pipeline and legal/compliance readiness: DORA, NIS2 implementation context, or PCI DSS 4.0.1. ISO/IEC 42001 is used initially to govern ZoikoShield’s own and customer-facing AI-control design; a marketed customer module remains demand-gated.

# **18 \| Privacy, Residency, Retention and Tenant Exit**

## **18.1 Privacy-by-Architecture Controls**

| **Control**                      | **Architecture Requirement**                                                                                                                                      |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Data classification**          | Every field/object/event is classified; restricted data has machine-enforced storage, access, export, AI and logging policy.                                      |
| **Purpose limitation**           | Collection, access, model use, sharing and export carry an approved purpose. Purpose is evaluated with identity and tenant policy.                                |
| **Minimization**                 | Source-side filters, field suppression, tokenization, sampling only where contractually safe, and configurable raw-payload retention.                             |
| **Residency before persistence** | Route decision occurs before durable storage using tenant, source region, data class, purpose, provider, transfer mechanism, key and contract.                    |
| **Transfer governance**          | Approved transfer mechanism, subprocessor and route are versioned; unsupported route fails closed to regional quarantine.                                         |
| **Retention**                    | Data-class, source, purpose, legal hold, contract and framework policy resolve into a versioned schedule; deletion is verifiable.                                 |
| **Data-subject operations**      | Search, review, restriction, export and deletion workflows with identity verification, exemptions and statutory clock.                                            |
| **Breach clocks**                | Incident facts, jurisdiction and personal-data scope activate legal review and notification clocks; platform does not make unilateral legal determinations.       |
| **Model training**               | Customer data is excluded from provider or Zoiko model training unless an explicit contract, lawful purpose, approved dataset and governance record authorize it. |

Every supported region/data-class combination has an explicit test. An unmatched or conflicting combination fails closed to quarantine and opens an operational/compliance event; it never falls back to a default global region.

## **18.3 Tenant Exit and Portable Proof**

| **Element**              | **Contract**                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Export scope**         | Configuration, identities/roles, assets, connectors, detections, cases/timelines, playbooks, controls, assessments, risks, exceptions, evidence metadata/content, model/agent records in scope, usage and frozen audit packages. |
| **Formats**              | JSON/JSONL for records, OCSF-aligned events, source-native evidence artifacts, CSV where useful, documented schemas and cryptographic manifests/proofs.                                                                          |
| **Verifier portability** | Exported audit packages remain verifiable offline after account closure using public key/checkpoint/witness material.                                                                                                            |
| **Legal hold**           | Held content and related metadata are segregated and disclosed in the exit manifest; deletion is blocked only to the extent required by approved hold policy.                                                                    |
| **Deletion**             | Store-by-store deletion or key destruction with backup expiry schedule, derived index/vector deletion and signed attestation. Claims distinguish immediate logical deletion from backup lifecycle.                               |
| **Testing**              | Quarterly synthetic-tenant export, verification, closure, deletion and restore-negative test. An untested exit path blocks GA for material schema/store additions.                                                               |

#  **19 \| Data Architecture and Information Governance**

| **Data Layer**                     | **Baseline Technology Class**                                           | **Authority / Constraint**                                                                                                                       |
|------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Transactional system of record** | Managed PostgreSQL-compatible relational database.                      | Authoritative tenant, commercial, case, control, policy and ledger metadata. Module schemas; row/tenant controls; no cross-module direct writes. |
| **Event backbone**                 | Managed Kafka-compatible or equivalent under ADR-01.                    | Durable transport/replay, not business source of truth. Ordering, retention, offset and schema contracts controlled.                             |
| **Security lakehouse**             | Object storage, open columnar formats and governed query engine.        | Raw/normalized telemetry, long-horizon analytics and replay; region/retention/tenant policies enforced.                                          |
| **Hot search/analytics**           | OpenSearch- or ClickHouse-class engine under ADR-02.                    | Operational search and correlation projection; rebuildable from authoritative events/objects.                                                    |
| **Context graph projection**       | Relational/analytics projection initially.                              | Relationships and attack paths; dedicated graph only after ADR-03 benchmark.                                                                     |
| **Evidence vault**                 | Encrypted content-addressed object storage; object lock where required. | Evidence content bound to Section 15 ledger; access independent from metadata.                                                                   |
| **AI retrieval indexes**           | Tenant/cell-scoped vector and keyword indexes.                          | Derived, rebuildable, source-versioned and included in deletion/offboarding. Never authoritative evidence.                                       |
| **Cache/coordination**             | Redis-compatible.                                                       | No sole durable authority; tenant and data-class keying; bounded TTL.                                                                            |
| **Metrics/time series**            | Prometheus/OpenTelemetry-compatible with long-term store.               | Platform, connector, security, AI, SLO and cost telemetry; customer content minimized.                                                           |

## **19.1 Data Ownership and Change**

- Each domain owns its write API, schema, data-quality contract, retention, lineage and reconciliation. Shared tables are prohibited.

- Cross-domain reads use published APIs, event projections or governed data products with owner and freshness SLO.

- Schema changes are backward-compatible during a declared migration window. Event consumers prove compatibility before producer cutover.

- Backfills and corrections create manifests with source range, code/version, counts, exceptions, costs and rollback; material conclusions affected by reprocessing are versioned, not silently replaced.

- Every derived fact records source IDs, transform/evaluator version and confidence. A derivative cannot outrank its authoritative source without an explicit policy.

## **19.2 Retention Classes**

| **Class**             | **Illustrative Baseline**                                               | **Rule**                                                                                     |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Hot telemetry**     | 30–90 days by plan/use case.                                            | Fast search and detection; exact period is contract and data-class controlled.               |
| **Warm telemetry**    | To 12 months or contracted.                                             | Lower-cost query; no silent performance degradation against promised use.                    |
| **Archive telemetry** | Multi-year only where contracted/required.                              | Open format, retrieval SLA, egress and legal-hold behavior explicit.                         |
| **Evidence**          | Per control, contract and jurisdiction; may exceed telemetry retention. | Integrity proofs and package metadata preserved according to assertion needs.                |
| **Operational audit** | Security/administrative events under separately approved schedule.      | Protected from ordinary support/admin mutation.                                              |
| **AI traces**         | Minimum necessary by use case and risk.                                 | Prompts/context may be more sensitive than outputs; redaction and shorter retention default. |

#  **20 \| API, Event and Partner Architecture**

## **20.1 API Families**

| **Family**                    | **External Surface**                                                    | **Key Controls**                                                                        |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Tenant / administration**   | Organizations, users, roles, environments, configuration.               | Federated identity, scoped admin, idempotency, audit and no bulk cross-tenant endpoint. |
| **Connectors / telemetry**    | Source setup, health, schema, event submission and replay.              | Signed requests, quotas, manifest, regional route and quarantine status.                |
| **Assets / exposure**         | Assets, identities, relationships, findings and remediation.            | Source/confidence, pagination, field-level access and export controls.                  |
| **Alerts / cases / response** | Alerts, cases, timeline, playbooks, approvals and action status.        | Authority, case reference, anti-replay, action separation and signed receipts.          |
| **GRC / evidence**            | Controls, tests, assessments, evidence, risks, exceptions and packages. | Versioned snapshots, access purpose, integrity metadata and package proofs.             |
| **Threat intelligence**       | Indicators, techniques, context and collections.                        | TLP/handling, provenance, confidence and expiry.                                        |
| **Commercial / usage**        | Entitlements, meters, obligations, forecast and invoices/adapters.      | Customer-visible reconciliation; sensitive partner cost hidden by role.                 |
| **AI / agent**                | Approved assistants, run status, citations and feedback.                | No arbitrary prompt/tool endpoint; registered profiles only; policy and budget.         |

## **20.2 Contract Rules**

- Public APIs are versioned with deprecation windows, compatibility tests and customer communication. Breaking changes require ADR and migration plan.

- Retriable writes require idempotency keys. Bulk operations return item-level results and never obscure partial failure.

- Tenant, actor, purpose, trace, policy and region context propagates end-to-end. Services re-authorize; they do not trust caller claims blindly.

- Errors use stable machine codes, safe messages and correlation IDs; sensitive internals and cross-tenant existence are not leaked.

- Webhooks are signed, replay-protected, rotatable, tenant-scoped and delivery-observable. Consumers can request replay within retention policy.

- SDKs derive from approved contracts; no integration receives direct database access.

## **20.3 Canonical Event Envelope**

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th>event_id, event_type, event_version, occurred_at, observed_at, produced_at,<br />
tenant_id, cell_id, legal_entity_id, environment_id, actor, subject, object,<br />
purpose, data_class, source, schema_version, correlation_id, causation_id,<br />
trace_id, idempotency_key, integrity, processing_state, payload_ref / payload</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

Domain events use past-tense names and carry enough identity, ordering, privacy and causation context for safe replay. Sensitive payloads may be referenced rather than copied. Consumer-specific projections are not allowed to become undocumented systems of record.

## **20.4 Partner/MSP Delegation**

Partners operate under explicit tenant grants, role scopes, time bounds and customer visibility. A partner cannot enumerate or traverse tenants outside its grant. Delegated operations are attributable to both partner identity and human actor. Partner tools run inside governed ZoikoShield workflows; parallel unmanaged case/evidence stacks are prohibited for contracted service delivery.

# **21 \| Platform Security and Crown-Jewel Threat Model**

ZoikoShield is a multi-tenant control plane with sensitive telemetry, audit evidence and potential response authority. It must be designed as a supply-chain prize and assume a capable adversary gains partial application, build, identity, connector or operator compromise.

<img src="ZoikoShield_Combined_Engineering_Specifications_media/media/image195.png" style="width:6.65in;height:0.70694in" alt="Figure 6 — Crown-jewel threat model and bounded command path." />

*Figure 6 — Crown-jewel threat model and bounded command path.*

## **21.1 Baseline Platform Controls**

- Private service networking, segmented management planes, controlled egress, TLS 1.3 preferred and mTLS/workload identity on service paths.

- Central secret/key management, envelope encryption, tenant-context keys, BYOK/HYOK by tier, HSM-backed anchor/action operations and tested rotation/revocation.

- JIT/PAM administration with phishing-resistant MFA, dual control for critical keys/policies, session recording and customer-content masking.

- Continuous tenant-isolation testing across API, relational, object, search, cache, queue, lakehouse, vector index, AI context and observability.

- Hardened minimal images, policy-as-code/admission, vulnerability remediation SLAs, signed releases, SBOM/AI-BOM and provenance verification.

- Network egress and DNS allowlists for connectors and AI providers; no arbitrary internet access from shield-core or analyst tooling.

## **21.2 Assume-Breach Scenarios**

| **Compromise**                 | **Blast-Radius Control**                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **shield-core application**    | No standing customer command credentials; actions require independent shield-action policy/signature. Tenant data is bounded by region, tenant authorization, keys and query guards. |
| **shield-action**              | Per-tenant key release requires valid policy/approval; global/cell/tenant/action ceilings; customer-side verification; customer kill switch; two-person out-of-band freeze.          |
| **shield-anchor**              | Cannot modify evidence content or business records. Key use is limited to valid checkpoint structures; witness consistency and key transparency reveal unauthorized history.         |
| **shield-ingest / connector**  | Connector credentials are per tenant/source and least privilege; runtime is sandboxed; it cannot invoke action broker or write authoritative control conclusions.                    |
| **shield-ai / model provider** | No direct action authority, no unrestricted database or cross-tenant search, no critical-path dependency; provider egress and data policy enforced centrally.                        |
| **Build/release system**       | Hermetic/reproducible build where feasible, signed provenance, admission verification, environment separation, canary tenants and rollback/freeze.                                   |
| **ZoikoID**                    | Independent step-up/freeze for privileged response; degradation to bounded read mode; service identity and tenant keys not derived solely from user session.                         |
| **Privileged insider**         | JIT/dual control, separation of write/anchor/action authority, session evidence, masking, anomaly detection and immutable access records.                                            |

## **21.3 Command Trust and Customer Attestation**

The customer-side integration or agent verifies signature, tenant, target, action allowlist, expiry, nonce and local policy before execution. R3 actions require customer-side verification; high-assurance tenants may require local second approval. Receipts are signed or otherwise source-authenticated and linked to the command.

## **21.4 Independent Security Gates**

1\. Architecture threat model and abuse-case review before Phase-0 exit, including AI, connector, action and evidence trust boundaries.

2\. Independent red team before any R2 automation GA, covering tenant isolation, action broker, command verification, freeze paths, AI/tool chain and software supply chain.

3\. Annual external assessment thereafter and after material changes to action key release, customer agent, anchoring, identity trust or agentic tools.

4\. Critical/high findings are closed and retested or accepted only at Board-delegated authority with explicit customer/claim impact.

# **22 \| Reliability, SLOs, Disaster Recovery and Continuity**

## **22.1 Hard Invariants Versus Service Objectives**

| **Type**            | **Examples**                                                                                                                                    | **Failure Treatment**                                                                     |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Invariant**       | No cross-tenant access; no unsigned response command; no unverifiable evidence conclusion; no residency fallback; no unbounded agent/tool loop. | P0/P1 integrity or security incident; error budget does not permit violation.             |
| **SLO**             | API availability, ingestion acceptance, detection latency, connector visibility, evidence freshness and recovery.                               | Measured over eligible events/requests; error budget drives release and reliability work. |
| **Contractual SLA** | Customer commitment and credits.                                                                                                                | Offered only after measured capability, tested topology and legal/commercial approval.    |

## **22.2 Internal Engineering Objectives**

| **Capability**                      | **v1.2 Objective**                                                                                                              | **Definition / Qualification**                                                                                         |
|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Control-plane API availability**  | 99.95% monthly at GA.                                                                                                           | Successful eligible requests; excludes customer/network/provider failures under the approved policy.                   |
| **Telemetry durable acceptance**    | 99.90% launch; 99.95% MDR GA; 99.99% later target.                                                                              | Valid authenticated events durably acknowledged by regional ingestion. No claim before measured redundancy.            |
| **Point detection latency**         | p95 ≤60 seconds.                                                                                                                | Durable acceptance to alert for point-class rules.                                                                     |
| **Windowed detection latency**      | p95 ≤ declared window + 60 seconds.                                                                                             | Rule-specific window/watermark semantics included.                                                                     |
| **Connector failure visibility**    | p95 ≤5 minutes from platform-observed failure.                                                                                  | Customer/operations state reflects degraded, unauthorized, delayed or failed.                                          |
| **Material audit reconciliation**   | ≥99.99% of sampled material operations reconcile to required audit event within 5 minutes; any missing high-impact event is P0. | Active reconciliation makes silent absence observable; this is not a claim that unknowable events are “100% complete.” |
| **Evidence checkpoint publication** | ≤24 hours at launch.                                                                                                            | Signed checkpoint to both witnesses; missed cadence creates integrity degradation and alert.                           |
| **Transactional recovery**          | RTO 4 hours / RPO 15 minutes standard.                                                                                          | Applies to authoritative transactional state; durably accepted telemetry is replayed from event/object stores.         |
| **Premium recovery**                | Target RTO 1 hour / RPO 5 minutes where contracted and exercised.                                                               | Requires paid topology and passing failover evidence.                                                                  |

## **22.3 Resilience Patterns**

- Multi-AZ production cells; quotas, backpressure, circuit breakers, bulkheads, poison-event quarantine and bounded retries.

- Idempotent consumers and replay manifests. Replay cannot duplicate response actions, billing meters, evidence records or customer notifications.

- Graceful degradation: model outage never stops deterministic detection; search outage never destroys ingestion; connector failure marks coverage incomplete; witness outage queues checkpoints and exposes degradation.

- Backups are encrypted, cross-account protected and restore-tested. Restored evidence state is reconciled against external checkpoints and event manifests; divergence is an integrity incident.

- Quarterly restore tests, annual regional recovery exercise before broad SLA claims, and tabletop exercises for identity, action-broker, anchor and provider compromise.

- Capacity is measured against Appendix A low/nominal/high envelopes with declared headroom and bottleneck ownership.

# **23 \| Observability, Security Operations and FinOps**

| **Signal**             | **Required Coverage**                                                                                                                                                            |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Traces**             | Tenant pseudonym, cell, service/module, actor class, purpose, policy decision, latency, downstream dependency and error; customer content excluded by default.                   |
| **Metrics**            | Availability, queue lag, throughput, parser quality, quarantine, detection latency, case clocks, action outcomes, connector/evidence health, AI quality/cost and unit economics. |
| **Logs**               | Structured, redacted, trace-correlated; no secrets, raw restricted payloads or unbounded model context.                                                                          |
| **Security audit**     | Authentication, authorization, privilege, support access, policy/configuration, connector, evidence, export, AI run/tool call, release, key and action changes.                  |
| **Business telemetry** | Entitlements, usage, obligation delivery, support tier, renewal risk, cost and margin attribution.                                                                               |
| **Customer telemetry** | Coverage health, usage/forecast, evidence freshness, action status and service clocks appropriate to role.                                                                       |

## **23.1 SLO and Integrity Monitoring**

SLOs are computed from independent source/observer signals where practicable, not only the component reporting itself healthy. Synthetic tenants continuously exercise authentication, ingestion, normalization, detection, case creation, simulated response, evidence package generation, offline verification and offboarding. Monitoring data required to prove service claims is itself retained as controlled evidence.

## **23.2 FinOps Controls**

- Cost attribution by tenant, cell, connector, data class/tier, storage temperature, query, model, agent profile, service family and partner.

- Budgets and anomaly alerts for ingestion bursts, search abuse, AI denial-of-wallet, orphaned resources, over-retention and custom connector overhead.

- Customer-visible usage and forecast before overage; disputed meters carry reconciliation state and correction records.

- Cost optimization cannot silently weaken contracted detection, retention, evidence or recovery. Any functional trade-off requires product, risk and customer treatment.

# **24 \| DevSecOps, AI Supply Chain and Release Governance**

## **24.1 Controlled Delivery Pipeline**

| **Stage**          | **Blocking Controls**                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| **Code / content** | Peer review, branch protection, signed commits where required, secrets scanning, SAST, dependency policy, architecture tests; detections/prompts/mappings treated as code. |
| **Build**          | Hermetic/reproducible where feasible, pinned dependencies, SBOM, AI/ML-BOM, provenance, signed artifact and no direct production secrets.                                  |
| **Verify**         | Unit/integration/contract/fuzz/security/privacy/tenant/AI/adversarial/performance/economics tests; synthetic end-to-end package verification.                              |
| **Deploy**         | Admission verifies signature/provenance/policy; canary synthetic tenants, staged cohorts, migration guard, feature/authority flags and rollback.                           |
| **Operate**        | SLO/error budget, security signals, drift, model/provider changes, cost, quality, customer impact and post-release evidence.                                               |

## **24.4 Mandatory Recurrent Tests**

- Every release: architecture boundaries, tenant negative tests, signed artifact/provenance, migration compatibility, deterministic replay, AI injection/tool abuse where relevant, and synthetic audit-package verification.

- Quarterly: tenant export/delete, backup restore, action-broker freeze/unfreeze, key rotation, connector permission drift and evidence witness failover.

- Annually: regional recovery, independent red team, AI red team, business continuity exercise, standards/license review and customer command-verification drill.

- After material change: targeted threat model and retest for identity, action, anchor, connector sandbox, AI tool boundary, cell topology or cryptographic construction.

# **25 \| Managed-Service Operating Model**

## **25.1 Service Families and Platform/Human Separation**

| **Service Family**       | **Platform Enablement**                                                                                     | **Human Obligation**                                                                                       |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **MDR / SOC**            | Telemetry, detections, triage queues, cases, response policy, communications and evidence.                  | 24/7 monitoring tier, investigation, escalation, approved response, reporting and quality review.          |
| **Compliance Assurance** | Control/test engine, evidence collection, assessments, exceptions and audit workspace.                      | Control-owner support, evidence review, readiness, auditor coordination within agreed scope.               |
| **IR Retainer**          | Readiness pack, contacts, access tests, incident workspace, hours/consumption and legal-sensitive controls. | Readiness activities, activation window, responders, coordination and post-incident review.                |
| **vCISO / Advisory**     | Risk register, roadmap, Board reporting, hour bank, decisions and deliverables.                             | Named advisor, scheduled hours, deliverables, approvals and escalation.                                    |
| **Exposure Management**  | Asset/exposure inventory, prioritization, remediation workflows and verification.                           | Analyst validation, remediation guidance and periodic review.                                              |
| **Penetration Testing**  | Scope/authorization, test window, evidence, findings, retest and report controls.                           | Qualified tester/partner execution and legally authorized testing.                                         |
| **Managed SIEM**         | Data tiers, detections, queries, cases and service metrics.                                                 | Gated analyst monitoring/tuning/response obligations; only after economics and scope ownership are proven. |

## **25.2 SOC Queue and Quality Controls**

- Assignment considers tenant/cell, severity, language, certification, data access eligibility, service tier, workload and conflict-of-interest policy.

- Shift handover is a structured object with open hypotheses, actions, clocks, customer dependencies and evidence; chat messages are not the record of authority.

- Material cases receive severity-based peer/supervisor review. Sampling covers closed lower-severity cases, customer communications and false-positive dispositions.

- Metrics never reward premature closure, under-escalation or automation rate. Quality, customer impact, evidence completeness and detection improvement dominate.

- Customer communications use versioned, legally reviewed templates but remain case-specific and evidence-linked. Severity and breach language cannot be model-invented.

- Analyst access is task-, tenant- and time-scoped; sensitive customer data is masked until required for the assigned investigation.

## **25.3 Follow-the-Sun and Overflow Partner**

At launch, Zoiko may combine an internal SOC team with a certified off-peak overflow partner. The partner operates in ZoikoShield under delegated scopes, shared quality rules, customer visibility and Zoiko-owned case/evidence records. A parallel partner case system may be used only for provider administration and may not become the source of truth for customer delivery.

This is intentionally more conservative than the proposed v1.1 estimate because AI governance, anchoring, connector certification, internal assurance and production operations are distinct obligations even when individuals cover multiple roles early.

## **27.1 Partner Certification**

- Security/privacy due diligence, DPA/subprocessor treatment, breach notification, business continuity and geographic/data handling.

- Connector schemas, permissions, negative tests, scale, action safety, version/deprecation and tested offboarding.

- Commercial data and secret credentials separated from technical configuration; margin and pass-through visibility role controlled.

- Joint support matrix, escalation, incident evidence, maintenance windows and change notification.

- Model providers additionally require data-use, retention, region, training exclusion, version-control, abuse monitoring and safety-incident terms.

- No partner is a single unmitigated dependency for a critical invariant. Where a second provider is uneconomic, deterministic/manual degraded mode is documented and tested.

## **28.1 Own-Assurance Sequencing**

| **Stage**                             | **Controlled Position**                                                                                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Design partners**                   | Permitted before Type II under precise contracts and Claim Register controls. Do not imply ZoikoShield has completed reports/certifications it does not hold.                               |
| **SOC 2**                             | Treat as an independent examination/report. Type I can establish design at a point in time; Type II covers operating effectiveness over a period. Public wording follows the issued report. |
| **ISO/IEC 27001**                     | Certification program and scope approved; certification claim only after accredited certification and maintained surveillance.                                                              |
| **Broad “continuous compliance” GTM** | Gated on measured product evidence, own operating assurance and claim-specific Legal/Compliance approval; architecture support does not equal customer compliance.                          |

## **28.2 Migration Doctrine**

- Inventory incumbent tools, data authority, response ownership, retention and contractual dependencies before proposing replacement.

- Connect and normalize first; compare coverage, detection, cost and evidence; rationalize only with named owner and rollback.

- Run parallel detections/assessments before cutover; preserve historical cases/evidence/legal holds and export manifests.

- No cutover without reconciliation, action-safety test, customer communication, rollback and post-cutover validation.

# **29 \| Quality Gates and Definition of Done**

| **Gate**                   | **Definition of Done**                                                                                                                             |
|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Architecture**           | Bounded context, owner, interfaces/events/data, dependency, failure mode, capacity, cost, ADR and extraction impact defined.                       |
| **Tenancy**                | Automated cross-tenant negative tests across API, DB, object, search, lakehouse, cache, queue, vector index, observability and AI context.         |
| **Identity/authorization** | Positive and negative policies, step-up, JIT, SoD, delegated support and degradation tested.                                                       |
| **Ingestion**              | Idempotency, replay, late/duplicate/malformed events, quarantine, schema drift, backpressure, residency and raw/normalized lineage tested.         |
| **Detection**              | Versioned content, deterministic replay, data availability, latency/cost, adversarial fixtures, canary and rollback.                               |
| **AI**                     | Registered use, model/prompt/agent/tool/data policy, injection and tool-abuse tests, groundedness, human factors, cost and deterministic fallback. |
| **Response**               | Authority, approval, signing, customer verification, simulation, rate limits, receipt, retry, rollback/compensation and freeze.                    |
| **Evidence**               | Canonicalization, hash/chain/checkpoint/witness, completeness states, migration, offline verifier and tamper-negative tests.                       |
| **Privacy/residency**      | Classification, purpose, minimization, routing, transfer, retention, DSR, provider and deletion tests.                                             |
| **Reliability**            | SLO instrumentation, load/soak, failover/restore, replay, graceful degradation, capacity headroom and runbook.                                     |
| **Commercial**             | Entitlement, meter, obligation, double-charge, usage reconciliation, cost allocation, margin and claim eligibility.                                |
| **Operations**             | Owner/on-call, alerts, dashboard, runbook, incident/communication, support and partner escalation.                                                 |
| **Claims**                 | Claim Register entry, evidence, scope, approved wording, expiry and monitoring.                                                                    |

## **30.2 Gate-0 ADR Set**

| **ADR**    | **Decision**                                     | **Owner**                            | **Deadline**                         | **Default**                                                             | **Acceptance Proof**                                         |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| **ADR-01** | Event backbone and managed-service choice        | CTO / Platform                       | Phase 0 + 6 weeks                    | Managed Kafka-compatible service.                                       | Load/replay/cost benchmark; failure and export plan.         |
| **ADR-02** | Hot analytics engine                             | Chief Architect / Data               | Before scale test                    | Managed OpenSearch-compatible baseline.                                 | Appendix A benchmark incl. cost/query/detection.             |
| **ADR-03** | Graph engine                                     | Data Architect                       | Before attack-path GA                | Relational/analytics projection.                                        | Measured query/scale need and lifecycle cost.                |
| **ADR-04** | Primary cloud, regions and legal entities        | Board / CTO / Legal                  | Before design-partner contract       | Primary region by signed pipeline; no implied UK/EU interchangeability. | Residency/legal/subprocessor and DR approval.                |
| **ADR-05** | Launch EDR partner and BYO policy                | Product / Security / Commercial      | Phase 0 + 8 weeks                    | One response-certified partner; BYO read-only.                          | API/action safety, MSP terms, certification tests.           |
| **ADR-06** | Price book, unit economics and margin thresholds | Commercial / Finance                 | Before quotes beyond design partners | Bespoke design-partner pricing; no public price.                        | Approved service-class cost model and catalog.               |
| **ADR-07** | Contractual SLAs and credits                     | Product / SRE / Legal                | Before MDR GA contracts              | Internal SLOs only.                                                     | Two quarters measured data or explicit limited pilot terms.  |
| **ADR-08** | Initial sector overlay                           | Product / Compliance / Legal         | Phase 2 midpoint                     | DORA only if signed pipeline and content readiness; otherwise defer.    | Customer demand, license/legal mapping and SME.              |
| **ADR-09** | Evidence canonicalization and digest profile     | Security / Data                      | Phase 0 + 8 weeks                    | Versioned canonical JSON/CBOR profile plus SHA-256 multihash baseline.  | Cross-language test vectors and migration plan.              |
| **ADR-10** | Witnesses and checkpoint cadence                 | Security / Compliance                | Phase 0 + 10 weeks                   | Daily, two independent witnesses.                                       | Failure, anti-equivocation, key rotation and cost test.      |
| **ADR-11** | AI providers, models and data terms              | AI Risk Committee / Security / Legal | Before production AI                 | Gateway only; no customer training; deterministic fallback.             | DPA/region/retention, evaluation and kill switch.            |
| **ADR-12** | AI agent framework and tool capability model     | Chief AI Architect / Security        | Before A2 production                 | Registered profiles, capability tokens, no direct action tool.          | Injection/tool abuse/limits/evidence tests.                  |
| **ADR-13** | Zoiko assurance sequence and audit firm          | Board / Compliance                   | Phase 1 start                        | SOC 2 Type I then Type II; ISO program scoped.                          | Scope, readiness, auditor/certification body and claim plan. |
| **ADR-14** | SOC launch staffing/partner model                | Service Ops / Security               | Phase 2 entry                        | Internal 8–12 plus certified overflow.                                  | Coverage model, quality, authority, data and exit.           |
| **ADR-15** | ZoikoID dependency SLA and fallback              | Platform / Identity / Security       | Phase 0 + 8 weeks                    | Bounded read continuation; privileged/action fail closed.               | Outage/compromise drill and token/key design.                |
| **ADR-16** | Regional cell allocation and failover            | Platform / Legal / SRE               | Before production tenant             | Single home cell; no automatic residency-breaking failover.             | Placement, evacuation, RTO/RPO and customer wording.         |

#  **31 \| Principal Risk Register**

| **ID**   | **Risk**                                    | **Primary Controls**                                                                                                 |
|----------|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **R-01** | Platform overreach                          | Wedge, team-row scope test, revenue gates, monolith-first and kill criteria.                                         |
| **R-02** | False assurance / stale evidence            | Explicit completeness/freshness, limitations, claim register, auditor verification and no silent green.              |
| **R-03** | Cross-tenant exposure                       | Context everywhere, cell boundary, isolation tests across all stores/AI and no shared admin bypass.                  |
| **R-04** | Unsafe response automation                  | Authority levels, independent broker, per-tenant signing, customer verification, ceilings/freeze and red team.       |
| **R-05** | Telemetry cost blowout                      | Service-class economics, scale benchmarks, customer forecast and managed-SIEM gate.                                  |
| **R-06** | Vendor lock-in                              | Open event/storage/export formats, adapter boundaries, managed-service exit and no provider-specific business logic. |
| **R-07** | Connector drift / false coverage            | Version/permission health, certification, schema drift, explicit degraded states and customer visibility.            |
| **R-08** | AI fabrication or unsupported claim         | Grounded structured facts/citations, registered profiles, evaluation, human disposition and claim restrictions.      |
| **R-09** | Commercial double count                     | Catalog relationships, ownership boundaries and override evidence.                                                   |
| **R-10** | Privileged insider                          | JIT, dual control, separated action/anchor/evidence authority, recording and immutable access evidence.              |
| **R-11** | Residency breach                            | Route before persistence, home cells, fail-closed unknown route and tested transfer policy.                          |
| **R-12** | Evidence tampering / equivocation           | Canonical chain, independent anchor, two witnesses, verifier, key transparency and anti-equivocation.                |
| **R-13** | Detection erosion                           | Detection-as-code, replay, data requirements, quality feedback, drift and retirement history.                        |
| **R-14** | Service obligation not delivered            | Obligation calendar, ownership, capacity, evidence, escalation and renewal treatment.                                |
| **R-15** | Certification / report misstatement         | Claim Register; SOC 2 examination terminology; ISO certification evidence; scope/expiry.                             |
| **R-16** | Recovery creates alternate history          | Restore reconciliation against event manifests and external checkpoints; divergence is an incident.                  |
| **R-17** | Software supply-chain compromise            | Provenance, signatures, SBOM, admission, canaries, separation and red team.                                          |
| **R-18** | Unclear data authority                      | Domain ownership, lineage, source conflict and no derived-store shadow truth.                                        |
| **R-19** | Buyer bifurcation                           | Standalone security/compliance landing, shared evidence spine and independent packaging/onboarding.                  |
| **R-20** | ZoikoShield used as customer attack vector  | Crown-jewel model, no core credentials, command verification, freeze, sandbox and bounded cells.                     |
| **R-21** | ZoikoID outage/compromise                   | Dependency SLA, read degradation, privileged fail closed and independent emergency controls.                         |
| **R-22** | Standards IP/licensing breach               | Licensing register, display enforcement, review chain and AI content controls.                                       |
| **R-23** | Selling assurance without own proof         | Own assurance roadmap and precise design-partner/public claim gates.                                                 |
| **R-24** | Auditors reject evidence model              | Early auditor participation, offline verifier, negative tests and Phase-1 exit gate.                                 |
| **R-25** | Prompt injection / agent hijack             | Untrusted-content labeling, capability tools, hard limits, no direct action and adversarial testing.                 |
| **R-26** | AI provider change or outage                | Pinned profiles, change monitoring, multi-provider where justified and deterministic/manual fallback.                |
| **R-27** | AI denial-of-wallet or data over-collection | Budgets, context minimization, token/tool/data ceilings, anomaly alerts and hard stop.                               |
| **R-28** | Witness or anchor key compromise            | Separated service/key custody, rotation/revocation, dual witnesses, public key history and incident procedure.       |
| **R-29** | Understaffed 24/7 operations                | Realistic coverage arithmetic, hybrid partner, queue/capacity model and quality-first gates.                         |
| **R-30** | Customer lock-in / failed exit              | Open export, proof portability, deletion attestation and quarterly exit test.                                        |

#  **32 \| Final CTO Recommendation**

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>RECOMMENDED BUILD POSITION</strong></p>
<p>Proceed with ZoikoShield as an AI-centric, evidence-first, integration-led security and compliance control plane. Enter through compliance-native MDR; build the proprietary proof, policy, correlation, governed-AI and response layer; deploy as a modular monolith with four isolated trust/scale satellites and regional cells; assume the platform itself is the prime target; and expand only through measured customer, assurance, capacity and economic gates.</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

The supplied market benchmark exposes a fragmented stack of overlapping services and inconsistent units. ZoikoShield must not reproduce that fragmentation in code, packaging, claims or organization. The platform’s defensibility is not “AI” alone. It is governed AI operating on trustworthy context, under explicit authority, producing evidence that a customer can verify independently.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 100%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr class="header">
<th><p><strong>FINAL CONTROL SENTENCE</strong></p>
<p>No threat decision without context. No AI conclusion without provenance. No response without authority. No compliance conclusion without evidence. No commercial entitlement without a controlled catalog. No public claim without proof. No scope without a team, a gate and a number.</p></th>
</tr>

# **APPENDIX A \| Reference Scale Envelope**

Every capacity, latency, cost and reliability claim is tested against a versioned low/nominal/high envelope. These are architecture planning loads, not customer commitments. The Scale Envelope Register records actual fleet data, benchmark method and release headroom.

| **Dimension**                             | **Phase 1 Design Partners** | **Phase 2 MDR GA** | **Phase 3 Assurance + SIEM** |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------|------------------------------|
| **Active tenants**                        | 3–10                        | 25–60              | 100–250                      |
| **Protected resources (fleet)**           | 2K–10K                      | 25K–75K            | 150K–400K                    |
| **Telemetry TB/day low / nominal / high** | 0.2 / 0.8 / 2               | 2 / 7 / 15         | 15 / 40 / 80                 |
| **Peak events/second**                    | 15K                         | 100K               | 500K                         |
| **Connector instances**                   | 50–200                      | 500–1,500          | 3,000–8,000                  |
| **Alerts / cases per day**                | 200 / 30                    | 3,000 / 400        | 15,000 / 1,800               |
| **Evidence objects/month**                | 50K                         | 750K               | 5M                           |
| **Concurrent investigations / searches**  | 10 / 50                     | 60 / 400           | 250 / 2,000                  |
| **AI calls/day (all profiles)**           | 5K                          | 80K                | 500K                         |
| **Concurrent agent runs**                 | 10                          | 100                | 500                          |
| **Response commands/day**                 | 25 simulation / 5 live      | 500                | 4,000                        |

- Benchmarks include noisy-neighbor, tenant distribution, event-size distribution, out-of-order/late data, hot/warm queries, connector bursts, model/provider latency and failure.

- Each release reports nominal and high-load headroom, cost per unit and the first limiting component. Averages without distribution and tenancy shape are rejected.

- An anonymized reference-customer profile records endpoint/identity mix, sources, GB/day, retention, detections, analysts and query behavior so capacity claims are reproducible.

#  **APPENDIX J \| Glossary**

| **Term**                 | **Meaning**                                                                                                                |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **ADR**                  | Architecture Decision Record.                                                                                              |
| **AI-BOM / ML-BOM**      | Inventory of models, providers, prompts/agents, tools, datasets/indexes and dependent software used by an AI feature.      |
| **Anchoring**            | Publishing a signed ledger checkpoint to independent witnesses so later history rewrites or equivocation are detectable.   |
| **Attestation / SOC 2**  | An independent CPA examination and report under AICPA criteria; not a product “certification.”                             |
| **Cell**                 | Repeatable regional deployment unit containing tenant-pinned compute, data, keys, queues and limits.                       |
| **Command attestation**  | Customer-side verification of response command signature, scope, authority, approval, expiry and anti-replay data.         |
| **Completeness state**   | Explicit declaration of whether all expected evidence for a scope/window was collected and evaluable.                      |
| **Design partner**       | Early contracted customer participating in evidence, workflow and auditor validation.                                      |
| **Dual landing**         | Independent security-led or compliance-led purchase and onboarding paths.                                                  |
| **Evidence ledger**      | Tenant-scoped append-only integrity structure binding evidence records to externally witnessed checkpoints.                |
| **Freeze switch**        | Dual-controlled, out-of-band mechanism stopping all action command issuance.                                               |
| **Gate-0**               | Load-bearing ADR and proof set required before build-ready declaration.                                                    |
| **Human-in-command**     | People retain authority for material/high-impact actions and conclusions; automation operates only within explicit policy. |
| **Modular monolith**     | Single deployable with enforced domain boundaries and service-compatible interfaces.                                       |
| **No-LLM critical path** | Critical security, identity, evidence and recovery functions operate without a probabilistic model.                        |
| **OCSF**                 | Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework.                                                                                       |
| **RAG**                  | Retrieval-augmented generation, governed here by tenant/source/version/purpose controls.                                   |
| **Scale envelope**       | Versioned low/nominal/high workload used for capacity, reliability and cost validation.                                    |
| **Witness**              | Independent append-only service or operator receiving signed checkpoint commitments.                                       |
| **Wedge**                | Initial market sequence: compliance-native MDR for regulated mid-market customers.                                         |

All standard security acronyms used in this document — ABAC, ATT&CK, BYOK/HYOK, CPQ, DORA, EDR, GRC, IGA, IR, JIT, MDR, OTel, PAM, RBAC, RPO, RTO, SBOM, SCIM, SIEM, SLO, SOAR, SPIFFE, STIX/TAXII, TLP, WORM and XDR — retain their established meanings.
